title: Post-1.0 compatibility and external-verifier roadmap
description:
## What & scope
Group the four explicitly registered post-1.0 roadmap deliverables without pulling any of them into G0-G4: the APFS Local durability profile after an asupersync non-io_uring backend exists, the harder Windows profile after APFS, BoltCompatProfileV2 write support with its own conformance gate, and the dependency-free external verifier SDK. This is a discoverability/closure epic, not a 1.0 release prerequisite.

## Why
Standalone roadmap tasks were semantically correct but easy to miss in epic-oriented planning. One post-1.0 aggregate makes deferral explicit, preserves prerequisite order, and prevents future documentation from silently implying these capabilities shipped in 1.0.

## Design and boundary
Each child retains its exact platform/protocol/proof ownership and independent gate. Every child depends on its declared foundation/1.0 prerequisite; this epic depends on the children. No G0-G4 gate, 1.0 workstream epic, or capability manifest may depend on this epic. Reserved schemas/profiles remain frozen where the plan requires, while activation stays absent until each child passes.

## Success Criteria
- All four children close with their own unit/property/fault/conformance/E2E and detailed diagnostic evidence.
- APFS remains blocked on the named asupersync backend; Windows remains ordered after APFS; Bolt V2 passes its write/TCK/differential corpus; the verifier SDK proves dependency-free independent verification.
- A graph test proves this epic is downstream of G4 and never in any G0-G4 prerequisite closure.
- Capability/docs tests prove each unfinished roadmap item is advertised as absent/post-1.0, never partial.
- The roadmap rollup emits versioned JSONL with child id, prerequisite/gate state, platform/profile/version, evidence references, verdict, and replay commands; no child may inherit another child or G4 green bar.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: attaching post-1.0 tasks to W10/W11/G4 epics in the blocking direction, silently dropping them, or representing them as vague prose. Risk is roadmap drift; explicit graph and capability tests keep status honest.

## Provenance
Plan registered platform/compatibility roadmap after §19 workstreams and §15 external verification/publication goals.

title: W5 Stage 1: implement and prove binary FreeJoin
description:
## What & scope
Implement and independently close the first Loom risk-reduction stage: the final GLA-compatible binary FreeJoin kernel over authorized Strata tries/cursors. Own binary relation binding, key-order negotiation, exact intersection/probe semantics, duplicate/multiplicity handling, cancellation/resource accounting, and a deliberately nonadaptive pinned plan profile. This is a final subset of the unified operator family, not a hash-join substitute or throwaway executor.

## Why
§20 identifies FreeJoin/factorization/adaptivity as the crown-jewel risk and mandates the evidence order binary FreeJoin -> run-trie WCOJ -> factorized columns -> adaptivity. A separately closable binary stage gives later work an oracle-grounded semantic and complexity baseline while preserving the one-family design.

## Design and phase contract
Use the canonical GLA rows, answer/security contracts, `QueryCx`, `ResourceLedger`, and Secure View cursors. The kernel accepts two trie-shaped inputs and emits canonical vector batches with exact Z/multiplicity semantics, deterministic CGSE tie breaks, positive/negative/gap witness traces, and complexity-witness counters. A pinned deterministic plan selects build/probe or ordered intersection from declared features; no learned/adaptive choice, factorized output, or multiway leapfrog activation is permitted in this stage. Spill and cancellation use the final executor obligations and never expose unauthorized cardinality.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests cover every binary key/order shape, empty/duplicate/skewed inputs, NULL/value semantics, multiplicities, witness emission, canonical ordering, arithmetic/resource boundaries, cancellation points, and fail-closed authorization.
- Property/model and differential tests compare arbitrary small binary joins against `fgdb-reference`, flatten vector batches, vary physical representations and compaction, and assert identical rows, witnesses, logical digests, and declared complexity counters.
- Mutation/fuzz suites attack GLA rows, trie cursors, codecs, key comparisons, corrupt batches, resource exhaustion, and cancellation at every obligation boundary.
- E2E runs authenticated GQL through binder -> pinned binary FreeJoin -> authorized Strata cursors -> SSI/constraint validation -> canonical result/replay across spill, restart, and representation changes; an unauthorized edge type fails before observation.
- The stage evidence report publishes semantic corpus results and operation/bytes/memory distributions separately from later WCOJ/factorization/adaptivity claims.
- Detailed JSONL diagnostics record `{run_id,stage:"binary-freejoin",query_and_plan_digest,input_relation_and_cursor_commitments,key_order,policy_epoch,pinned_action,rows_and_multiplicities,witness_digest,op_count,bytes,memory_spill,cancel_or_fault,oracle,verdict,evidence_refs,seed,replay_command}` with protected facts redacted.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a separate hash-join engine, parser-interpreted execution, post-filter authorization, unbounded materialization, or borrowing later-stage evidence. Risk is a baseline optimized to one representation; representation differential and explicit counters prevent it.

## Provenance
Plan §§8.1-8.4, §15, §17, §20 FreeJoin risk mitigation, B3/B5, FG-INV-05/06/09/19/20.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Reference semantics, RootSlot, and RootBootstrap
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Reference semantics, RootSlot, and RootBootstrap. This task embeds source-plan lines 1388-1444 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

## Appendix A — On-Disk Object Formats (normative contract)

`RoleTransitionActivationState` is the closed role union `Meta{migration_nonce,transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,continuity_reservation_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionContinuityReservationReceipt>,target_service_visibility_epoch,phase:ProjectionPreparedHidden{activation_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef}|ServicePrepareApplied{prepare_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef}|FinalizedPendingIndependentReopen{finalize_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_state:Unsealed|Sealed{seal_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionPromotionRootSeal<Meta>>}}|MetaReopenedAwaitingShardAcks{reopen_confirm_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionPromotionRootSeal<Meta>>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionIndependentReopenProof<Meta>>}|Complete{completion_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_release_state}}|Shard{migration_nonce,transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,shard_id,continuity_reservation_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionContinuityReservationReceipt>,target_service_visibility_epoch,phase:ProjectionPreparedHidden{install_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef}|OpenedPendingIndependentReopen{open_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_state:Unsealed|Sealed{seal_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionPromotionRootSeal<Shard>>}}|ShardOperationalAwaitingMetaCompletion{reopen_confirm_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionPromotionRootSeal<Shard>>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionIndependentReopenProof<Shard>>}|Complete{completion_apply_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_release_state}}`. This exact schema supersedes any earlier compact navigation rendering. The state object, reached by the payload's existing strong field, is the canonical owner of role-transition seals/proofs; `None` is legal only outside a role transition. Post-publication visibility/state certificates live in the certificate ledger and are supplied separately to later pin-release/service consumers as `CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>`; the Complete root cannot embed the certificate that certifies itself. Generated construction-DAG negatives reject that future back-edge. Generated phase/bootstrap/admission rows require `RoleTransitionPreparedHidden` through prepare, `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen` through Unsealed/Sealed, `Operational` plus an awaiting phase after reopen, and ordinary service only in `Complete`.

All durable encodings use a declared format major/minor, little-endian fixed integers, canonical unsigned LEB128 only where the field says varint, length-before-allocation, checked arithmetic, and per-kind maximum sizes. Unknown additive-minor fields are length-delimited and skipped; unknown required flags fail closed. `CanonicalScalarProfile` defines float/decimal/string/time bytes. Readers authenticate/validate headers and resource bounds before allocating or decompressing.

**Reference semantics.** Every ObjectId-bearing edge declares a wire tag: `StrongRef{oid}` (always followed); `StrongMarkerRef{marker_ref}` and `StrongCommandRef{command_ref}` (retain the named history object); `ConditionalCoordinateRef{oid,graph,branch}` (sequence-neutral payload whose retention sequence comes from its enclosing committed marker); `ConditionalMarkerRef{marker_ref,axis:Global|Branch(graph,branch)}` and `ConditionalCommandRef{command_ref,axis:Logical}` (followed until an authenticated matching checkpoint/cut); `WeakMarkerIdentity{marker_oid,commit_seq}` (provenance/identity only); `WeakLocator`/`PhysicalRealizationRef` (nonretaining local lookup metadata); or `WeakDigest{digest}` (comparison only). Bare `MarkerRef{marker_oid:[u8;32],commit_seq:u64}` and `CommandRef{command_record_oid:[u8;32],logical_command_seq:u64}` are identities, **not reachability by themselves**; an enclosing tag supplies that. `StrongCommandRef` always means a previously constructed `LogicalCommandRecord`; an applied result cites its already identified input and assigned order only through the exact closed `AppliedControlRef`, `AppliedAbortRef`, or `AuthorityAppliedRef` tags below, never an ambient/local-only assumption.

`ConsensusDomain {database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Local|Meta|Shard{shard_id},group_id}` is the indivisible authority/consumer identity in every signed, MACed, indexed, or retained cross-group transcript. `group_id` is also a random 256-bit database-global unique identifier, but no validator relies on uniqueness without matching the complete domain. Later shorthand `authority_group_id`, `consumer_group_id`, or `group_id` in a cross-group schema means the corresponding full `ConsensusDomain`; wire encoders never serialize the scalar alone. `RemoteObjectIdentity {authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,object_oid,object_kind,canonical_digest}` is comparison-only and never a local reachability edge.

`RootAuthorityTrustBody` is the signature-free immutable `{authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,artifact_kind:FreshShardedGenesis|CertifiedLocalRoleTransition,canonical_genesis_or_transition_bytes,target_configuration_oid,target_configuration_canonical_digest,externally_pinned_root_policy_id,expected_root_verification_key_set_digest,threshold,source_identity_or_transition_continuity_commitment,body_digest:BodyDigest<RootAuthorityTrustBody>}`; its registered body transcript includes every preceding field and excludes exactly `body_digest`. `RootAuthorityTrustArtifact` is `{body_ref:StrongRef<RootAuthorityTrustBody>,body_digest:BodyDigest<RootAuthorityTrustBody>,canonical_root_authority_signature_set,signed_transcript_digest:TranscriptDigest<RootAuthorityTrustArtifact>}`. Each root signature signs the domain-separated tuple `{schema/tag,authority_domain,artifact_kind,body_digest,externally_pinned_root_policy_id}`; the artifact transcript includes the body digest and canonically sorted signatures and excludes exactly `signed_transcript_digest`. Validation first resolves the deployment's externally pinned policy, key set, and threshold and byte-matches their IDs/digest to the body, then verifies signatures and transcript; keys merely embedded in the object can never select their own trust root. The canonical genesis/transition bytes and policy evidence remain strongly retained and independently reverified. `RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence` is the nonrecursive imported leaf `{authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,configuration_oid,configuration_canonical_digest,canonical_configuration_bytes,configuration_adoption_raft_index,adoption_log_prefix_digest,member_verification_key_set,payload_predicate_digest,trust_transition:Genesis{root_authority_trust_artifact_ref:StrongRef<RootAuthorityTrustArtifact>}|Successor{predecessor_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,joint_transition_transcript,old_configuration_quorum_signatures,new_configuration_quorum_signatures,final_retirement_floor_digest}|ValidatedCheckpointSuccessor{predecessor_anchor_ref:StrongRef<ValidatedRemoteConfigurationAnchor>,joint_transition_transcript,old_configuration_quorum_signatures,new_configuration_quorum_signatures,final_retirement_floor_digest},minimum_configuration_retention_floor,signer_epoch,configuration_quorum_signatures}`. Current-member signatures alone are never a trust root. Embedded canonical configuration bytes recompute the OID/digest and self-bind the complete domain; the transition proves adoption from an already trusted root artifact, predecessor, or anchor. `RemoteConfigurationRef` means a consumer-local `StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>`.

Authority-local certificate object `T` and its imported representation are deliberately different schemas. `ExportLeaf<T> {domain:ImportedCertificateDomain,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,export_projection_version,object_specific_scalar_projection,local_strong_ref_projection[RemoteObjectIdentity],target_closure_inventory_digest,authority_ledger_floor,quorum_signatures}` replaces every authority-local strong reference with a typed remote identity/closure commitment while preserving every verifier-relevant scalar. Its generated projector is injectively bound to the canonical digest of `T`; a consumer never decodes an authority-local `StrongRef` as local. `RemotePayloadAvailabilityEvidence` is the consumer-local leaf `{authority_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,certificate_export_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>>,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,target_closure_inventory_digest,payload_predicate_digest,receipt_set_commitment,encoding_placement_coverage,failure_domains,authority_retention_floor,signer_epoch,authority_quorum_signatures}`; the authority ledger separately roots the real certificate/receipts.

W12's one cross-consensus edge is `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T> {authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,authority_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,export_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<T>>,target_closure_inventory_digest,payload_availability_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemotePayloadAvailabilityEvidence>,retention_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>}`. Every `StrongRef` inside it targets a complete consumer-local leaf; none targets `T` in the authority group. The generated `T -> ExportLeaf<T>` verifier and field-level schema registry define exactly which refs become remote identities. `grant_id = H("fgdb:remote-grant:v1", authority_domain, consumer_domain, target_identity, grant_nonce)`; consumer and authority maps are keyed by `(authority_domain,grant_id)`, and any collision with nonidentical bytes fails closed. `RemoteGrantTargetRef` is the containing-schema-generated closed union with one typed strong-reference arm per exportable authority-local target kind; it has no generic target arm. `RemoteRetentionGrantSpec` is authority-group input `{grant_id,authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,authority_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,target_ref:RemoteGrantTargetRef,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,target_closure_inventory_digest,payload_availability_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>,minimum_authority_checkpoint_floor,grant_nonce}`. The target ref and identity must be the exact registered pair. Authority apply creates `RemoteRetentionGrantRecord {spec_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantSpec>,authority_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,state:Active}` in `RemoteRetentionObligationRoot`, which roots the exact target closure. Its quorum exports `RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence {authority_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,grant_record_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,grant_id,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,target_closure_inventory_digest,payload_availability_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemotePayloadAvailabilityEvidence>,authority_order_index,minimum_authority_checkpoint_floor,grant_nonce,signer_epoch,authority_quorum_signatures}`. The consumer may publish the wrapper only after authenticating all leaves and byte-matching both complete domains; the authority ledger, not the evidence, owns the remote target.

Release is an explicit six-transition handshake, never inferred from time or a missing client. (1) After canonically removing/replacing every reference while retaining the grant leaf, the consumer orders `RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestSpec {grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,consumer_release_state_identity:WeakDigest,complete_consumer_root_digest,consumer_checkpoint_floor,successor_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>?,release_nonce}`; apply rechecks the complete consumer root, constructs `RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestRecord {spec_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestSpec>,consumer_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,consumer_no_reference_floor_digest}`, and installs `ReleaseRequested`. That type state cannot acquire or create another local ref under the old grant; any concurrent/new use must first acquire and publish a distinct successor grant. (2) Only afterward does the consumer quorum create authority-local `RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,request_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestRecord>,complete_consumer_root_digest,consumer_no_reference_floor_digest,successor_grant_identity?,release_nonce,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}` after rechecking the root. A generated specialized `ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate>` replaces its local refs with remote identities; the later consumer publish control installs this portable leaf as `ReleaseCertified`. (3) The authority imports that leaf and orders `RemoteRetentionReleaseApplySpec {active_grant_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantRecord>,release_request_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate>>,expected_active_grant_digest,verified_consumer_no_reference_floor,successor_transfer_proof?}`. Apply rechecks every stronger authority root, removes the active grant, and creates `RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone {grant_record_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,grant_spec_digest:WeakDigest,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,request_certificate_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,release_nonce,authority_command_input_digest:WeakDigest,authority_order_index}` with no strong edge to the active record, spec, target, or apply command. The release command/log retains those inputs only until its verified cut. (4) Only after that applied root does the authority quorum create local `RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,tombstone_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone>,grant_id,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,release_nonce,authority_order_index,authority_state_root_digest,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}` and its specialized portable ExportLeaf. (5) A later authority publish control atomically creates `RemoteRetentionAckPublishRecord {ack_certificate_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>,ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,authority_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,summary_key}` and installs `RemoteReleaseSummaryEntry {authority_domain,consumer_domain,grant_id,target_identity,release_nonce,ack_leaf_identity,ack_digest,authority_order_index,published_at_order_index,permanent_release_proof_floor}` in `RemoteReleaseSummaryRoot`. The summary and nonrecursive archive-backed ack leaf remain available through the database's capability-safe permanent release-proof floor and require no new releasable grant merely to prove the old grant released. (6) The consumer imports the portable leaf without a CRSR, rechecks that its current complete root still contains no old-grant ref, orders `ConsumeReleaseAck`, and creates `RemoteRetentionConsumeAckRecord {ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,consumer_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,current_no_old_grant_ref_proof_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionNoOldGrantProof>,summary_key}`; only then may it retire request/grant evidence after its checkpoint floor. `AuthorityAppliedRef = Local{command_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,logical_command_seq}|Meta{command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>,global_logical_command_seq}|Shard{command_ref:StrongRef<ShardControlCommand>,shard_raft_index}` is used only inside its owning group and prevents role ambiguity. A crash at any point leaves an authority target root, permanent release proof, or replayable pending transition; no imported leaf contains an ordinary strong edge into its source group.

W12 history wrappers are distinct rather than overloading the local `LogicalCommandRecord` tag: `StrongGlobalCommandRef{record_oid,global_logical_command_seq}`, `ConditionalGlobalCommandRef{record_oid,global_logical_command_seq,axis=GlobalLogical}`, and `WeakGlobalCommandIdentity{record_oid,global_logical_command_seq}` target `GlobalTxnRecord|GlobalControlRecord`; `ConditionalGlobalTxnInputRef{command_oid,assigned_global_logical_command_seq,axis=GlobalLogical}` targets the already-built `GlobalTxnCommand` and is valid only when the record at that sequence names the same input; `StrongShardCommandRef{record_oid,shard_id,shard_raft_index}`, `ConditionalShardCommandRef{record_oid,shard_id,shard_raft_index,axis=ShardRaft}`, and `WeakShardCommandIdentity{record_oid,shard_id,shard_raft_index}` target `ShardCommandRecord`. Strong variants retain, conditional variants stop only at a verified matching meta/shard checkpoint cut, and weak variants compare only. Cross-group carriage of any target still requires `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef`; these wrappers are only within the owning consensus group.

Canonical result objects that can be produced in either posture use closed role tags rather than pretending every input is local: `AppliedControlRef = Local{command_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,logical_command_seq} | Meta{command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>,global_logical_command_seq}`; `AppliedAbortRef = LocalControl{command_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,logical_command_seq} | LocalTxn{command_ref:StrongRef<AdmittedTxnAbortCommand>,logical_command_seq} | MetaControl{command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>,global_logical_command_seq} | MetaTxn{command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnCommand>,global_logical_command_seq}`; and `AuditCandidateRef = Local{blocked_after_logical_command_seq,candidate_state_root_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStateRoot>} | Meta{blocked_after_global_logical_command_seq,candidate_state_root_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStateRoot>}`. The group-role and lifecycle-stage validator accepts only the matching tag: active/unadmitted Local cancellation uses LocalControl, admitted Local abort uses LocalTxn, active/unadmitted Meta cancellation uses MetaControl, and admitted Meta abort uses MetaTxn. These tags are part of the v1 durable schema and the generated spec/result compatibility matrix; no decoder infers posture from ambient configuration.

Key-envelope openers use the separate retaining physical edge `StrongCiphertextRef<T> { logical_oid, ciphertext_id, dek_id, ciphertext_digest, protected_length, key_opener_ref:KeyOpenerRef<T>, recoverability_profile, selected_realizations[CiphertextRealizationRef<T>],payload_availability_certificate_ref:PayloadAvailabilityCertificateRef<T> }`. `KeyOpenerRef<T>`, `CiphertextRealizationRef<T>`, and `PayloadAvailabilityCertificateRef<T>` are generated exact unions whose arms are legal for that ciphertext class and owning role; no bare `StrongRef` or cross-role certificate decodes. Its target ciphertext, complete authenticated realization inventory, opener, and certificate exist before the referring envelope object, and the certificate must prove that the selected set satisfies the named profile under the exact configuration. It pins that `CiphertextId` and the selected recoverable `EncodingId`/`PlacementId` set; recoding or movement first creates a successor envelope/grant edge with a newly certified set before the old set can retire, while re-encryption cannot substitute a new ciphertext under a live reference. This is intentionally stronger than ordinary logical reachability and is included in GC, reconfiguration, backup, and key-destruction floors.

The schemas below use a flattened prose rendering, but **names and suffixes never imply reference strength**. Every field's exact type, cardinality, identity class, target, role/posture predicate, retention/cut behavior, and `PriorObject` construction annotation come from §5.1's generated `durable_fields.toml`; the rendering checker rejects any brace field that lacks or disagrees with its row. A compact phrase such as “typed mandatory inventory” is a named closed sub-schema, never an open bag or slash-separated set of ambient refs. Bootstrap-slot root identity is an external GC root and is followed as strong. Pending/prepared traversal treats a registered `ConditionalCoordinateRef` as strong because no committed-marker cut context exists. Archive and prior-incarnation identities are separate nonlocal classes and can never enter the current local ObjectId mark set. Every concrete target of a strong or currently followed conditional edge must exist before the parent encoder runs. Recursive persistent nodes are legal only in that child-before-parent direction. Generated schema/reference/DAG checkers compare the field table, Appendix rendering, Rust encoders, and registry rows; they reject unresolved, untyped, role-invalid, self, mutual, or future-result cycles and fail G0 on drift. Unknown tags or context fail closed.

**RootSlot + RootBootstrap.** Each slot is exactly 4096 bytes at offsets 0 and 4096:

```text
RootSlot {
  magic="FGRT", format_major:u16, format_minor:u16, slot_generation:u64,
  local_writer_fence_epoch:u64, database_id:[u8;16],
  database_security_namespace_id:[u8;32], cluster_incarnation:u64,
  incarnation_continuity_profile_id:u16,
  cluster_incarnation_continuity_digest:[u8;32], continuity_cas_version:u64,
  service_visibility_epoch:u64,
  root_manifest_oid:[u8;32],
  bootstrap: RootBootstrap, reserved_zeroes, tear_checksum:[u8;32]
}
RootBootstrap {
  root_encoding_id:[u8;32], root_placement_id:[u8;32],
  root_placement_epoch:u64, failure_domain_policy_id:[u8;32],
  root_failure_domain_id:[u8;32], segment_id:[u8;16], offset:u64,
  encoded_len:u64, root_symbol_inventory_digest:[u8;32],
  object_kind:u16, canonical_plaintext_len:u64, codec_profile:u32,
  compressed_len:u64, data_crypto_profile:u32, dek_id:[u8;32],
  nonce_len:u8, nonce_or_siv:[u8;32], object_tag_len:u8,
  fec_profile:u32, transfer_length:u64, oti_common:u64, oti_scheme:u32,
  symbol_size:u32, source_block_count:u32, symbol_auth_profile:u16,
  ciphertext_id:[u8;32], ciphertext_digest:[u8;32], opener_kind:u16,
  oid_key_id:[u8;32], opener_payload_len:u16, opener_payload:[u8;1024],
  opener_digest:[u8;32]
}
```

Unused nonce/opener bytes are zero. Profile registries fix bounds and tag lengths. Together with `root_manifest_oid`, these fields reproduce the root's exact `CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest`, complete `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId`, and specialized `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId { encoding_id, root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy_id, ContiguousSpan { root_failure_domain_id, segment_id, offset, encoded_len, root_symbol_inventory_digest } }` byte-for-byte. Recovery scans the declared span, authenticates canonical SymbolRecords, verifies the sorted inventory commitment, and recomputes `root_placement_id` before decode. `opener_payload` is a versioned bundle of inline wraps or authenticated KMS/HSM locators sufficient to recover both the named root DEK and immutable `K_oid` without consulting the object index; its digest covers kind, key IDs, locators/wraps, and namespace/incarnation. The authenticated root repeats the exact database/security-namespace/incarnation tuple, and recovery rejects disagreement before following its closure. A structurally valid highest-generation slot is never silently rolled back after authentication/closure failure (§5.1).

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

There is direct precedent for the slice owner choosing and recording it as contestable — shard_id=u32, GraphId=u64, BranchId=u64, release_nonce-as-bytes were all a01 rulings of exactly this shape. The signer-lock pair additionally has no named target schema anywhere in the plan and affects every SameGroupCertificate family, so it is genuinely cross-slice.

=== 2. THE ANNOTATION / SEMANTIC-BINDING / EVIDENCE LAYER (CATALOG-SCALE) ===

This is not an a01 choice and should not be made as one. Today the catalog has ZERO annotation, semantic_binding, expansion_binding, and evidence rows across ALL 21 slices, with all four EXPECTED_*_COUNT consts pinned at 0.

The completion law is per-TARGET, not per-slice (appendix_a.rs, the definition_status=="complete" block). Every complete target requires:
  - exactly one annotation
  - exactly one semantic binding
  - at least one static evidence row covering G0
  - at least one runtime evidence row, planned or live
  - a source-reconciled top|/field|/union|/arm| contract
So the layer is roughly four rows per target. Current cost, by slice, at 534 targets:
  a01 219 (~876 rows)   a16 170 (~680)   g0 35 (~140)   a15 29 (~116)
  a04  16 (~64)         a10  16 (~64)    a06 11 (~44)   a20 10 (~40)
  a19   8 (~32)         a03   6 (~24)    a02  5 (~20)   a11  4 (~16)
  a17   4 (~16)         a07   1 (~4)
  TOTAL ~2136 rows, and it grows with every target any lane lands.

WHAT EACH OWNER WOULD HAVE TO DO, and why this must be one contract rather than 21 improvisations: an annotation is source-checked (source_annotation_contract_mismatch requires it to byte-match the census exact_type and cardinality, and top-level annotations must discharge the generic signature through concrete expansions), so annotations are largely DERIVABLE and should be generated, not hand-written. Semantic bindings and evidence rows are NOT derivable — they name owner bead, crate, checker, test/scenario/event IDs and gate. Those are per-owner knowledge.

PROPOSED SHAPE, for the other slice owners to adopt or contest:
 (a) Freeze the four row schemas and their pin mechanics ONCE, in one reviewed increment, before any slice authors a single row. Getting this wrong after 2000 rows exist is a mass migration.
 (b) Generate annotations from the census the way projections are generated today, with a sanctioned writer command and a byte-diff law, so annotation drift is impossible by construction. Do not hand-author 2136 rows.
 (c) Author semantic bindings and evidence per slice, by that slice's owner, since only they know the checker/test/gate IDs.
 (d) Sequence it AFTER the residual field/union/arm coverage of each slice, never before: an annotation binds to a target_row_id, so every target minted later needs its own four rows anyway. Front-loading it just means editing the same rows twice.
 (e) Nobody should flip definition_status="complete" until (a)-(d) are done for that slice, because the flip arms all of these laws simultaneously, plus source_complete_census_uncovered and source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved.

=== 3. WHAT I PROPOSE TO DO NEXT, CONCRETELY ===
 - Land the two provably-landable ExportLeaf<T> rows (uncovered 12 -> 10). Small, no ruling, positional tags.
 - File the tracked items as beads in ONE batched br create pass with the architecture bead-provenance pins re-frozen in the SAME commit, under the catalog token, so architecture-check is never transiently red for the other five agents.
 - Add the dependency edge a01 -> a04 rather than inventing a ruling for two types the plan already defines.

WHY THIS IS GENUINELY UNSAFE AND NOT MERE UNTIDINESS: reserved means the member layout is not frozen. PlacementRecord's transcript is IDENTITY-BEARING — the record's ObjectId is a function of the canonical bytes of a type whose layout may still change. An active identity law over a mutable layout is the same hazard class as a derived structure outranking its source: today's placement_id and tomorrow's can differ for identical placements, with nothing detecting it.

IS THE CHECKER MISSING A LAW? YES, verified rather than assumed. PhysicalKind.transcript is typed as an opaque String (identity.rs:103) and is never decomposed; no law cross-references a physical kind's transcript against the lifecycle status of the types it names. Control: 10 other status/lifecycle checks exist in identity.rs, so the grep is sound and the absence is real. Note the CONTRASTING precedent — union_arm_lifecycle_mismatch rejects only 'retired' and 'experimental', so a RESERVED target is explicitly legal for a union arm. That is defensible for a plain reference and NOT defensible for an identity-bearing transcript, which is exactly the distinction no law currently draws.

MY RULING, three parts with distinct owners:
 (a) DO NOT 'fix' this by flipping the wire type to active now. Its members are still unregistered (none of a02's three names exist), so activating it would freeze an empty shell and be strictly worse. The reserved state is a LEGITIMATE TRANSIENT.
 (b) The anomaly RESOLVES ITSELF under Ruling 1: once a02 registers the members, the wire type earns active status and the active-referent-over-reserved-type state disappears. So the sequencing is a02 registers members -> wire type activates -> anomaly gone. No emergency.
 (c) THE MISSING LAW IS THE REAL DELIVERABLE, and it is checker/scaffold work, not a01 data: an ACTIVE physical record kind whose identity-bearing transcript names a type must require that type to be ACTIVE. Without it this state is invisible and will recur; cc_1 found this instance by eye, which does not scale. Implementing it means giving transcript enough structure to name its referents rather than leaving it an opaque String — that is the non-trivial part and it belongs with the scaffold/checker owner.

WHAT I WILL LAND when I next take catalog as pane3-a01: only the small (Ruling 1) fix — re-cite the 0x001e encoding_context from a01:1388-1444 to a02:1449. I will NOT flip any status and will NOT touch a02's rows.

comments.text:
COMPLETION-LAYER FINDING FOR ALL 21 SLICES: PARTIAL ANNOTATION SETS ARE LEGAL, AND THE GATE IS PER-TARGET, NOT PER-SLICE.

A slice at definition_status=declared may carry any number of annotation rows, including zero or a handful, because every mandatory-annotation law keys on a TARGET being complete: appendix_a.rs ~11137 emits complete_slice_annotation_missing only after the guard `if row.definition_status != "complete"` skips non-complete targets, and source_annotation_contract_ambiguous (verify_annotation_source_contracts, appendix_a.rs:7369, the check ~54 lines in) fires only when the source is non-exact AND target.definition_status == "complete". So you can annotate incrementally, target by target, without flipping anything.

THE ONE LAW THAT DOES APPLY REGARDLESS OF STATUS: if a field target's census source IS exact, any annotation you write for it must byte-match the census exact_type and cardinality — that check sits OUTSIDE the complete-gate. So partial is legal, but wrong is not: an annotation on a declared target is validated against the source the moment it exists.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR SEQUENCING: it means the completion layer does NOT have to be an all-or-nothing per-slice campaign. Slices can land annotations progressively as their coverage closes, and a slice can pilot a handful of rows to prove the contract before committing to hundreds. That was the open question in my cross-slice proposal and it is now answered in the permissive direction.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER PROPOSAL, because it will otherwise mislead planning. I argued annotations were "largely derivable" and should be GENERATED rather than hand-authored. Against the schema cod_1 actually froze, that is wrong. Annotation has NINETEEN fields, and only exact_type and cardinality are census-forced. The other seventeen - including posture, authority, locality, redaction_class, resource_bounds, compatibility, digest_recipe and retention_and_cut_rule - are per-row judgement, and there is no generator: ANNOTATION_CONTRACT is [AnnotationContractPin; 0] and each row additionally needs a reciprocal compiled pin with the same 19 fields. So the layer costs roughly two hand-authored 19-field records per target, not one generated row. My reality-check estimate of ~4 rows per target understated the effort per row; the row COUNT was right, the per-row cost was not. Anyone planning the layer should either build a generator for the derivable subset first or budget for hand-authoring.

ANNOTATION PILOT DESIGN (a01), complete enough that the hold is an apply. Designed off-token against HEAD 795830a. I will queue for catalog as pane3-a01pilot; cc_1 goes first with the bead-provenance split.

=== PILOT SET: FOUR ROWS, CHOSEN TO SPAN THE TRAP CLASSES RATHER THAN TO BE EASY ===
All four are a01 RootSlot field targets whose census source is EXACT, so their annotation exact_type and cardinality are FORCED and I am testing the contract rather than arguing about content.
  1. a01:field:root-slot-cluster-incarnation                   exact_type=u64       cardinality=one              baseline
  2. a01:field:root-slot-incarnation-continuity-profile-id     exact_type=u16       cardinality=one              repeatability
  3. a01:field:root-slot-database-id                           exact_type=[u8;16]   cardinality=many-or-indexed  CARDINALITY-VOCABULARY trap
  4. a01:field:root-slot-magic                                 exact_type="FGRT"    cardinality=one              QUOTED-LITERAL trap
Deliberately four, not one: a single-row pilot proves the plumbing but finds no traps, and traps are the whole reason to pilot before 227.

=== SCOPE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE a01 CLOSURE MAP ===
Of a01's field targets, 95 have an EXACT census source (annotation exact_type/cardinality forced) and 74 DO NOT. That second number is a completion blocker I had not quantified: a complete target MUST have an annotation (complete_slice_annotation_missing), and an annotation on a complete target whose source is non-exact fires source_annotation_contract_ambiguous. So a01 cannot reach complete until those 74 census sources are disambiguated - which is source work, in the same family as the ambiguous-candidate problem blocking CertificateSignerLock. Add it to the closure map: a01 needs 4 coverage keys + 2 adjudications + 74 source disambiguations + the annotation layer, not just the first two.

=== ANNOTATION TEMPLATE (19 fields; only the first two are forced) ===
  row_id                  derived - DO NOT hand-write, see trap 3
  target_row_id           the a01:field:... id above
  exact_type              FORCED, byte-match census
  cardinality             FORCED, byte-match census as_str()
  layout / role / posture / authority / locality            authored
  generic_expansions[] / role_expansions[]                  empty for these four (no generics, no role indexing)
  reference_semantics     "none" for all four (RootSlot scalars are not references)
  target_schema_ids[]     empty (follows from reference_semantics=none)
  construction_order / retention_and_cut_rule / digest_recipe / redaction_class / resource_bounds / compatibility   authored
Each row ALSO needs a reciprocal compiled AnnotationContractPin with the same 19 fields; ANNOTATION_CONTRACT is currently [AnnotationContractPin; 0], so I am the first consumer and there is no precedent row to copy.

=== LANDING ORDER ===
The four rows are mutually independent - an annotation binds only to its target_row_id, so there is no inter-row ordering law. Order is therefore: (a) splice all four TOML rows + four compiled pins together, (b) bump ANNOTATION_CONTRACT array 0->4 and EXPECTED_ANNOTATION_COUNT 0->4 TOGETHER (catalog_annotation_contract_pin_inconsistent fires if they diverge), (c) derive EXPECTED_ANNOTATION_SHA256 from the loader's own drift message, (d) gate. One increment, not four.

=== TRAPS I EXPECT, WITH THE MITIGATION ===
 1. CARDINALITY VOCABULARY. Cardinality::as_str() emits "one" | "optional" | "many" | "many-or-indexed". The annotation byte-match compares against THAT string, so database_id must carry "many-or-indexed". My own 2A-era note says census ManyOrIndexed maps to "many" in the FIELD-ROW vocabulary - that is a different row kind with a different vocabulary. Using "many" here will fail the byte-match. This is exactly why row 3 is in the pilot.
 2. QUOTED LITERAL. root-slot-magic's census exact_type is the four characters F G R T WRAPPED IN DOUBLE QUOTES, i.e. the quote characters are part of the value. The TOML must escape them. Getting this wrong looks like a trivial typo and fails a byte-match.
 3. ROW_ID DERIVATION. Per the a01 2G precedent, do not guess: land the row, read catalog_row_id_derived_mismatch, adopt the expected value it prints. lower_kebab mangles punctuation in ways that are not guessable.
 4. RUSTFMT BEFORE PATCH. The compiled pin entries must be rustfmt-canonical before the patch is derived, or cargo fmt --check fails the gate and the patch is stale the moment it is fixed. Fix the GENERATOR output, never run cargo fmt across appendix_a.rs - a whole-file reformat on a file several lanes edit can silently rewrite someone else's just-landed region. (Cost me a cycle in 2H.)
 5. THE FOUR INVISIBLE PIN SITES. I EXPECT none to apply: annotations add no target, move no epoch, and use no projection| fallback form. But expectation is not evidence - a green loader has never once been sufficient on this trail, so I will run g0_identity_e2e.sh and the composite regardless and report actual exit codes.
 6. STALE RLIB. Rebuild registry_check as the first action of the hold; three lanes have moved pins since my last build and cc_1 measured three stalenesses inside one hold.

=== WHAT THIS PILOT DELIVERS BEYOND FOUR ROWS ===
The first worked example of the completion layer for all 21 slices: a validated 19-field template, the reciprocal-pin mechanics, the two vocabulary traps, and a measured pin surface. That is the artifact - the rows are almost incidental.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Filesystem, cipher, encoding, placement, and symbols
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Filesystem, cipher, encoding, placement, and symbols. This task embeds source-plan lines 1445-1463 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**Filesystem durability and writer takeover.** `FilesystemDurabilityProfile` is a signed/checked-in artifact `{ profile_id, profile_version, os/kernel_range, allowed_filesystems_and_mount_predicates, forbidden_layers/options, required_lock_primitive, owner_death_rule, stable_inode_rule, slot_write_rule, file_sync_rule, directory_sync_rule, rename_no_replace_rule, cache_flush_assumption, probe_suite_oid }`. `FGFS-LINUX-LOCAL-V1` has exactly §5.1's ext4/XFS allowlist; a profile/mount not matching every predicate is not writable. A local `FilesystemInstanceRecord { profile_id, probe_suite_oid, mount_id, filesystem_type, canonical_mount_options, device_chain_digest, directory_device_inode, manifest_device_inode, checked_at, result_digest }` is diagnostic evidence, never a transferable proof or semantic root.

The takeover checker accepts only `NoGuard -> LeaseHeld(identity) -> ClosureRecovered(old_epoch) -> PendingFenceGuard(old_epoch+1) -> FenceRootDurableAndReread(old_epoch+1) -> WriterEnabled(FenceToken)`. Creation is `NoGuard -> StagingInodeLease -> PendingCreationGuard(epoch=1) -> CompleteStagingRootVerified -> RenameNoReplaceAndDirectorySync -> CanonicalRootReread -> WriterEnabled`. `PendingFenceGuard` is linear and can encode/seal exactly one fence-only `RootManifest` preserving the recovered state plus its inactive `RootSlot`; `PendingCreationGuard` can encode/seal only the registered Genesis closure and epoch-1 slot. Neither type implements user-segment, prepared-owner, receipt, Raft, canonical-transition, or general-root traits. `FenceToken` is nonserializable and nonconstructible outside the VFS/commit boundary; it binds the live lease handle, stable directory/root identity, profile, slot generation, and epoch. The fence-only root/slot must retain the exact prior canonical logical root, Raft/audit candidate, prepared root, and durable/applied/visible positions. Every immutable segment trailer records `{ database_security_namespace_id, cluster_incarnation, local_writer_fence_epoch, segment_id, sealed_len, inventory_digest, trailer_checksum }`; after promotion the local VFS refuses a seal, prepared-root update, receipt signature, Raft append acknowledgement/proposal, or root publication without the matching live token. Already receipted/ordered records from an older epoch remain strong obligations but cannot authorize new old-epoch publication. The crash matrix cuts after every lease/identity/recovery/object-sync/slot-write/slot-sync/staging-rename/directory-sync/reread step and includes owner death, path replacement, mount drift, stale descriptors, epoch overflow, competing creators, orphan staging, and a lying-sync profile that must be rejected.

**Cipher/encoding/placement records and SymbolRecord.** `CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest` is `{ logical_oid, object_kind, canonical_plaintext_len, codec_profile, compressed_len, data_crypto_profile, dek_id, object_nonce_or_siv, object_tag_len }`. Object AAD is the domain string plus logical OID and this canonical descriptor. `CiphertextRecord` is `{ descriptor, ciphertext_id, ciphertext_digest, object_tag_digest, protected_length }`; `CiphertextId` hashes descriptor+ciphertext+object tag. Immutable `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` is `{ ciphertext_id, fec_profile, transfer_length, oti_common, oti_scheme, symbol_size, source_block_count, symbol_auth_profile }`, and `EncodingId` hashes the domain/version plus its **complete canonical bytes**. Separately, `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId` is `{ encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }`, where `location_form = ContiguousSpan{failure_domain_id,segment_id,offset,encoded_len,symbol_inventory_digest} | Explicit{sorted_symbol_inventory_and_locators,failure_domains}`. `PlacementId` hashes the placement domain/version plus exactly that descriptor; immutable `PlacementRecord { placement_id, descriptor }` merely stores and cross-checks it. Moving/adding symbols creates a new placement record without changing encoding identity. KEK/wrap epoch is absent from both ciphertext and encoding identity. The authenticated local physical-realization index maps `CiphertextId`, `EncodingId`, and `PlacementId` to these records with nonretaining locators. An ordinary decoder obtains the complete descriptor/OTI/auth profile from an authenticated `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` (or FGP's authenticated encoding prelude) before accepting any symbol; a bare `SymbolRecord` is never self-authorizing.

```text
SymbolRecord {
  magic="FGEC", format_version:u16, header_len:u16, record_len:u32,
  logical_oid:[u8;32], ciphertext_id:[u8;32], encoding_id:[u8;32],
  object_kind:u16, source_block:u32, esi:u32, symbol_len:u32,
  transfer_length:u64, oti_common:u64, oti_scheme:u32, flags:u32,
  symbol_mac_profile:u16, symbol_mac_len:u16,
  payload:[u8;symbol_len], symbol_mac:[u8;symbol_mac_len]
}
```

The symbol MAC key/transcript are exactly §5.1's domain-separated construction. All framing/OTI/length fields and payload are MACed. Truncated/noncanonical tails are ignored only in proved-unreferenced staging; a reachable sealed tail triggers authenticated repair or fail-closed recovery.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

## Provenance
Complete audited plan Appendix A lines 1445-1463.

STARTING STATE: 4 physical kinds + 1 wire type + 5 targets landed; 0 of 70 field candidates covered. Top-level coverage was 3 of 9.

WHAT LANDED, and why these two first. CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest (0x003b, 9 members) and EncodingDescriptorWithoutId (0x003c, 8 members) were already LOAD-BEARING for landed ACTIVE physical kinds while themselves unregistered: CiphertextRecord's object AAD binds the cipher descriptor, and EncodingRecord's identity_law is literally BLAKE3("fgdb:encoding:v1" || canonical(EncodingDescriptorWithoutId)). An active record whose identity law names an unregistered structure is precisely the "apparent ref/OID/descriptor with no explicit row" Appendix A forbids, so this was the highest-value pair in the slice, not merely the easiest.

The census corroborated the source independently: 9 and 8 field candidates for these two owners, matching the a02:1449 bodies member-for-member. That agreement is why I trusted the member lists without hand-transcribing them.

THREE RULINGS, each derived from precedent rather than chosen.
 1. CLASS = wire/record, on a02's own ContiguousSpan precedent — a descriptor embedded in an active physical record, kind="record", 256-byte bound. Both descriptors get the same 256 bound; each is comfortably under it (32-byte identity plus small scalars).

OFF-TOKEN DESIGN PACKAGE for the remaining a02 families, plus the class ruling written up as asked, plus TWO CORRECTIONS to my own earlier comments in this thread. Nothing here needs the token; all of it is probe-derived against HEAD.

=====================================================================
1. THE CLASS RULING, WRITTEN UP PROPERLY (asked for, and cheap now)
=====================================================================
Applies to all four a02 wire types I have landed (0x003b-0x003e).

FORCED BY THE SOURCE:
 * That the schema is registered at all. Each is a confirmed top-level candidate with an explicit structural body; Appendix A makes an unregistered one unencodable.
 * The member set and order. Verbatim from the source bodies, corroborated independently by the census field-candidate counts (9, 8, 14, 10) matching member-for-member.

FORCED BY LANDED CONVENTION (derivable, not chosen):
 * CLASS = wire/record. All 7 landed physical kinds carry BOTH identity_law and owning_identity, i.e. a physical kind is a content-addressed stored record. None of these four has an identity law in the source, so physical-kind is excluded; among a02's three declared projection classes (physical_record_kinds, wire_types, durable_fields) wire_types is the residual. Note this is convention-derived, not law-enforced: expected_projection_classes is read into a transcript and is NOT checked, so nothing would have stopped a wrong class mechanically.
 * IDENTITY_CLASS flip unclassified -> wire on the candidate row. Forced by projection_identity_class, which maps target_kind "wire-type" onto identity_class "wire". Omit it and both catalog_target_class_mismatch and catalog_candidate_class_mismatch fire.
 * NO [[reservation]] row. Reservation bijection law: none of the four is a StrongRef family.
 * STATUS. active for the two descriptors, reserved for the two filesystem rows. See the correction in section 4 — the basis is narrower than I first stated.

DECIDED BY ME (revisit these first):
 * max_size_bytes: 256 for the two descriptors (ContiguousSpan precedent, and both are comfortably under it: a 32-byte identity plus small scalars), 65536 for the two filesystem rows (a15 reserved-shell precedent). Neither is derived from a source bound, because the source states none.
 * allowed_containing_schemas: ["CiphertextRecord"] / ["EncodingRecord"] for the descriptors are READ OFF the source (each is the body of exactly that record), so those are forced. ["*"] for the two filesystem rows is NOT — neither has any container in the source, so there is no list to read off, and ["*"] is a residual on the WeakDigest/MarkerRef precedent.
 * The encoding_context prose wording throughout.

=====================================================================
2. SYMBOLS: COMPLETE, and here is the exactness evidence rather than a coverage number
=====================================================================
The operator's framing is right that exactness matters more than breadth here, so I audited the thing that actually carries the durability claim: FG-INV-09, "Identity recomputation: ObjectId/CiphertextId/EncodingId/PlacementId from registered transcripts; digest-recipe discipline."

Every a02 physical-kind identity law now resolves to a REGISTERED structure:
  CiphertextRecord  ciphertext_id  -> CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest   (a02 wire, active)
  EncodingRecord    encoding_id    -> EncodingDescriptorWithoutId     (a02 wire, active)
  PlacementRecord   placement_id   -> PlacementDescriptorWithoutId    (a01 wire, RESERVED)
  SymbolRecord      symbol_record  -> self-contained, no external schema reference
TWO OF THESE FOUR WERE ONLY MADE RESOLVABLE BY 352bccd. Before it, CiphertextId's and EncodingId's recomputation transcripts named unregistered structures, so FG-INV-09 could not be discharged for them. That is the precise value of increment 1 and it is stronger than the "load-bearing but unregistered" phrasing I used at the time.

SymbolRecord specifically needs nothing further: its transcript already enumerates every serialized header field except the MAC bytes (framing lengths, identities, object kind, source block, ESI, transfer length, OTI, flags, auth profile, payload length) plus the payload, and pins the derivation MAC under K_symbol = KDF(DEK, "fgdb:symbol-auth:v1" || EncodingId). Its 19 census field candidates will never become [[field]] rows — catalog-wide all 53 field-row owners are logical kinds, zero of 61 wire types and zero of 7 physical kinds carry any. Its DefinitionWithoutStructuralBody ambiguity is benign: the body is a fenced code block and the prose mention has no adjacent structural expression.

=====================================================================
3. PLACEMENT: CORRECTION, and the real defect is not what I said
=====================================================================
CORRECTION TO MY EARLIER COMMENT. I wrote that PlacementDescriptorWithoutId "is not a top-level candidate, so it needs an ownership ruling first", implying it was unlanded. IT IS ALREADY REGISTERED — a01 wire type 0x001e, status reserved, encoding_context "Appendix A reference-semantics family PlacementDescriptorWithoutId (a01); exact member layout per plan lines 1388-1444". I reached the wrong conclusion by probing a02's candidate list and never controlling against the whole catalog: exactly the false-negative shape I have been warning about, committed by me two comments after describing it. The lesson generalises — "not in MY slice" is not "not registered".

SO THE ACTUAL PLACEMENT DEFECT IS TWO THINGS, both sharper than "unlanded":
 (a) A STATUS INCOHERENCE, and it is the same defect class 352bccd fixed. PlacementRecord is ACTIVE and its FG-INV-09 identity law depends on PlacementDescriptorWithoutId, which is RESERVED. An active identity law resting on a non-live row is precisely the incoherence that FORCED active for the two descriptors. Screening every wire type catalog-wide, this is the ONLY row in the entire catalog that is reserved while having an active referent. It is an a01-owned row, so the fix is cross-slice, not mine to make unilaterally.
 (b) THE DIVERGENT BODY, now with a concrete consequence. The a01 row pins its member layout to lines 1388-1444, i.e. the a01:1443 spelling (root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy_id, ContiguousSpan INLINED, root_* members). a02:1449 and plan:280 give a different body (placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, and a location_form union). So the landed registration asserts a layout that a02's own source contradicts. That is why the census emits ConflictingCandidateEvidence, why location_form never parses into a union candidate, and why the Explicit arm is registered nowhere while ContiguousSpan is: the a01-pinned body has no location_form at all, so the second arm was never needed.
 RESOLUTION SPACE, not mine to choose: reconcile the two bodies by erratum; or widen the a01 row to cover both; or rule them two schemas and rename one. All three are a01+a02 cross-slice.

=====================================================================
4. TWO SCREENS THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR, both clean, both with a mechanism
=====================================================================
 * SELF-REFERENCING RETAINING WRAPPERS (the u3gr screen): CLEAN. Zero occurrences of any of the nine retaining wrapper spellings targeting any a02 family across lines 280, 1443, 1445, 1447 and 1449. Nothing from a02 belongs on fgdb-u3gr. Same result cc_2 got on a04.
 * CONSTRUCTION-ORDER CONSTRAINTS: STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE IN a02, which is a stronger statement than "none found". The [[logical_kind]] row schema carries construction_order; [[physical_kind]] and [[wire_type]] do NOT — their key sets are {identity_law, max_size_bytes, name, owning_identity, record_kind, row_id, slice_id, status, transcript} and {allowed_containing_schemas, encoding_context, kind, max_size_bytes, name, row_id, slice_id, status, wire_type_id}. The construction DAG is evaluated over field rows resolved through logical kinds. Since a02 mints only physical kinds and wire types, no a02 row can carry or violate an order constraint. So "derive orders from both directions" has no purchase in this slice, and that is a mechanism, not an absence.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN STATUS RULE, because I overstated its scope in b861833's commit message. I claimed the rule "active iff >=1 already-active referent" holds "without exception across all 15 a02+a15 wire types". True for that population, but tested against all 61 wire types it holds 41/61. The 20 exceptions split cleanly: 19 are foundational primitives (StrongRef, WeakDigest, MarkerRef, StrongMarkerRef, ConditionalCommandRef, LocalCommandOrigin and its arms, AuthorityBoundHeader, HlcTimestamp, DispatchOriginPlane and its arms, ServicePromotionExternalOperationKind and its arms, PreBootstrapArtifactRef) which are active because they are referenced universally via allowed_containing_schemas ["*"] rather than named in any transcript — my referent detector only finds name mentions, so it undercounts them; and the 20th is the genuine PlacementDescriptorWithoutId defect in section 3(a). The honest rule is therefore: for slice-minted NON-PRIMITIVE structural records, active iff it has an active referent. The filesystem pair are non-primitive with zero referents of any kind, so reserved still follows — the decision stands, the justification was too broad.

=====================================================================
5. PIN CASCADE, PRECOMPUTED, WITH cc_2 DEPENDENCE MARKED
=====================================================================
cc_2/pane3 holds the catalog token for a 45-minute chained hold (a04 mint, then eik0, then atke) and lands into the same five files, so:
  cc_2-DEPENDENT — must be re-derived from the loader AFTER they land, never carried forward:
    target_count and target_source_assignment_sha256          (they add targets)

    all four scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh literals: target_count, both "targets", "projection_rows", plus the assignment sha
    logical_object_kinds registry_epoch and the LOGICAL assignment pin  (a04 mints a logical kind; eik0 adds field rows)
  LIKELY DISJOINT but must still be re-verified:
    wire_types registry_epoch and the WIRE assignment pin — a04/eik0/atke should touch logical kinds, field rows and arm counts, not wire types. My current base is epoch 11 / fnv1a64:ab616e6b014bf5b7. The disjointness CHECK that worked last rebase: after they land, re-run the loader; if the recomputed WIRE pin equals the pre-rebase value byte-for-byte, the two increments are provably disjoint on that registry. That is how I confirmed a15's 69ae5f8 did not perturb my wire base.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Local logical state and durable transaction formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Local logical state and durable transaction formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 1464-1543 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**LogicalStatePayload / LogicalStateRoot.** The following is a compact Local navigation projection of generated `LogicalStatePayload`, not a field-exhaustive alternate schema: `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,bootstrap_phase:Genesis|CheckpointInstalled|Operational|RecoveryReconciling|RecoveryAbandoned|OperationalPendingIndependentReopen,applied_logical_command_seq,applied_commit_seq,global_transaction_marker_head:StrongMarkerRef?,branch_head_map_root(entries carry StrongMarkerRef),branch_manifest_root,branch_key_epoch_registry_root,key_envelope/grant_registry_root,branch_merge_ledger_root,graph_partition_state_roots,catalog_root,schema_roots,id_allocator_root,identity_continuity_record_ref,constraint_state_roots,resource_ledger_root,privacy_ledger_root,privacy_continuity_record_ref,dp_request_index_root,txn_outcome_index_root:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeIndex>,local_begin_idempotency_index_root:StrongRef<LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex>,local_statement_index_root:StrongRef<LocalStatementIndex>,local_txn_outcome_summary_root:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,local_delta_batch_index_root:StrongRef<LocalDeltaBatchIndex>,local_delta_frontier,terminal_certification_reservation_root:StrongRef<TerminalCertificationReservationRoot<Local>>,recovery_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>?,retained_stream_floor,retention_map_root:StrongRef<RetentionMap>,derived_generation_registry_root:StrongRef<DerivedGenerationRegistry>,replay_registry_root,logical_hlc_state,topology_epoch,policy_epoch,revocation_index,replicated_key_wrap/signing/capability-verifier roots,audit_ticket_index_root,audit_root,transparency_root,backup_registry_root,restore_state_ref:StrongRef<RestoreState>?,restore_retention_anchor:RestoreRetentionAnchor<Local>,gc_decision_root,remote_retention_authority_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionObligationRoot>,remote_retention_consumer_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot>,remote_configuration_trust_root:StrongRef<RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot>,sharding_migration_state_ref:StrongRef<ShardingMigrationState>?,config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>?}`. Independent result/cursor/artifact delivery, the imported audit-continuity release head, and the audit visibility pipeline are protocol slots, not fields silently omitted from this semantic projection. The exact bounded `LocalDeltaBatchIndex` and cut lifecycle are defined with `LogicalDeltaBatch` below. `ShardingMigrationState` is `FreezePendingAudit{freeze_ref:StrongRef<ShardingFreezeRecord>}|FrozenVisible{freeze_ref,visibility_advance_maintenance_identity:MaintenanceAppliedRef}|RoleTransitionLocked{begin_ref:StrongRef<BeginRoleTransitionRecord>}|Resolved{terminal_identity}`; no variant names a future semantic command. Remote roots are empty reserved values before W12 preparation. Fresh bootstrap permits Genesis -> CheckpointInstalled -> Operational; restore/reopen/abandonment follow the exact later state machine and the retention anchor must match each phase. `LogicalStateRoot` is `{payload_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStatePayload>,logical_command_head:StrongCommandRef?}`; fresh genesis alone has no head.

For Local, the activated **semantic** state-slot closure additionally requires `security_state_binding_root`, `valid_time_slice_registry_root`, `constraint_reservation_index_root`, `escrow_ledger_root`, `allocation_reservation_and_disposition_root`, `txn_ownership_directory_root`, `txn_capability_lineage_root`, `artifact_output_request_registry_root`, `replay_manifest_registry_root`, `format_compatibility_state_ref`, `bulk_load_registry_root`, `derived_build_registry_root`, `audit_terminal_freeze_index_root`, and `restore_registry_root`. `local_result_delivery_index_root`, `result_independent_retention_index_root`, and `delivery_lease_registry_root` are obsolete alternate names for the one canonical Protocol slot `result_independent_retention_index`; none is encoded in `LogicalStatePayload`. Semantic owners store only delivery ID/detachment commitments, while RootManifest's protocol root owns the bytes. The audit pipeline is likewise not a payload slot, avoiding a content cycle. No input names its future applied record, payload, command record, root, lease, marker, or summary leaf.

`GenerationRootRef` is the posture-closed union `Local{generation_root:StrongRef}` or `Distributed{manifest_ref:StrongRef<DistributedDerivedGenerationManifest>}`. `DerivedGenerationRegistry` maps a full `DerivedIdentity` strong reference to `{generation_root:GenerationRootRef,global_frontier?,answer_contract:AnswerContract,retention_class,status:Building|Active|Retiring}` and never reconstructs a singular graph/head/schema key. `ShardDerivedComponent` binds `{derived_identity_ref,shard_id,topology_epoch,input_global_batch_interval,resulting_global_frontier,partition_and_authority_coverage,answer_contract,component_root:StrongRef}`; `ShardDerivedComponentCertificate` adds `SameGroupCertificateHeader`, availability/retention floors, and quorum signatures. A meta-local `DistributedDerivedGenerationManifest` is `{derived_identity_ref,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,exact_global_frontier,sorted_component_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardDerivedComponentCertificate>],complete_partition_and_authority_commitment,answer_contract,build_policy_epoch}`. Shard build/advance controls root components in `shard_derived_component_registry_root`; a meta activation control changes `Active` only after every required certified component at one topology/frontier exists. Partial, stale-topology, or mixed-frontier generations remain nonqueryable, and reads use the exact fallback path when the active manifest is missing. Checkpoint/configuration floors, remote grants, topology transfer, backup/replay, and GC retain every Building/Active/Retiring generation through its terminal transition.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

## Provenance
Complete audited plan Appendix A lines 1464-1543.
