title: Appendix A exact catalog: Rollback-protected authority-time formats and rotation
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Rollback-protected authority-time formats and rotation. This task embeds source-plan lines 2157-2246 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**Rollback-protected authority time.** Canonical logical HLC orders database state; it is never an expiry clock. Process-local monotonic time may enforce a short-lived in-memory use budget and drive advisory timers; ambient wall time is display-only. Any authorization, lease-validity, expiry, release, retirement, key destruction, archive downgrade, restore fencing, or retention-cut decision uses the following rollback-protected authority-time contract or fails closed.

`AuthorityInstant` is `{time_domain_id,authority_epoch,tick:u128}` and compares only within one domain/epoch; windows are closed-open: `not_before <= true_authority_time < expires_at`. `AuthorityInterval` is the exact `{earliest:AuthorityInstant,latest:AuthorityInstant}` with byte-identical domain/epoch fields and `earliest.tick <= latest.tick`; intervals from different domains/epochs are never ordered, intersected, or bridged by scalar conversion. `TimeAuthorityProfile` is the immutable threshold-signed `{schema_version,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,tick_scale,external_registry_id,ordered_signers[{signer_id,key_id,verification_key}],threshold,maximum_source_uncertainty_ticks,maximum_challenge_round_trip_ticks,maximum_guard_use_ticks,comparison_semantics:ClosedOpen,unavailable_policy:FailClosed,predecessor_profile_digest:WeakDigest?,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`.

External time evidence is reference-free. `PortableTimeAuthorityObservation` is the fresh challenged signed `{profile_oid,profile_digest,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,challenge_nonce,subject_digest,intended_use_digest,authority_sequence,possible_time_interval:AuthorityInterval,external_registry_head_digest,external_registry_cas_version,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`. It never claims process-local send/receive counters.

`ShardTimeAuthorityProjection` is the shard-local certified Meta projection `{source_meta_prefix,source_meta_configuration_identity,source_meta_time_registry_generation,selected_profile_oid,sorted_profile_projections[{profile_oid,profile_digest,issuance_state:ActiveForIssuance|ClosingRequested|IssuanceClosing|IssuanceQuiescent|Draining|Retired,verification_live_through_commitment}],time_authority_registry_head_digest,verifier_and_offline_issuer_floor_commitment,retention_grant_and_payload_availability_evidence,typed_projection_payload_identity_and_digest,projection_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaControlProjectionCertificate>,body_digest}`. Its certificate's `TypedCertifiedMetaProjectionPayload` arm is exactly `TimeAuthorityRegistryProjection` and byte-matches the payload identity/digest and source prefix/effect. It is installed only through the exact contiguous ActiveMetaProjectionRoot time-authority slot and is invalid after that source prefix/configuration/trust or retention evidence ceases to be current.

`LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness` is the nonportable `{process_incarnation_id,challenge_nonce,send_monotonic_tick,receive_monotonic_tick,checked_elapsed_ticks,monotonic_source_profile_id,conversion_to_authority_uncertainty_ticks,body_digest}`. `TimeAuthorityObservationImport` is the closed role-local union `Local{role_and_group,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_publication_commitment,profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityObservation>,current_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Local>>,local_round_trip_witness:LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness,exact_profile_registry_and_transcript_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}|Meta{role_and_group,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_publication_commitment,profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityObservation>,current_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Meta>>,local_round_trip_witness:LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness,exact_profile_registry_and_transcript_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}|Shard{role_and_group,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_publication_commitment,profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityObservation>,current_meta_time_authority_projection_ref:StrongRef<ShardTimeAuthorityProjection>,local_round_trip_witness:LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness,exact_profile_projection_and_transcript_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}`. The import verifies the portable profile identity/digest, current registry or certified projection, role/group/configuration/fence, same-nonce local round trip, interval, subject, intended use, and signatures before any local validator may consume it. Challenge nonce, subject, and use are signed. Replay, wrong profile/domain/epoch, noncurrent registry head, excessive checked round trip/uncertainty, process-incarnation mismatch, role substitution, or signature failure is unusable.

`time_bound_subjects.toml` is the single exhaustive source for the closed `TimeBoundSubject` union. Each row names one concrete durable schema or one exact capability variant, its canonical pre-evidence transcript recipe, profile/window field tags, legal intended uses, evidence owner, expiry/retirement transition, and retention floor. It forbids raw refs, a generic object arm, a generic capability arm, and overlapping transcripts. `TimeValidationEvidence` is the already-built role-local immutable `{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,subject:TimeBoundSubject,intended_use_digest,classification:Usable{not_before,expires_at,validated_process_incarnation_id,guard_deadline_local_monotonic_tick}|NotYetValid{not_before}|Expired{expires_at},validator_version,validation_digest}`. `Usable` exists only when the imported portable observation's `possible_time_interval.earliest >= not_before`, the local round-trip witness belongs to the current process incarnation, and `checked_add(possible_time_interval.latest.tick,maximum_guard_use_ticks)` succeeds in the same domain/epoch and is `< expires_at`; its local guard deadline is derived with checked arithmetic from the same receive tick and conservative remaining budget. A linear use guard can be constructed only in that same process incarnation while its current monotonic tick is strictly before the recorded deadline. Durable Usable bytes surviving restart therefore authorize nothing until a fresh observation/import/evidence exists. `NotYetValid` exists only when `possible_time_interval.latest < not_before`; `Expired` only when `possible_time_interval.earliest >= expires_at` and remains durable across restart. An interval overlapping either boundary yields no evidence and the uniform retryable `TimeAuthorityUnavailable`, before any protected lookup or disclosure. Tick addition, bound normalization, challenge-round-trip subtraction, and profile drain arithmetic are checked; overflow, saturation requirement, or domain/epoch mismatch yields `TimeAuthorityUnavailable` and never wraps.

`ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjectionSource` is the closed union `Bootstrap{bootstrap_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<RestoreShardBootstrapProjectionCertificate>,bootstrap_projection_identity_and_digest,source_lease_projection_payload_identity_and_digest}|Refresh{meta_control_projection_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaControlProjectionCertificate>,typed_meta_projection_payload_identity_and_digest}`. `ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection` is `{source:ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjectionSource,source_meta_prefix,source_meta_configuration_identity,lease_identity,generation,portable_lease_state_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest,selected_grant_generation_and_digest,window_profile_domain_epoch_and_bounds,archive_counter,holder_and_subject_set_commitment,retention_grant_and_payload_availability_evidence,body_digest}`. Bootstrap validates the exact `RestoreShardBootstrapProjectionCertificate` and its certificate-free payload; Refresh uses only `TypedCertifiedMetaProjectionPayload::RestoreSourceLease`, must name the same restore/plan/shard/lease lineage and unchanged holder/subject/inventory/recipient commitments, and may advance only `g -> g+1` with the exact successor proof. A Shard never owns a canonical lease record and cannot renew or release it.

`RestoreArchiveRef<T> {source:PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T>,lease_identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,permitted_inventory_leaf,leaf_proof}` contains no strong lease-generation edge. `RestorePublicationArtifactRef<T> {source:BackupPublicationArtifactRef<T>,lease_identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,permitted_grant_subject_leaf,grant_subject_leaf_proof,publication_receipt_binding}` is legal only for exact publication-envelope artifact kinds and proves the locator row against the lease-bound publication receipt/grant subject set. Every reference and registry common field must match both source and target identities. Before the bridge, resolution uses the current prebootstrap owner; afterward Local/Meta resolution requires the latest canonical live lease record and Shard resolution requires the exact current certified projection, plus subject-preserving grant lineage, `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, and the exact inventory/grant proof.

Source acquisition precedes canonical target creation and is externally recoverable. Pre-send `RestoreIdentityKeyPlan` is the closed union `PreserveSameIdentity{identical_namespace_basis,source_k_oid_identity_and_commitment,recover_and_rewrap_operation_recipe,target_rewrap_recipient_commitment,required_key_equality_proof_profile,required_zero_plaintext_persistence_proof_profile}|CloneFreshIdentity{distinct_namespace_basis,source_k_oid_source_open_only_commitment,recover_source_k_oid_for_decode_operation_recipe,create_target_k_oid_operation_recipe,target_k_oid_recipient_commitment,required_source_key_nontransplant_proof_profile}`. It contains only recipes, expected identities, and proof profiles. Post-provider `RestoreIdentityKeyDispositionEvidence` is the distinct closed union `PreservedSameIdentity{plan_digest,identical_namespace_proof,recover_and_rewrap_receipt_ref:RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef,source_k_oid_commitment,target_rewrapped_k_oid_commitment,key_equality_proof,zero_plaintext_persistence_proof}|ClonedFreshIdentity{plan_digest,distinct_namespace_proof,recover_source_k_oid_receipt_ref:RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef,create_target_k_oid_receipt_ref:RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef,source_k_oid_source_open_only_commitment,target_k_oid_commitment,source_key_nontransplant_proof}`. Clone source `K_oid` and DEKs authorize source decoding only; every target ciphertext receives a fresh target DEK under the newly created target identity.

`RestoreClaimedTargetAuthorityRecipe` is the pre-claim closed union `RecoverSameIdentity{expected_operational_or_fence_predecessor_digest_and_cas_version,restore_id,source_backup_identity,planned_target_incarnation,recovery_writer_authority_digest,service_visibility_epoch,prior_lease_fence_plan_commitment}|CloneNewIdentity{identity_reservation_id,expected_reserved_head_digest_and_cas_version,claim_id,claimant_identity,target_database_and_security_identity,target_incarnation,recovery_writer_authority_digest,service_visibility_epoch,continuity_profile:DirectoryBound{filesystem_profile_id,mount_device_directory_and_target_manifest_inode_identity,target_manifest_staging_inode_creation_nonce_digest,whole_inode_fence_identity,parent_directory_durability_recipe,fixed_local_continuity_recipe_and_digest,zero_existing_root_slot_proof_recipe,directory_bound_creation_evidence_recipe_digest}|ExternalCas{expected_continuity_predecessor_digest_and_cas_version,enter_clone_reserved_operation_recipe,recovery_only_lease_recipe}}`. It contains no resulting claimed/reserved head and no plan digest field that would make the plan self-referential. DirectoryBound carries no external continuity head or CAS recipe; ExternalCas requires both.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

comments.text:
THE UNRESERVED-CANDIDATE CLASSIFICATION CALLS: SCOPED, EVIDENCED, AND PARTITIONED. Done off-token; no shared file touched.

FIRST, A COUNT CORRECTION. The standing trail says "15 unreserved unclassified candidates". The live figure is 33. A candidate needs a call when it has no [[target]], no [[reservation]], no [[source_symbol_disposition]], and no minted logical kind. The 15 was an earlier, narrower reading; plan on 33.

METHOD, and its limits stated up front. Two probes: one for definition-site evidence (census owner_statuses, definition_kinds, body_conflict, source locations, and whether the census renders a structural BODY), one for USAGE across the whole appendix field census (bare-type use, StrongRef target, nested/list use, arm-token match). Usage is the stronger signal — a symbol strong-referenced from anywhere MUST be a logical kind, and a symbol that appears in the census arm set is an arm token no matter how its brace body reads. THE LIMIT, stated because it changes how one bucket must be read: my usage scan covers Appendix A FIELD types only. It does not see references from command contracts, Appendix B intents, or ordering prose. So "no external use" means "no Appendix A field names it", NOT "not durable". Several symbols in that bucket are the command-contract-owned specs and authorities the trail already identified, and they will be referenced from the command_contracts registry instead. Do not classify anything in that bucket as not-a-durable-schema on this evidence alone.

ONE CALL IS DECIDED, WITH SOURCE PROOF. `Retired` is NOT a top-level schema — it is a union arm token of the TimeAuthorityRegistry profiles issuance-state union. The census flagged it as an AmbiguousUnownedStructure top-level candidate because the brace body `Retired{terminal_summary_ref}` parses like a definition, but the source at a16:2223 reads "deterministically creates TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role>, SELECTS Retired{terminal_summary_ref}" — selection of an arm, not a definition. It also matches the census arm set directly. This is exactly the a05/a20 precedent recorded as a20 gotcha 1 (the bogus `Sharded` candidate, which is the manifest posture enum value). Disposition it as an arm, never mint it as a kind. That is the one call I would land today without further reading.

FIVE HAVE NO STRUCTURAL BODY AT ALL, which is the cleanest discriminator the census offers: CommitCx, MacaroonTokenBytes, PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest, PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent, ReplayArchiveLease. CommitCx is an asupersync capability context (see AGENTS.md doctrine 3) and is categorically not a durable format — it is the Cx the writer holds, mentioned in ordering prose. MacaroonTokenBytes and PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest are byte/digest value types. PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent and ReplayArchiveLease are named states/leases whose bytes live in another schema. None of the five should become a logical kind; each needs a value-type or not-a-durable-schema disposition, and the two prebootstrap ones must be settled with the a17 owner (still-open gotcha 3 on that bead).

ELEVEN ARE USED BARE AS A FIELD TYPE, which is what makes them the field-unblocking set: AuthorityInstant, AuthorityInterval, ClusterIncarnationLease, LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness, PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpoint, PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest, PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T>, RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity, TimeAuthorityProfileRetirementSpec<Role>, TimeAuthorityRetirementCleanupAuthority<Role>, TimeAuthorityTransitionCompletionAuthority<Role>. Each is a genuine fork: a named sub-record used bare is either (a) its own logical kind, with consumers holding a StrongRef, or (b) a WIRE TYPE, inlined into the consumer's bytes with no independent object identity. The evidence that decides it is whether the plan ever gives the symbol an independent lifecycle — its own publication, retention, or reference — and that is a per-symbol read of the source, not something a probe settles. AuthorityInstant and AuthorityInterval (3 and 2 members) are almost certainly wire types: they are time VALUES, inlined everywhere, with no lifecycle of their own. RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity (21 members) and TimeAuthorityTransitionCompletionAuthority<Role> (20 members, plus 1 union) are large enough that a logical kind with its own identity is the likely call. PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T>, RestoreArchiveRef<T> and RestorePublicationArtifactRef<T> are reference WRAPPERS by name and shape and belong in the wire class beside StrongRef/CertifiedRemoteStrongRef, not as logical kinds.

ONE IS USED ONLY NESTED: TimeAuthorityProfileTransitionSpec<Role>, inside a list. A list-of-X still needs X to be a named type, so it lands in the same fork as the eleven.

THE REMAINING TWENTY are in the "no Appendix A field names them" bucket and must be read against the command contracts before classification: ArchiveRetentionGrantWindow, ArchiveSourceReleasePreparedHoldWindow, BackupPublicationFreshness, BackupTransparencyFreshness, GroupTimeIssuanceAdmissionFreezeCertificate, IrreversibleDispatchObservationWindow<Role>, PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseOwner, PreBootstrapTimeValidationEvidence, ProfiledResourceReservationDeadline<Role>, RestoreArchiveRef<T>, RestorePublicationArtifactRef<T>, TimeAuthorityRotationIntentSpec<Role>, TimeIssuanceAdmissionFreezeSpec, TimeObservationServiceContract, TxnOutcomeLookupWindow<Role>, VerifierKeyWindow and the four already named above. Note PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseOwner (23 field keys) and PreBootstrapTimeValidationEvidence (13 field keys, 1 union) are the two largest bodies in the whole unclassified set and they are prebootstrap artifacts — the a16 trail has already established these belong to the prebootstrap artifact class, and the a17 owner has to co-sign. comments.text:
A LATENT UNSATISFIABLE CONSTRUCTION-ORDER CONSTRAINT IN A RELEASED KIND — found by designing TimeAuthorityRegistry's field body, and it must be settled before that body can be modelled at all.

THE FACTS, all probe-derived against the cf58ccb snapshot rather than the live tree. The source at a16:2181 reads: TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> is {role,generation,profiles[profile_oid -> ActiveForIssuance{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,issuance_generation}|ClosingRequested{...}|IssuanceClosing{...}|IssuanceQuiescent{...}|Draining{...}|Retired{...}],selected_profile_oid,profile_retirement_floor,body_digest}. So `profiles` is an INDEXED MAP whose value is a closed six-arm union.

The census does NOT emit a union candidate for it. It emitted ZERO union candidates under TimeAuthorityRegistry and instead produced 23 nested FIELD keys at depth three: profiles.ActiveForIssuance.profile_ref, profiles.Draining.drain_hold_ref, profiles.Retired.terminal_summary_ref, and so on. The reason is a parser-coverage gap, not a source defect: the census recognises the `field:A|B` union spelling (that is what I2a/I6a/I6b modelled) but not the `field[key -> A|B]` indexed-map spelling. Evidence that both spellings really are in use: ShardTimeAuthorityProjection.sorted_profile_projections.record.issuance_state IS recognised as a union candidate, and it is written with an explicit `record.` segment.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS AN EMPTY ORDER WINDOW. Probing the order law from both directions, as the law requires: the strong references inside those arm interiors reach TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role> (order 65), TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role> (60), TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role> (55), RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure<Role> (40) and others, so modelling them as field rows on TimeAuthorityRegistry demands construction_order >= 65. Its six strong-ref consumers (TimeAuthorityObservationImport at 23, plus the four unminted Spec/Authority symbols and TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord) demand <= 23. TimeAuthorityRegistry is minted at 21. 65 > 23, so there is NO order that satisfies both directions. Nobody has hit this yet only because none of those 23 interior keys has a field row; the contradiction is latent, and the first agent to model `.profiles` as flat or nested strong fields will hit a wall that looks like a bad order rather than a modelling error.

FOUR RESOLUTIONS, with my reading of each. (a) TEACH THE CENSUS THE INDEXED-MAP UNION SPELLING so `.profiles` gets a union plus six arms; the interiors are then committed by arm payload digests, which create no DAG edge, and the registry stays at 21. Most faithful to the source, and it reuses the exact mechanism every other embedded union already uses — but it changes the census parser, which moves candidate counts and sha pins for EVERY slice, so it is a heavy catalog-wide change and emphatically not a unilateral one. (b) MINT THE MAP VALUE AS ITS OWN NAMED SCHEMA (a profile-registry-entry type) at an order >= 65 and have `profiles` hold entries INLINE, committed by the registry's own body digest; no DAG edge, registry stays at 21, and it needs no parser change. If instead the entries were held by StrongRef the constraint returns unsatisfiable, so the inline reading is the only workable form of this option. (c) WEAKEN the interior references to weak_digest or conditional. This removes the constraint but changes retention semantics — a registry pointing at the profiles it is currently administering plainly means to retain them — so I think this is wrong, and it would be the a01 identity-versus-reachability law applied backwards. (d) MOVE the registry's order: impossible, the window is empty.

I RECOMMEND (a) as correct and (b) as the pragmatic fallback if the census change is judged too expensive, and I am NOT deciding it. It is either a census/checker change with catalog-wide pin consequences or a change to the object graph of a released kind; both exceed what an increment inside a16 should settle alone. Escalating to the granular owner (w9-time-authority-0rv6) and whoever owns the census parser. This also warrants its own bead, which I did not create because bead creation moves the architecture bead-provenance pins and that needs the catalog token, currently held by cc_2 — file it on the next hold.

SCOPE OF THE BLOCK: TimeAuthorityRegistry has 6 flat members and 23 interior keys, 29 uncovered field keys in total, and it is the second-largest uncovered owner in a16. All 29 are blocked on this ruling. The same indexed-map spelling should be swept for across the other slices before the ruling is made, since the parser gap is not a16-specific.

A METHOD NOTE FOR THE NEXT AGENT, because it is the reason this surfaced at all: the owner probe prints the order window from BOTH directions — max order of anything the owner strong-refs (lower bound) and min order over every consumer that strong-refs it (upper bound). Reading only the consumer side, as the trail warned in I5, would have shown a comfortable `<= 23` and hidden the contradiction entirely.

COMPOSITE GATE RECORD — ATTRIBUTABLE TO COMMIT cf58ccb. This is the record that has been owed for three increments, and it is now taken in a form that needs no quiescence and is repeatable by anyone at any HEAD.

RESULT: scripts/check.sh exit 0, ALL GATES GREEN, all seven steps in sequence — cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test (822 tests across 30 binaries, zero failures), registry-check all, scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh, architecture-check. The recurring "error: unclosed table, expected `]`" lines in the log are the known asupersync deliberately-malformed test fixture (tests/fixtures/migration_readiness_planner/malformed/Cargo.toml), not failures.

METHOD, and why it beats waiting for a clean tree. In a six-agent shared checkout a clean working tree is not reliably obtainable — the window opened and shut twice while I was waiting for it, and the two composite runs I attempted against the live tree were both unattributable because another lane had uncommitted work in it. Instead:
  SNAP=/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/gate-snapshot-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
  mkdir -p "$SNAP" && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$SNAP"
  cd "$SNAP" && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/snapshot-target ./scripts/check.sh
`git archive HEAD` materialises exactly the committed state including tracked .beads/, with no agent's WIP. scripts/check.sh derives its own ROOT from its own location, so the whole run stays inside the snapshot; nothing can dirty the real tree and no concurrent commit can perturb the run mid-flight. The separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR means the run neither waits on nor holds the shared target-dir lock. architecture-check must run LOCALLY, not through rch, because remote workers do not sync .beads/ and it fails there with "issues.jsonl: No such file or directory".

ONE TRAP, PAID FOR AND WORTH RECORDING. My first snapshot run failed at clippy with "multiple workspace roots found in the same workspace" — and that was self-inflicted, not a real defect. I had earlier repointed a scratch probe crate's path dependency at the snapshot's tools/registry-check and, to make it build standalone, appended a [workspace] table to its Cargo.toml. That second workspace root inside the snapshot broke clippy for the whole run. THE RULE: a snapshot used as a gate record is READ-ONLY. Anything that mutates it invalidates the record. The fix was a fresh snapshot plus giving the probe its own private copy of registry-check, after which clippy passed — which is also the proof that the failure was mine and not the tree's.

WHAT THIS RECORD COVERS. cf58ccb is the tip of this session's a16 work: 0246145 (the fgdb-tfow reconstruction fix, the pipe-bearing union it unblocked, and the 19 forced I7 adjudications), 7cff9e6 (the 21 derivable strong-reference field rows), and the bead-evidence commits between them. EXHAUSTIVE CATALOG-WIDE CONSTRUCTION-ORDER SWEEP — complete result, all slices, read-only analysis off the token, measured against the cf58ccb snapshot.

METHOD, and the gap it closed in my own earlier number. Three reference populations were swept, because each is enforced differently: (A) landed field rows, (B) landed reference-union arms — both already enforced by dag_future_result — and (C) census references with no landed row, which NOTHING enforces. My first measurement matched only the literal `StrongRef<` spelling; this sweep matches all nine retaining wrapper spellings (StrongRef, CertifiedRemoteStrongRef, StrongCommandRef, StrongMarkerRef, StrongCiphertextRef, StrongGlobalCommandRef, StrongShardCommandRef, ConditionalCoordinateRef, ConditionalMarkerRef). Non-retaining identity spellings — MarkerRef, CommandRef, WeakDigest, the *Identity wrappers — are deliberately EXCLUDED: they are bare identity with no traversal, so they impose no ordering obligation. That is the a01 identity-is-not-reachability law used as the sweep's own admission rule.

THE LAW, stated exactly, because the brief slightly overstated it: dag_future_result fires on `target.construction_order > containing.construction_order`. Strictly greater. EQUAL orders are legal and common — a16 alone has twelve kinds at order 27 — so a sweep for `>=` would report false positives. I report strict violations as the defect set and equal-order pairs separately as zero-slack information.

RESULT 1 — STRICT VIOLATIONS: 14 witnesses, 7 DISTINCT EDGES, 2 HOSTS, 2 SLICES. (Each edge appears twice because the census records both the aggregate member type and the specific nested path; they are one edge counted at two granularities.)
  a10  ControlCommand@10 -> PayloadAvailabilityCertificate@20
       via ControlCommand.payload_availability_certificate_ref
  a16  TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>@21 -> six targets, all through the .profiles indexed map:
         TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence@27, RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure@40,
         RoleTimeIssuanceReservationClosure@41, TimeAuthorityDrainHold@55,
         TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord@60, TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary@65
ZERO violations came from populations (A) or (B). Every one is census-latent. That is the headline: the checker is doing its job perfectly on everything it can see, and 100% of the defect lives in the population it cannot see.

RESULT 2 — CLASSIFICATION, and it is the same verdict for both, reached independently.
  * NOT an ORDER error. I checked whether either host can simply be re-ordered, deriving the window from BOTH directions as required. ControlCommand needs >= 20, but it is retained from above by CommitCapsule@10 and LogicalCommandRecord through landed reference-union arms, so it is pinned <= 10. TimeAuthorityRegistry needs >= 65, but its consumers pin it <= 23 (TimeAuthorityObservationImport@23 in census; TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord@60 landed). BOTH windows are empty. NEITHER violation is fixable by re-ordering, and there is no minimal re-assignment to compute — that is the answer to the re-ordering question, and it is a negative one.
  * a16 is a SCHEMA-SHAPE error: `.profiles` is written `profiles[profile_oid -> A|B|...]`, an indexed map the census does not recognise as a union, so its six retained targets surface as nested field keys instead of arm interiors. Arms would create no DAG edge at all. Fix is fgdb-ovok: teach the census the indexed-map spelling, or mint the map value as an inline entry schema.
  * a10 is REFERENCE-STRENGTH, most likely. ControlCommand is a command; a payload-availability certificate is evidence ABOUT a command's payload, produced independently and later. A command retaining a certificate that is constructed after it is precisely the "future result" the law names. The natural reading is that the command should carry the certificate's IDENTITY, not reachability to it — a weak digest or a bare identity rather than a StrongRef. That is an a10 call and I am not making it; flagging it to the a10 owner.

RESULT 3 — THE GRAPH: 68 nodes, 76 edges, and it does NOT layer cleanly. Kahn leaves three nodes undrained, and the reason matters:
  * PreparedCommitRecord.predecessor_ref -> PreparedCommitRecord (SELF-EDGE)
  * TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>.predecessor_ref -> TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation (SELF-EDGE)
  * CheckpointStateVector is NOT itself defective — it is merely DOWNSTREAM of the first, through a landed reference-union arm CheckpointStateVector@35 -> PreparedCommitRecord@12 which is perfectly legal (12 <= 35). It never drains only because its predecessor never does.
The two self-edges are the banked `predecessor_ref` hazard, and this sweep shows it is not an a16 quirk: the identical pattern exists in PreparedCommitRecord in another slice. Per the cycle rule these are schema-shape errors, not ordering errors, and the fix is the same a01 law — a predecessor link is lineage to be COMPARED, never traversed, so it must be weak_digest or conditional, never a flat strong field. Modelled as strong it trips dag_self_edge. Once both are reclassified the retaining graph is acyclic and layers cleanly.

RESULT 4 — ZERO-SLACK EQUAL ORDERS: 4, all legal, all worth knowing because they have no room to absorb a future change: CommitCapsule@10 -> CommitCommand@10, CommitCapsule@10 -> ControlCommand@10, RemoteRetentionGrantSpec@20 -> PayloadAvailabilityCertificate@20, RootManifest@40 -> LogicalStateRoot@40.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Restore prebootstrap journal and source acquisition formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Restore prebootstrap journal and source acquisition formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 2247-2348 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

`RestoreSourceAcquisitionActionKey` is a plan key, not a second dispatch-action registry. Its generated total mapping selects exactly one live **RestorePreBootstrap contract row** in `irreversible_dispatch_contracts.toml`, whose action kind is one of `EnterRestoreFencePending|PriorIncarnationLeaseIssuerFence{issuer_key}|PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortRevoke{issuer_key,cohort_key}|EnterRestoreReserved|ReservationClaim{reservation_kind,reservation_id}|EnterCloneReserved|RestoreArchiveAcquire|CommitAcquisitionRefinementBootstrapOpeners|CommitAcquisitionRefinementVerifiedObjectInventory|RecoverAndRewrapPreservedObjectIdKey|RecoverSourceObjectIdKeyForDecode|CreateTargetObjectIdKey|RecoverSourceBootstrapDek{artifact_key}|RecoverSourceObjectDekForReprotect{inventory_ordinal}|RestoreArchiveLeaseRenew{family_id,ordinal}|RecoveryIncarnationLeaseAcquireOrRefresh{family_id,ordinal}|RestoreArchiveLeaseRelease|ReservationBurnBeforeUse{reservation_kind,reservation_id,claim_id?}|CatalogTombstoneRestoreTarget{catalog_profile}|RestoreContinuityAbandon|RevokeTransientRecoveryWrap{artifact_key}|DestroyFreshUnpublishedTargetObjectIdKey{artifact_key}|RestoreUnpublishedTargetPhysicalDelete{target_ordinal}`. Every key maps bijectively to one exact `dispatch_contract_id`, operation/body recipe, source-gate recipe, prebootstrap attempt/import type, resource relation, and cleanup disposition; a canonical-plane row for the same provider action is a different contract and cannot satisfy the mapping. No alias may rename or merge dispatch kinds. `EnterCloneReserved`, both refinement-commit actions, `RecoveryIncarnationLeaseAcquireOrRefresh`, and `RestoreContinuityAbandon` are ExternalCas-only. `CatalogTombstoneRestoreTarget` is inhabitable only for `ExternalCasCataloged|DirectoryBoundCataloged` and is forbidden for `DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog`. DirectoryBound refinement and target-authority transitions are local authenticated journal/RootSlot publications, not transport keys. Source `K_oid` and source DEK destruction are uninhabited; cleanup may revoke only transient recovery wraps/grants. Destruction is legal solely for a clone-created target `K_oid` with key-origin plus zero-canonical-publication proofs. `RetainedTombstonedNoUse` is a local resource disposition, never an externally dispatched action.

Repeated prebootstrap operations use a bounded family fixed before the first member can be authorized. `PreBootstrapActionFamilyRecipe` is `{family_id,action_kind:RestoreArchiveLeaseRenew|RecoveryIncarnationLeaseAcquireOrRefresh,max_members,member_key_and_operation_id_recipe,member_idempotency_recipe,stable_subject_and_action_body_invariants,per_member_predecessor_and_window_recipe,resource_budget,terminal_history_and_nonreuse_floor,body_digest}`. A member key is exactly `{family_id,ordinal}` with `0 <= ordinal < max_members`; the operation/idempotency identities are deterministic from the sealed recipe and ordinal, and no member may change the lease/continuity subject, holder/writer, scope, target incarnation, first-root action digest, or other stable action bytes. The source-renew recipe derives member `n` only from the journal-durable terminal result of `n-1`, binding the then-current Active head/CAS, generation, portable lease-state digest, grant lineage/counter, and requested successor window. The recovery-lease recipe likewise binds the current lease generation/status and requested successor window produced or observed after `n-1`. The next ordinal may be authorized only after every prior ordinal is terminal and the resulting current head is journal-authority durable. Family exhaustion permanently abandons this restore attempt; recovery may start only a new `restore_id` under the profile's required fresh claim and, for same-identity recovery, a strictly newer incarnation—never mutate or extend the committed family. Source-lease renewal and ExternalCas recovery-incarnation-lease acquire/refresh are the only v1 families; fixed issuer/cohort/reservation/key/refinement/release/cleanup actions remain singleton keys. `RestoreBridgeFreezeSpec` closes the source-lease-renew family at an exact final ordinal, proves every created renew member terminal and no later renew member authorized, consumes all source/projection guards, and leaves only the separately bounded recovery-incarnation refresh family open. The sealed import, terminal accumulator, availability certificate, action/resource bijection, status API, and nonreuse floors retain every member—not merely the family name.

Availability construction is acyclic and does not assume that one local staging inode survives the declared failure model. `PortableRestorePlanRecipe` contains all Phase-A plan fields with one typed `AvailabilityCertificateDigest` hole and action recipes with their later `PlanDigest` holes. Before any target claim or dispatch-capable local root, recovery creates stable random `journal_id`, nonexportable `K_restore_journal`, and exact `PreBootstrapRestoreRecoveryCapsule {format_version,restore_id,journal_id,plan_recipe_bytes_and_digest,recovery_or_admin_authority_bytes_and_digest,journal_key_commitment,wrapped_journal_key_bytes_and_digest,wrap_recipient_and_profile,journal_mac_profile_oid,initial_generation_capsule_recipe_digest,availability_service_identity_and_locators,required_failure_domain_policy,recovery_and_relocation_policy,resource_ceiling,body_digest}`. The capsule contains no plaintext journal key and is itself encrypted/authenticated to the recovery authority.

`PreBootstrapJournalGenerationCapsule` is the exact complete encrypted state `{journal_id,restore_id,head_generation,dispatch_state_generation,predecessor_journal_head_digest_and_cas_version,plan_recipe_or_final_plan_digest,availability_certificate_digest?,current_staging_incarnation,complete_dispatch_root_body,dispatch_state_digest,complete_action_attempt_artifact_lease_and_resource_map,local_slot_generation_and_predecessor_digest,journal_mac_profile_oid,canonical_capsule_digest}`. Every journal-authority successor increments `head_generation` exactly once. `dispatch_state_generation` increments only when the plan/action/attempt/artifact/lease/resource state changes; a pure relocation preserves it and `dispatch_state_digest` while changing the staging incarnation and capsule bytes. The capsule contains only values known before the journal-head CAS—never a future authority head, receipt, status, or provider-result hole. In particular a generation that changes an ordinary target action to SentUnknown contains that complete SentUnknown state.

`prebootstrap_journal_publication_contracts.toml` has exactly two contracts, Bootstrap and SuccessorOrRelocation. Their fixed protocol is: (1) construct the complete immutable encrypted capsule; (2) replicate and independently reopen it in every required failure domain; (3) CAS reference-free `PreBootstrapJournalAuthorityHead {journal_id,restore_id,head_generation,dispatch_state_generation,dispatch_state_digest,encrypted_generation_capsule_digest,plan_recipe_or_final_plan_digest,availability_certificate_digest?,current_staging_incarnation,predecessor_head_digest,current_cas_version,publication_operation_id,publication_idempotency_digest,state:Active|TerminalCanonicalized{certificate_digest,target_root_publication_commitment,retention_floor}|TerminalAbandoned{certificate_digest,zero_canonical_publication_commitment,retention_floor},authority_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`; (4) mirror the exact returned head and capsule locally; and only then (5) allow any ordinary target request whose SentUnknown state is contained in that head/dispatch generation to leave. Receipt/status knowledge from that target action is known data in a later complete capsule/head generation. The authority permanently indexes `(journal_id,head_generation,publication_operation_id)` and supports authenticated status/idempotent exact retry; changed capsule bytes at the same identity are rejected. Only Active accepts SuccessorOrRelocation. Either terminal arm permanently rejects relocation, application-state publication, or another terminalization. Because the head CAS publishes a complete predecessor-known generation rather than its own attempt state, the protocol is nonrecursive.

Initial head publication uses signed bootstrap recovery/admin authority stored in `PreBootstrapRestoreRecoveryCapsule`; every successor CAS requires the exact current head and current staging incarnation. `PreBootstrapRestorePlanAvailabilityCertificate` is the portable threshold-signed `{restore_id,plan_recipe_digest,journal_id,initial_journal_authority_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,journal_key_commitment,journal_key_wrap_recipient_profile_and_digest,journal_mac_profile_oid,initial_capsule_generation_and_root_digest,recovery_capsule_locations_and_digests,recovery_and_relocation_policy,canonical_action_recipe_set_digest,required_failure_domain_policy,verified_reopen_quorum,retain_until:Canonicalized{root_slot_durable_sealed_journal_import_and_covering_cut}|Abandoned{terminal_certificate_and_all_external_status_nonreuse_resource_floors},signer_set_epoch,signatures}` and does not name the final plan. The final portable plan fills only the availability-certificate hole; its actions later fill only their plan-digest holes. A claim, fence, archive receipt, or refinement commit alone never releases a plan/refinement/journal capsule.

If the current local journal inode is lost or becomes unusable, recovery opens the latest authenticated authority head/capsule and performs the SuccessorOrRelocation publication contract with `result_head_generation = prior_head_generation + 1`, unchanged dispatch state generation/digest, and a strictly newer `current_staging_incarnation`. `PreBootstrapJournalRelocationReceipt` is the head CAS's portable signed `{journal_id,prior_head_generation,result_head_generation,unchanged_dispatch_state_generation_and_digest,publication_operation_id,publication_idempotency_digest,prior_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,old_staging_incarnation,new_staging_incarnation,new_filesystem_profile_mount_device_inode_and_creation_nonce_commitment,old_staging_fenced_by_head_successor:true,unchanged_plan_action_attempt_lease_and_resource_lineage_commitment,result_capsule_digest,result_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,authority_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. It is journal-publication evidence, not an `ExternalActionRequestBinding`/application receipt. Because it names the result head, it is never embedded in the result capsule/head it proves; recovery retains it as authenticated side evidence and may copy it only into a later successor capsule whose own head it does not name. The new inode is materialized from the result capsule, acquires a fresh whole-inode fence, and becomes dispatch-capable only after its local mirror byte-matches the result head. Every old inode's guard fails the current-head/staging-incarnation check. Equal-head-generation disagreement remains fatal because no relocation reuses a head generation. Thus the local two-slot file is a fenced publication cache/mirror, while the loss-tolerant journal authority and encrypted capsules are durable recovery authority; no same-inode recreation claim is required.

`PortableRestoreSourceAcquisitionPlan` is the immutable Phase-A prebootstrap-artifact schema `{restore_id,mode,claimed_target_authority_recipe:RestoreClaimedTargetAuthorityRecipe,plan_availability_certificate_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PreBootstrapRestorePlanAvailabilityCertificate>,source_publication_envelope_identity,selected_grant_head,requested_lease_identity_and_window,phase_a_actions,identity_key_plan:RestoreIdentityKeyPlan,recipient_and_reprotection_profile,decoder_bootstrap_profiles,global_resource_ceiling,prebootstrap_abandonment_resource_disposition_recipe,phase_a_action_authority_and_cleanup_bijection}`. It intentionally does not pretend to know the encrypted manifest/projection's complete per-object inventory.

After ArchiveAcquire, `RestoreSourceAcquisitionPlanRefinement` is the prebootstrap-artifact closed phase union `BootstrapOpeners{phase_a_plan_digest,archive_receipt_digest,authenticated_publication_envelope_and_recovery_projection_cipher_inventory,source_k_oid_and_exact_manifest_projection_bootstrap_dek_actions,resource_suballocation,refinement_commit_recipe:DirectoryBoundLocalJournal|ExternalCasContinuity,complete_bootstrap_artifact_action_bijection}|VerifiedObjectInventory{phase_a_plan_digest,bootstrap_refinement_digest,verified_manifest_and_recovery_projection_digests,exact_object_key_cipher_encoding_and_format_inventory,per_object_dek_actions,decoder_and_format_inventory,resource_suballocation,refinement_commit_recipe:DirectoryBoundLocalJournal|ExternalCasContinuity,complete_verified_object_action_bijection}`. `PreBootstrapRefinementAvailabilityCertificate` is the portable signed `{restore_id,phase,phase_a_plan_digest,predecessor_refinement_digest?,refinement_recipe_and_digest,journal_id,current_journal_authority_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,current_capsule_generation_and_root_digest,current_staging_incarnation,recovery_capsule_locations_and_digests,recovery_and_relocation_policy,required_failure_domain_policy,verified_reopen_quorum,retain_until:Canonicalized{root_slot_durable_sealed_journal_import_and_covering_cut}|Abandoned{portable_terminal_abandonment_certificate_and_all_external_status_nonreuse_resource_floors},signer_set_epoch,signatures}`.

DirectoryBound refinement commitment uses two journal generations to avoid a receipt/head cycle. The commit generation contains only `LocalRefinementCommitMarker {restore_id,phase,phase_a_plan_digest,predecessor_refinement_digest?,candidate_refinement_digest,availability_certificate_digest,journal_staging_incarnation,journal_staging_inode_identity,journal_whole_inode_fence_identity,prior_dispatch_root_identity_and_generation,candidate_result_dispatch_root_body_digest,committed_refinement_artifact_locator_and_digest,exact_candidate_journal_membership_proof,marker_digest}` and CASes the journal authority to the committed head. After that head is known, recovery constructs MAC-authenticated `LocalRefinementCommitReceipt {restore_id,phase,phase_a_plan_digest,predecessor_refinement_digest?,candidate_refinement_digest,availability_certificate_digest,journal_id,predecessor_journal_authority_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,committed_journal_authority_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,journal_staging_incarnation,journal_staging_inode_identity,journal_whole_inode_fence_identity,prior_dispatch_root_identity_and_generation,committed_dispatch_root_identity_and_generation,commit_marker_digest,committed_refinement_artifact_locator_and_digest,exact_candidate_journal_membership_proof,mac_under_k_restore_journal}`. A later receipt-import generation stores that already-complete receipt and advances the journal head again; the receipt never names its own containing receipt-import head. Only the receipt-import generation constructs `RefinementCommittedGate` and may authorize actions introduced by the refinement. The target-manifest inode is plan context only and can never inhabit the marker, receipt, or gate. ExternalCas uses the registered continuity-CAS external action and its ordinary later terminal import. Each refinement is made loss-tolerantly available and profile-validly committed before any introduced action can be Armed. BootstrapOpeners derives only from the signed archive receipt/publication envelope; after those openers recover, recovery independently opens/verifies the manifest and projection and only then creates VerifiedObjectInventory. Thus encrypted inventory is never magically known, while every per-object provider action is fixed before send.

A late-bound recipe contains one typed `PlanDigest` or `RefinementDigest` hole; the containing artifact hashes recipe identity/parameters-with-hole, then derivation fills exactly that hole after the digest exists. Full request bytes never feed the artifact that they themselves name, and external heads commit portable canonical digests rather than future target-keyed ObjectIds.

RecoverSameIdentity Phase A requires EnterRestoreFencePending, one issuer-fence row per issuer, one revoke action for every cohort selected Revoked, EnterRestoreReserved, AllocationEpoch claim, ArchiveAcquire, the complete `RestoreIdentityKeyPlan`, and complete phase-A cleanup recipes. CloneDirectoryBound Phase A requires NewDatabaseIdentity and AllocationEpoch claims, the exact target-manifest filesystem/directory/inode recipe, whole-inode fence and zero-existing-RootSlot proof, ArchiveAcquire, the fresh-target-key creation recipe, and no EnterCloneReserved action or external continuity head. CloneExternalCas adds EnterCloneReserved and a live RecoveryOnly continuity lease. No key-provider operation runs in Phase A. BootstrapOpeners, after its refinement is committed, performs the mode-valid same-identity source-`K_oid` recovery/rewrap or clone source-`K_oid` source-open-only recovery plus fresh target-`K_oid` creation, together with the exact publication/projection DEK recovery set. VerifiedObjectInventory requires one source-DEK recovery per verified inventory member. The hierarchical bijection proves every issuer/cohort/reservation/key/object/lease/continuity resource and every transient/fresh key cleanup appears exactly once across Phase A and both refinements; continuity abandonment is ExternalCas-only, while DirectoryBound abandonment proves zero RootSlot under the target-manifest inode fence and burns/destroys only its claimed or freshly created resources.

`PreBootstrapRestoreDispatchGateHeader` is That successor has no strong path back to the sealed import, canonicalization import, detailed plan/refinement copies, wrapper ciphertexts, reencryption owner/proof, acquisition bundle, or destruction receipt, so ordinary GC can actually reclaim them. Every nonterminal restore state retains one canonicalized substate after canonicalization, and terminal common/tombstones retain the tag-refined union until their compact status/nonreuse floor. No implication from a command chain substitutes for this owner.

`RestoreCanonicalAcquisitionWorkingSet<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the pre-freeze target-keyed closure `{authority_bound_header,plan_copy_ref,bootstrap_refinement_copy_ref:CanonicalBootstrapOpenersRef<Role>,verified_object_refinement_copy_ref:CanonicalVerifiedObjectInventoryRef<Role>,source_gate_copy_ref,archive_receipt_ref,sorted_key_provider_receipt_refs,identity_key_disposition_evidence,source_k_oid_wrap_and_key_commitment,target_k_oid_wrap_and_key_commitment,sorted_object_dek_opener_recipes,decoder_and_format_profile_inventory,complete_plan_refinement_manifest_projection_object_key_provider_receipt_and_opener_bijection,live_prebootstrap_dispatch_root_identity_and_generation,body_digest}`. It is usable only with a live `RestoreProjectionBuildGuard` that revalidates the current dispatch root and source-lease owner; by itself it authorizes no source read or provider action.

`RestoreSourceAcquisitionBundle<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is created only after bridge freeze and is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,plan_import_record_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceAcquisitionPlanImportRecord<Role>>,working_set_ref:StrongRef<RestoreCanonicalAcquisitionWorkingSet<Role>>,source_gate_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceAcquisitionSourceGate>,archive_receipt_ref:StrongRef<PortableRestoreArchiveAcquisitionReceipt>,canonical_lease_record_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceLeaseRecord<Role>>,frozen_latest_lease_generation_and_portable_state_digest,sorted_key_provider_receipt_refs[RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef],identity_key_disposition_evidence:RestoreIdentityKeyDispositionEvidence,source_k_oid_wrap_and_key_commitment,target_k_oid_wrap_and_key_commitment,sorted_object_dek_opener_recipes[{source_object_identity,source_ciphertext_and_encoding_identity,portable_receipt_member_commitment,opener_policy_oid,target_recipient_commitment,proof_of_inventory_membership}],decoder_and_format_profile_inventory,complete_prebootstrap_artifact_plan_gate_manifest_projection_object_key_provider_receipt_opener_and_cleanup_bijection,bridge_freeze_commitment,body_digest}`. It contains only wrapped material/recipient commitments and canonical copies of typed portable receipts; no prebootstrap artifact locator remains load-bearing after import. Missing source `K_oid`, missing target `K_oid` creation/rewrap, a missing DEK opener, uncovered subject, unclassified format, or created artifact without cleanup disposition fails before the first authoritative target-format escape.

The acquisition uses the registered pre-bootstrap dispatch machine because the target has no canonical RootManifest yet. Before the plan, recovery creates the stable journal/capsule authority above. `RestoreAcquisitionDispatchRoot` is a two-slot, tear-checked and MAC-authenticated, whole-inode-fenced **local mirror/cache** in the exclusive `journal_staging_inode`—outside the target database directory and registered as the sole pre-bootstrap local mutable-root exception. Each slot MAC covers `{restore_id,journal_id,current_journal_authority_head_digest_and_cas_version,portable_plan_digest_or_recipe_digest,plan_availability_certificate_identity,current_staging_incarnation,journal_staging_inode_identity,slot_index,generation,predecessor_slot_digest,complete action map and typed artifact locators,current prebootstrap time basis,current lease owner,resource dispositions,state}` under `K_restore_journal`; recovery rejects equal-generation disagreement, invalid MAC, wrap/claim/head mismatch, rollback, or artifact-locator substitution. No local generation is dispatch-capable until the matching encrypted generation-capsule recipe is available in the required failure domains, the journal authority head has advanced to it, and the local mirror byte-matches that result.

Its payload state is `Building|AcquiredProjectionAllowed|BridgeFrozenForCanonicalCreation{bridge_freeze_spec_artifact_ref,working_set_projection_and_bridge_recipe_commitment,frozen_latest_source_lease_generation_and_portable_state_digest,recovery_incarnation_refresh_family_state?,complete_terminal_attempt_and_resource_owner_bijection}|FirstRootPublicationFrozen{first_root_freeze_spec_artifact_ref,closed_recovery_incarnation_refresh_family_final_ordinal?,final_recovery_incarnation_lease_generation_and_window?,final_sealed_import_bundle_and_creation_guard_commitment,complete_terminal_attempt_family_member_and_resource_owner_bijection}|AbandonmentDrainPending{sealed_abandon_intent_artifact_ref,frozen_new_action_projection_and_creation_guards,outstanding_preexisting_attempt_bitmap,zero_canonical_publication_proof}|AbandonmentAuthorized{sealed_abandonment_spec_artifact_ref,complete_terminal_preexisting_attempt_inventory,complete_action_and_resource_disposition_plan,zero_canonical_publication_proof}|CleanupInProgress{sealed_abandonment_spec_artifact_ref,sorted_action_dispositions,sorted_resource_dispositions,outstanding_cleanup_bitmap}|TerminallyAbandoned`. `AcquiredProjectionAllowed` permits source opens, transform/projection construction, status resolution, and exact source-lease renewal through the live journal. `RestoreBridgeFreezeSpec` is a sealed prebootstrap artifact whose fields commit the completed working set, transform/projection identities and digests, exact first-bridge recipes, latest source-lease owner generation/state, current ExternalCas RecoveryOnly incarnation-lease generation if applicable, zero unresolved source/provider attempt proof, the closed source-renew family ordinal, and the complete action/resource owner/disposition bijection. Its one journal-authority-backed root transition consumes every projection/source-use guard, forbids new source/provider operations and source-lease renewal, and enters `BridgeFrozenForCanonicalCreation` while leaving only the bounded recovery-incarnation refresh family open.

The sole operation after bridge freeze but before the second freeze is exact `RecoveryIncarnationLeaseAcquireOrRefresh` for an ExternalCas target. Its action body preserves database/security identity, target incarnation, writer identity, `RecoveryOnly` scope, current continuity head/CAS, and first-root action digest; only the current predecessor lease generation/status, requested validity window, and pre-minted member identity advance. It grants no archive/key/source access. A successful refresh advances the journal head/dispatch state, invalidates every unrooted sealed-import/bundle/creation-guard candidate derived from the prior lease, and deterministically rebuilds candidates against the new lease. DirectoryBound has no such action.

`RestoreFirstRootPublicationFreezeSpec` is the second sealed prebootstrap artifact. It consumes the current bridge-frozen state, exact latest terminal recovery-lease member/head, final sealed-import/bundle/creation-guard recipes, and a proof that no refresh member is Armed, SentUnknown, unresolved, or authorizable beyond the selected final ordinal. Its journal-authority-backed transition closes the recovery-incarnation refresh family and enters `FirstRootPublicationFrozen`; only then are the final `SealedPreBootstrapDispatchJournalImport<Role>`, `RestoreSourceAcquisitionPlanImportRecord<Role>`, `RestoreSourceAcquisitionBundle<Role>`, and role-valid first-root creation guard constructible. After this second freeze the only legal outcomes are byte-exact first-root publication under that guard or transition to abandonment drain. If the closed lease/window becomes unusable before publication, the restore fails closed to abandonment and a new restore attempt; the family can never reopen.

Abandonment begins with `PreBootstrapRestoreAbandonIntent`, not a cleanup gate. Its journal-authority-backed transition enters `AbandonmentDrainPending`, revokes every **new** action/projection/creation authorization, and freezes the exact set of already Authorized/Armed/SentUnknown attempts. `PreBootstrapAbandonmentDrainCarryForwardGuard<Action>` is inhabitable only for one frozen preexisting attempt: it preserves the attempt's original request and original source-gate commitment, permits status-first recovery, permits byte-identical retry only when the original row/status/eligibility allows it, and permits an Armed-unsent attempt to use its original never-sent proof. It cannot create a new operation, change bytes, open source data, build projection, or publish service. Registered ArchiveAcquire and every other provider-started attempt therefore roll forward under their original identity until Applied/AlreadyApplied/refused/conflict or a definitive never-sent terminal; an unchanged Registered head is never zero-effect.

Only after the outstanding bitmap is empty may `PreBootstrapRestoreAbandonAuthorizeSpec` construct the exact total cleanup plan and enter `AbandonmentAuthorized`. That state permanently revokes all old carry-forward guards; only new action-specific release/burn/revoke/destroy cleanup operations, their status recovery, and disposition publication are legal. CleanupInProgress monotonically records one typed action/resource disposition at a time under `PreBootstrapAbandonmentCleanupGate`. Every attempt uses the universal generated state machine and owns action-typed `PreBootstrapArtifactRef` values for status results, receipts/refusals/conflicts, portable terminal evidence, and import records; a digest alone is not recoverable authority. `PreBootstrapDispatchPublicationEvidence<Action>` and `PreBootstrapNeverSentProof<Action>` are specific to the journal authority plus local mirror and cannot be decoded as ordinary RootManifest evidence.

While `BridgeFrozenForCanonicalCreation`, recovery may construct and independently verify only unrooted candidate copies for the sealed import, canonical lease, plan import, bundle, and creation guard; every refresh invalidates them. Only `FirstRootPublicationFrozen` may construct the final canonical artifacts, whose immutable history covers every pre-first-root renewal/refresh/status transition and whose creation guard consumes that exact final journal head/mirror generation. Journal-key destruction/zeroization waits until the detailed-import floor is replaced by the explicitly preterminal `PreBootstrapDispatchTerminalAccumulator<Role>`. Abandonment instead seals the complete disposition transcript and retains its loss-tolerant recovery capsule through the same external nonreuse/status floor.

Prebootstrap time validation is explicit. `PreBootstrapTimeAuthorityBasis` is the portable certified `{restore_id,claimed_continuity_or_identity_reservation_authority,plan_digest,plan_availability_certificate_digest,permitted_time_profile_identities_and_digests,authority_domains_and_epochs,challenge_service_contracts,maximum_round_trip_and_uncertainty,valid_through,signer_set_epoch,signatures}` committed by every target claim/head. `PreBootstrapTimeAuthorityObservationImport` pairs that basis with a challenged portable observation and same-process `LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness`; it creates a linear nonserializable guard for only the named prebootstrap action. The first Local/Meta bridge proves exact profile/epoch/service handoff or a dual-signed transition into the canonical `TimeAuthorityRegistry`; no prebootstrap observation survives restart or authorizes post-bootstrap work.

`PendingRestoreAcquisitionGuard` is the linear/nonexportable `{restore_id,portable_plan_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PortableRestoreSourceAcquisitionPlan>,plan_availability_certificate_artifact_ref,exclusive_journal_staging_inode_identity_and_whole_inode_lease,current_dispatch_root_generation,current_prebootstrap_time_basis,exact_current_target_claim_continuity_reservation_and_grant_observation_imports,resource_bounds,remaining_action_bitmap,allowed_effects:DispatchOrAbandon,unconsumed}`. It may publish only registered prebootstrap attempts, immutable unreachable prebootstrap artifacts, lease-owner generations, or the abandonment transition. It becomes `RestoreProjectionBuildGuard<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` only after target `K_oid` exists and the complete required-success/equivalent action bijection/current lease owner are terminally imported. That linear guard is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,canonical_working_set_ref:StrongRef<RestoreCanonicalAcquisitionWorkingSet<Role>>,live_dispatch_root_identity_and_generation,current_prebootstrap_lease_owner_and_time_guard,authorized_archive_ref_set,decoder_opener_key_and_resource_inventory,allowed_effects:OpenTransformProjectRenewFreezeOrAbandon,unconsumed}`. Every archive/key open re-reads `PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent`, the live grant/time evidence, and the unchanged action/resource inventory; the working set or a transform-plan digest alone never authorizes a read. The guard may build the exact transform plan/projection, renew through the same journal, or convert to abandonment. After projection and bridge recipes are complete it may consume itself only into `RestoreBridgeFreezeSpec`; the bridge-frozen guard can create/rebuild unrooted canonical candidates, refresh only the recovery-incarnation lease, enter the second freeze, or abandon, but can perform no source open or renewal. The second frozen guard can only publish the one first root or abandon.

Pre-bootstrap abandonment has separate total action and resource disposition protocols because no RestoreRegistry exists yet. `PreBootstrapActionDisposition` is the closed one-per-action union `NotAuthorized{action_key,zero_authorization_membership_proof}|AuthorizedNeverArmed{action_key,authorization_artifact_ref,zero_armed_membership_proof}|AbandonedBeforeSend{action_key,armed_publication_evidence_artifact_ref,typed_prebootstrap_never_sent_proof_artifact_ref}|Succeeded{action_key,typed_receipt_artifact_ref,portable_terminal_evidence_artifact_ref,terminal_import_artifact_ref,final_external_head_commitment}|NoEffect{action_key,disposition:PermanentlyRefused|ConflictNoEffect|ExpiredNotRegisteredNoEffect,typed_provider_tombstone_artifact_ref,portable_terminal_evidence_artifact_ref,terminal_import_artifact_ref,unchanged_external_head_commitment}`.

`UnpublishedTargetObjectSetQuarantine` is the exact prebootstrap artifact `{restore_id,journal_id,projection_result_identity_and_digest,zero_root_slot_and_zero_canonical_reference_proof,sorted_logical_ciphertext_encoding_placement_and_segment_inventory,sorted_local_staging_members[{filesystem_profile,mount_device,target_manifest_staging_inode_or_segment_identity,name_generation,whole_inode_or_segment_fence,expected_extent_inventory}],sorted_remote_members[{provider,target_identity,operation_family_and_pre_minted_cleanup_ids}],target_k_oid_disposition_basis,complete_projected_object_to_physical_owner_bijection,cleanup_floor,body_digest}`. `UnpublishedTargetObjectSetDisposition` is `CryptoErasedAwaitingPhysicalGc{quarantine_ref,target_k_oid_destroy_receipt_and_terminal_evidence,proof_every_ciphertext_depends_on_destroyed_fresh_target_identity,registered_physical_gc_family_and_retention_floor}|PhysicallyDeleted{quarantine_ref,sorted_local_member_deletion_receipts[FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader+exact_inode_name_generation_extent_proof],sorted_remote_deletion_terminal_imports[ExternalTerminalImportRecord<RestoreUnpublishedTargetPhysicalDelete,PreBootstrap>],complete_target_to_receipt_bijection,zero_remaining_owned_placement_proof}`. Crypto erasure is legal only for a clone-created fresh target identity; same-identity recovery must physically delete or retain quarantine until ordinary GC can prove deletion. Remote/object-store deletion uses registered dispatch; local deletion uses a member-issued fenced physical receipt. Neither a directory scan nor dropping a filename is terminal evidence.

`PreBootstrapResourceDisposition` is the closed one-per-resource union `ReleasedArchiveLease{resource_key,lease_identity,released_through_generation,disposition_action_key,typed_receipt_and_full_no_successor_proof_ref}|RegisteredArchiveAcquisitionRolledForwardThenReleased{resource_key,original_archive_acquire_action_key,registered_head_and_status_lineage_commitment,active_receipt_and_lease_identity,release_action_key,release_receipt_and_full_no_successor_proof_ref}|BurnedReservation{resource_key,reservation_kind,reservation_id,claim_id?,disposition_action_key,typed_burn_receipt_and_nonreuse_commitment}|CatalogTargetCleanup{resource_key,target_catalog_row_key,profile:ExternalCasCataloged|DirectoryBoundCataloged,terminal_disposition:PreBootstrapCatalogRestoreTargetTerminalDisposition::Cataloged}|ContinuityCleanup{resource_key,restore_id,target_incarnation,terminal_disposition:PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityCleanupDisposition}|DirectoryBoundZeroPublicationClosed{resource_key,target_manifest_staging_inode_and_fence_identity,zero_root_slot_proof,claim_burn_set_commitment,catalog_disposition:Cataloged{catalog_resource_key_and_terminal_commitment}|EmbeddedNoCatalog{zero_catalog_applicability_proof}}|RevokedTransientRecoveryWrap{resource_key,wrap_or_grant_identity,disposition_action_key,typed_terminal_evidence_commitment}|DestroyedFreshUnpublishedTargetObjectIdKey{resource_key,key_origin_proof,zero_canonical_publication_proof,disposition_action_key,typed_terminal_evidence_commitment}|UnpublishedTargetObjects{resource_key,quarantine_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<UnpublishedTargetObjectSetQuarantine>,terminal_disposition:UnpublishedTargetObjectSetDisposition}|RetainedTombstonedNoUse{resource_key,permanent_nonuse_commitment}`. Source-key destruction has no arm. ExternalCas cleanup has exactly one ContinuityCleanup row and, unless its authenticated profile proves no target catalog applies, one prior CatalogTargetCleanup row; a no-mutation continuity disposition is just as explicit as a CAS abandonment. DirectoryBound uses DirectoryBoundZeroPublicationClosed, requires its catalog sub-arm to match the profile, and cannot encode a continuity action. `TerminallyAbandoned` proves every projected logical object, ciphertext, encoding, placement, segment/extent, transient wrap, fresh key, claim, lease, and continuity/catalog resource appears exactly once in this disposition inventory.

`PreBootstrapRestoreAbandonIntent` is first sealed with the exact zero-canonical-publication proof, frozen current action/resource inventory, and cleanup-policy recipe, then its authenticated journal transition enters `AbandonmentDrainPending` as above. After every preexisting attempt terminalizes, `PreBootstrapRestoreAbandonAuthorizeSpec` seals the now-exact total action/resource disposition plan and enters `AbandonmentAuthorized`. Only that durable state can construct `PreBootstrapAbandonmentCleanupGate` and enter CleanupInProgress. It schedules exactly the lease release, reservation burns, profile-valid continuity abandonment or DirectoryBound zero-publication closure, transient-wrap revocations, clone-target-key destruction/tombstoning, and unpublished target-object disposition required by the resource inventory. If ArchiveAcquire was already RegisteredPending, drain recovery preserves its original request/source gate until it reaches Active, then the later cleanup plan immediately releases the returned lease and records `RegisteredArchiveAcquisitionRolledForwardThenReleased`. Release/status remains legal after lease expiry under its exact cleanup contract; claim/ordinary acquisition does not. No cleanup send is legal while the root remains Building, AcquiredProjectionAllowed, BridgeFrozenForCanonicalCreation, or AbandonmentDrainPending.

Terminal journal state is `TerminallyAbandoned{sorted_action_dispositions[PreBootstrapActionDisposition],complete_planned_action_and_family_member_bijection,sorted_resource_dispositions[PreBootstrapResourceDisposition],complete_claimed_acquired_created_resource_bijection,action_to_resource_disposition_relation,full_operation_idempotency_request_source_gate_status_and_typed_terminal_lineage_commitment,final_external_head_set_commitment,zero_canonical_publication_proof,terminal_body_digest}`. No two-receipt shortcut or duplicate release/burn row exists. Crash before Armed may use the typed never-sent proof; crash after SentUnknown must status-resolve the same bytes; crash after acquisition can only resume the same projection/creation until AbandonmentAuthorized is durable, after which it can only complete the exact disposition set. The plan availability capsule, claimed authorities, external heads, typed portable artifacts, and sealed journal—not an unrooted local file—are durable recovery authority.

Before `K_restore_journal` can be destroyed on the no-RootManifest path, recovery constructs unsigned reference-free `PortablePreBootstrapAbandonmentTerminalCertificateBody {restore_id,journal_id,predecessor_active_journal_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,predecessor_head_and_dispatch_state_generations,final_active_capsule_digest,plan_recipe_and_final_plan_digests,plan_and_refinement_availability_certificate_digests,terminal_journal_body_digest,complete_action_and_family_member_terminal_accumulator_root,complete_resource_disposition_accumulator_root,final_external_head_and_provider_operation_tombstone_set,permanent_operation_id_and_reservation_nonreuse_floors,zero_canonical_RootManifest_RootSlot_and_target_authority_publication_proof,profile_terminal_disposition:ExternalCasCataloged{catalog_tombstone_terminal_commitment,continuity_cleanup_disposition:PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityCleanupDisposition}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{catalog_tombstone_terminal_commitment,zero_publication_closure_commitment}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{zero_catalog_applicability_proof,zero_publication_closure_commitment},unpublished_target_object_terminal_disposition_commitment,journal_key_commitment,journal_key_destruction_authorization_digest,retention_floor,body_digest}`. It names only the already-existing Active predecessor, never the future terminal head. The profile arm, action accumulator, and resource accumulator must agree exactly on whether catalog and continuity actions existed; no generic “abandoned” bit can hide a missing cleanup stage.

The journal authority verifies and threshold-signs that body as `PortablePreBootstrapAbandonmentTerminalCertificate`, computes its digest, and atomically CASes the exact Active predecessor to `TerminalAbandoned{certificate_digest,retention_floor}` with `head_generation + 1`. It returns separate `PreBootstrapJournalAbandonmentTerminalizationReceipt {journal_id,publication_operation_id,publication_idempotency_digest,predecessor_active_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,certificate_digest,result_terminal_head_bytes_and_digest_and_cas_version,authority_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. The certificate never contains the result-head digest, and neither certificate nor terminal head embeds the later receipt. The receipt is retained outside the result capsule and may enter only a later immutable recovery package that does not name its own publication result. `PreBootstrapJournalKeyDisposition::AbandonedThenDestroyed` retains the certificate, receipt, and authenticated terminal head. None contains a local inode, artifact locator, journal MAC, or plaintext/key-dependent proof. Local zeroization or provider destruction evidence byte-matches the certificate and its key-destruction authorization. Thereafter recovery/status/nonreuse checks use the certificate, terminalization receipt/head, and authenticated provider heads/floors, never the destroyed MAC key. Successful creation instead imports and seals the complete journal lineage into the first canonical RootManifest.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.
