title: Appendix A exact catalog: Restore promotion, independent reopen, completion, and release formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Restore promotion, independent reopen, completion, and release formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 2575-2608 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

`RestorePromotionAuthorityProfile` is the portable closed union `ExternalCasCataloged{expected_reserved_continuity_head_digest_and_cas_version,expected_catalog_predecessor_digest_and_version,continuity_transition_body_digest,catalog_endpoint_set_commitment}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{directory_bound_creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,expected_catalog_predecessor_digest_and_version,catalog_endpoint_set_commitment}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{directory_bound_creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,zero_external_catalog_applicability_proof,embedded_endpoint_or_inprocess_admission_commitment}`. The two DirectoryBound arms are Local-only; Sharded/Meta is always ExternalCasCataloged. The signed `RestoreServicePromotionManifest` is the portable closed posture union with common `{restore_id,database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,target_posture:Local|Sharded,service_visibility_epoch,authority_profile:RestorePromotionAuthorityProfile,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}` and exactly one body: `Local{local_prepare_evidence:PortableCertificateProjection<LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,local_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}` or `Sharded{meta_prepare_evidence:PortableCertificateProjection<GlobalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,sorted_shard_ready_evidence[PortableCertificateProjection<RestoreShardServiceReadyAck>],complete_group_topology_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}`. `PortableCertificateProjection<T>` embeds the target `RemoteObjectIdentity`, complete export projection bytes, canonical configuration/trust evidence bytes, and signatures; it contains no `StrongRef`, `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef`, or consumer-local locator. Nullable cross-posture/profile fields are forbidden.

`RestorePromotionRootSeal<Role>` closes the proof-of-reopen race. After the role's promotion/finalize/open candidate is durably public under the role-valid proof—`PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local|Meta>` for Local/Meta, `ShardStatePublicationCertificate` for Shard—and RootSlot-visible, recovery first builds `RestorePromotionRootSealRecipe<Role>` and completes the exact pin-ledger activation family. Only after `RestoreTerminalPinDurabilityReceipt<Role,Operational>` exists does it construct the seal `{authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,recipe:RestorePromotionRootSealRecipe<Role>,sealed_role_state_root_ref:StrongRef<RoleStateRoot>,sealed_root_manifest_ref:StrongRef<RootManifest>,typed_physical_inventory_ref:StrongRef<RestoreTerminalPhysicalInventory<Role,Operational>>,pin_durability_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreTerminalPinDurabilityReceipt<Role,Operational>>,seal_digest}`. The receipt byte-matches the recipe digest and inventory but never contains the seal identity; the recipe excludes the receipt, so the construction graph is publication -> recipe/inventory -> pin activation receipt -> seal. The publication evidence, applied identity, state root, manifest, and winning slot must describe one publication; a Shard seal never claims an audit-visibility advance it does not have. The role-specific ordered seal-install spec installs the seal into still-hidden `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed`. Before seal installation the only legal work is exact promotion recovery, source-lease renewal where owned, Local/Meta audit visibility or Shard publication recovery, pin activation/status recovery, evidence canonicalization/key cut, shutdown, or seal installation. Afterward only those operations plus reopen confirmation are legal. Every allowed successor preserves the same Active pin ledger/basis; ordinary admission, unrelated maintenance, checkpoint, GC, reconfiguration, key/policy/schema/data mutation, and a second promotion are rejected.

`RestoreIndependentReopenProof<Role>` opens the seal from an independent fresh process/context, not merely the current mutable head. It binds the seal, reopens every typed pinned object/encoding/key, reconstructs the sealed canonical/prepared/Raft closure, revalidates the exact profile-specific promotion authority receipt and service epoch, and supplies an authenticated proof that every successor from the sealed root to the current pending root is one of the allowed nonsemantic/recovery classes. An ExternalCas proof revalidates catalog and continuity heads; DirectoryBoundCataloged revalidates the catalog row plus inode-bound local promotion receipts; DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog revalidates the inode/fence/slot lineage and zero-catalog-applicability proof. Slot churn or a lease renewal therefore cannot erase the proof basis or legitimize an intervening mutation. The role-specific reopen-confirm command consumes that exact proof and is the only transition to `Operational`; its published successor installs `RestoreTerminalPinBasis<Role>::Operational`. An abandonment finalize/apply instead installs `RestoreRetentionAnchor<Role>::AbandonmentPinPending` from the prebuilt pending owner; only the later role-specific pin-install command, after the abandonment root is durably published and its physical inventory is pinned, replaces that anchor with `RestoreTerminalPinBasis<Role>::Abandoned`. Local/Meta retain the matching terminal pin basis until `RestoreSourceLeaseReleaseFinalizeSpec`; that finalize atomically removes the Local pin owner or starts the Meta participant-release protocol and emits no promotion-shaped authority for an abandoned restore. Each shard retains its matching basis through its operational or abandonment acknowledgement and removes it only through `ShardRestoreTerminalPinReleaseSpec` consuming the matching certified terminal authorization. Release/tombstone floors retain every basis, seal or abandonment evidence, inventory, proof where applicable, and pin receipt until all configured shard release acknowledgements and the source-release terminal are complete. Crash tests cut every seal-build or abandonment-basis build, pin, slot publish, proof open, confirm, source-access cleanup, source-release, and shard-pin-release step, including arbitrary slot convergence and allowed lease renewals.

Promotion is profile-discriminated and service remains hidden throughout. For cataloged profiles the catalog exposes a CAS-linear per-database row head, so unrelated rows never force request rewriting. `ServiceCatalogPromotionReservationReceipt` is the portable result of `CatalogReserveHidden` and binds `{external_request_binding,restore_or_transition_id,target_database_and_security_identity,target_posture,target_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,manifest_digest,expected_target_row_predecessor_digest_and_version,reservation_id,reservation_digest,reserved_target_row_digest_and_version,endpoint_set_commitment,state:ReservedHiddenNonexpiring,authority_signatures}`. The row CAS accepts only the exact predecessor, `AlreadyReservedEquivalent` for the same operation/request, or a semantically equivalent target-row descendant whose target remains absent/hidden with identical reservation semantics. It never accepts an arbitrary rebased row. The reservation is nonexpiring after the profile's pending boundary and blocks every competing endpoint install.

`ServicePromotionExternalOperationKind` is `CatalogReserveHidden|ContinuityEnterPromotionPending|CatalogActivateReserved|ContinuityFinalizeOperational`, specialized by `operation_subject:Restore{restore_id}|RoleTransition{migration_nonce}`. The continuity arms are inhabitable only for ExternalCas. Each external action has a distinct `ServicePromotionExternalOperationRecord<Role>` created by an ordered hidden Semantic authorize spec with exact action-body recipe, operation/idempotency identity, expected predecessor, original promotion authorization/header, resource hold, and no future publication evidence. Only its role-valid publication initializes the universal Armed/SentUnknown/status/receipt-import machine.

The exact profile sequences are:

- `ExternalCasCataloged`: (1) external `CatalogReserveHidden`; (2) external continuity CAS `RestoreReserved|CloneReserved|RoleTransitionReserved -> PromotionCatalogPending`; (3) external `CatalogActivateReserved` to `CatalogActivatedHidden{admission=CompositePromotionReceiptRequired}`; (4) external continuity CAS `PromotionCatalogPending -> Operational{PromotionReceiptRequired}`. The four noninterchangeable results are `CatalogPromotionReservationReceipt`, `PromotionContinuityPendingReceipt`, `CatalogPromotionActivationReceipt`, and `PromotionContinuityFinalizeReceipt`, each with its exact request binding/status/import lineage.
- `DirectoryBoundCataloged`: (1) external `CatalogReserveHidden`; (2) ordered Local `DirectoryBoundEnterPromotionPendingSpec` consumes the current `DirectoryBoundCreationEvidence<Local>`, hidden prepare certificate, reservation receipt, live inode lease/sequencer, and exact current slot, then RootSlot-publishes `DirectoryBoundPromotionPending`; only afterward may `DirectoryBoundPromotionPendingReceipt` be issued with `FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader`, prior/result state-root and slot evidence, fixed local continuity digest, and catalog-reservation binding; (3) external `CatalogActivateReserved` binds that local pending receipt and remains admission-hidden; (4) ordered Local `DirectoryBoundFinalizeOperationalAuthoritySpec` consumes the activation receipt and current pending state, RootSlot-publishes `DirectoryBoundOperationalReceiptRequired`, then emits distinct `DirectoryBoundOperationalAuthorityReceipt` with exact inode/fence/slot/state lineage. No external continuity action, record, CAS version, status, or receipt is created.
- `DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog`: ordered Local pending and operational-authority transitions exactly as above but bind the manifest's zero-catalog-applicability proof and in-process admission commitment; no catalog action/row/version/receipt and no external continuity action exist.

The pending transition is the irreversible no-downgrade boundary for both DirectoryBound profiles. Before it, cancellation requires exact no-send/no-publication evidence and, for DirectoryBoundCataloged, a durable catalog reservation cancellation/tombstone. After it, recovery has only profile-specific roll-forward authority. Every local transition revalidates the same creation evidence, live inode lease, publication sequencer, fixed continuity digest, hidden service gate, and exact predecessor RootSlot immediately before publication; a member-issued receipt from unreachable staging or a different inode is invalid.

`RestoreServicePromotionReceipt` is the portable closed union `ExternalCasCataloged{restore_id,manifest_digest,service_visibility_epoch,catalog_reservation_lineage,continuity_pending_lineage,catalog_activation_lineage,continuity_finalize_lineage,prior_pending_and_operational_continuity_heads_and_cas_versions,catalog_predecessor_reserved_and_activated_versions,endpoint_set_commitment,complete_four_stage_bijection_digest,authority_signatures}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{restore_id,manifest_digest,service_visibility_epoch,catalog_reservation_lineage,directory_bound_pending_receipt_bytes_and_digest,catalog_activation_lineage,directory_bound_operational_authority_receipt_bytes_and_digest,creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,catalog_predecessor_reserved_and_activated_versions,endpoint_set_commitment,complete_profile_stage_bijection_digest,authority_signatures}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{restore_id,manifest_digest,service_visibility_epoch,directory_bound_pending_receipt_bytes_and_digest,directory_bound_operational_authority_receipt_bytes_and_digest,creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,zero_catalog_applicability_proof_digest,embedded_admission_commitment,complete_profile_stage_bijection_digest,authority_signatures}`. `ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionManifestRef` and `ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef` are generated tag-refined strong references whose validators require respectively the Sharded/ExternalCas manifest arm and the ExternalCasCataloged receipt arm; variant syntax is never used as a reference target. The receipt exists only after every stage of its one profile succeeds, and decoders reject cross-profile optionality or fabricated placeholder versions.

`RestorePromotionConflictAbandonSpec` is profile-specific. ExternalCasCataloged and DirectoryBoundCataloged first install a rooted no-endpoint catalog tombstone/cancel the reservation. ExternalCas then CASes the matching reserved or PromotionCatalogPending continuity head to RestoreAbandoned; DirectoryBound instead orders the inode-fenced local abandonment state and never emits a continuity CAS. Embedded DirectoryBound orders only that local abandonment. No profile can restore the same incarnation to service after its permanent conflict/abandon terminal.

`GlobalRestoreServiceFinalizeSpec {restore_id,prepare_certificate_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,manifest_ref:ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionManifestRef,promotion_receipt_ref:ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef,exact_sorted_ready_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<RestoreShardServiceReadyAck>],expected_meta_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_profile_terminal_authority_state,service_visibility_epoch,terminal_audit_gate}` verifies the complete rooted ExternalCas four-stage lineage and clears Meta restore state only into `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed`; request admission and routing remain disabled. After its audit visibility advance it yields `GlobalRestoreServiceFinalCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,restore_id,finalize_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,manifest_profile_and_receipt_digests,ready_ack_commitment,post_apply_global_state_root_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStateRoot>,service_visibility_epoch,visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}`.

A shard leaves `RecoveryReconciling` only through `ShardRestoreServiceOpenSpec {final_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalRestoreServiceFinalCertificate>,own_ready_ack_ref:StrongRef<RestoreShardServiceReadyAck>,locally_verified_promotion_receipt_ref:ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef,expected_local_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,service_visibility_epoch}` under its exact outer Meta authority, and that command selects `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed`, not Operational. After the open root has a durable `ShardStatePublicationCertificate`, it builds/installs the role seal above. A fresh process then creates `ShardRestoreIndependentReopenProof`, and `ShardRestoreReopenConfirmSpec {restore_id,final_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalRestoreServiceFinalCertificate>,seal_ref:StrongRef<RestorePromotionRootSeal<Shard>>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<ShardRestoreIndependentReopenProof>,expected_pending_state:OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed,service_visibility_epoch}` selects OperationalAwaitingSourceAccessClosure. Only after `ShardRestoreSourceAccessCloseSpec` installs the exact closure may the applied-and-durable ParticipantComplete root produce `RestoreShardOperationalAck {SameGroupCertificateHeader,restore_id,final_certificate_identity,own_ready_ack_identity,reopen_confirm_applied_identity,source_access_close_applied_identity,post_close_state_root_ref:StrongRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,reopen_publication_certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardStatePublicationCertificate>,seal_ref:StrongRef<RestorePromotionRootSeal<Shard>>,operational_terminal_pin_basis_ref:OperationalRestoreTerminalPinBasisRef<Shard>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<ShardRestoreIndependentReopenProof>,source_access_closure_ref:StrongRef<ShardRestoreSourceAccessClosure>,terminalizing_projection_commitment,applied_shard_raft_index,service_visibility_epoch,root_slot_durability_digest,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}`. The seal supplies the earlier open-root publication evidence; the reopen certificate byte-matches `reopen_confirm_applied_identity`, and the closure/basis/projection byte-match the post-close root. Meta routing waits for the target shard ack; direct shard endpoints reject every pending-reopen or pending-source-closure phase and require the current ExternalCas receipt, final Meta certificate, Operational participant-complete root, and reopen proof.

Meta follows the same pattern after finalize: it installs `RestorePromotionRootSeal<Meta>`, a fresh context produces `MetaRestoreIndependentReopenProof`, and `GlobalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec {restore_id,final_certificate_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRestoreServiceFinalCertificate>,meta_seal_ref:StrongRef<RestorePromotionRootSeal<Meta>>,meta_independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<MetaRestoreIndependentReopenProof>,exact_sorted_operational_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<RestoreShardOperationalAck>],promotion_receipt_ref:ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef,expected_restore_registry_state:PromotedAwaitingReopen,expected_meta_pending_state:OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed,expected_source_lease_generation,terminal_audit_gate}` verifies one ack from every required shard and alone selects Meta Operational. Its audit visibility advance installs `RestoreRetentionAnchor::TerminalPinBasis` with the operational basis and moves the registry to `AwaitingSourceAccessCleanup::Operational`; only the later complete source-access cleanup finalize may enter AwaitingSourceRelease. It neither hides an unready group nor releases the source lease/pins directly.

The exact Local path is independent of sharded evidence. `LocalRestoreReadyCertificate` is `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,restore_id,restore_epoch,service_visibility_epoch,current_hidden_state_root_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStateRoot>,reconciliation_completion_proof_ref:StrongRef<RestoreReconciliationCompletionProof<Local>>,ready_closure_inventory_ref:StrongRef<RestoreReadyClosureInventory<Local>>,current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,current_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>,current_config_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>,root_slot_durability_digest,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. `LocalRestoreActivationSpec` is `{restore_id,ready_certificate_ref:StrongRef<LocalRestoreReadyCertificate>,expected_local_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_configuration_checkpoint_and_floor,promotion_authority_basis:ExternalCasCataloged{expected_reserved_continuity_digest_and_cas_version}|DirectoryBound{creation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<DirectoryBoundCreationEvidence<Local>>,fixed_local_continuity_digest},service_visibility_epoch,terminal_audit_gate}` and moves only Reconciling -> VisibilityCommitted. After its gap-free release, `LocalRestoreActivationCertificate` owns the hidden root, exact ready evidence, profile basis, and `visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local>>`. `LocalRestoreServicePrepareSpec` is `{restore_id,activation_certificate_ref:StrongRef<LocalRestoreActivationCertificate>,expected_local_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,exact_configuration_and_endpoint_set,promotion_authority_profile_recipe:ExternalCasCataloged{expected_catalog_predecessor_version}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{expected_catalog_predecessor_version}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{zero_catalog_applicability_proof},service_visibility_epoch,terminal_audit_gate}` and moves only to ServicePreparedHidden; its gap-free release yields `LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate` over the prepare record, hidden root, visibility certificate, endpoint/configuration commitment, exact promotion-authority profile basis, epoch, and signer transcript.

The Local arm of `RestoreServicePromotionManifest` executes exactly its selected profile and produces that profile's composite receipt first. `LocalRestoreServicePromotionSpec {restore_id,prepare_certificate_ref:StrongRef<LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,manifest_ref:StrongRef<RestoreServicePromotionManifest{target_posture=Local}>,promotion_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreServicePromotionReceipt>,exact_profile_stage_operation_dispatch_or_local_publication_lineage_refs,expected_local_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_profile_terminal_authority_state,service_visibility_epoch,terminal_audit_gate}` requires manifest/prepare/receipt/profile equality and clears restore state only into `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed` after its exact `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local>` is durable; its registry becomes PromotedAwaitingReopen and still owns the source lease. It then installs `RestorePromotionRootSeal<Local>`. The exact generated `RestoreIndependentReopenProof<Role>` schema is the seal-bound proof above, including the allowed-successor-chain proof rather than an unpinned observation of whichever slot happens to be current. A fresh process produces `LocalRestoreIndependentReopenProof`; `LocalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec {restore_id,promotion_record_ref:StrongRef<LogicalCommandRecord>,promotion_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreServicePromotionReceipt>,seal_ref:StrongRef<RestorePromotionRootSeal<Local>>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<LocalRestoreIndependentReopenProof>,expected_restore_registry_state:PromotedAwaitingReopen,expected_pending_state:OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed,expected_source_lease_generation,terminal_audit_gate}` alone selects Operational; its gap-free release installs `RestoreRetentionAnchor::TerminalPinBasis` with the operational basis, moves the registry to `AwaitingSourceAccessCleanup::Operational`, and yields the completion visibility certificate. Complete source-access cleanup then enters AwaitingSourceRelease; source release uses the ordered operation/dispatch/receipt/finalize protocol above. Completion never directly drops the lease or pin.

Every handshake/session/request/forwarded shard request/transaction/query child/delivery cursor/cross-session capability carries `{cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch}`. Mixed or stale epochs fail before authorization or observation. `RestoreSourceLease` remains live through promotion/finalize/open, independent target reopen, operational acknowledgements, and the role-valid post-open completion audit visibility advance. `CloneNewIdentity` uses the same transform/result/guard/reconciliation/promotion machinery but assigns a new database/security namespace, `K_oid`, continuity domain, current groups/authority, and Audit clone boundary; historical evidence remains carried, old capabilities remain invalid, and source authority is never current target authority. `source_posture == expected_posture` is mandatory for both modes; Local-to-W12 is a later separate role transition.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

## Provenance
Complete audited plan Appendix A lines 2575-2608.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Replay, authorization, capability, DP, audit, and transparency formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Replay, authorization, capability, DP, audit, and transparency formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 2609-2728 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**ReplayManifest / executable and archive closure.** `ReplayCompleteness` is `Replayable|StructuralReplay|VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied|AuditOnly` with explicit class lists. `ArchiveObjectIdentity` is nonlocal and never a local reachability edge. `ReplayObjectRef<T>` is exactly `LocalStrong{ref:StrongRef<T>}|CertifiedRemote{ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>}|Archived{identity,expected_logical_object_id,expected_canonical_digest}`. CertifiedRemote requires a live matching authority configuration/trust selector/grant and participates in two-sided retention; Archived resolves only through the active registry and never marks local data. Every slot uses `ReplayEvidenceRef<T> = Present{object:ReplayObjectRef<T>}|Unavailable{class,expected identity/digest?,reason}|Redacted{class,commitment?,policy}`. `ReplayLogicalStateEvidence = Local{state:ReplayEvidenceRef<LogicalStateRoot>}|Sharded{global_state:ReplayEvidenceRef<GlobalStateRoot>,topology:ReplayEvidenceRef<TopologyState>,exact_global_prefix,sorted_shard_states[ReplayEvidenceRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>],complete_partition_commitment}`; a Sharded grade is no stronger than its weakest required group/evidence lease.

`ReplayManifest` binds `{format major/minor,slot schema,database/security namespace/incarnation,logical/commit seq,logical_state:ReplayLogicalStateEvidence,graph bindings,topology/policy/revocation epochs,language/semantic/scalar/numeric profiles,answer requirement/result contract,logical/physical plan IDs,bound/normalized query,typed parameters,replay authority,module/UDF set,external inputs,derived generation snapshots,decision cards/policies/evidence,executable artifacts,structural projection,result encoding/digest,structural completeness,archive requirements,created HLC}`. The generated slot schema derives the maximum grade: Replayable requires every execution-semantic Local or Sharded slot live; structural replay requires its typed projection; supply-later carries all identities/digests; audit/redaction is explicit. Live effective grade may only weaken as any local, certified-remote, or archive trust/lease/authority fails. Legacy Local manifests survive activation unchanged.

`ExecutableArtifactSet` binds `{ exact_binary:ReplayObjectRef | reproducible_build_closure[ReplayObjectRef], source_tree:ReplayObjectRef?, rust_toolchain:ReplayObjectRef,target,cpu_feature_contract,runtime_allocator_config:ReplayObjectRef,vm_jit_compiler_artifacts[ReplayObjectRef],kernel_profile_registry:ReplayObjectRef,platform_abi:ReplayObjectRef,build_recipe:ReplayObjectRef,artifact_digest }`; exactly one executable route must be complete whenever this set is present. `StructuralReplayProjection` binds its reproduced event/data-shape classes, canonical projection schema, required evidence-slot classes, omitted/redacted classes, expected commitments, and output verifier. `ReplayArchiveRecord` is immutable `{ archive_id,generation,predecessor_record_digest:WeakDigest?,security_domain,resolver_profile_oid,authenticated_external_locator,archive_closure_digest:WeakDigest,sorted_object_inventory[{identity:ArchiveObjectIdentity,expected_logical_object_id,expected_canonical_digest,length}],availability_commitment,time_authority_profile_oid,lease_not_before,lease_not_after,status:Active|Revoked|Expired,signer_set_epoch,signatures }`; its signature transcript covers the profile and both bounds. Its inventory/closure explicitly excludes the record itself, `ReplayRegistry`, and the locally rooted manifest, so archive and manifest identities can be constructed in the order `external evidence inventory -> archive record -> manifest -> registry` without a digest cycle. `ReplayRegistry` maps `manifest_id -> {manifest:StrongRef<ReplayManifest>,lease/status}` and `archive_id -> latest_record:StrongRef<ReplayArchiveRecord>`. Renewal creates a logical-command-sequenced successor after re-verifying the entire inventory and validating fresh Usable evidence. Revocation/expiry never asserts deletion; the ordered status successor retains the exact subject-bound time evidence when expiry is its cause, then consensus removes the registry availability edge, after which ordinary GC may release otherwise-unrooted local manifest objects/records. A manifest is advertised `Replayable` only while every required local object opens and every archive requirement resolves through an active, time-validated, trusted record with a matching inventory/closure digest. Resolver credentials and replay contents require scoped `Replay` authority; capability-safe lookup does not disclose whether another authority's manifest/archive exists.

**Authorization, durable capabilities, DP, resources, and audit records.** `MutationPermitRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,issuer,policy_semantics_ref:StrongRef<PolicySemantics>,exact_role_bearing_read_bindings,role_free_write_coordinates,allowed_snapshot_scope,allowed_query_operator_disclosure_scope,result_answer_contract_ceiling,operation_scope,presentation_binding:ServerInternal|SessionBound{session_binding,auth_generation}|ChannelBound{transport_exporter_digest},nonce,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expiry,signer_epoch,signature_or_mac_transcript,body_digest}`. `ReadPermitRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the distinct no-write format `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,issuer,policy_semantics_ref:StrongRef<PolicySemantics>,exact_role_bearing_read_bindings,allowed_snapshot_scope,allowed_query_operator_disclosure_scope,result_answer_contract_ceiling,presentation_binding,nonce,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expiry,signer_epoch,signature_or_mac_transcript,body_digest}`; it has no write coordinate, mutation capability, or empty-effect convention. The header supplies namespace/incarnation/service/tenant/principal/ceiling/policy/revocation exactly once, and every permit transcript covers the complete referenced binding, scope, presentation binding, time profile, and closed-open window.

`AuthorityPermitRef<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is exactly `ReadOnly{permit_ref:StrongRef<ReadPermitRecord<Role>>}|ReadWrite{permit_ref:StrongRef<MutationPermitRecord<Role>>}`. `MutationPermitReadProjection<Role>` is `{permit_ref:StrongRef<MutationPermitRecord<Role>>,permit_body_digest,authority_binding_body_digest,exact_role_bearing_read_bindings,allowed_snapshot_scope,allowed_query_operator_disclosure_scope,result_answer_contract_ceiling,presentation_binding,projection_digest}` and may only narrow the referenced mutation permit. `ReadCapablePermitRef<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `DedicatedRead{permit_ref:StrongRef<ReadPermitRecord<Role>>}|MutationReadProjection{projection_ref:StrongRef<MutationPermitReadProjection<Role>>}`. `ImportedReadCapablePermitEvidence` is the generated shard-portable exact union carrying the source permit/projection public identity, complete read projection, exact `ShardAuthorityBindingProjection`, source configuration/prefix/retention evidence, and signatures; a permit identity plus digest or bare security projection is insufficient. Clients never serialize or choose local `PermitRecord` refs: FGP/embedded calls present credentials, token bytes, and their required session/channel binding, the trusted verifier persists the role-local record, and only a nonconstructible verified typed ref crosses into database code. Use requires matching fresh `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, the exact current-or-held authority binding, and a linear guard. `AuthorizationLease` is the exact profiled signed consensus-domain/service-epoch/snapshot-range/read-binding/query-disclosure/answer-ceiling lease defined in §14.3, not an inferred extension. Rust exposes only verified nonconstructible wrappers.

Admission, recovery, and completeness semantic transitions use StructurallyInapplicable gates; visibility and activation maintenance use distinct system-authority arms; terminal consumes the existing ticket.

`AuditCloneBoundary` is `{source_database_security_namespace_id,source_audit_domain_id,source_continuity_head_digest,target_database_security_namespace_id,target_audit_domain_id,clone_manifest_ref,retained_source_evidence_contract,source_signatures,target_signatures}` and never rewrites source tickets into the target domain. `AuditSegment` is a contiguous signed range with previous-chain digest, ticket/resolution ranges, event records, redaction profile, signing epoch, and external-anchor ref. `AuditTicketIndex` makes every issued ticket pending or uniquely resolved and retains its event, external receipt, and local import status across recovery. `AuditCheckpoint` commits retained ticket/event floors and heads, unresolved-ticket set, continuity/gap heads, signer-rotation chain, and anchor. Missing external evidence disables completeness-gated operations; it never silently weakens the advertised profile.

**WitnessPolicy / TransparencyCheckpoint.** `WitnessPolicy` is `{format_version,log_id,security_domain_id,policy_epoch,claim_class:EquivocationDetection|NonEquivocation,ordered_witnesses[{witness_id,key_id,verification_key,endpoint_identity,optional_cross_log_authority}],n,threshold_t,byzantine_bound_f,signature_profile,consistency_proof_profile,durable_head_state_profile,anti_rollback_profile,authenticated_gossip_profile:None|Required{transport_auth_profile,peer_identity_registry,checkpoint_message_schema,replay_window,evidence_retention_floor,maximum_convergence_delay},activation_log_size,maximum_checkpoint_age,cross_log_policy:None|Required{ordered_authorities,threshold},rotation:Genesis|JointSuccessor{predecessor_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>}}`. Canonical validation requires exactly `n` unique ordered witnesses, `0 <= f < t <= n`, supported signature/consistency/persistence profiles, and—before `claim_class=NonEquivocation` is usable—`2t > n + f`. A detection claim that relies on gossip requires the complete authenticated profile; an unnamed/best-effort channel proves nothing. Each honest witness durably stores `{log_id,security_domain_id,policy_oid,last_size,last_root,anti_rollback_counter}` before acknowledging a signature; it signs only a verified append-only consistency extension, never two roots at one size or non-extending histories. Rollback or loss of this state disables that witness until an authenticated recovery/rotation procedure; it cannot silently start fresh.

`TransparencyCrossLogReceipt` is the reference-free signed `{authority_id,authority_key_id,source_log_id,source_security_domain_id,source_policy_identity_and_digest,source_checkpoint_digest,source_log_size,source_root,target_log_id,target_policy_identity_and_digest,target_log_size,target_inclusion_commitment,target_inclusion_proof,target_checkpoint_digest,target_checkpoint_consistency_proof,receipt_time_authority_profile_oid,receipt_window:{not_before:AuthorityInstant,expires_at:AuthorityInstant},canonical_receipt_digest,signature}`. The target inclusion leaf is exactly the domain-separated source checkpoint digest plus source log/domain/policy/size/root; it provides causality without comparing clocks from different authorities.

`TransparencyCheckpoint` is `{format_version,mode:LocalRollbackDetection|WitnessedEquivocationDetection{witness_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>}|WitnessedNonEquivocation{witness_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>},log_size,global_mmr_root,branch_head_commitment_root,security_domain_commitment,previous_checkpoint_digest:WeakDigest,consistency_proof_from_previous,issuance_time_authority_profile_oid,issuance_window:{not_before:AuthorityInstant,expires_at:AuthorityInstant},operator_key_id,operator_signature,sorted_witness_signatures[{witness_id,key_id,signature}],cross_log_receipt_refs[StrongRef<TransparencyCrossLogReceipt>],rotation_proof:None|JointActivation{old_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>,new_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>,old_sorted_signatures[],new_sorted_signatures[]}}`. Every signature covers the domain-separated canonical checkpoint body excluding all signature arrays. A witnessed mode requires its policy identity, threshold of distinct configured keys, and any required cross-log receipts; freshness is never inferred from an unprofiled `issued_at` scalar.

Local `TransparencyCheckpointValidationRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<TransparencyCheckpoint>,checkpoint_freshness_basis_ref:StrongRef<TransparencyCheckpointFreshnessBasis>,checkpoint_time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,sorted_cross_log_validations[{receipt_ref:StrongRef<TransparencyCrossLogReceipt>,freshness_basis_ref:StrongRef<CrossLogTransparencyFreshness>,time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,target_checkpoint_verification_evidence_ref}],policy_threshold_and_consistency_verification_digest,validated_claim_class,body_digest}`. The two generated time-basis schemas from §16 bind the exact checkpoint/receipt bodies and their windows; they cannot be replaced by wall time, logical HLC, or a raw age calculation.

Canonical cross-log validation requires `1 <= cross_log_policy.threshold <= count(unique ordered authorities)`; at least that many receipts come from distinct configured authority/key pairs, and every accepted receipt's source policy/log/security domain/checkpoint digest/size/root equals the current checkpoint exactly. Its target inclusion proof and target checkpoint consistency proof must verify under the named target policy/log/size, the inclusion leaf must causally contain the exact source checkpoint digest, and both the source checkpoint and each receipt/target checkpoint must have independently usable profiled freshness evidence in their own time domains. No validator orders or subtracts instants across domains/epochs. Duplicates, foreign source roots, stale evidence, missing target-checkpoint verification, or self-asserted target sizes fail. `JointActivation` additionally requires: the old policy equals the currently active policy; `new.rotation == JointSuccessor{predecessor=old}`; old/new log and security-domain identities are equal; `new.policy_epoch > old.policy_epoch`; checkpoint mode names the new policy; `log_size >= new.activation_log_size`; and the checkpoint body has valid distinct-key thresholds under both old and new policies. Only after that exact activation checkpoint may successors use the new policy alone.

The branch commitment is domain-separated and reveals no plain branch identity/head; authorized clients receive scoped inclusion/consistency proofs under the metadata-declassification policy, and mutually hidden branch sets use distinct security-domain logs. `LocalRollbackDetection` proves only consistency relative to a client's cached head. `WitnessedEquivocationDetection` promises durable evidence once conflicting heads reach the declared gossip/cross-log path. Only `WitnessedNonEquivocation` with a valid intersection-safe policy, honest durable-head assumption, consistency proofs, joint rotation, and freshness may claim split-view prevention. If any premise fails, verification fails closed or downgrades the advertised claim to detection/local scope; later gossip is never relabeled as prevention. **DecisionPolicyEpoch** is `{policy_id,version,scope,logical_effect_class,pinned_table_oid,fallback_oid,evidence_refs[],previous_epoch_oid}`; statistical evidence may justify promotion but is never encoded as an invariant. It is not `SecurityPolicyEpoch`.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

title: Build registry-generated durable codecs, walkers, and golden corpora
description:
## What and scope

Implement the missing W1 owner repeatedly named as `w1-generated-parsers`: registry-generated, bounded canonical durable encoders and decoders; exact generated Rust tagged unions and reference wrappers; reachability, GC, checkpoint, backup, construction, compatibility, size-limit, and fuzz walkers; and the complete cross-version golden and mutation corpus for every frozen G0 identity, field, command, state, language, and format row. This is foundational format machinery, not the W10 import/export `fgdb-formats` surface and not W2 storage publication.

## Why

Gate G0 freezes every durable identity, field, tag, digest recipe, version law, and capability predicate before implementation. W1 must then make those registries executable without creating a second hand-maintained allowlist. The current graph and several descriptions refer to `w1-generated-parsers`, but no task owns it. Without an explicit owner, checker rows for generated encoder/decoder round trips and golden-corpus replay remain stubs, Appendix renderings can drift from Rust bytes, and later workstreams can invent local codecs. B1 requires one identity universe; B5 requires byte-replayable canonical semantics; both fail if registry rows and executable bytes are not in a total bijection.

## Normative design

The checked G0 registries and their checked-in schema annotations are the sole generator input. Generate exact Rust types and bounded canonical encoders/decoders for all five identity classes: content-addressed logical objects, physical records, bootstrap frames, restore-only prebootstrap artifacts, and inline wire types. Generate every `durable_fields.toml` field/tag, containing-schema-specific reference union, command/state arm, role/posture specialization, language-contract arm, and reserved-but-unavailable tag. No prose name, suffix, wildcard arm, generic `RegisteredStrongRef`, or manually duplicated list may grant encodability.

Generation emits deterministic checked-in artifacts and a regeneration manifest containing input registry hashes, generator version, output hashes, row counts, and ordered row-to-symbol mappings. CI regenerates into an isolated directory and byte-compares every output. Adding, retiring, or changing a row without the matching generated artifact and golden/mutation evidence fails. Reserved rows generate typed unavailable arms that can be decoded only under their registered compatibility rule and can never advertise a live capability.

Encoders use declared format major/minor, canonical little-endian fixed integers, canonical unsigned LEB128 only where registered, deterministic field order, checked arithmetic, length-before-allocation, per-kind resource bounds, and the pinned CanonicalScalarProfile. Decoders reject duplicate tags, noncanonical encodings, unknown required flags, retired or experimental production tags, illegal role/posture arms, cross-class references, missing required fields, trailing ambiguity, and resource claims before allocation. Additive-minor unknown fields are skipped only when the exact registered length-delimited compatibility rule permits it; breaking-major mismatches fail closed.

Generate exact reference and retention walkers from the field table, including strong, currently-followed conditional, weak identity, locator, archive/prior-incarnation, bootstrap-root, and W12 certified-remote semantics. Generate the concrete construction DAG for every command tag and activated state slot, not merely one family-level order. Generated checks reject self, mutual, future-result, role-invalid, missing/extra target, wrong-strength, and cross-consensus local-StrongRef edges.

Every digest field consumes one registered TargetDigest, TranscriptDigest, WeakIdentityDigest, or BodyDigest recipe. Encoder, decoder, field-table checker, golden-vector harness, and mutation corpus call the same generated include/exclude recipe. This task produces canonical plaintext and digest transcripts; W2 object identity supplies keyed ObjectId/CiphertextId/EncodingId/PlacementId cryptographic realization and publication, and must consume these generated bytes rather than re-encode them.

The generated code remains std-only except for the explicitly allowed foundation crates, uses Rust 2024 nightly, and has `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. It does not use serde, parser generators, proc-macro dependencies outside the closed universe, or host locale/tzdb.

## Invariants and interactions

Directly supports FG-INV-07 construction and registry closure, FG-INV-09 identity transcript recomputation, FG-INV-12 canonical value and representation equivalence, and FG-INV-19 replay artifact identity. A checker flips from stub to live only with its implementation and negative tests in the same change; no runtime capability activates merely because a codec exists.

Consumes the completed G0 epic, including the exhaustive Appendix A catalog, identity and durable-field registries, command/state contracts, language contracts, format arms, scalar/semantic profiles, and capability/activation rows. Produces the canonical format layer consumed by `fgdb-reference`, W2 Chronicle/ECS/bootstrap, every later durable subsystem, backup/restore, conformance, fuzzing, and replay. The W10 `fgdb-formats` task continues to own CSV/JSONL/Parquet-lite/Arrow/archive interchange projections, not these authoritative durable codecs.

## Acceptance criteria and tests

- A total two-way bijection proves every live or reserved registry row has exactly one generated type/field/arm/codec/walker entry and every generated entry resolves to exactly one row. Orphans, aliases, duplicate tags, wildcard arms, and hand-written extra variants fail.
- Regeneration from a clean checkout is byte-identical and emits a deterministic manifest with per-registry input hashes and per-output hashes.
- Cross-version golden vectors cover every identity class, top-level schema, inline type, union arm, field, command/state arm, reference wrapper, digest recipe, role/posture specialization, and unavailable reserved tag. Encode-decode-encode is byte-identical where accepted.
- Mutation/property suites remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, truncate, extend, corrupt, weaken, cross-role substitute, and cross-version substitute every normative field/arm/reference class and prove typed rejection. BodyDigest mutations name the exact recipe and mismatching byte offset.
- Fuzz targets cover every generated decoder and walker under adversarial lengths, varints, nesting, tags, and feature predicates; there are no panics, hangs, unchecked arithmetic paths, or allocations before validated limits.
- Construction and reachability tests compare generated DAG/walkers against the registry and Appendix rendering for every command tag and activated state slot.
- Locale, timezone, platform, target-endian, and iteration-order perturbations leave canonical bytes unchanged under the same pinned profiles.
- Checker-index rows `idr_generated_encoder_decoder_roundtrip` and `idr_golden_corpus_replay` become live only when the corresponding artifacts and negative tests land. The W2 identity checker remains stub until keyed cryptographic recomputation is implemented there.
- E2E script `scripts/w1_generated_formats_e2e.sh` regenerates into an isolated directory, byte-compares checked artifacts, compiles the generated types, replays every golden corpus, plants representative defects in temporary fixtures, and emits versioned JSONL. It exits on the first mismatch.
- Detailed JSONL includes event schema version, registry, row/schema/field/arm ID, format version, role/posture, input and output digest, resource bound, checker, outcome, mismatch offset, artifact references, deterministic seed, and replay command. Protected bytes and keys never enter logs.

## Risks and rejected alternatives

Rejected: hand-written codec inventories, serde-derived durable enums, generator output that is not reproducible, treating registry parse success as byte-level proof, delaying golden corpora until each engine subsystem, and making W10 interchange formats authoritative. Risk: the exhaustive G0 catalog is large; generation and corpus sharding must stay deterministic and independently replayable rather than weakening coverage.

## Provenance

Plan sections 5.1, 18.1, 19 W1; Appendix A canonical format rules; G0 epic identity/format clauses; the missing `w1-generated-parsers` references in the W1 epic and foundation-type interactions.
close_reason: Duplicate of fgdb-w1-generated-parsers-i3k; exhaustive corpus work is already owned by fgdb-w1-format-test-corpora-lyf. Additional audit requirements were preserved as comments on those canonical beads.

title: Epic G0: exact Appendix A durable-schema catalog and ownership closure
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the complete Appendix A durable-format contract as a set of exact, reviewable catalog slices and generate one closed schema-to-owner-to-checker matrix across them. The child tasks embed every source-plan byte from Appendix A and assign every schema, field, arm, reference, digest transcript, role restriction, state transition, and compatibility rule to its granular implementation bead. This epic is the constitutional format-closure proof; it does not replace subsystem implementation.

## Why
The audit found that architectural summaries were strong but exact type families could disappear between workstreams. Durable bytes are the public recovery/replay/compatibility contract, so “covered in spirit” is not enough. G0 must freeze even reserved W12 arms before Local implementation begins, while later workstreams retain phase-correct ownership.

## Design and ownership
The catalog is partitioned only for reviewability and CLI size. Concatenating its ordered slices exactly reconstructs Appendix A from the audited plan revision. Each slice generates rows in durable_fields.toml; the epic generates cross-slice reference DAG, state-transition, construction-order, authority-bearing, lifecycle-owner, compatibility, invariant/evidence/cost, verification, and gate-consumer matrices. Every row names one implementation owner and may name multiple consumers. Wildcards, “and similar,” unexpanded generic/role arms, bare StrongRef arrays, duplicate logical schema names, or aliases with different body hashes fail G0.

## Success Criteria
- Ordered child slices cover Appendix A continuously from its heading through the final transparency contract with no gap, overlap, truncation, or paraphrase.
- A checksum/line-range manifest proves exact reconstruction of the audited Appendix A text.
- Every exact named type/field/arm/state/transition/reference/digest/role constraint has a stable catalog row and exactly one implementation owner.
- Generated construction and reference DAGs are finite, role-correct, future-result-free, and closed across slices.
- Unit tests cover catalog parsing, stable IDs, generic/role expansion, ownership uniqueness, and exact reconstruction.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests reject missing/duplicate/reordered slices and fields, unknown arms, weakened references, cross-role substitutions, and digest drift.
- Simulation and E2E matrices map every durability/dispatch/recovery/authority boundary to task-specific scenarios and detailed redacted JSONL diagnostics with replay artifacts.
- Cross-version golden vectors and compatibility fixtures cover every durable schema; all downstream gates reject unowned or unchecked rows.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a single oversized CLI argument, summaries as normative bytes, and treating the catalog as one implementation task. The partition preserves exact content while keeping review and mutation reliable.

## Provenance
Complete normative Appendix A of the audited comprehensive plan.

    227  complete_slice_static_evidence_missing
    227  complete_slice_runtime_evidence_missing
    227  complete_slice_target_declared
      2  complete_slice_source_contract_unverified
      1  slice_census_pin_mismatch
THE HEADLINE: a01's visible residual is 6 items. Its actual last mile is ~1,138, i.e. roughly 190x the visible number, and 1,135 of those are PER-TARGET work over 227 targets. I had previously costed this layer at 4 rows per target; the measurement shows FIVE actions — the four metadata rows plus flipping each target off definition_status=declared, which complete_slice_target_declared enforces and which nobody has mentioned on any trail.
Good news buried in it: only 2 complete_slice_source_contract_unverified remain, so the union/arm source-checker gap that blocked a01 in July is essentially closed by 2C's coverage generalization. That was the historic blocker and it is no longer the binding one.

=== 3. STRUCTURAL BLOCKERS RANKED BY BREADTH — THE SEQUENCING ANSWER ===

  iz2x  (annotation/semantic-binding/evidence layer)  blocks 21 of 21 slices.  MEASURED: annotations 0,
        semantic_bindings 0, evidence 0, expansion_bindings 0 catalog-wide. No slice can reach complete
        without it, unconditionally. It is the universal gate.
  u3gr  (self-referencing retaining wrappers)         blocks  7 of 21 slices, 10 members.  MEASURED with
        both known errata as passing controls: a03 LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration; a06 MetaPreparedCommandRecord,
        ShardPreparedPayloadRecord; a08 MetaConstraintReservationRecord, ShardPrepareRecord,
        TopologyTransitionRecord; a10 PreparedCommitRecord; a13 KeyEnvelopeNode;
        a16 TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>; a21 WitnessPolicy. a04 screened CLEAN.
  ovok  (indexed-map union spelling)                  NOT MEASURED — see section 4.
  owlp  (latent order violations)                     NOT MEASURABLE until field bodies land, by its own
        definition. It is a future-detection gap, not a present blocker.

SEQUENCING CONCLUSION, and it is not the obvious one. iz2x has by far the widest reach, but it CANNOT simply be done first: an annotation binds to a target_row_id, so every target minted later needs its own four rows anyway. Doing iz2x before a slice's coverage is complete means editing the same rows twice. The critical path is therefore per-slice: coverage -> then iz2x for that slice -> then complete. What iz2x genuinely blocks TODAY is only a01 and a02, because they are the only slices whose coverage is near done. So the highest-value sequencing is: freeze the iz2x row schemas and pin mechanics ONCE now (cheap, one reviewed increment, no rows), then let it be applied per-slice as each slice's coverage closes. Freezing it late, after ~2,000 rows exist across slices, is a mass migration. Freezing it now costs one increment.
u3gr is second: 7 slices, and unlike iz2x it is a SOURCE erratum — the plan spells something unlandable — so it needs a spec decision, not catalog work, and it will silently block those 7 slices at their last mile regardless of how much coverage they accumulate first.

=== 4. WHAT I AM EXPLICITLY NOT IN A POSITION TO JUDGE ===
 - ovok's breadth. I did not measure it. I know the shape (indexed-map union spelling leaving an unsatisfiable order) but not which slices carry it, and I will not guess a number into an epic assessment.
 - Whether the plan can be errata'd at all for u3gr's 10 members. That is a spec-owner decision about the normative source; I can only say the two laws are jointly unsatisfiable as spelled.
 - Whether the iz2x annotation layer is genuinely GENERATABLE. I proposed generating annotations from the census (source_annotation_contract_mismatch already forces them to byte-match census exact_type/cardinality, which strongly suggests derivability) but I have NOT proven it by building a generator. Semantic bindings and evidence are definitely not derivable — they name owner bead, crate, checker, test/scenario/event IDs.
 - Any runtime or implementation readiness. G0 is the format freeze; W1-W12 execution is entirely outside what I measured. Nothing here says whether the database works.
 - Calendar or effort estimates. I have no throughput data I trust. I can say a01 is ~1,138 checker-enumerated items from complete; I cannot say how long that takes, and the per-item cost is very uneven (a generated annotation is not comparable to a hand-authored evidence row).
 - The 8 zero-target slices. I measured their census sizes but have not read their source, so I cannot say whether they are large-but-mechanical or genuinely hard.

=== BOTTOM LINE ===
Gate G0 is roughly 5% through its census coverage with zero slices complete, and the last mile per slice is ~190x its visible residual because the annotation/evidence layer has never been started anywhere. The two things worth doing before more slices accumulate rows are (a) freeze the iz2x row schemas and pin mechanics in one reviewed increment, and (b) get a spec decision on u3gr's 10 members, because both get monotonically more expensive with every target that lands.

STRUCTURAL FINDING, EPIC-LEVEL: THE COMPLETION LAW IS CURRENTLY UNSATISFIABLE FOR ANY SHORTHAND MEMBER THE PLAN DOES NOT TYPE INLINE. This is not a01-local and no amount of ruling or adjudicating can clear it. Found while designing a disambiguation rule for a01's 74 non-exact sources; the rule turned out to be the wrong deliverable.

=== THE MECHANISM, verbatim (appendix_a.rs:7418) ===
    let source_is_exact = ambiguity_is_discharged
        && !field.type_conflict
        && matches!(field.exact_types.as_slice(), [_])
        && matches!(field.cardinalities.as_slice(), [_]);
    if !source_is_exact {
        if target.definition_status == "complete" {
            out.push(... "source_annotation_contract_ambiguous" ...)
        }
        continue;
    }
matches!(x, [_]) requires EXACTLY ONE element. Measured over a01: all 74 non-exact field targets have signature (0 exact_types, 1 cardinality) - zero types, not competing types. So the third conjunct is false and source_is_exact is false. The first conjunct, ambiguity_is_discharged, IS satisfiable by a maps-to-source adjudication - and a01 has already landed exactly such adjudications for five of these members in 2H - but discharging the ambiguity does not SUPPLY a type. An adjudication clears field.ambiguous; it cannot make exact_types non-empty.

CONSEQUENCE: a field target whose plan text gives no inline type can never be part of a complete slice. The plan will not grow inline types by itself, so this is permanent until something changes in (a), (b) or (c) below.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT a01-LOCAL ===
These are shorthand members - the "shorthand field has no exact type" census class. a01 has 74 of them among its field TARGETS alone, and a01 is the most-covered slice in the catalog. Every slice that lands field targets over prose-rendered schemas will accumulate them. My earlier reality check said the completion layer was the universal blocker; this is a second universal blocker sitting behind it, and unlike the annotation layer it cannot be discharged by doing more work at the slice level.

=== IT IS THE u3gr PATTERN AT COMPLETION SCOPE ===
u3gr is two laws jointly unsatisfiable for one member shape (reference_semantics forced strong by the source wrapper, dag_self_edge forbidding it). This is the same shape one level up: the annotation contract demands a census exact_type, the census cannot produce one for a shorthand member, and the adjudication mechanism that exists to resolve exactly this class does not feed the predicate that consumes it. Both are "the catalog is internally consistent and the goal state is unreachable".

=== THE THREE POSSIBLE RESOLUTIONS, and my read ===
 (a) PLAN ERRATUM adding inline types for every shorthand member. Correct in principle, enormous in practice (74 in a01 alone, likely many hundreds catalog-wide), and it puts normative-source edits on the critical path for a format freeze. I do not recommend it.
 (b) LET AN ADJUDICATION SUPPLY THE TYPE. The natural fix and the smallest: extend the maps-to-source adjudication row (or add a sibling row kind) to carry the ruled exact_type, and have source_is_exact accept an adjudicated type where the census has none. This preserves every guarantee that matters - the type is still recorded, reviewed, pinned and byte-matched against the annotation - while making the goal state reachable. It also retroactively validates the 2G/2H pattern, where a01 already ruled five such members from landed precedent and pinned the rulings.
 (c) WEAKEN THE COMPLETION LAW to accept a zero-type census source. Worst option: it drops the byte-match that currently prevents an annotation from silently disagreeing with the source.
My recommendation is (b), and it is checker/scaffold work, not slice work. It should be decided before any slice invests in the annotation layer, because (b) changes what an annotation row must contain.

=== WHAT I MEASURED ALONG THE WAY, still useful under (b) ===
Of a01's 74 untyped members, 47 are DETERMINED by unanimous catalog-wide name-family precedent and 27 are not; zero have no precedent at all. The derived rule, where precedent is unanimous:
  *_bytes -> bytes    *_commitment -> digest256   *_coverage -> bytes    *_domain -> ConsensusDomain
  *_domains -> bytes  *_epoch -> u64              *_floor -> u64         *_index -> u64
  *_key -> id256      *_nonce -> bytes            *_oid -> oid256        *_proof -> bytes
  *_set -> bytes      *_signatures -> bytes       *_threshold -> u16     *_zeroes -> bytes
The 27-item residue is dominated by three split families, each with a KNOWN discriminator rather than genuine doubt: *_digest splits 32 digest256 vs 3 WeakDigest (discriminator: WeakDigest iff the member points at a concrete target schema, digest256 otherwise - the ruling a01 already made in 2G); *_identity splits 11 RemoteObjectIdentity vs 3 (RemoteObjectIdentity where the source spells it); *_id splits across id256/digest256/bytes (grant_id already ruled digest256 in 2B as an H() output). So under (b) the 74 would be roughly 47 mechanical + 27 precedent-guided, not 74 hand decisions. That is the rule the operator asked for - it exists and it is cheap - but it cannot be applied until (b) makes an adjudicated type mean anything to the checker.

=== WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING ===
I have not measured how many shorthand members exist in the other 20 slices, only that a01 has 74 among its targets and that nothing about the mechanism is a01-specific. I have also not verified that (b) is implementable without disturbing the existing adjudication pin mechanics; that is for whoever owns the checker.

SWEEP FOR UNSATISFIABLE COMPLETION LAWS — result: ONE NEW INSTANCE, making FOUR in the class. Read-only against HEAD. No remedy proposed as authorized.

METHOD: enumerated every law gated on definition_status == "complete" (12 codes), characterized the input signature each demands, then measured whether any real population can present it. Where possible I measured EMPIRICALLY by flipping a slice to complete in a scratch copy and reading what the checker emits, rather than reasoning from the source alone.

=== NEW INSTANCE #4: A SLICE OWNING A projection| FALLBACK TARGET CAN NEVER COMPLETE ===

MECHANISM, appendix_a.rs:11109 and :11126, both inside the same `for row in closure_targets` loop over EVERY target of a complete slice:
    if row.definition_status != "complete" {
        out.push("complete_slice_target_declared", ... "complete slice contains a target that is still declared")
    }
    let source_contract_supported = row.source_key.starts_with("top|")
        || row.source_key.starts_with("field|")
        || (row.target_kind == "union" && row.source_key.starts_with("union|"))
        || (row.target_kind == "union-arm" && row.source_key.starts_with("arm|"))
        || ordinary_union_wire_source_supported;
    if !source_contract_supported {
        out.push("complete_slice_source_contract_unverified", ...
            "...reference-only and projection fallback targets remain declared")
    }
A source_key of the form projection|... matches none of the five accepted prefixes. Critically the second check is NOT gated on the target's own status, so:
  - leave the target declared -> complete_slice_target_declared fires
  - flip the target to complete -> complete_slice_source_contract_unverified STILL fires
Either way the slice cannot be complete. The law's own message says such targets "remain declared", which is precisely the state the sibling law forbids inside a complete slice. This is the u3gr shape - two laws jointly unsatisfiable - lifted to slice-completion scope.

MEASURED POPULATION: 98 targets across 12 slices (551 targets total; source_key forms are top 134, field 210, projection 84, arm 91, union 32).
    g0 35   a04 16   a10 12   a15 9   a06 6   a02 3   a03 3   a19 3   a17 4   a20 4   a01 2   a07 1
EMPIRICAL CONTROL, two independent slices, both exact: flipping a01 to complete emits exactly 2 complete_slice_source_contract_unverified against a predicted 2; flipping a04 emits exactly 16 against a predicted 16. So the ordinary_union_wire_source_supported escape rescues ZERO of them, and the static count is trustworthy.

CAN AN ADJUDICATION OR RULING CLEAR IT? PROVABLY NOT, and this is worse than the zero-exact-type case. That one at least consults adjudications (ambiguity_is_discharged is a real conjunct, it simply cannot supply a missing type). Here the test is a pure structural match on the source_key PREFIX with no adjudication, ruling, or override consulted anywhere in the expression. The only way to satisfy it is for the target to stop being a projection| fallback, i.e. to acquire a real source construct - and the fallback exists precisely because the projection row has none. Note also that the e2e's phase 3e asserts every checked-in projection requires one target, so the fallback target cannot simply be deleted while its projection row exists.

=== LAWS SWEPT AND FOUND SATISFIABLE (they demand work, not impossibilities) ===
  complete_slice_target_missing (11057)          needs >=1 target. trivial.
  complete_top_level (11087)                     census pin over top-level keys; satisfiable by targeting or
                                                 not-a-durable-schema adjudication.
  complete_ambiguity_adjudication (11100)        census pin; satisfiable by adjudicating all slice ambiguities.
  complete_slice_annotation_missing (11137)      needs one annotation per target. work, not impossible.
  complete_slice_semantic_binding_missing (11150) same shape.
  complete_slice_static_evidence_missing (11161)  same shape.
  complete_slice_runtime_evidence_missing (11172) same shape.
  source_complete_census_uncovered (7182)        every census key targeted, adjudicated, or arm/wire-covered.
                                                 a01 is at 4 uncovered, so demonstrably approachable.
  source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved (7311) one approved final adjudication per raw ambiguity, no extras.
                                                 a01 is at 2 outstanding, so approachable.
  ordinary arm / union annotation contracts (6947, 6972) demand annotation fields equal to source tokens; satisfiable.

=== LIMITATION OF THIS SWEEP, stated plainly ===
My empirical flip test only exercises LOAD-TIME laws. When a slice is flipped to complete the catalog fails to load, so verify_source never runs and the two source-pass laws (7182, 7311) were characterized by reading the source only, not by measurement. I judge them satisfiable from their predicates and from a01's approach to zero, but I have not proven it the way I proved the projection| case. Also, I swept COMPLETION laws as instructed; laws guarding individual member landing were not swept, so the class may extend further down.

  fgdb-dbvf  reserved kind under an active identity law   1 row (PlacementRecord), self-resolving once a02 registers members

The new one is the smallest population but the hardest shape: it is the only one of the four with no mechanism, even in principle, by which a ruling could clear it.

IS INSTANCE #4 A CHECKER GAP OR A REAL CONTRADICTION? ANSWER: BOTH, IN MEASURED PROPORTIONS — and the 98 is three different problems wearing one violation code. Your instinct that "projection is absent from the accepted list, not rejected by a rule" is correct for part of it and wrong for the majority.

=== THE 98 DECOMPOSES THREE WAYS ===

  (A) 14 targets — DEFINITE CHECKER GAP, no owner decision needed.
      source_key is a REAL census arm key but target_kind is "wire-type", e.g.
        arm|KeyDestroyExternalAckRef|KeyDestroyExternalAckRef|Backup      (a15, x8)
        arm|NewDatabaseIdentityTargetCreationCommitment|...|Dir            (a19, x2)
        arm|ServicePromotionExternalOperationKind|...|CatalogActivate      (a20, x4)
      The law accepts arm| ONLY when target_kind == "union-arm":
          || (row.target_kind == "union-arm" && row.source_key.starts_with("arm|"))
      These are the per-arm WIRE VARIANT rows — the a15 KeyDestructionTarget pattern the a01 2C trail
      documented as an approved shape. The source contract exists and is a plain census arm key; the
      vocabulary simply does not admit the (arm| source, wire-type target) pairing. This is exactly the
      unimplemented case you described, and we can fix it ourselves.

  (B) 25 of the 84 projection| targets — PROBABLE CHECKER GAP, needs per-case confirmation.
      16 have BOTH owner and member present in Appendix A text; 9 have the owner present but not the
      member. So there is plan text to reconcile against; whether it is reconcilable in the census's
      terms I have not established per row.

  (C) 59 of the 84 — GENUINELY SOURCELESS, and NOT a plan erratum either.
      The symbol does not occur anywhere in Appendix A. The dominant sub-class is REGISTRY-INVENTED
      ROLE SPECIALIZATIONS: RaftSnapshotLocal / RaftSnapshotMeta / RaftSnapshotShard,
      RootManifestMeta / RootManifestShard, CheckpointStateVectorMeta / CheckpointStateVectorShard.
      The plan spells a SINGLE role-tagged construct; the registry created one kind per role. The a04
      pre-work brief flagged this same divergence independently ("logical_object_kinds has RootManifest
      0x0007 active + RootManifestMeta/Shard 0x0104/0x0105 ... while a04 reserves single role-tagged
      RaftSnapshot"). Others are registrar-named constructs: SegmentTrailer, whose name cc_1 explicitly
      recorded as a naming ruling because "the source supplies NO name".
      For these, projection| is the HONEST source key — it correctly says "this row has no source". The
      law then correctly refuses to call such a target source-reconciled. Nothing is contradictory; the
      registry contains rows the plan does not.

=== SO WHAT IS THE ACTUAL DECISION? ===
Not "erratum vs checker fix". It is: MAY A SLICE CONTAIN REGISTRY-INVENTED ROWS AND STILL BE COMPLETE?
If yes, the completion law needs a sanctioned category for source-free registry rows. If no, those rows
must move somewhere that is not a completing slice — note g0 already holds 35 of the 98, the largest
single holding, so segregating registry-infrastructure rows into a non-completing owner is a shape the
catalog already partly uses. That is a registry-modeling question for the owner, and it is a different
question from u3gr.

=== DO THE FOUR SHARE ONE ROOT CAUSE? NO — THEY ARE THREE DIFFERENT MISMATCHES ===
All four are "the law set assumes something about the source that is not true", but the DIRECTION differs,
and the direction determines the fix and the owner:
  u3gr              the SOURCE CONTAINS a construct no legal row shape can express     -> source erratum, owner
  zero-exact-type   the SOURCE OMITS information a law requires (types)                -> owner: erratum vs relax the test
  #4 part (C)       the REGISTRY CONTAINS rows the source does not                     -> registry-modeling, owner
  #4 parts (A)+(B)  the VOCABULARY omits a form both source and registry already use   -> checker fix, ours
  dbvf              a missing lifecycle law, plus a transient that self-resolves        -> checker fix, ours
So the owner is deciding about THREE things, not four and not one: (1) u3gr, (2) the zero-exact-type test,
(3) whether registry-invented rows may live in a completing slice. Items (A), (B) and dbvf are ours to fix
without escalation — that removes 14 targets definitely and up to 25 more probably, i.e. up to 39 of the 98,
and it unblocks nothing on its own because most affected slices hold rows in category (C) as well.

=== METHOD NOTE, because it nearly produced a wrong headline ===
My first run of this measurement reported 68 of 84 absent from the plan. That was FALSE. I had written
r'\\b' inside a raw string, so the regex matched a literal backslash followed by 'b' and never matched
anything. The positive control caught it instantly: ConfigurationState and RootSlot both reported "absent"
when both are demonstrably in Appendix A. Corrected escaping gives 16 / 9 / 59 with the control reading
in / in / out as expected. Ninth instance today of "the tool reported OK because it was never asked the
right question" — and the first where the broken tool was the measurement I was about to escalate.

--- 1. THE FOUR INSTANCES, MECHANISM AND POPULATION ---

[I] fgdb-u3gr — SELF-REFERENCING RETAINING WRAPPER
  Mechanism: two laws jointly unsatisfiable. catalog_annotation_reference_semantics_mismatch forces
  reference_semantics from the source's concrete wrapper (probed: for a StrongRef<X> source, "strong" is
  the ONLY accepted value; weak_digest, none, conditional and identity all fire), while dag_self_edge
  rejects strong, conditional and weak_digest alike when the target resolves to the owner. Strong is
  forced by the first and forbidden by the second; every alternative is rejected before reaching the DAG.
  Order-independent: the self-edge check returns before construction_order is compared.
  Population: 10 members across 7 of 21 slices — a03 LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration; a06
  MetaPreparedCommandRecord, ShardPreparedPayloadRecord; a08 MetaConstraintReservationRecord,
  ShardPrepareRecord, TopologyTransitionRecord; a10 PreparedCommitRecord; a13 KeyEnvelopeNode;
  a16 TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>; a21 WitnessPolicy. a04 screened CLEAN.
  Can a ruling clear it? NO. There is no landable row shape in any spelling.

[II] fgdb-dbvf — RESERVED KIND UNDER AN ACTIVE IDENTITY LAW
  Mechanism: PlacementRecord (physical 0x0003, status=active) has identity law
  placement_id = BLAKE3("fgdb:placement:v1" || canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId)) while that wire
  type is status=reserved, i.e. its layout is not frozen. An active identity law over a mutable layout
  means placement_id can differ for identical placements.
  Population: exactly 1. Measured exhaustively: only two physical kinds carry a canonical(X) transcript —
  EncodingRecord -> EncodingDescriptorWithoutId (wire:active, clean) and PlacementRecord (the violation).

  nobody can currently clear. PhysicalKind.transcript is an opaque String (identity.rs:103), never
  decomposed, which is why no law exists.

[III] ZERO-EXACT-TYPE COMPLETION BLOCKER — the largest
  Mechanism, appendix_a.rs:7418:
      let source_is_exact = ambiguity_is_discharged && !field.type_conflict

  absence, not competing candidates. Adjudication IS consulted (ambiguity_is_discharged is a real
  conjunct, and a01 has landed such adjudications) but it clears field.ambiguous; it cannot supply a type.
