  (63.7% of 11,683), 3,767 distinct member names, 21 of 21 slices. All 74 are in a01 only because a01
  holds 169 of the 210 field targets in the whole catalog; other slices read 0 for lack of coverage, not
  for health. 7,442 is the number to cost against.
  Is the plan deficient or is the loader failing to extract? PLAN, established both ways. a02:1449 reads
  "CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest is { logical_oid, object_kind, canonical_plaintext_len, ... }" — bare
  names, no types. CONTROL in the other direction: the plan DOES spell member:Type elsewhere
  (a01 RootBootstrap: root_placement_epoch:u64, segment_id:[u8;16]) and the loader DOES extract those —

  members across the appendix gives 3,064 typed vs 6,906 bare = 69%, close to the census-derived 63.7%.

  Can a ruling clear it? NOT AS WRITTEN.

[IV] projection| FALLBACK TARGET IN A COMPLETE SLICE
  Mechanism: two laws in the SAME loop over every target of a complete slice.
      :11109  if row.definition_status != "complete" { out.push("complete_slice_target_declared", ...) }
      :11126  source_contract_supported = top| || field| || (union && union|) || (union-arm && arm|)
              || ordinary_union_wire_source_supported;
              if !supported { out.push("complete_slice_source_contract_unverified", ...) }
  The second is NOT gated on the target's own status. Leave the target declared and the first fires; flip
  it to complete and the second still fires. The law's own message says such targets "remain declared" —
  precisely the state its sibling forbids inside a complete slice.
  Population: 98 targets across 12 slices (g0 35, a04 16, a10 12, a15 9, a06 6, a17 4, a20 4, a02 3,
  a03 3, a19 3, a01 2, a07 1). EMPIRICALLY CONTROLLED on two independent slices by flipping each to
  complete in a scratch copy: a01 predicted 2 / measured 2; a04 predicted 16 / measured 16. The
  ordinary_union_wire escape rescues zero.

--- 2. THE THREE CATEGORIES, AND WHO OWNS EACH ---

Instance [IV] is not one problem. It decomposes:

  (A) 14 targets — CHECKER MERELY INCOMPLETE. OURS.
      source_key is a REAL census arm key but target_kind is "wire-type": arm|KeyDestroyExternalAckRef|...
      (a15 x8), arm|NewDatabaseIdentityTargetCreationCommitment|... (a19 x2),
      arm|ServicePromotionExternalOperationKind|... (a20 x4). The law admits arm| only when
      target_kind == "union-arm". These are the per-arm WIRE VARIANT rows, an approved shape (the a15
      KeyDestructionTarget pattern). Source exists; the vocabulary omits a pairing both source and
      registry already use.
  (B) 25 of the 84 projection| targets — PROBABLE CHECKER GAP, unconfirmed per row.
      16 have both owner and member present in Appendix A text; 9 have the owner but not the member.
  (C) 59 of the 84 — NEITHER a checker gap NOR a plan erratum. A REGISTRY-MODELING QUESTION.
      The symbol does not occur in Appendix A at all. Dominant sub-class is REGISTRY-INVENTED ROLE
      SPECIALIZATIONS: RaftSnapshotLocal/Meta/Shard, RootManifestMeta/Shard,
      CheckpointStateVectorMeta/Shard — the plan spells ONE role-tagged construct and the registry created
      one kind per role (a04's pre-work brief flagged the same divergence independently). Others are
      registrar-named: SegmentTrailer, whose name cc_1 recorded as a naming ruling because the source
      supplies none. For these, projection| is the HONEST source key and the law correctly refuses to call
      them source-reconciled. Nothing is contradictory: the registry contains rows the plan does not.

--- 3. WHAT UNBLOCKS WHAT (the part that changes sequencing) ---

  * Fixing (A) + (B) removes up to 39 of the 98 and UNBLOCKS ZERO SLICES, because every affected slice
    also holds category (C) rows. It is worth doing for correctness; it is not a schedule win.
  * [II] dbvf blocks nothing today and self-resolves on a02's next increment.
  * [I] u3gr blocks 7 slices at their LAST MILE regardless of how much coverage they accumulate first,
    so it gets monotonically more expensive to discover late but not more expensive to fix.
  * [III] blocks ALL 21 slices and is the only instance whose cost grows with every target that lands.
  * [IV](C) blocks 12 slices and is likewise unaffected by more coverage work.
  * NO SLICE CAN COMPLETE until [III] is resolved. a01, the closest slice at 6 residual coverage items,
    still emits 1,138 violations when flipped to complete — 227 targets x 5 required actions (annotation,
    semantic binding, static evidence, runtime evidence, and flipping the target off "declared"), plus 2
    source-contract and 1 census pin. The visible residual understates the last mile by ~190x.

--- 4. PROVABLY THE OWNER'S CALL vs PROVABLY OURS ---

  OWNER — the plan is genuinely deficient or the model diverges from it:
    [I]   u3gr: the source spells a construct no legal row shape can express. Erratum or law change.
    [III] the source OMITS types a law requires, at 7,442 occurrences / 3,767 names. Options are a plan
          erratum (paid per occurrence, and it puts normative-source edits on a format freeze's critical
          path while re-hashing slice pins that 21 beads are pinned against), or changing what counts as
          exact (paid once; whether it disturbs existing adjudication pin mechanics is UNVERIFIED — I have
          not prototyped it), or weakening the byte-match (loses the only check stopping an annotation
          disagreeing with its source).
    [IV](C) may a slice contain REGISTRY-INVENTED rows and still be complete? If yes the completion law
          needs a sanctioned category for source-free registry rows; if no, those rows must move to a
          non-completing owner — note g0 already holds 35 of the 98, so that shape is partly in use.
  OURS — the checker is merely incomplete, no escalation needed:
    [IV](A) admit the (arm| source, wire-type target) pairing. 14 targets.
    [IV](B) confirm and admit per row. Up to 25.
    [II]   add the missing lifecycle law once a02 unblocks it, and give PhysicalKind.transcript enough
           structure to name its referents (canonical\(([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\) suffices; not a general parser).

--- 5. DO THE FOUR SHARE ONE ROOT CAUSE? NO — THREE DIRECTIONS OF MISMATCH ---
  [I]      the SOURCE CONTAINS something unrepresentable
  [III]    the SOURCE OMITS something a law requires
  [IV](C)  the REGISTRY CONTAINS what the source lacks
  [IV](A)(B), [II]  the VOCABULARY/LAW SET omits a form both already use
  So the owner is deciding THREE things, not four and not one: u3gr, the exactness test, and whether
  registry-invented rows may live in a completing slice.

--- 6. WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH ---
  * ovok's breadth: not measured. I know the shape, not which slices carry it, and will not guess.
  * Member-landing laws were not swept; I swept COMPLETION laws only, so the class may extend downward.
  * The two source-pass completion laws (source_complete_census_uncovered :7182,
    source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved :7311) were read, not measured: flipping a slice to
    complete makes the catalog fail to LOAD, so verify_source never runs. I judge them satisfiable from
    their predicates and from a01's approach to zero, but I did not prove it the way I proved [IV].
  * Whether the (III) remedy is implementable without disturbing adjudication pin mechanics.
  * 7,442 is an UPPER BOUND: a field that ends up arm- or wire-covered rather than targeted never reaches
    the law. 74 is the exact figure for today.

title: Scaffold the canonical Appendix A annotation catalog and generated identity projections
description:
## What & scope
Land the shared G0 catalog infrastructure that every Appendix A slice A01-A21 requires before substantive rows can be added. The canonical machine-readable source is one checked-in `registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml` containing the complete 21-slice manifest plus 21 explicit logical slice sections and the structured schema annotations needed to regenerate all identity projections. The existing logical/physical/bootstrap/prebootstrap/wire/durable-field TOMLs remain checked-in normative projections for consumers, never independently hand-authored authorities.

## Why
The Appendix epic partitions one exact contract into 21 reviewable slices, but all slices need the same stable row-ID grammar, source pins, type-ID census, generator, owner/reference closure, and projection-diff check. Making each slice invent that substrate duplicates authority and creates conflicts; making identity own it recreates the dependency cycle because identity depends on the completed Appendix epic.

## Design
`appendix_a_catalog.toml` contains one source manifest (plan path, Appendix range/hash, exact ordered A01-A21 ranges/counts/hashes/adjacency) and structured annotations grouped into 21 logical slice sections. Annotations cover schema/field/arm IDs, class/tags, exact types/cardinality/layout, role/posture/authority/locality, reference/cut/construction semantics, generic and role expansions, digest recipes, ownership/consumers, compatibility, checker/scenario/gate bindings, and declared/complete state. One shared generator/checker in the existing registry-check surface emits and byte-diffs `logical_object_kinds.toml`, `physical_record_kinds.toml`, `bootstrap_frames.toml`, `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml`, `wire_types.toml`, and `durable_fields.toml`. `durable_fields.toml` remains the sole downstream input to generated reachability/GC/checkpoint/backup/DAG/compatibility/size/fuzz walkers; they never reinterpret the source catalog. Use std-only SHA-256 with standard vectors for source pins; retain FNV only for noncryptographic assignment fingerprints. No per-slice checker modules, binaries, tests, or E2E scripts.

## Acceptance criteria
- Strict schema/version/unknown-key validation for the catalog, manifest, slice, annotation, binding, and status rows.
- Exact raw-UTF8-LF SHA-256 proof of Appendix A lines 1384-2654 and all 21 contiguous ordered slices; missing, duplicate, reordered, overlapping, gapped, truncated, off-by-one, wrong-hash, or wrong-Bead mutations fail.
- One stable row-ID grammar and full top-level type/code reservation census allow declared cross-slice references without wildcards; complete slices require all concrete fields/arms/rules.
- Deterministic generation and byte-diff of all six checked-in projections; repeated generation is byte-identical and reports first file/line/byte divergence.
- Cross-slice exact-owner, owner-Bead/crate, reference, role/generic expansion, construction-DAG, compatibility, checker/scenario/gate, and planned/live evidence closure; no residual `<T>`, `<Role>`, generic StrongRef, fallback owner, or unresolved arm.
- Existing identity tests and G0 identity E2E cover source reconstruction, generation diff, ownership, cross-slice closure, mutation corpus, deterministic redacted JSONL, and SHA-256 vectors; scripts/check.sh runs the gate.
- This scaffold proves static catalog infrastructure only. Runtime codecs, goldens, simulation, recovery, public protocols, and later W12 behavior remain mandatory under their named downstream owners and do not block G0 definition.

## Provenance
Plan §5.1 annotation/generation law; complete normative Appendix A; Bead fgdb-appendix-a-catalog-91ol.

title: Freeze the thesis, foundation/SOTA rationale, rejections, and bibliography decision record
description:
## What & scope
Preserve the complete thesis, constitutional constraints, foundation audit, state-of-the-art distillation, deliberate rejections, calibration/control rationale, and reviewed bibliography as the project's self-contained architectural decision record. The exact source text is embedded below; generated decision-to-owner links connect every adopted lesson, rejected shortcut, dependency boundary, residual risk, and research anchor to the implementation and evidence bead that realizes it.

## Why
Implementation beads naturally emphasize what to build and can lose why a choice exists. The user explicitly requires future-self background, reasoning, justification, and over-arching intent without reopening the source plan. This record prevents later “simplification” from reintroducing rejected architectures and distinguishes reused foundation capability from graph-specific work we must build.

## Exact thesis, constraints, foundation, and SOTA record

# COMPREHENSIVE PLAN FOR THE DESIGN OF FRANKENGRAPHDB

*A blank-slate, memory-safe, ultra-high-performance graph database in Rust, built entirely on the Franken/asupersync ecosystem, designed to leapfrog every commercial and open-source graph system in existence.*

---

## 0. The Thesis: What "Leapfrog" Actually Means Here

Every graph database on the market today is a compromise fossilized around a decision made years ago:

- **Neo4j** fossilized around pointer-chasing "index-free adjacency" on the JVM: superb ergonomics, mediocre analytics, painful memory behavior, and a query runtime that took 15 years to get vectorized.
- **TigerGraph** fossilized around MPP analytics with a proprietary language and an operational footprint that makes it a platform decision, not a library.
- **Kùzu** got the query processing story *right* (columnar CSR + vectorization + factorization + worst-case-optimal joins) and then left the commons: Kùzu Inc. was acquired by Apple (acquisition agreed October 2025, disclosed February 2026 via Apple's EU DMA filing), the upstream repository was archived read-only on 2025-10-10, and community forks (LadybugDB, Kineviz's bighorn, ryugraph, Vela) continue the architecture while inheriting its gaps. Upstream Kùzu's execution surface was incomplete — single-writer (the one gap the Vela fork explicitly targets with multi-writer agent memory), no replication story, no temporal story, no deterministic testing story.
- **Memgraph / FalkorDB** are fast in-memory engines with thin durability and no principled answer to larger-than-memory, history, or verification.
- **JanusGraph / NebulaGraph** fossilized around generic KV underlays (Cassandra/RocksDB) and pay a permanent impedance-mismatch tax on every traversal.
- The **academic frontier** (Sortledton, Teseo, LiveGraph, GTX, Spruce, RadixGraph; factorized WCOJ processing; DBSP; AeonG) has solved, *in isolation*, essentially every hard subproblem — transactional adjacency at near-CSR speed, unified join processing, automatic incrementalization, cheap temporal storage — and **no shipping system has ever composed them.**

FrankenGraphDB's leapfrog is not one trick. It is the *composition* of six bets, each individually at or beyond the current frontier, made feasible only because the foundation libraries already exist:

| # | Bet | One-line statement | Why nobody else can do it |
|---|-----|--------------------|---------------------------|
| **B1** | **One Version Universe** | MVCC publication, retained time-travel history, replication order, change subscriptions, and git-style database branches share one append-only, content-addressed, RaptorQ-protected commit mechanism, while their retention and proof products remain explicitly distinct. | Requires ECS-style durability substrate (frankensqlite) + fountain codes (asupersync) designed in from byte zero. |
| **B2** | **Graph-Structured LSM ("Strata")** | Adjacency lives in three temperature tiers—versioned delta blocks → sealed compressed CSR runs → archived checkpoints—so one store can target high transactional ingest and static-CSR-class scans; actual rates remain §17 benchmark gates. | Existing systems choose different write/scan/space points; Strata makes the representation choice per stable adjacency descriptor without changing semantics. |
| **B3** | **Unified Factorized/WCO Execution ("Loom")** | One Free-Join-style physical family covers binary and multiway join strategies plus factorized intermediates, using only the trie orders that Strata/Beacon actually expose and building spillable COLTs for missing orders. | Kùzu and Free Join validate important pieces; the integration over mutable, authorized, larger-than-memory graph storage remains the engineering bet. |
| **B4** | **Incremental Everything ("Ripple")** | One checked Z-set delta algebra powers the registered recursive-query subset, materialized views, standing queries/subscriptions, and eligible incremental analytics; final committed effects produce the canonical ordered delta batches. | Requires B1's final-effect stream and a typed operator inventory whose derivatives, deletion laws, recursion bounds, and fallbacks are explicit. |
| **B5** | **Determinism, Evidence, and Calibrated Adaptivity** | CGSE tie-break policies, complexity witnesses, and evidence-closed manifests make every eligible **STRICT** result reproducible and auditable while its full closure is retained. Every adaptive decision emits a replayable **decision card** under a versioned policy epoch. The **Sextant** calibration plane evaluates policies against pinned deterministic fallbacks, but statistical evidence is never mislabeled as a safety proof. The whole database runs under asupersync's lab runtime for bounded DPOR exploration, seed replay, and chaos injection, with scoped Lean/TLA+ anchors. | Requires franken_networkx's CGSE + asupersync's lab runtime + a codebase that threads `Cx` capability contexts through every effect from day one. |
| **B6** | **Agent-Native by Construction** | Branch-per-agent isolation with semantic intent-log merge, capability-scoped (macaroon) subgraph authorization, provenance as first-class edges, hybrid vector+text+graph retrieval in one planner, and retained-evidence replay of strict agent reads—purpose-built for GraphRAG and multi-agent memory. | Requires B1 (branches), B4 (fresh incremental views), B5 (scoped replay), and asupersync's macaroon security layer. |

The 2026 market context makes the timing exact: GraphRAG and agent memory have become the first mainstream non-fraud use case pulling enterprises into graph databases; practitioners have converged on hybrid vector+graph architectures; and reviewers explicitly flag governance/access-control and freshness-of-derived-state as the unsolved problems of current systems. Meanwhile the strongest technical design in the space was removed from open source at the exact moment demand inflected: Apple acquired Kùzu Inc. (agreed October 2025, disclosed February 2026 via Apple's EU DMA filing) — at once the wildcard in this market and the strongest available validation of the embedded-graph thesis. The Kùzu-shaped hole is not empty and is not staying open: community forks (LadybugDB, bighorn, ryugraph, Vela) carry the architecture forward, and cloud GQL gravity is consolidating the query surface — Microsoft Fabric Graph is GA with native ISO GQL and NL2GQL over OneLake, Spanner Graph is GQL-compatible, and Neo4j itself is converging on GQL through Cypher 25 and Neo4j 6 — which makes ISO GQL conformance table stakes, not a wedge. What the market has demonstrated it lacks is an abandonment-proof, governance-grade embedded engine: GitLab adopted Kùzu for its Knowledge Graph, then declared it an unviable foundation and began a forced migration — a marquee adopter burned by embedded-graph abandonment, now shopping for exactly the durability, governance, and continuity properties this plan specifies. The correct move is therefore not to refill the hole as it was — it is to build the system Kùzu would have become in 2030, plus the durability, temporal, verification, and multi-writer stories it never had. FrankenGraphDB is the only embedded graph engine that combines git-grade branches, deterministic byte-level replay for STRICT results, capability governance, and outsider-verifiable proofs.

**Anti-goals of this document:** There is no "MVP", no "v1 simplification", no "phase where we use RocksDB temporarily." Section 19 sequences *integration*, not ambition: every workstream below is specified at full strength. Horizontal sharding is explicitly post-1.0: the 1.0 formats reserve the identities and fencing fields it needs, but this plan does **not** claim that adding distributed atomic commit, distributed SSI, or a global-time service is a configuration-only activation. Those protocols have their own workstream and proof gates before sharding may ship.

---

## 1. Constraints and Non-Negotiables

1. **The dependency universe is closed.** Allowed: `core`/`alloc`/`std`, the Rust nightly toolchain (both asupersync and franken_networkx already pin nightly), and the three foundation projects — `asupersync` (with whatever it vendors internally; its choices are its own), the `fnx-*` crates of `franken_networkx`, and *design-level* reuse of `frankensqlite` (we fork/adapt specific modules into `fgdb-*` crates rather than linking `fsqlite-*` wholesale, because graph objects are not SQLite pages — see §2.3). Everything else — compression codecs, sketches, ANN indexes, inverted indexes, radix trees, wire protocols, columnar readers — is built in-house (§18 is the complete inventory). No serde, no tokio, no rocksdb, no arrow, no tantivy, no hnswlib. The Python package may consume `fnx-python` as an allowed `fnx-*` foundation crate and therefore its already-pinned transitive binding runtime, but `fgdb-*` crates may not add a direct PyO3 dependency; the database engine, server, CLI, and durable formats remain free of that packaging boundary.
2. **Memory safety is structural.** Every ordinary crate root and the workspace default use `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. Rust's `forbid` level cannot be lowered, so the few raw-pointer implementations (buffer arenas, SIMD kernels, VFS mappings) live in separately named `fgdb-unsafe-*` boundary crates whose roots use `deny(unsafe_code)` plus narrowly scoped, ledgered `allow` sites. Safe-facing crates never relax `forbid`. Every unsafe operation gets a ledger row: path, invariant, evidence, scalar or safe fallback, and no-claim boundary; CI rejects an unledgered site.
3. **`Cx` everywhere.** Every function that performs I/O, takes a lock, allocates from a shared arena, or can block accepts `&Cx` (asupersync's capability context). This is what makes B5 possible: swap the `Cx`, and the entire database runs under the lab runtime with virtual time, deterministic scheduling, and fault injection. It is also what makes cancellation-correct query timeouts, deadline propagation, and capability narrowing (read-only connections *cannot* express writes) structural rather than conventional.
4. **Deterministic by default, with an explicit domain.** The strict contract is: same evidence closure (root object and branch head, normalized query and parameters, semantic/capability/policy epochs, executable artifacts, index generations, numeric profile, and recorded external inputs) ⇒ byte-identical **canonical logical-result encoding**, including order. Transport chunking is not part of logical identity. Cross-machine strict mode uses the portable numeric profile in §8.6; relaxed floating execution is opt-in and certificate-declared.
5. **Single artifact, three postures.** One codebase produces: (a) an embedded library (`fgdb`) usable like Kùzu/DuckDB from Rust and Python; (b) a server binary (`fgdbd`) speaking the native protocol, HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, and a Bolt-compat subset; (c) a CLI binary (`fgdb`, implemented by the `fgdb-cli` crate). Larger-than-memory operation is first-class in all three.
6. **The published recovery root is the source of truth.** Before history truncation, logical state is reconstructed from an authoritative checkpoint projection plus the complete contiguous `LogicalCommandRecord` stream. Transaction markers and committed effects are the transaction-only subsequence; schema, policy, delivery, accounting, audit, configuration, GC, and other control commands are equally necessary to reconstruct canonical state. After the truncation horizon advances, the newly installed checkpoint and retained logical-command suffix become the authoritative recovery basis; reclaimed capsules are no longer claimed to be available truth. The only **published** bytes updated in place are the two fixed root-pointer slots in §5.1. Newly created staging files may be written until sealed, but are unreachable and disposable by proved recovery rules; every reachable root object, checkpoint, marker batch, capsule, and derived object is immutable and content addressed. Derived indexes and views never become authoritative for base semantics or constraints.
7. **No JVM, no GC, no mmap-as-durability, no generic KV underlay, no eventual-consistency defaults.** These are the fossils we refuse to inherit.
8. **Narrowed capability contexts.** Subsystems receive purpose-typed wrappers over `Cx` (`QueryCx`, `TxnCx`, `CommitCx`, `MaintCx`, `ReplCx`) exposing only their legal effects as obligations (`pin_snapshot`, `reserve_prepared_bytes`, `reserve_raft_payload_space`, `publish_segment`, ...). The sharpest instance: the merge ladder's intent-replay evaluator receives a `Cx` with **no clock, entropy, network, or filesystem capability** — deterministic rebase is guaranteed *by construction*, not by review.
9. **Prohibited shortcuts (constitutional).** No global-lock "interim" transaction model; no `HashMap<VId, Vec<EId>>` presented as storage; no snapshot isolation quietly labeled "ACID"; no parser-interprets-AST engine; no non-durable benchmark mode reported as a result; no serde-derived enum as a durable format; no detached background thread. Early code may implement a *subset* of each final abstraction — never a substitute for it.
10. **Adaptivity is classified, or it does not ship.** Every adaptive decision is exactly one of: *answer-preserving physical* (cache eviction, prefetch, equivalent kernel selection, local pacing); *answer-affecting execution* (approximate generation/candidate/fusion/stopping choices represented by the execution's `AnswerRequirement`/realized `AnswerContract`); or *canonical-state-affecting* (view/index publication, watermark advancement, security/retention/configuration changes). Answer-affecting choices are legal only inside the requested requirement, are fully pinned in the bound plan/certificate/replay closure, and emit decision cards; a policy-table change that can alter them is stream-sequenced. Canonical-state-affecting choices change only through logical commands under stream-sequenced `DecisionPolicyEpoch` or their own typed epoch. Physical-only choices may adapt locally but still log cards and must pass answer-equivalence tests. Logged propensity supports off-policy evaluation only for candidate actions covered by the logging policy. Statistical promotion evidence is `FG-EVID-*`, never an `FG-INV-*` safety proof, and the deterministic fallback remains valid when assumptions fail.
11. **Claims have types.** Every load-bearing statement is registered as exactly one of: `invariant` (must hold on every execution), `proof` (theorem within a named formal model), `bounded_model` (checked only within declared bounds), `statistical` (confidence statement under named assumptions), `slo` (empirical operational target), or `benchmark` (measured on a pinned fixture). A weaker claim class may inform policy but may not enforce or justify a stronger one. `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness invariants; `evidence.toml` and `slo.toml` carry statistical and empirical claims.
12. **Costs are registered claims.** Constraint 11 governs what a statement may assert; this constraint governs what a mechanism may cost. Every operation class has a row in the operation-cost registry (Appendix G) stating its sequenced semantic commands, total Raft log entries, ordered durability barriers with their amortization law and fusion legality, external-authority interactions, and minted durable objects. Every §17 gate must be derivable from that registry — a latency gate must be ≥ its declared class's ordered-barrier count × the benchmark manifest's pinned measured fsync p50, and a gate that a registry row makes arithmetically impossible is a registry error that fails CI, never an ambitious target. Any change that adds sequenced commands, durability barriers, external-authority interactions, or per-object identity structure updates the registry in the same change; CI rejects a divergence. Structure lives in the registry; µs and throughput budgets are `slo.toml` rows and are never invariants.

### 2.3 frankensqlite (~1.28 MLOC): the architectural donor

frankensqlite is inspiration-by-dissection: we adopt its *designs*, re-instantiate them for graph objects, and where a module is genuinely object-agnostic we fork it into an `fgdb-*` crate (attribution preserved) rather than depending on `fsqlite-*` and dragging SQLite's page/B-tree world along.

### 2.4 What the foundations do *not* provide (and we therefore build)

Columnar graph storage, adjacency compression codecs, a query language front end, a cost-based optimizer, a vectorized/factorized executor, WCOJ machinery, a Z-set incremental engine, secondary/FTS/vector indexes, graph statistics sketches, the wire protocol's graph payloads, the calibration plane's graph-specific scores and ledgers (`fgdb-calibrate` wraps the runtime's e-process/conformal machinery rather than reimplementing it), the verifiability accumulator (Merkle Mountain Range + transparency checkpoints), and the replication state machine (Raft sequencing itself — though membership, anti-entropy, coded fan-out, and convergent metadata are *compositions* of existing protocol machines per §2.1, not new construction). That is the actual FrankenGraphDB codebase, estimated 275–440 KLOC of new Rust — large, but *smaller than frankensqlite*, on a foundation that already absorbed the hardest systems problems (scheduling, cancellation, networking, fountain coding, deterministic testing, sequential statistics). The complete build-it-ourselves inventory is §18.

### 3.1 Dynamic graph storage (the write/scan/space trilemma)

| Source | Core idea | Verdict for FrankenGraphDB |

| **CSR** (static baseline) | Contiguous offset+neighbor arrays; unbeatable scans; zero update capability | **Adopt** as sealed per-`(stable partition, edge type, direction)` runs with explicit ordinal maps and per-list codecs; mutable labels remain membership/derived projections, never primary placement (§6.3) |
| **Sortledton** (VLDB '22) | Sorted neighborhoods in cache-friendly blocks; unrolled skip lists for hub vertices; transactional; ~1.22× CSR analytics at ~2.1× CSR memory | **Adapt** as the *delta tier* block layout (§6.2): sorted 256-edge blocks, per-block version pointers; hub vertices escalate to skip-list-of-blocks |
| **Teseo** (VLDB '21) | PMA + ART fat tree; great point latency, rebalance latency spikes, high memory on skewed graphs | **Reject** PMA as primary (rebalance storms conflict with p99 goals); **adopt** its lesson that the vertex table must not be a straitjacket — our vertex directory is an index, not the store |
| **LiveGraph** (VLDB '20) | Purely sequential per-vertex logs; fast ingest; scans degrade, deletes awkward | **Adapt**: the *hot-vertex overflow log* (§6.2.4) borrows the append-only trick for write bursts, but logs are bounded and compacted into sorted blocks |
| **Aspen** (PLDI '19) | Purely functional compressed trees; O(1) snapshots; single writer; 3–10× CSR memory | **Adopt the spirit** (immutable structural sharing ⇒ free snapshots) at *run granularity* instead of tree-node granularity — same benefit, a fraction of the pointer overhead |

### 3.4 What we deliberately reject

Generic KV underlays (JanusGraph/Nebula tax); Gremlin as the primary language (imperative, optimizer-hostile — provided only as a later compat shim if ever); RDF-first modeling (property graph first; RDF import/view later); JVM anything; mmap-as-the-durability-story; PMA global rebalancing; eventual consistency as a default; external crates (constraint #1).

Four seductive alternatives were evaluated in depth and rejected with recorded reasons: (a) native hyperedges; (b) an unbounded per-fragment representation zoo; (c) a separate full GraphBLAS executor; and (d) plan racing as the default. Racing survives only behind deterministic-output buffering and registered safe cutovers (§8.5). Weaver-style refinable timestamps were set aside for 1.0 because one global scalar commit order simplifies Chronicle, branches, Ripple, and replay; post-1.0 sharding workstream W12 must preserve that contract through a meta-Raft global transaction record or explicitly reopen the decision.

Further rejections: (e) a second Calvin-style transaction lane unless measured aborts justify reopening it; (f) WASM as a foreign UDF runtime; (g) external-codegen JIT; (h) TrueTime-class infrastructure for 1.0—HLC plus consensus-fenced read contracts supplies the semantics actually specified, not arbitrary follower linearizability; (i) FHE/MPC/ORAM in the initial threat model; (j) learned indexes as authoritative access paths; and (k) a spatial index in 1.0 — `Point(2D/3D)` values are storable scalars but are not orderable and not indexable, a declared index over a `Point` property fails closed as a typed error, and the canonical `Point` byte encoding exists for digests and equality only and is explicitly not a spatial order; the recorded post-1.0 route is a Z-order/Hilbert-curve mapping over the existing B-tree machinery, with an in-house R-tree admitted only if profiling defeats the curve mapping, and the Neo4j differential corpus documents the divergence (`point()`, `distance()`, point indexes) as a registered non-goal. DP and leakage measurements remain scoped mechanisms, not substitutes for noninterference.

| **Empirical Bayes / James–Stein shrinkage** (Robbins; Efron); **Good–Turing** unseen-mass estimation; robust estimators (median/MAD, Catoni) | Lower aggregate risk only for their declared loss/model classes; unseen-mass estimates and heavy-tail-resistant summaries each retain assumptions and finite-sample limits | **Evaluate** for per-block selectivities, cold-predicate cost floors, and controller estimators (§8.5); no graph-workload slogan substitutes for fixture-specific risk evidence |
| **Off-policy evaluation** (importance-weighted / doubly-robust estimators, Dudík et al.); online-to-batch conversion; learning-augmented algorithms | Candidate policies are evaluable only with positivity/overlap, controlled variance, and a defined outcome/counterfactual model; distillation does not automatically transfer a bound | **Adopt conditionally** with logged probabilities, support exclusions, effective sample size, deterministic fallback, and explicit deployment evidence (§6.6) |
| **CVaR** (Rockafellar & Uryasev); **extreme value theory** (peaks-over-threshold/GPD); convex duality (KKT shadow prices) | Coherent tail-risk objectives; POT/GPD extrapolation and intervals only after threshold, tail-family, dependence, and stability diagnostics; dual prices only within the optimization model | **Adopt as model-qualified control evidence** for background scheduling, tail gates, and admission (§16.6, §17); never call a fitted extreme quantile “certified” |
| **Network calculus** (min-plus service curves; Le Boudec & Thiran); max-plus event algebra; queueing theory (M/G/1, Kingman); Little's law | Compositional bounds when valid arrival/service curves hold; queueing approximations under their assumptions; Little's law for a stable, consistently delimited system | **Adopt conditionally** for plan/view envelopes, sizing, backpressure, and telemetry audits (§9.4, §16), with every assumption and violation fallback recorded |
| **Submodular maximization** (Nemhauser et al.; lazy greedy, constraint-specific algorithms) | Approximation ratios only when the registered objective is actually monotone submodular and the budget/independence constraint matches the theorem | **Adopt selectively** for validated coverage objectives in synopsis, landmark, fault-campaign, or placement decisions; otherwise retain the greedy trace as a heuristic, not a certificate (§10, §15.1, §14) |
| **CALM theorem** (Hellerstein & Alvaro); Red–Blue consistency; escrow transactions (O'Neil) | Monotonicity characterizes coordination-free distributed computation only in the declared model; escrow preserves named numeric invariants after coordinated rights allocation and while local rights suffice | **Adopt with scoped proofs**: context-derived `ConsistencyClass` (§7.4) and a modeled escrow-counter merge mode (App. B), never a context-free “no coordination” label |
| **Lineage-driven fault injection** (Alvaro et al.); delta debugging (Zeller); record/replay of mediated nondeterminism boundaries (rr lineage) | Prioritize causal fault hypotheses, shrink reproducible failures, and replay only the nondeterminism and external inputs actually captured | **Adopt with replay-completeness grades** in the verification ladder (§15.1); redacted or incomplete production bundles cannot promise deterministic identity |
| **Certificate transparency**, Merkle Mountain Ranges, authenticated data structures, PDP/PoR | Inclusion/consistency relative to trusted roots; cross-client anti-equivocation requires mandatory witness/gossip/cross-logging; storage challenges prove only their sampled statement | **Adopt with explicit proof scopes and transparency modes** (§5.8) |
| **Differential privacy** (Dwork et al.; Rényi accounting, Mironov; smooth sensitivity, Nissim et al.) | Provable per-query information-leakage bounds with tight composition accounting | **Adopt** as a Warden capability class: ε-budgeted aggregate access with a per-tenant privacy ledger (§12) |
| **MTTDL Markov models** (absorbing-chain first-passage analysis) | Model-qualified expected loss time under fitted rates, independence/failure-domain assumptions, repair policy, and sensitivity | **Adopt** as `FG-CFG-01`, alongside—not instead of—crash, restore, and failure-domain tests (§5.7) |
| **SWIM + Lifeguard** (Das et al.; Dadgar et al.); closed timestamps (CockroachDB lineage); Merkle anti-entropy (Dynamo lineage) | Scalable probabilistic membership with local-health-aware suspicion; follower reads with named staleness contracts; O(log n) divergence detection | **Adopt** via asupersync's implementations (§14) |
| **Rollback/persistent union-find** (Conchon & Filliâtre lineage); offline dynamic connectivity | Exact historical connectivity for a sealed operation interval via a segment tree over time plus rollback DSU, with preprocessing/space and query costs stated for that construction; insert-only current windows admit cheaper DSU | **Adopt as one Beacon generation type** (§10.7), with explicit projection, interval, deletion, branch-overlay, and fallback contracts rather than a universal polylog claim |
| **Dostoevsky/Fluid LSM** (Dayan & Idreos); **S3-FIFO** (Yang et al. 2023); AMAC interleaving (Kocberber et al.); radix joins (Balkesen et al.) | Pareto-optimal compaction policy families; simpler-than-ARC scan-resistant eviction; memory-level parallelism inside a core; cache-shaped partitioned joins | **Adapt**, each behind a benchmark gate: per-partition compaction policy family (§6.3), eviction shadow-duel (§6.7), executor micro-optimizations (§8.7) |

## Generated decision and provenance matrix
Generate a stable DecisionRecordId for every thesis bet, non-negotiable, foundation capability/limitation, SOTA lesson, deliberately rejected alternative, calibration claim, and bibliography anchor above. Each row records adoption/rejection status, rationale, assumptions, no-claim boundary, owning workstream/bead, affected invariant/evidence/SLO/cost/format rows, verification strategy, negative-evidence trigger, and review/expiry policy. Every implementation bead's provenance resolves to these IDs; every “build in-house” row resolves to the workspace topology and a concrete owner; no external dependency may enter merely because it appears in the bibliography.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded sections exactly preserve plan lines 1-184 and Appendix E lines 3196-3199 with checksums and no truncation.
- Every bet, constraint, foundation asset/gap, SOTA lesson, rejection, calibration principle, and citation has a stable decision/provenance row and owner.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: keeping rationale only in prose, treating bibliography entries as dependencies, and silently replacing rejected designs with “temporary” substitutes. Risk: research ages; rows carry review status and dates without rewriting historical intent.

title: Generate RemoteGrantTargetRef and close the exportable-target-kind set
description:
a01:1402 defines RemoteGrantTargetRef as 'the containing-schema-generated closed union with one typed strong-reference arm per exportable authority-local target kind; it has no generic target arm.' It is the exact_type of RemoteRetentionGrantSpec.target_ref, which is one of a01's uncovered census field keys.

Two things are missing and neither is an a01-local call:
1. The arm set is the closure of every EXPORTABLE authority-local target kind, which spans slices. Nobody has enumerated that closure.
2. The generated-reference-union path itself. All five existing reference unions (MandatoryInventoryRef, LocalCommandInputRef, LogicalCommandInputRef, MetaAppliedResultRef, ShardProtocolEvidenceRef) are per-anchor, containing-schema-generated names, keyed by union_name alone and anchored to exactly one (containing_schema, field_tag). That is the right shape for RemoteGrantTargetRef, but the generation contract has never been exercised for a union whose arms come from a cross-slice closure.

Note this is NOT the same problem as AuthorityAppliedRef, which a01 2D resolved as an inline composite wire type precisely because it is ONE shared union reused across many schemas rather than a per-anchor generated one. RemoteGrantTargetRef is genuinely the generated kind.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLOSURE ENUMERATED (the bead's missing piece #1), and the union is measurably unlandable today. Both results below are machine-derived from the plan and the live catalog, with a control run on the probe.

THE EXPORTABLE-TARGET-KIND CLOSURE IS 74 KINDS. a01:1402 defines RemoteGrantTargetRef as one typed strong-reference arm per exportable authority-local target kind. The exportable set is exactly the T of W12's one cross-consensus edge, CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T> (a01:1401), since the retention grant exists to keep that authority-local target alive while a consumer holds the edge. Enumerated over the WHOLE plan: 74 distinct instantiations, plus the bare generic. Highest-arity: GlobalControlRecord (7 sites), ShardAppliedAck (6), ShardCheckpointCertificate / RestoreShardBootstrapProjectionCertificate / MetaControlProjectionCertificate (5 each), GlobalAttemptRegistration (4). The tail spans Topology*, Restore*, ShardKey*, GlobalBackup*, Gc*, RoleTransition*, Legacy* and the Global/Shard txn families — i.e. essentially every W12 slice a05-a21, which is why no single slice owner could have enumerated it from their own bytes.

ONLY 4 OF THE 74 CAN CURRENTLY FORM AN ARM. A [[reference_union_arm]] row carries target_schema_id, which must resolve to a registered kind (the shape is fixed by the five existing unions: [[reference_union]] {union_name, containing_schema, field_tag, role} plus N x [[reference_union_arm]] {..., arm_tag, stable_name, target_schema_id, identity_class, reference_semantics=strong, role_predicate, retention_and_cut_rule, version_status, max_size_bytes=40}). Checked every one of the 74 against registries/logical_object_kinds.toml:
  kind row PRESENT (arm can resolve):  4  — GroupTimeIssuanceQuiescenceCertificate,
                                            MetaAuthorityBindingProjection,
                                            ShardTimeAuthorityRetirementAck,
                                            ShardTimeBoundSubjectInventoryCertificate  (all a16)
  kind row ABSENT  (arm impossible):  70
The containing schema itself, RemoteRetentionGrantSpec, IS registered, so the anchor is fine; it is purely the arm targets that do not exist.

WHY IT CANNOT BE PARTIALLY LANDED. a01:1402 says the union 'has no generic target arm', so there is no placeholder arm to stand in for the 70, and a closed union landed with 4 of 74 arms would be a false freeze of a set the plan defines as complete. The honest state is declared-and-blocked, not partially landed.

PROBE CONTROL, because a 0-or-near-0 result is exactly the shape of a false negative: my first pass matched 'symbol = "<name>"' and returned 0 of 74, which I did NOT report, because the same pattern also returned 'not found' for CommitCapsule and ExportLeaf, which are certainly registered. logical_object_kinds.toml keys rows as [[kind]] with 'name = ...'; re-run with the correct key the control passes and the real answer is 4. Any future census of this file must control against a known-present kind first.

DISPOSITION: blocked on the Appendix-A catalog reaching kind coverage for the W12 slices, not on any design decision within atke. Missing piece #2 from the bead text (the generated-reference-union path itself) is NOT actually missing — the five existing unions establish the exact row shape and RemoteGrantTargetRef fits it unchanged; it is only the arm targets that are unavailable. So this bead is one unblocker away from mechanical, and that unblocker is slice buildout, not a contract question. Full 74-name list is derivable in one command: grep -o 'CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<[A-Za-z0-9_]*>' on the plan, drop the bare <T>, sort -u.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN COUNT, found by applying the two-step control discipline to my own finding. The number is 1 of 74, not 4 of 74. Disposition is unchanged (still blocked, in fact harder), but the reasoning was wrong and a wrong number on a bead gets acted on.

WHAT I GOT RIGHT: the measurement. 4 of the 74 exportable target kinds have a [[kind]] row. That survived a positive control (my first probe returned 0/74 keyed on 'symbol' when rows are [[kind]]/'name', caught because the same probe also 'missed' CommitCapsule).

WHAT I GOT WRONG: the interpretation. I wrote that those 4 'can currently form an arm'. I had INFERRED the arm-resolution rule from the row shape instead of reading identity.rs. Reading it shows arm validity is TWO laws, not one:
  identity.rs:2617  union_arm_unresolved         — target_schema_id must be a registered logical object
  identity.rs:2650  dag_future_result            — target's construction_order must be <= the containing schema's
I had only applied the first. Checking the second against RemoteRetentionGrantSpec (construction_order 20):
  MetaAuthorityBindingProjection             order 10  -> OK
  ShardTimeBoundSubjectInventoryCertificate  order 35  -> FAILS dag_future_result
  GroupTimeIssuanceQuiescenceCertificate     order 39  -> FAILS dag_future_result
  ShardTimeAuthorityRetirementAck            order 52  -> FAILS dag_future_result
So exactly ONE of the 74 arms is currently constructible. Corrected figure: 1 resolvable, 73 not.

A THIRD THING I ASSERTED WITHOUT READING, now verified and it happens to be in my favour: union_arm_lifecycle_mismatch rejects only 'retired' and 'experimental', so a RESERVED kind IS a legal arm target. My probe counted any kind row regardless of status, which matches the law — but that was right by construction, not because I had checked. Worth stating because the natural assumption is that arms need ACTIVE targets, and they do not.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER LANDS THIS: RemoteGrantTargetRef is not merely waiting on 70-odd mints. Every one of the 74 arm targets must ALSO be minted at a construction_order at or below RemoteRetentionGrantSpec's. Three of the four kinds that already exist violate that today, and they are a16 certificate/ack kinds whose orders (35/39/52) were reasonably chosen for their own DAG position. title: Implement fgdb-bigint canonical signed-limb arithmetic kernel
description:
## What and scope
Create the first real engine crate at crates/fgdb-bigint and implement the final canonical signed-limb arithmetic kernel required by W1 and Ripple. The representation is private, normalized sign plus little-endian u64 magnitude limbs: zero has exactly one representation, nonzero values have no high zero limbs, and equality/order/hash therefore agree structurally. Implement exact signed add, subtract, multiply, negate, scalar construction, checked i128 conversion, magnitude inspection for codecs, and deterministic diagnostics.

This is a final subset of fgdb-w1-foundation-types-tjk, not a prototype. It deliberately does not invent a durable wire encoding: durable codec tags/bytes remain owned by the generated-format Bead. It also does not claim Ripple integration. All allocation-capable arithmetic accepts an explicit LimbLimit and fails before allocating above that limit, so later fgdb-resource accounting can wrap the kernel without an unbounded bypass.

## Why
The plan requires in-house canonical exact integers for ZWeight promotion and overflow-free STRICT rational comparisons. Producing this kernel now creates substantive reusable product code while the wider G0 registry work continues independently.

## Acceptance criteria
- Add crates/fgdb-bigint as a real workspace member with Rust 2024 and forbid unsafe code.
- Preserve the unique canonical representation across every constructor and operation.
- Exact signed addition, subtraction, multiplication, negation, total ordering, equality, hashing, and checked i128 conversion work across carry, borrow, sign change, zero, u64 boundaries, and i128 MIN/MAX.
- LimbLimit rejection reports operation, required limbs, and limit and occurs before result allocation beyond the declared bound.
- No external dependency or durable-format invention is introduced.
- Unit and deterministic property tests cover canonicalization, randomized i64 differential arithmetic against i128, multi-limb ring laws, order laws, carry/borrow chains, multiplication boundaries, limit failures, and conversion limits.
- A crate-scoped E2E script runs the complete test target twice from an isolated Cargo target and proves deterministic success.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, and UBS over changed files complete before closure.

## Boundaries
No parser, storage engine, mutable state, I/O, unsafe code, serde, or compatibility shim. Resource-ledger integration, spill, ZWeight, and the registered durable codec remain downstream work.

title: CalibrationWindow permits invalid direct construction despite rejecting constructor
description:
## Finding

`crates/fgdb-evidence/src/lib.rs:667-683` documents `CalibrationWindow` as a closed half-open `[start_seq, end_seq)` window, and `CalibrationWindow::new` rejects `start_seq >= end_seq`. The two fields are nevertheless public at lines 670-672, so downstream code can bypass the constructor. `EvidenceEnvelope::new` at lines 777-793 accepts `Option<CalibrationWindow>` without revalidation, allowing the invalid value into the otherwise immutable envelope.

## Controlled evidence

The constructor census found the known `CalibrationWindow::new` production/example/test uses, so the probe was capable of finding the intended path. Direct source reading then established the bypass. A standalone external-crate probe compiled the actual `fgdb-evidence/src/lib.rs` against thin `fgdb_claim` and `fgdb_types` type stubs and successfully constructed `CalibrationWindow { start_seq: 9, end_seq: 2 }`. The stubs prove this module's public construction surface only; they do not prove claim-lattice or cross-crate integration behavior.

The existing `windows_reject_empty_and_inverted` test at lines 1417-1429 exercises only `CalibrationWindow::new`, so it cannot detect direct literal construction.

## Required closure

Make invalid windows unrepresentable or revalidate them at every accepting boundary. Prefer private fields plus read-only accessors, retain the fallible constructor as the sole admission path, add a `compile_fail` doctest for direct construction and a compiling constructor companion, and add an envelope regression proving empty/inverted windows cannot enter `EvidenceEnvelope`.

- The same type exposes `pub start_seq` and `pub end_seq` at lines 668-669, so an external caller can construct `CalibrationWindow { start_seq: 9, end_seq: 2 }` without calling the validator.
- `EvidenceEnvelope::new` accepts `Option<CalibrationWindow>` without revalidating it, so the invalid value remains plausible evidence rather than becoming a typed error.
- A controlled external-crate probe compiled the actual evidence module with thin foreign-type stubs and successfully constructed the invalid literal. That probe proves the public construction surface; it does not claim full integration behavior.

Its only two references are `use fgdb_evidence::CalibrationWindow;` at policy_epoch.rs:1545 and `CalibrationWindow::new(60, 66)?` at :1718 — BOTH inside `mod tests` (which begins at :1535), and the second goes through the validated constructor.

title: Appendix A: PlacementDescriptorWithoutId is reserved while an active kind's identity law depends on it, and its a01-pinned body contradicts a02:1449

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
TWO COUPLED DEFECTS ON ONE a01-OWNED ROW, both blocking a02 completion and neither resolvable inside a02. All probe-derived; controlled where a bare absence would otherwise have been the finding.

THE ROW: `a01:wire-type:placement-descriptor-without-id`, wire_type_id 0x001e, status "reserved", encoding_context "Appendix A reference-semantics family PlacementDescriptorWithoutId (a01); exact member layout per plan lines 1388-1444".

DEFECT 1 — STATUS INCOHERENCE, and it is the same class already fixed once in this slice. `PlacementRecord` is an ACTIVE physical kind whose FG-INV-09 identity law is BLAKE3("fgdb:placement:v1" || canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId)). So an active identity-recomputation transcript rests on a non-live row. That is exactly the incoherence that FORCED status=active for CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest and EncodingDescriptorWithoutId in 352bccd, where CiphertextRecord and EncodingRecord are the active dependants.
MEASURED CATALOG-WIDE, not asserted: screening all 61 wire types against the rule "active iff at least one already-ACTIVE row references it", 41 conform, 19 are foundational primitives that are active without a named referent because they are used via allowed_containing_schemas ["*"] (StrongRef, WeakDigest, MarkerRef, AuthorityBoundHeader, HlcTimestamp and similar — my referent detector only finds name mentions, so it undercounts them), and PlacementDescriptorWithoutId is THE ONLY ROW IN THE CATALOG that is reserved while having an active referent. One row, one exception, and it is this one.
FIX: flip 0x001e to active. It is an a01 row, so an a02 increment must not do it unilaterally.

DEFECT 2 — THE PINNED BODY CONTRADICTS a02's SOURCE, and this is why a02's placement family cannot be modelled at all. Three renderings exist and two disagree materially:
  plan:280   { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }
  a01:1443   { encoding_id, root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy_id,
               ContiguousSpan { root_failure_domain_id, segment_id, offset, encoded_len,
                                root_symbol_inventory_digest } }
  a02:1449   { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }
a01 renames two members, root-prefixes two more, and INLINES ContiguousSpan instead of carrying the `location_form` union at all — consistent with a root placement always being contiguous. a02 and plan:280 agree with each other and disagree with a01. The landed row's encoding_context pins the layout to lines 1388-1444, i.e. the a01 rendering.
DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCES, all three observable today:
 (a) The census emits ConflictingCandidateEvidence on the family ("the same schema source key has divergent structural bodies").
 (b) Because two bodies compete, `location_form = ContiguousSpan{...} | Explicit{...}` never parses as a union. a02 is the ONLY slice of 21 with zero union candidates and zero arm candidates — controlled: every other slice is nonzero (a01 13/36, a03 49/129, a07 92/245, a15 51/162, a16 31/79, a21 64/196), so the zero is real rather than a broken probe.
 (c) One arm of a closed union is registered standalone and the other does not exist anywhere: ContiguousSpan is a02 wire type 0x000a, active; `Explicit` has 0 catalog rows and 0 wire_types rows. That asymmetry is not a design choice — it is what happens when the union is unparseable and someone registers the arm they needed.

RESOLUTION SPACE, deliberately not chosen — all three are a01+a02 cross-slice and (2) amends a normative appendix:
 (A) Erratum reconciling the two bodies to one rendering, then re-pin the a01 row's encoding_context and let location_form parse.
 (B) Widen the a01 row to cover both renderings explicitly, if the intent is genuinely one schema with a root specialisation.
 (C) Rule them TWO schemas that collide on a name — a general PlacementDescriptorWithoutId and a root-specialised one — and rename one. Note ContiguousSpan's landed allowed_containing_schemas is already ["RootBootstrap", "PlacementRecord"], which is weak evidence for the two-context reading.
My own lean is (C) or (A); I am not deciding it.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG HERE, stated so nobody re-derives it:
 * Not an ordering problem. a02 cannot carry a construction_order at all — [[physical_kind]] and [[wire_type]] rows have no construction_order key, and the DAG is evaluated over field rows resolved through logical kinds.
 * Not a fgdb-u3gr instance. The erratum screen over the full a02 range found zero occurrences of any of the nine retaining wrapper spellings targeting any a02 family, so there is no self-referencing retaining wrapper anywhere in placement or symbols.
 * Not an adjudication gap. bdac80c already landed the ConflictingCandidateEvidence adjudication as maps-to-source, which is forced because the family IS registered. "Does this map to a durable schema" (yes) is a separate question from "which body is normative" (this bead).

BLOCKS: fgdb-a02-filesystem-cipher-dsi3 (the location_form union and the Explicit arm are its only remaining work) and fgdb-a01-reference-roots-2k0q (it owns the row and the 1443 rendering).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ANSWER TO "BAD ROW OR MISSING LAW": IT IS A MISSING LAW — and more precisely a MODELLING GAP, which is the worse of the two. Plus a CORRECTION to my own claim in this bead and in commit 2db58b3.

THE CORRECTION FIRST. I wrote that PlacementDescriptorWithoutId is "the ONLY row in the catalog that is reserved while having an active referent". THAT IS WRONG. It was only true of the population I screened — wire types. Sweeping ALL classes for "an active row that names a reserved row", there are TWO:
    PlacementRecord (active [[physical_kind]], a02)      -> PlacementDescriptorWithoutId (reserved [[wire_type]], a01)
    LocalCommandOrigin.RecoveryBridge (active [[wire_type]], g0) -> RecoveryBridgeSpec (reserved [[logical_kind]], a19)
All four statuses individually verified. This is the same false-negative shape I have now hit three times: a probe confined to one population, reported as a catalog-wide fact. "Only row in the catalog" should have been "only wire type", and I did not control it across classes before writing it down.

WHY THE CHECKER PERMITS IT — three findings, each controlled:
 1. NO LAW COMPARES A REFERRER'S STATUS TO ITS REFERENT'S. Grepping identity.rs for containing.status / containing_kind.status returns nothing. There is no active-implies-active rule anywhere.
 2. `reserved` IS DELIBERATELY REFERENCEABLE, and correctly so. It appears in the valid-status set at identity.rs:872 and :1620, and the only lifecycle rejections are for "retired" | "experimental" (identity.rs:1425 for parents, :2628 for union arm targets). That is right: the whole catalog is built from reserved shells that legitimately reference one another before activation, so a blanket "reject reserved targets" rule would be wrong and would break a15's entire key-destruction family.
 3. AND THE DECISIVE ONE: for this instance there is NO EDGE TO CHECK. The [[physical_kind]] row schema is exactly {identity_law, max_size_bytes, name, owning_identity, record_kind, row_id, slice_id, status, transcript} — it has NO typed target field of any kind. PlacementRecord's dependency on PlacementDescriptorWithoutId exists ONLY inside the transcript free-text string, "BLAKE3(\"fgdb:placement:v1\" || canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId))". Same for the second instance: the dependency lives in an encoding_context string. So the checker is not failing to apply a law it has; it has no representation of the dependency at all.

SO THE VERDICT, stated as asked:
 * The ROW is wrong and should be flipped to active — cheap, a01's call, defect (1) of this bead.
 * There IS a missing law, and the correct statement of it is NARROW: "an ACTIVE row's identity law or encoding context may not depend on a NON-ACTIVE row." Not "reserved is unreferenceable", which would be false.
 * But that law is currently UNENFORCEABLE for exactly the rows where it matters, because physical-kind and wire-type dependencies are expressed in prose rather than as typed edges. Implementing it therefore means one of: (a) parse schema names out of transcript/encoding_context and check their lifecycle — cheap, slightly fragile, and it would catch both known instances today; or (b) give physical_kind and wire_type a typed dependency field so the edge exists in the model — more faithful, and it would also make FG-INV-09's "identity recomputation from REGISTERED transcripts" mechanically checkable rather than prose-checkable, which is what let CiphertextId and EncodingId sit on unregistered structures until 352bccd.
 I lean (b) as the real fix with (a) as an immediate guard, but this is a checker-contract decision above a slice increment, and the two known instances are in a01/a02 and g0/a19 — four slices — so it wants its own bead and owner rather than being folded into this one.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS BEAD: defect (1) is still real and still a01's to flip, but it is now one of two instances of a class rather than a unique anomaly, which strengthens the case for the law and weakens the case for treating the row as a one-off typo. Defect (2), the divergent body, is unaffected by any of this.

title: Freeze the exact DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence schema and consumer matrix
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the missing exact durable schema for DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence, the independently addressable evidence referenced by Appendix A LifecycleAuthoritySource::PresentedCapability (plan line 2623) and ResultResumeTransitionSpec (lines 1510/1498 family). The plan names this StrongRef target but never defines its body, role shape, field/tag set, digest transcript, construction order, or retention law. For each grouped subject/action, generation emits one row for every listed concrete subject, row-declared validation context, and compatible concrete presentation tag; CurrentLocal pairs only with the corresponding Local presentation arm, CurrentMeta only with the corresponding Meta arm, and LegacyLocalToMetaMigration only with ReadyChannelMeta. ReadyChannel expands again over `NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket`. It then emits one row per allowed replay relation and outcome: Current -> `CurrentAccepted`; ConsumedImmediatePredecessor -> `ConsumedPredecessorExactRetry`; MigratedConsumedExactRetry -> the same-named outcome. Current Local/Meta rows allow only the row-declared `Exact|Narrowed` authority relation; every migration row requires `Narrowed`. Every row fixes the matching concrete `TimeBoundSubject` arm, `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, canonical action-scope recipe, current-state predicate named by the direct consumer, and exactly one retention class. Current rows for `TxnReattach`, `TxnRenew`, `ResultRotateResume`, `SubscriptionPause`, `SubscriptionResumeAfterPauseOrDisconnect`, all three subscription ACK actions, `ArtifactOutputResume`, and `ReadYourWritesWait` can select a successor and therefore use `ThroughInstalledSuccessorAcknowledgedOrSubjectTerminal`; their exact ConsumedImmediatePredecessor retry rows only return an already-installed successor and use `ThroughConsumerTerminal`. Other status, admission, merge, result ACK/release, subscription close, and artifact ACK/release Current rows also use `ThroughConsumerTerminal`; an action that terminally disposes its subject remains there until the exact receipt/tombstone resolution. Audit status uses `ThroughAuditReceiptResolution`. The two selection classes require the downstream resolution arm above, so a post-validation CAS loser or other terminal consumer that selected no successor/index entry cannot leak its evidence. No generated row admits a management handle, embedded owner token, Bolt DISCARD/RESET, Shard context, negative-time status classifier, or a presentation class absent from the table.

Each concrete row ID is `dcv:v1:<subject-u16>:<action-u16>:<context-u16>:<presentation-outer-u16>-<presentation-nested-u16>:<replay-u16>:<authority-relation-u16>:<outcome-u16>:<retention-u16>`. Every `u16` is exactly four lowercase hexadecimal digits without `0x`; presentation nested is the ReadyChannel surface or Bolt request-kind tag and is `0000` only for Embedded. Thus the ID encodes the complete presentation cell, is at most 64 ASCII bytes (and therefore within the registered 128-byte field bound), and cannot collide across nested surfaces. The canonical row-set hash is `BLAKE3("fgdb:registry-set:durable-capability-validation-compatibility:v1" || canonical(sorted_complete_rows_with_every_dimension_and_consumer_schema_id))`. Generation proves the row ID is injective over the full tuple, that the sorted set equals the exact expansion above, that the computed longest ID is `<=128` bytes, and that no wildcard, duplicate, omitted cross-product cell, or extra row exists.

The permanent static mutation corpus independently removes, duplicates, retags, reorders, weakens, or changes the type/cardinality of every field and nested arm; substitutes every context/subject/action/presentation/time/key/format/lineage/authority/outcome/retention matrix dimension; injects a future command/result/root edge or a raw capability/MAC/protected-subject field; and changes the exact matrix row-set hash. Its real-CLI redaction scenario injects one unique secret sentinel into a catalog value, capability-like bytes, malformed row ID, and projection value, then requires byte-identical repeated JSONL whose stdout and stderr contain only the stable diagnostic code, sanitized known row ID or `<invalid-row-id>`, registry, and fixed reason class—never the sentinel, attacker value, capability/commitment, protected subject, handle, tenant, or principal.

W10's durable-capability slice is the unique schema/Bead integration owner. Implementation ownership is intentionally split: W9's `fgdb-warden` boundary owns canonical decode, key selection, MAC verification, and current authority/security/time/lineage validation and constructs the evidence; W10 owns the exact lifecycle/protocol/admission/receipt consumers of the resulting nonconstructible ref. Exact crate/path consumers are `fgdb-formats`, `fgdb-protocol`, `fgdb-bolt`, `fgdb-txn`, `fgdb-chronicle`, `fgdb-branch`, `fgdb-subs`, `fgdb-audit`, `fgdb-secure-view`/read admission, embedded `fgdb`, `fgdb-server`, `fgdb-reference`, `fgdb-sim`/fuzz/format verification, and the W12 role-transition/migration path. Runtime codec/golden/fuzz, key/time rotation, restart/replay, lifecycle/race, migration, adapter parity, and public-noninterference checker rows are planned rather than live until their named W9/W10/W12 owners provide executable evidence.

Any action-specific receipt constructed from a presented durable capability strongly retains this validation ref; management-handle, authenticated-session/embedded-owner, and Bolt V1/V2 release alternatives are distinct authority arms and do not fabricate one. ACK/release/status receipts remain the later action authority objects rather than being replaced by generic validation evidence. Every concrete matrix row pins subject/subkind, presented role, current authority role, consumer schema and action tag, allowed presentation arm, lineage relation, exact `TimeBoundSubject`, required `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, authority relation, current-state predicate, outcome, and retention class. Cross-kind/subkind/role/presentation substitution, stale service or security state, equal scalar under a different security root, NotYetValid/Expired evidence in a validation row, wrong verifier/key epoch/format, lineage drift, widening, action/scope substitution, use after retirement, and any unregistered row fail uniformly.

Construction is acyclic and fixed: current replay/key plus current authority/security/session request plus `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable` plus the fresh same-process linear time-use guard plus any nonwidening proof and current lineage membership -> `DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence` -> exact lifecycle/transition/admission/receipt spec -> command -> applied result/successor/root. A durable Usable record surviving restart is not authority; each process must revalidate current state and acquire a fresh linear guard. A successor ref appears only in ConsumedImmediatePredecessor or MigratedConsumedExactRetry evidence after that successor already exists; the migration form also points backward to its initial validation generation and never forward to a later one. While its consumer or retry floor remains rooted, the object strongly retains the replay record, verifier key, time evidence and its profile/import basis, complete current authority/security basis, session authorization, and any nonwidening proof. Rejected input constructs no durable validation record. Diagnostics and events emit only a validated catalog row ID, context/action tag, and public outcome class; they never emit raw or committed capability/header/body/MAC values, protected subject fields, tenant/principal/handles, or attacker-controlled row/value text. The G0 schema, compatibility, construction-DAG, and sentinel-redaction checkers may be live once exact; codec/golden/fuzz, key/time rotation, restart/replay, race, migration, and public-noninterference evidence remain explicitly planned under W9/W10/W12 until their real checkers run.
