every other tag is reserved-invalid. `AuthenticatedDurableCapabilityStatusBasis` is the embedded role-closed `u16` union `0x0001 Local{current_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,current_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Local,presented_replay:DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef,presentation_binding:DurableCapabilityPresentationBinding,presented_capability_commitment,presented_header_digest,presented_kind_body_digest,verified_mac_transcript_digest,verifier_key_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityVerifierKey>,verifier_key_identity,capability_format_version,time_subject_digest:TargetDigest<TimeBoundSubjectBody>,action_scope_digest:TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope>,authority_relation:0x0001 Exact|0x0002 Narrowed{proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>},action:TxnStatusLookup|MergeStatusLookup,canonical_status_request_digest}|0x0002 Meta{current_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,current_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Meta,presented_replay:DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef,presentation_binding:DurableCapabilityPresentationBinding,presented_capability_commitment,presented_header_digest,presented_kind_body_digest,verified_mac_transcript_digest,verifier_key_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityVerifierKey>,verifier_key_identity,capability_format_version,time_subject_digest:TargetDigest<TimeBoundSubjectBody>,action_scope_digest:TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope>,authority_relation:0x0001 Exact|0x0002 Narrowed{proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>},action:TxnStatusLookup|MergeStatusLookup,canonical_status_request_digest}`; every other outer or authority-relation tag is reserved-invalid. The Local basis requires one of the two Local replay arms and ReadyChannelLocal or EmbeddedLocal; the Meta basis requires the corresponding Meta arms. `authority_relation` compares the complete current header/session authority with the replay's issuance header: Exact requires byte equality, while Narrowed requires the named proof over those exact two commitments; widening is uninhabited even when time cannot be classified. The status action-scope digest is recomputed from the exact `TxnStatusLookup` or `MergeStatusLookup` selector, canonical request, presentation-binding digest, capability commitment, and requested scope; its action, request digest, and time-subject digest must byte-match the other basis fields. It is constructible only after header/body/MAC, key, domain, current security, role, session, presentation, kind, request, action scope, time subject, and same-or-narrower authority authentication succeeds; it contains commitments, not raw token/MAC bytes.

`TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence` is the embedded closed `u16` failure union `0x0001 BoundaryOverlap{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,time_subject_digest,intended_use_digest,possible_time_interval,not_before,expires_at}|0x0002 CheckedArithmeticFailure{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,time_subject_digest,intended_use_digest,operation,operands_commitment}|0x0003 ProfileOrEpochUnavailable{profile_oid,required_domain_and_epoch,current_registry_commitment,time_subject_digest,intended_use_digest,stable_failure_class}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. `DurableCapabilityStatusClassification` is the inline `u16` union `0x0001 Usable{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>}|0x0002 NotYetValid{authenticated_basis:AuthenticatedDurableCapabilityStatusBasis,time_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_classification:NotYetValid}|0x0003 Expired{authenticated_basis,time_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_classification:Expired}|0x0004 TimeAuthorityUnavailable{authenticated_basis,failure:TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. In every negative arm, the evidence/failure `time_subject_digest` equals the authenticated basis's typed subject digest and `intended_use_digest` equals its exact action-scope digest; profile/window/request/presentation/capability fields must also agree, so another subject or request cannot supply the classification. It is legal only inside `StatusLookup`; the three negative arms cannot read the outcome/merge index, distinguish existence/current state, rotate a capability, or authorize any effect, and may emit only their named public time class. Invalid MAC/domain/security/role/presentation/kind/request produces `NotVisibleOrUnknown` with no classification object. `TokenExpired` additionally requires the existing durable expired requirement arm before send; the inline classifier does not invent expiry or retire bytes.

`LifecyclePresentedPermitRef<Role>` is a generated associated type: Local contains only `AuthorityPermitRef<Local>`, Meta only `AuthorityPermitRef<Meta>`, and Shard is uninhabited. `LifecycleAuthoritySource<Role>` is the generated closed union `PresentedPermit{permit_ref:LifecyclePresentedPermitRef<Role>}|RegisteredAuthority{registration_ref:RoleExactRegistrationRef,current_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,nonwidening_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>}|PresentedDurableCapabilityStatus{classification:DurableCapabilityStatusClassification}|AuthenticatedSession{session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,request_digest}`; only role-valid arms inhabit each operation row. `PresentedDurableCapabilityStatus` is mandatory for a capability-bearing StatusLookup; its Usable arm owns the positive `DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence` ref and may proceed to the exact protected lookup, while its negative arms may only select the matching public time class. That source is forbidden for every non-status operation, and no ordinary PresentedDurableCapability Lifecycle arm exists. The durable capability kind/subkind is derived from the validation record or authenticated status basis, never repeated as an independently forgeable scalar. `LifecycleOperation` is exactly `RegisterAttempt|PrepareAdmissionScaffolding|RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active|PrepareAdmitted}|StatusLookup{registered_status_kind}|CapabilityManagement{registered_kind,action}`, where the generated associated action type is the disjoint union `Durable{Revoke}|Macaroon{Attenuate|Revoke}`; no generic Rotate or durable Attenuate arm exists. Client-authorized durable rotation is performed only by the exact typed transition surfaces and validation rows `TxnReattach|TxnRenew|ResultRotateResume|SubscriptionPause|SubscriptionResumeAfterPauseOrDisconnect|SubscriptionAckBaseline|SubscriptionAckDelta|SubscriptionAckResetOrGap|ArtifactOutputResume|ReadYourWritesWait`; their own authorization/spec/receipt records retain positive validation evidence, and Lifecycle cannot add a second generic rotation path. The separately registered `SubscriptionDeliveryTransitionSpec::RotateCapability` is system-authorized Protocol maintenance with no presented client capability or DCVE compatibility row; it is distinct from Lifecycle rotation and uses only its structural authority arm. The `GlobalControlCommand(kind=CancelActiveAttempt)` and Local `TxnAbortSpec` both require `RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active}`; admitted Local/Meta abort requires `stage:PrepareAdmitted`. `LifecycleEffectClass<Operation>` is a generated associated closed tag: registration and preparation use their exact scaffolding classes; terminal abort uses `TerminalAbortNoEffectReleaseOnly{stage,registered_result_workspace_conflict_and_hold_disposition_schema}`; status is read-only projection; and capability management uses only the exact kind/action class above. There is no nullable permit, catch-all maintenance class, or wildcard rotate/attenuate/revoke row. `LifecycleAuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>` is the pre-result form `{authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,operation:LifecycleOperation,authority_source:LifecycleAuthoritySource<Role>,sequence_neutral_spec_body_digest,requested_snapshot_or_scope_commitment,effect_class:LifecycleEffectClass<operation>,operation_audit_admission_commitment?,decision,authorization_audit_gate:AuthorizationAuditGate}`. The generated Role/operation matrix fixes every authority/source/effect arm, and the source, requested scope, audit evidence, lifecycle stage, and containing command must byte-match. RegisterAttempt uses a PresentedPermit; PrepareAdmission uses `PrepareAdmissionScaffolding` with exact NotRequired proof while its spec embeds the one GlobalMutation decision for complete effects; RequestTerminalAbort uses RegisteredAuthority plus the exact authenticated client request or the distinct administrative record. Capability-bearing status uses PresentedDurableCapabilityStatus; administrative durable revocation requires RegisteredAuthority or AuthenticatedSession, and macaroon attenuation remains in the macaroon/permit family. Protocol/system maintenance uses its registered structural system-authority command arm, never Lifecycle. ReadClose uses GlobalRead; each shard basis uses its own Read decision. A mutation/read/status decision, scalar epoch pair, fabricated zero effect, wrong-stage abort, or `StatusOrMaintenance` alias cannot substitute.

`TerminalAuditGate` is the same-group-only union `StructurallyInapplicable{exemption:StructuralAuditExemption}|NotRequired{evidence:NonRequiredAuditEvidence}|Required{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,event_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>,terminal_resolution_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketResolution>}`. A required gate is encodable only in the ticket-owning consensus domain and only when all three objects and the earlier authorization gate agree on namespace/domain/profile/principal/request; the resolution owns the event and its typed outcome matches the command/spec. The sole Local `TxnOutcomePreparationRecord` body is the PrepareAdmitted CAS schema in the Local transaction section; `Absent` and `Submitted` tags are unregistered. W12 exclusively uses the separate gate-free `GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord`; no object is reinterpreted or wrapped as the other kind, and only the later `GlobalTxnCommand` carries W12's terminal gate. `DurableCapabilityVerifierKey {issuer_id,key_id,key_epoch,algorithm,public_or_protected_verifier_material,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,verify_through,format_versions[],rotation_predecessor?,status}` is Chronicle-sequenced and strongly retained until no live capability can require it; retirement requires exact Expired evidence for its registered subject/action. Each capability uses the exact common header/body/MAC format, names this key, and is never reinterpreted across versions or visibility epochs.

comments.author: codex-review
comments.text:
Read-only contract adjudication published for scaffold handoff. This is the exact proposed repair; no registry/checker files have been touched.

IDENTITY AND ROLE
- One non-generic logical kind: DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence, stable ObjectKind 0x028f. Do not generate Local/Meta object identities.
- The mandatory closed validation_context is CurrentLocal, CurrentMeta, or LegacyLocalToMetaMigration. Shard is uninhabited. CurrentLocal and CurrentMeta carry the exact AuthorityBoundHeader plus the complete currently selected security-state basis. Migration carries the current Meta header/security basis plus certified Local-to-Meta successor/transition evidence and an exact same-principal/no-wider Meta authorization decision.
- The schema definition may be complete and its static G0 checker live, but codec/golden/fuzz/restart/rotation/runtime behavior remains planned. Do not label runtime evidence active/live.

SUBJECT UNIVERSE
The mandatory closed validated_subject has exactly six arms:
1 TxnOutcome
2 ResumeSubscriptionCursor
3 ResumeBufferedResult
4 ResumeDurableArtifactOutput
5 MergeOutcome
6 ReadYourWrites
Each arm retains the exact role-valid replay record and exact current lineage membership, or the exact consumed-immediate-predecessor plus already-installed successor for byte-identical retry only. Resume subkinds never substitute. MacaroonTokenBytes, permits, AuthorizationLease, and Shard capability validation do not inhabit this schema.

FIELDS AND DIGEST
Use stable tags 0x0001..0x0015:
schema_version; validation_context; validated_subject; presented_capability_commitment over header/body/MAC; presented_header_digest; presented_kind_body_digest; verified_mac_transcript_digest; replay_relation; verifier_key_ref; verifier_key_identity {issuer_id,key_id,key_epoch}; capability_format_version; presentation_binding; compatibility_row_id; validation_action; action_scope_digest; time_validation_evidence_ref; authority_relation Exact|Narrowed{StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>}; validation_outcome CurrentAccepted|ConsumedPredecessorExactRetry; validator_semantics_oid; retention_class; body_digest.
The exact final tag numbering must remain contiguous and reserve body_digest last; if the catalog represents embedded unions as separately tagged durable fields, preserve this semantic order and pin every nested arm/tag too.
Body digest domain is fgdb:body:durable-capability-validation-evidence:v1 over schema major 1 and every preceding canonical field; it excludes only body_digest. Raw capability bytes, MAC bytes/material, protected subject fields, tenant/principal/public handles, and future command/result/root identities are forbidden.

PRESENTATION
- FgpReady binds a StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>, READY/service binding, session/channel/transcript generations, and canonical request digest.
- Embedded binds the exact authorized host session generation and canonical call digest.
- BoltCompatProfileV1 is always rejected because plan line 1050 forbids capability presentation.
- Because line 1052 normatively defines post-G4 Bolt V2 bookmarks as ReadYourWritesCapability values, reserve one explicit BoltV2Bookmark presentation arm and planned compatibility row for ReadYourWrites only, pinned to negotiated BoltCompatProfileV2 and the exact bookmark/RUN/session digest. There is no generic Bolt arm and no V1 row.
- LegacyLocalToMetaMigration is FGP CAPABILITY_MIGRATE only.

EXACT ACTION MATRIX
- TxnOutcome: TXN_STATUS current only; Reattach and Renew current or exact predecessor retry. Renew also requires its separate fresh successor-window evidence.
- ResumeBufferedResult: rotate/resume current or exact predecessor retry; ACK and explicit release current only, with terminal retry authorized by the action-specific receipt/tombstone rather than reclassifying the capability.
- ResumeSubscriptionCursor: pause, resume-after-pause/reconnect, baseline ACK, delta ACK, reset/GAP ACK, and close. Only the plan-defined rotate/resume and idempotent ACK rows may accept exact predecessor retry; terminal close retry resolves through disposition/tombstone.
- ResumeDurableArtifactOutput: rotate/resume, ACK, explicit release, with the same current/predecessor and receipt/tombstone laws as the corresponding plan transitions.
- MergeOutcome: execute and status lookup, current only.
- ReadYourWrites: BEGIN, EXECUTE, EXECUTE_TEXT visibility-floor admission current only; READ_YOUR_WRITES_WAIT current or exact predecessor retry when that operation already rotated the capability.
- All six subjects: one exact PostActivationCapabilityMigrate arm under LegacyLocalToMetaMigration. Retry resolves only through CapabilityMigrationIndex; a retired legacy capability is never generally usable.
- No wildcard StatusOrMaintenance/Rotate row. No generic Attenuate row. Macaroon attenuation stays in the macaroon family; durable revocation is administrative/registered-authority state, not self-authorization by a presented durable capability.
ACK/release/client-control receipts are the later authority objects, but their construction rows must consume and retain this exact validation evidence when a durable capability is the presented source. A management handle or authenticated-session alternative uses its own explicit authority row and does not synthesize this evidence.

CONSTRUCTION AND RETENTION
current replay/key + current authority/security/session + TimeValidationEvidence::Usable + fresh same-process linear use guard + optional nonwidening proof -> DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence -> exact lifecycle/transition/admission/receipt spec -> command -> applied result/successor/root.
A durable Usable record surviving restart is not authority; every process reacquires the linear guard. A successor ref is legal only for consumed-predecessor exact retry after that successor already exists. While the consumer/retry floor is rooted, the validation record strongly retains replay, verifier key, time evidence/profile/import, complete current authority/security basis, session authorization, and any nonwidening proof.

SOURCE REPAIRS
- Type both line-1006 TxnOwnershipTransitionSpec validation inputs as StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>.
- Replace line-2623 PresentedCapability with PresentedDurableCapability and remove the independently forgeable capability_kind scalar, or require it to be a generated projection that byte-matches the exact subject arm.
- Connect the implicit FGP/embedded consumers above, including RYW BEGIN/EXECUTE/EXECUTE_TEXT and the exact result/cursor/artifact receipts.
- Freeze MergeOutcome and RYW current-index membership inside their subject arms.
- Keep CapabilityManagement kind-specific; do not claim a complete rotate/attenuate/revoke wildcard matrix.

OWNERSHIP AND PROOF
Unique semantic owner is W10 capabilities in fgdb-warden. Consumers include fgdb-protocol, fgdb-txn, fgdb-chronicle, fgdb-branch, fgdb-subs, embedded fgdb, fgdb-server, secure-view/read admission, and W12 role-transition/migration paths. Static G0 checkers must separately prove schema exactness, compatibility matrix exactness, construction DAG, and diagnostic redaction. Runtime codec/golden/fuzz, key/time rotation, restart/replay, race, migration, and public noninterference rows remain planned.

INTEGRATION PRECONDITIONS
The scaffold must stop hard-coding exactly one unresolved family and synthetic first-use owner/crate/consumer rows; support real owner/consumer/checker/scenario/gate metadata; parse a structured capability-validation compatibility table rather than prose; represent static-live versus runtime-planned evidence honestly; resolve or explicitly declare exact dependency targets; and sanitize diagnostics. A sentinel mutation must prove neither stdout nor stderr can echo attacker-controlled catalog values, row IDs, capability-like bytes, commitments, or protected subjects.

title: Freeze the ExportLeaf and signer-lock shorthand member types
description:
Seven Appendix A census field keys carry no inline type in the plan and are not covered by any wire envelope, so their exact wire type is a design decision somebody must record.

FIVE in ExportLeaf<T> (a01:1400): export_projection_version, object_specific_scalar_projection, target_closure_inventory_digest, authority_ledger_floor, quorum_signatures. ExportLeaf is a LOGICAL kind (0x0295), so unlike a01's 32 wire-covered fields there is no envelope contract committing these bytes.

TWO one_digest_signer_lock_ref, on RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate and RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate (a01:1404). These additionally have NO named target schema anywhere in the plan, and the field appears across the SameGroupCertificate families, so the choice is cross-slice rather than a01-local.

Precedent for how to record it: a01 already made exactly this class of ruling for plan-silent widths (shard_id=u32, GraphId=u64, BranchId=u64, release_nonce as bytes), each recorded as contestable on the bead trail. Do the same here.

comments.text:
RULING: generic-signed containing_schema on FIELD rows. Posting immediately and out of band because cc_1/pane2 has 8 Tier B generic-target rows blocked on it and currently holds the catalog token — cc_1, you can act on this inside your current hold; you do not need to wait for my 2G to land, and you should not re-derive any of it.

THE RULING IS: THERE IS NOTHING TO RULE. The contract you are waiting for already exists and is already law — YOUR OWN commit 4081560 ("feat(a16): generic-family field hosts and the five generic embedded unions") added it. identity.rs resolves a field row's containing_schema through the generic-free family:

    let containing_family = generic_free_family(f.containing_schema.as_str());
    let containing_logical = logical_by_name.get(containing_family);

so a field row whose containing_schema is `Foo<Bar>` resolves through the registered bare `Foo` kind row. The family is a LOOKUP ONLY: tag uniqueness, anchor matching and BodyDigest recipes all still key on the exact signed containing_schema, so two expansions never merge. I had this recorded as an open blocker on a01 and that was simply wrong — 4081560 predates my own 2D.

VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. I spliced real generic-host field rows into a scratch copy of HEAD and validated: zero structural violations, specifically no field_unresolved_schema and no wire_context_mismatch. Then I landed two of them for real in 1828232 (ExportLeaf<T>.target_identity and ExportLeaf<T>.local_strong_ref_projection), gates green, e2e 94/0. So the path is proven end to end, not merely legal on paper.

WHAT YOU CAN DERIVE DIRECTLY, for your 8 Tier B rows:
 1. Write containing_schema as the EXACT census schema_owner, generic signature included — e.g. "TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role:Local|Meta|Shard>", not the bare family. The target source_key must match the census key byte-for-byte, and the census key carries the signature.
 2. row_id derivation is the one real gotcha, and it will fail your first attempt if you guess. lower_kebab renders the signature's punctuation as separators, so `ExportLeaf<T>` becomes `export-leaf-t`. Do not hand-write these: land the row, read catalog_row_id_derived_mismatch, and adopt the expected value it prints. That is how I got mine.
 3. construction_order must equal the containing kind's, per identity.rs:1681 — forced, not chosen.
 4. If a row's exact_wire_type is a type that PREDATES the A10 erratum (a builtin, or a wire type like RemoteObjectIdentity), the frozen-history witness cannot see it via post_erratum_union(&field.exact_wire_type), because that predicate matches union NAMES. Such rows need an explicit (containing_schema, stable_name) retain in idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen, plus the field-count assertion bumped. This bit me in 2D and again in 2F; it will bite your Tier B rows for any builtin-typed member.

SEPARATELY — the five ExportLeaf<T> shorthand member types, which are the a01 half of fgdb-eik0. I am landing these as 2G the moment the catalog token frees. Every one is DERIVED from landed a01 precedent rather than invented, which is the point:
    export_projection_version          u16 / 2          format_major, format_minor and
                                                        incarnation_continuity_profile_id are all u16/2
    object_specific_scalar_projection  bytes / 16777216 canonical_configuration_bytes precedent; the
                                                        layout is fixed per expansion of T, so the bound
                                                        is the declared per-kind ceiling, not a width
    target_closure_inventory_digest    digest256 / 32   three landed instances, unanimous;
                                                        digest_class=target, scalar/none — the
                                                        RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence shape, not the
                                                        weak_digest one, because a generic T has no
                                                        concrete target schema to point at
    authority_ledger_floor             u64 / 8          authority_retention_floor,
                                                        minimum_authority_checkpoint_floor and
                                                        authority_order_index are all u64/8
    quorum_signatures                  bytes / 65536    two landed instances in this same release
                                                        family, plus authority_quorum_signatures
Tags are source positions in the eight-member body at a01:1400, so the body stays positional (1 domain, 2 and 5 already landed in 1828232). Rehearsed green against HEAD: 0 structural, 0 pin violations at 541 targets, identity suite 64 passed. Contest any of the five here if you disagree; they are recorded as contestable in the same way a01's shard_id=u32 / GraphId=u64 / BranchId=u64 / release_nonce-as-bytes rulings were.

The two one_digest_signer_lock_ref members are NOT covered by this ruling and stay open on fgdb-eik0: they have no named target schema anywhere in the plan and the field appears across the SameGroupCertificate families, so that one is genuinely cross-slice.

YOUR TimeAuthorityRegistry ORDER BEAD: you hold the catalog token now, so you are the right owner to file it — bead creation needs that token anyway for the architecture pin re-freeze, and batching it into a commit you are already making is strictly cheaper than me guessing at your intent. Per ADDENDUM 2, also take the `beads` token for the flush+stage+commit and hold it for seconds.

USE THE RECORD-LEVEL SWEEP CHECK, not a file-level diffstat:

    git diff --cached -- .beads/issues.jsonl | grep "^[+-]{" | jq -r ".id" | sort -u

If any bead ID you do not own appears, do not commit — wait for that agent to land first. I am flagging this specifically because a diffstat CANNOT catch it and I nearly told you to rely on one: in the c4cc90a incident the committing agent did run `git diff --cached --stat -- .beads/`, saw "1 file changed, 7 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)", and reasonably read that as its own single comment. It was that comment PLUS three of my brand-new beads and three foreign comment updates. In a JSONL export every record is exactly one line, so a one-line comment edit and a one-line brand-new bead are indistinguishable by line count. Only the ID list distinguishes them.

title: Gate G0 — Constitutional Contracts: registries, claim types, and the format freeze
description:
## What & scope
Gate G0 — Constitutional Contracts — is the root of the entire FrankenGraphDB program: before a single line of Genesis implementation code is written, every semantic choice that any workstream could otherwise invent locally is decided, frozen, and machine-registered. G0 lands: the threat/trust model; the six-bet vocabulary; the exact twenty-invariant spine with its clause-granular activation contract; `invariants.toml`, `evidence.toml`, `slo.toml`; the four disjoint identity registries (`logical_object_kinds.toml`, `physical_record_kinds.toml`, `bootstrap_frames.toml`, `wire_types.toml`) — §5.1 defines the restore-only fifth identity class `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` beside them, which G0 also lands — plus the exhaustive cross-indexes `durable_fields.toml`, `command_contracts.toml`, `command_type_classification.toml`, `state_payload_fields.toml`; registered BodyDigest/transcript recipes and acyclic construction/reference checks; every reserved W12 kind and role-tagged Raft/root/checkpoint variant; the operation-cost registry (Appendix G); frozen tagged `LanguageContract`s for every advertised surface; proof-lane manifests; the per-posture external-authority footprint; and the entire G0 decision batch (SnapshotQuery, fused autocommit arm, BranchRetire, ErasureCut, ExpiryContract, AllocationContinuityProfile, activation batching, identity-column codecs, PackedObjectGroup, tiered FEC, DIFF, externally_verifiable markings, sync-obligation column, Point decision, fgdb-reference allowlist, ArchiveReadOnlyOpen, replay/chaos exposure rows, freshness reservations, RaftHardFrame spike). Before G0 can pass, generated clause coverage also fixes the eleven §19 pre-pass semantic areas (normalized valid-time slice algebra/disclosure; first-escape/finalization allocation; escrow conservation/custody/transfer; complete `SecurityStateBinding` on every authority-bearing schema; state-shaped independent result and durable artifact-output ownership with explicit release; transaction ownership/reattachment/expiry; one external DP charge/seed/Meta-noise lineage; audit terminal freeze/plan abandonment plus the gap-free visibility pipeline; bulk logical-manifest/staging and derived shadow-build activation; exact Local/Meta/Shard GC physical start/cancel/progress/completion; durable-format advertise/activate/first-write/rewrite/decoder-retirement), each with command/state registry rows, construction-DAG recipes, checkpoint/floor/backup/restore/GC classes, checker and negative-test entrypoints, and feature-disable behavior (detailed in g0-command-contracts). It also generates and validates README/AGENTS as checked release artifacts.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Every failure mode this plan is built to escape — Neo4j's fossilized JVM decisions, JanusGraph's KV impedance mismatch, Kùzu's abandonment — traces to semantics decided implicitly, locally, or late. G0 exists because the plan's method is registry-driven generation with **no second source of truth**: hand-written lists in prose are checked readability projections regenerated and byte-compared by CI, never normative. This is what makes B5 (determinism/evidence/calibrated adaptivity) structural: claims have types (§1 constraint 11), costs are registered claims (constraint 12), and a weaker claim class may never enforce a stronger one. It is what makes B1's One Version Universe honest — every durable byte has exactly one identity class and one registered schema before anything writes it. It is what makes the six bets composable at all: W1–W12 all consume G0's registries as generated code, so omission cannot degrade into an unreachable recovery state, and "no workstream may invent a missing semantic choice locally" is enforceable, not aspirational.

## Design — normative detail
G0's constitution has four pillars. (1) **Claim-type constitution**: every load-bearing statement is exactly one of `invariant`, `proof`, `bounded_model`, `statistical`, `slo`, `benchmark`; `invariants.toml` holds only exact safety/liveness invariants, `evidence.toml`/`slo.toml` carry statistical and empirical claims. (2) **The twenty-invariant spine**: Appendix F contains exactly twenty top-level invariant IDs (FG-INV-01..20); G0 materializes each as one or more stable subordinate clause records, each recording exact statement, activation predicate, dependencies, resolvable enforcement and negative-test entrypoints, model/proof scope or liveness fairness assumptions, owner, first gate, status, and `waiver=forbidden`. CI verifies the twenty-ID/table hash, dependency DAG, checker/test existence, and the compiled-plus-negotiated activation closure; every reachable clause must be live, otherwise the corresponding capability is absent. (3) **Identity/command registries**: five disjoint identity classes generated from checked-in schema annotations, a total command-contract bijection, and cross-plane durable-state-slot registry, so every reachability/GC/checkpoint/backup/fuzz walker is generated, never hand-maintained. (4) **The decision batch**: G0 decides and freezes every closed-union arm, registry row, and reserved field the current revision entails — implementation is permitted to trail the frozen rows, but the rows exist first. G0 finally runs self-containment, dependency-DAG, justification, and fresh-review checks, and synchronizes README/AGENTS summaries whose normative examples are validated against the registries; any contradictory summary blocks G0.

## Invariants & claim types
This epic owns the meta-invariant machinery itself: the Appendix F preamble law (exactly twenty IDs; subordinate clause keys create no new IDs; `waiver=forbidden` on every clause) and §1 constraints 11 and 12 (claims have types; costs are registered claims — every operation class has an Appendix G row and every §17 gate must be derivable from it). Nothing in this epic is itself slo/benchmark class; its artifacts are the registries that give every later slo/benchmark/FG-CFG/FG-EVID claim a typed home.

## Interactions
Child anchors: g0-claim-registries, g0-invariant-spine, g0-identity-registries, g0-command-contracts, g0-cost-registry, g0-language-contracts, g0-threat-model, g0-format-arms, g0-doc-sync. Every W1+ epic consumes G0 output: w1-generated-parsers builds encoders/decoders from the registries; w2a/w2b/w2c implement the frozen Chronicle rows; w5-parsers pin g0-language-contracts; w9-threat-tokens implement g0-threat-model's authority types; perf-cost-ci enforces g0-cost-registry's three laws; verif-reference honors the g0 dependency allowlist; gate-genesis cannot open until G0 passes.

## Success Criteria
G0 passes when: all named TOML registries exist, parse, and pass schema validation; the twenty-ID table hash matches Appendix F; every reachable invariant clause resolves a checker and a negative-test entrypoint; the generation bijections (command arms ↔ contract rows ↔ handlers; gates ↔ cost rows) pass; every decision-batch artifact has its frozen rows; README/AGENTS regenerate byte-identically from the frozen plan; and the self-containment/dependency-DAG/justification/fresh-review CI jobs are green. A dedicated `g0-verify` CI script logs, per registry: row counts, hash, orphan/unreachable entries, and bijection diffs — failing loudly with the exact offending row.

Named unit/property/fuzz suites: `g0_registry_schema_valid_<registry>` (one per TOML), `g0_twenty_id_hash_pin`, `g0_bijection_command_arms_handlers`, `g0_bijection_gates_cost_rows`, `g0_decision_batch_complete` (item-by-item against §19 line 1313), `g0_clause_coverage_eleven_areas`, property test `g0_clause_dag_acyclic` (randomized clause-record orderings never admit a cycle), and fuzz test `g0_registry_toml_fuzz` (mutated registry bytes are rejected with a typed error, never a panic). E2E: `scripts/g0_e2e.sh` exercises the entire gate on a clean checkout — regenerate every registry from annotations, validate schemas, run every bijection/coverage/hash check, regenerate README/AGENTS and byte-compare, then run the self-containment/dependency-DAG/justification/fresh-review passes — exiting nonzero on the first failure and emitting a machine-readable `g0-verify.report.json`. DETAILED LOGGING (mandatory for the harness and every checker): structured JSONL events `{check_id, registry, row_count, content_hash, duration_ms, outcome, offending_ids[]}` per check; every failure names the exact offending row/clause and prints the diff hunk; the final summary event records per-registry content hashes so any later run is byte-comparable against the frozen baseline.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: "land registries incrementally as code needs them" (that is precisely the local-invention failure mode); prose-normative specs with best-effort code review (the frankensqlite lesson is that generated bijection checks are the only durable enforcement); waiverable invariants (a waiver culture converts invariants into slo rows silently — hence `waiver=forbidden`). Risk: G0 is front-loaded design work with no runnable database — mitigated by the decision-batch discipline that lets implementation trail frozen rows, and by §19's rule that G0 is a gate, not a phase of code.

## Provenance
§19 (G0 paragraphs, lines 1311–1313), §1, Appendix F, Appendix G, §18.1, §5.1.

title: Epic: observability & operations — Observatory, system graph, doctor, SLO wiring (§16)
description:
## What & scope
Epic for §16's observability and operations plane as owned by this region: the `ObservatoryRegion` telemetry/early-warning stack (`obs-observatory`), the queryable system graph with its declared Prism degraded mode (`obs-system-graph`), `fgdb doctor` and the ops verbs (`obs-doctor`), and `slo.toml` wiring with alerts and attribution (`obs-slo`). Explicit boundaries: §16.6 admission ledgers belong to `w10-qos`; §16.6 backup/restore machinery to `w11-backup`/`w11-restore`; §16.7 durable-format capability/activation to `w11-format-activation`; §16.8 external-authority surface to `w9-authority-surface`. This epic wires their observable surfaces, not their mechanisms.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 (agent-native): the database dogfoods its own data model as its ops surface — sessions, transactions, queries, plans, waits, compaction jobs, and subscriptions are a read-only temporal property graph queryable in GQL, so agents (and humans) debug the database with the database. B5: every alert and estimate is model-qualified — Little's-law checks and shadow prices are diagnostics under stationarity/model assumptions living in evidence/SLO registries, never the safety-invariant registry; hard safety comes only from bounded queues, resource reservations, cancellation checkpoints, and deterministic fallback controls. Market: operators get an honest ops story — quiescence is asserted only from exact terminal ledger state, probabilistic estimates name their model, and degraded modes are typed, never silent.

## Design — normative detail
Process tree (Spork supervision, restart topologies declared): `FgdbRootRegion` supervises `ChronicleRegion` (WriteCoordinator, scrubber, checkpointer), `StrataRegion` (sealers, compactors per partition-group, GC/demotion), `RippleRegion` (view circuits, subscription fan-out, stats maintainers, index feeders), `BeaconRegion` (index builders, HNSW mergers, path-index manager), `PrismRegion` (analytics bulkhead), `WardenRegion` (policy/revocation authority, lease issuer, DP coordinator, audit anchor), `AegisRegion` (raft, replication streams, donor service), `FabricRegion` (listeners, sessions, admission), and `ObservatoryRegion` (metrics export, task inspector, spectral health, deadline monitor).

Telemetry (§16.2): asupersync metrics + OTel export, authorized/redacted trace context, `EXPLAIN` and `SHOW` surfaces covering transactions, compaction debt, Ripple/index watermarks, buffer residency, resource reservations, obligations, GC membership epoch, key epochs, and commit phases. Early warning (§16.3): wait-graph, futurelock, autocorrelation/variance, and coupled-controller monitors give model-qualified alerts; `FG-CFG-02` rejects defaults predicted unstable by a versioned fluid model with sensitivity analysis — it does not claim every real workload lies in that model. Ops verbs (§16.4): online `COMPACT`/`SCRUB`/`REBUILD INDEX`/`ANALYZE`; `fgdb doctor`; support bundles with replay-completeness/redaction grades; cancellation exposing phase and deterministic drain progress. System graph (§16.5): read-only, access-controlled temporal property graph with the `FeatureDisabled` degraded mode when `fgdb-prism` is posture-disabled, and the §16.3 early-warning wait-cycle probe owned by `fgdb-observatory` with its own small bounded cycle check so the observability plane never imports the analytics bulkhead for an alerting primitive.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row is created here; the binding discipline is negative: nothing in this epic may be claimed as an invariant. `FG-CFG-02` (modeled controller stability: model/equilibrium, parameter uncertainty, predicted margin, deterministic hard guards and soak results) and `FG-CFG-03` (view/index staleness SLO feasibility: arrival/service assumptions, resource reservation, predicted envelope, actual watermark and fallback policy) are `slo.toml`-class configuration-model claims; scrub/corpus health evidence is `FG-EVID-02`; telemetry-derived quantities are diagnostics. Quiescence claims require exact terminal obligation/resource-ledger state — never a probabilistic estimator.

## Interactions
`obs-observatory` is the substrate; `obs-system-graph` and `obs-doctor` build on it; `obs-slo` wires `g0-claim-registries` slo rows and `w9-authority-surface` availability lines into alerts. Consumes redaction/authorization from `w9-enforcement`/`w9-redaction-erasure`; feeds `perf-bench-*` (law 3 compaction disclosure needs Observatory counters) and `verif-replay-products` (support bundles).

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when: the process tree boots under Spork with declared restart topologies and a supervision-tree kill test recovers every region; `SHOW`/`EXPLAIN` surfaces return every enumerated domain; the system graph answers the canonical wait-for GQL query and returns typed `FeatureDisabled` with Prism disabled; `fgdb doctor` passes its full verification list on a healthy store and fails precisely on seeded corruptions; alerts fire from slo.toml rows with attribution and every alert names its model. E2E scripts log region lifecycle events, alert provenance (rule id, model version, inputs), and redaction decisions.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: observability becomes a covert channel — mitigated by capability-scoped redaction (§12.6) and secret hygiene (seeds/keys redacted from metrics, errors, crashpacks, decision cards). Risk: alert fatigue from model-qualified monitors — every alert carries its model and sensitivity. Rejected: importing Prism analytics into the alerting path (bulkhead violation); safety claims from telemetry (quota authority is the durable ledger, "neither local session counters nor telemetry are quota authority"); silent feature degradation.

## Provenance
§16.1-16.5 (1177-1193), §16.8 boundary (1222-1228), §12.6/§12.8 touchpoints, Appendix F FG-CFG/FG-EVID rows (3151-3165).

title: Epic: performance doctrine — registry-derived gates, six laws, deterministic benches (§17)
description:
## What & scope
Epic for the FrankenGraphDB performance program: implement §17's performance doctrine — the full gate table, the six standing laws, the pinned-manifest discipline, and the Appendix G cost-registry CI laws — as bench binaries, committed baselines, and CI gates. Children: `perf-bench-core` (load/ingest/point-read/scan/join/LDBC), `perf-bench-anatomy` (lifecycle command/entry counts, ordered-sync counts, byte economy), `perf-bench-history` (time-travel, branch/snapshot, recovery, tier churn), `perf-bench-governance` (audit-Required plane-segment gates vs simulated authority), `perf-bench-scale` (sequencer/cursor scale, 10k-branch churn, endurance, compaction debt, memory), `perf-cost-ci` (Appendix G generation + three CI laws), `perf-freshness-vector` (vector/temporal/freshness/tail gates + FG-CAL rows). Out of scope: the deterministic harness runtime (`verif-perf-apparatus`) and `slo.toml` alert wiring (`obs-slo`).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Performance claims here are *registered* claims: §1 constraint 12 extends §1.11's correctness-claim registry to cost, so no mechanism accretes protocol weight without a priced Appendix G row and no benchmark flatters the system by measuring less than the protocol does. This is B5 applied to performance: seeded deterministic workloads, replayable regressions, disclosed policy epochs. The gate table serves every bet — B2 (scan/ingest/compaction-debt gates at Sortledton-and-beyond levels), B3 (factorized and WCOJ gates within 2x of static-CSR systems), B4 (view-maintenance and freshness gates), B1 (branch/snapshot/time-travel gates proving the One Version Universe is cheap), B6 (the `SnapshotQuery` class priced at 0 commands / 0 barriers so agent-scale point reads are structurally cheap). Market: LDBC leadership runs are the publishable receipts (§15.7; "ambition includes the receipts").

## Design — normative detail
Reference machine: 32-core/64-thread, 256 GB RAM, PCIe-4 NVMe, single node. A gate is a provisional `EmpiricalGate`, activated only when its benchmark manifest pins: CPU/microcode; kernel/filesystem/mount options; NVMe model/firmware and the *measured* fsync distribution; toolchain/build; database configuration; graph/schema; transaction size and concurrency; retention/FEC/encryption/index policy; cold/warm state; result consumption; and the statistical comparison rule. Every gate additionally declares its **operation class** (a row of the Appendix G operation-cost registry) and its **counting unit** (client-visible requests versus internal probes), and must be derivable from that row: a latency gate below its class's ordered-barrier count x the manifest's pinned measured fsync p50, or a throughput gate above the apply ceiling its sequenced-command count implies, fails CI as a registry divergence (§1 constraint 12), never as a missed benchmark. External "best" comparisons pin a publication, version, dataset, and configuration; moving or unavailable comparators cannot be CI gates.

Six standing laws bind every published number: (1) **no benchmark-only semantics** — durability, isolation, and result consumption match the declared production mode; (2) **distributions, not averages** — p50/p95/p99/p99.9 and worst hot-key behavior are always reported, with extreme quantiles carrying their fitted-tail confidence intervals rather than raw sample maxima; (3) **never hide compaction** — foreground latency during compaction, checkpoint, GC, and index build is part of the result; (4) **memory is a first-class metric** — bytes per live edge include versions, indexes, witnesses, and allocator slack, not just payload; (5) **adaptive numbers disclose their policy epoch** — any result produced under a non-fallback policy names it, and the fallback's number is published beside it; (6) **no unpriced protocol weight** — every gate names its Appendix G operation class and counting unit, every published number is checked against that row's derived floor, and any change that adds sequenced semantic commands, ordered durability barriers, external-authority interactions, or per-object identity structure updates the operation-cost registry in the same change; CI rejects the divergence.

Method (normative): every gate has a bench binary, a committed baseline, a variance budget, and a flamegraph artifact on regression; the harness is deterministic (seeded workloads, pinned schedules) so regressions replay. Performance work follows the asupersync discipline: profile -> remove one contention/allocation -> re-verify determinism and cancel-correctness -> commit with evidence — one lever per change, never a bundle. Waivers (§15.6): correctness, security, durable-format, recovery, authorization, invariant-checker, and required conformance gates are **nonwaivable**; a public, expiring waiver may cover only a named empirical performance threshold, statistical-evidence threshold, or non-safety coverage budget, records owner/evidence/reduced claim/expiry/fallback, and cannot weaken an invariant. Complexity-witness locks: an operator whose instrumented operation count exceeds its registered bound on an in-domain fixture fails CI.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row binds this epic directly; its constitution is the claim-type discipline: every microsecond or throughput budget is an `slo.toml` row keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`; Appendix G registry rows are exact structural counts, or exact bounds in declared configuration parameters for tilde-ranged columns, enforced by the same generation bijection that governs command contracts; the maintenance-stream capacity model is a configuration-model claim (`FG-CFG-04`), never an invariant; calibration/evidence rows (`FG-CAL-01/02/03`, `FG-EVID-01/03/04`) live in `evidence.toml`; `FG-CFG-01/02/03/04` and all performance/durability-model/controller targets live in `slo.toml`. `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness obligations — performance numbers never enter it.

## Interactions
Rests on `g0-cost-registry` (Appendix G artifacts) and `verif-perf-apparatus` (deterministic harness). `perf-cost-ci` enforces gate<->registry derivability for every child; `obs-slo` consumes gate values as alerting rows; `risk-register` carries the hardening<->cost same-change rule.

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when: every §17 gate row has a bench binary + pinned manifest + committed baseline + variance budget in CI; the derivability/coverage/same-change CI laws demonstrably fail on seeded violations; a six-laws report linter rejects any published number missing distributions, compaction disclosure, memory census, policy epoch, or operation class/counting unit; regression replay from seed reproduces a flagged regression; waiver machinery enforces expiry and cannot attach to a nonwaivable gate class. Detailed-logging bar: every gate run logs manifest digest, seed and schedule id, baseline id, measured distributions, variance verdict, derivability arithmetic (ordered-barrier count × pinned fsync p50; sequenced-command apply ceiling), compaction/GC/checkpoint/index-build activity during the run, and the memory census, so every published number is post-hoc reconstructible from run logs; the regression-replay e2e demonstrates seed → identical flagged result → attached flamegraph with all steps logged.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: provisional numbers ossify into folklore before manifests pin real hardware — the `EmpiricalGate` activation rule prevents this. Risk: comparator drift — pinned-comparator rule; moving comparators are reports, not gates. Rejected: benchmark-only durability/isolation modes; averages-only reporting; gating on live external systems; treating registry counts as tuning targets ("any operation class that wants a smaller row must change the protocol first, and this registry in the same change").

## Provenance
§17 (lines 1232-1274), §15.6, §15.7, §1 constraint 12, Appendix G (3169-3193).

title: Verification & calibration doctrine (B5): sim-first, oracles, formal anchors, Sextant
description:
## What & scope
The B5 verification-and-calibration epic for the 1.0 product through G4. It integrates §15.0-§15.6 over Local, language/storage, G3 Warden/Fabric/multi-member behavior, claim-typed evidence, replay products, and performance discipline. It uses asupersync's lab/LDFI/delta-debug/dual-run/trace assets rather than rebuilding them. Post-1.0 W12 Meta/Shard/global verification is explicitly excluded and owned by `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5 (determinism, evidence, calibrated adaptivity) is a founding bet: every claim the system makes is claim-typed, every failure replays from a seed, every adaptive policy is inspectable and has a deterministic fallback. B6 depends on it — agents consume machine-checkable evidence, graded replay bundles, and honest conformance matrices, not prose. The other bets are enforced through this epic: B1's commit-stream invariants get crash matrices and TLA+ models; B2's seal/compaction gets metamorphic equivalence suites; B3's unified execution gets the reference-engine differential plus TCK/ISO matrices; B4's incrementality gets the derivative-equals-batch differential. §15.7's publishing ambition ("ambition includes the receipts") — six papers, including "Calibrated adaptivity: anytime-valid statistical governance of a self-tuning DBMS" — requires this stack to exist and be honest. §3.5 fixes the adopt/adapt/reject posture for every piece of statistical machinery used here.

## Design — normative detail
The claim-type constitution binds the whole epic. Every evidence envelope carries a `ClaimClass` from the closed union: `SafetyInvariant` (must hold on every execution; failure is a correctness defect) | `FormalModelClaim` (theorem or model-check result with abstraction, bounds, and refinement status) | `StatisticalClaim` (population, sampling/selection rule, alpha, power/effective sample size, and assumptions) | `ConfigurationModelClaim` (model version, fitted inputs, sensitivity, and validity domain) | `EmpiricalGate` (fixture, machine/profile, sample count, variance budget, and comparison rule). Registry split: `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness obligations; `evidence.toml` contains `FG-CAL-*` and `FG-EVID-*`; `slo.toml` contains `FG-CFG-*`, performance, durability-model, and controller targets. Never-mislabel law: sampled e-processes are statistical sentinels in `evidence.toml`, never the enforcement column of `invariants.toml`; a monitor that drives no named decision is dead code, but binding it to a decision does not make it an invariant. Independence law: every invariant has at least one checker outside the optimized component it checks, where practical. Appendix F holds exactly twenty top-level invariant IDs (FG-INV-01..20); G0 materializes each as stable subordinate clauses recording exact statement, activation predicate, dependencies, resolvable checker/negative-test entrypoints, proof/model scope and bounds, owner, first gate, status, and `waiver=forbidden`; every reachable clause must be live, otherwise the corresponding capability is absent. §15.6's waiver law: correctness, security, durable-format, recovery, authorization, invariant-checker, and required conformance gates are nonwaivable; only a named empirical performance threshold, statistical-evidence threshold, or non-safety coverage budget may carry a public, expiring waiver.

## Invariants & claim types
This epic owns the live enforcement side of every Appendix F clause activated by the 1.0/G0-G4 capability closure. It supplies independent Local SCC/history, root/recovery crash matrices, reference plus Lean visibility, obligation leak/quiescence, G3 external-authority/protocol/HA campaigns, and all 1.0 claim/evidence/configuration registries. The same twenty top-level IDs may contain W12-activated subordinate clauses, but those remain disabled/pending here and become live only through `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike`; registry presence is never coverage.

## Interactions
Children: verif-sim, verif-reference, Local verif-oracles, Local verif-torture, 1.0 differential/conformance/fuzzing, 1.0 formal anchors, Sextant, replay products, perf apparatus, plus `fgdb-g3-protocol-authority-oracles-w27f` and `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4` for concrete W9-W11 integration. Genesis/G1-G4 cite this epic. Gate W12 cites only the separate W12 verification epic in addition to its implementation epic; it cannot inherit a green G4.

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when all eleven dependency tasks are complete and the 1.0 closure is green: twenty-ID/table hash and phase-aware clause DAG checks pass; every activated G0-G4 clause resolves to independent checker/negative/evidence symbols; disabled W12 clauses are provably absent from the 1.0 capability manifest; every G0-G4 gate cites correctly typed evidence; reference allowlist and chaos-facade boundaries pass; no statistical claim appears in `invariants.toml`; no invariant is enforced solely by its optimized subject.
- E2E rollup: boot a whole Local three-member server under sim and real-process modes, run a mixed reference-checked workload through each supported adapter, exercise one external authority, audit/DP/protected-output state, leader loss, and injected fault, then require legal recovery and an executable §15.1 replay artifact. A boundary negative attempts to import W12 evidence and must be rejected.
- Detailed-logging bar: every child emits structured JSONL `{claim_or_clause_id,ClaimClass,phase_owner_bead,first_required_gate,row_state,evidence_refs,seed_schedule_or_bounds,expected,actual,verdict}`. The rollup validates ancestry against registries; unlogged, phase-misattributed, pending-as-live, or unreplayable enforcement counts as unenforced.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: post-hoc QA, one monolithic suite, self-checking, unbounded formal ambition, statistics mislabeled as invariants, or letting the 1.0 epic absorb W12. Risks are controlled by nonwaivable gates, phase-aware ownership, trace export, dual runs, mutation tests, and the separate W12 epic.

## Provenance
§15 (lines 1102-1174), §3.5 (159-183), §18.1-18.2, §19 gates, Appendix F.


## Phase boundary
This epic ends at G4. `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike` is the sole W12 verification rollup. No dependency from G4 to that epic is permitted; Gate W12 must depend on it directly.

title: Epic W1: Bedrock + security foundations — the closed-universe crate layer
description:
## What & scope
W1 lands the foundation layer of the `fgdb-*` workspace, on which every later workstream (W2 Chronicle onward) is built: `fgdb-types`, `fgdb-bigint`, `fgdb-delta-types`, `fgdb-claim`, `fgdb-evidence`, `fgdb-resource` (foundation value/claim types), `fgdb-authz-types` + `fgdb-policy` (nonconstructible permits and the restricted verifier IR), `fgdb-crypto`, `fgdb-codec`, `fgdb-collections`, `fgdb-sketch`, `fgdb-calibrate`, the three unsafe islands `fgdb-unsafe-simd`/`fgdb-unsafe-arena`/`fgdb-unsafe-vfs` with their CI-enforced ledger, and the registry-generated format encoders/decoders with golden vectors and mutation corpora. W1 depends only on G0's frozen constitutional registries; it produces no durable database state itself.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The foundation audit (§2) is the reason W1 is small enough to be credible. **asupersync (~580 KLOC)** is the operating system: region tree/obligations/`Outcome` lattice/three-lane scheduler (every background service and every parallel query is a region); `Cx` capability contexts (constraint 3: every function that performs I/O, takes a lock, allocates from a shared arena, or can block accepts `&Cx` — swap the `Cx` and the entire database runs under the lab runtime with virtual time, deterministic scheduling, and fault injection; this is what makes B5 structural); the lab runtime with DPOR/chaos/trace replay/crashpacks; the Lean/TLA+ formal layer; RFC 6330 systematic RaptorQ (never reimplemented here); ATP transport; the entire TCP/QUIC/HTTP/WebSocket/TLS/gRPC stack; cancel-correct channels and combinators; Spork/OTP supervision; `remote.rs` leases/idempotency/HLC; macaroons and authenticated types; fs/VFS/io_uring reactor, region heaps with generational handles, EBR; the e-process/conformal/decision-contract statistical governance machinery; SWIM+Lifeguard, Merkle anti-entropy, coded symbol distribution, CRDT ledgers; LDFI/delta-debugging/dual-run/~24-oracle verification tooling; e-graph rewrite certificates and the (min,+) latency algebra. **franken_networkx (~247 KLOC)** is the algorithm brain and semantics doctrine: 550+ algorithm functions as catalog and semantics oracle; the `GraphView` compatibility target (explicitly NOT a zero-copy match today); CGSE — 13 `TieBreakPolicy` variants, `ComplexityWitness {n,m,dominant_term,observed_count,policy,seed,decision_path_blake3}`, `WitnessLedger`, Strict/Hardened modes — the B5 determinism doctrine generalized from algorithms to queries; fuzz-hardened legacy-format parsers; deterministic generators; RaptorQ sidecar/scrub precedent; NetworkX-parity ordering reference. **frankensqlite (~1.28 MLOC)** is the architectural donor under the dissection-not-linking doctrine (§2.3): adopt its designs — page-granularity MVCC becomes block-granularity MVCC; page-SSI + first-committer-wins + eager locking is a donor pattern whose deadlock-freedom/soundness do NOT transfer by analogy; intent logs + deterministic rebase ladder; native-mode ECS (content-addressed objects, `SymbolRecord` envelopes, root publication, capsules/markers); `WriteCoordinator` shape; ARC pool mechanics; time-travel/checkpoint+delta thinking; Argon2id KEK hierarchy as a starting point only; the conformance/differential/metamorphic QA house style — and where a module is genuinely object-agnostic, fork it into an `fgdb-*` crate with attribution, never linking `fsqlite-*` and dragging SQLite's page/B-tree world along, because graph objects are not SQLite pages. §2.4/§18.2 then names what none of the foundations provide and W1 begins building: compression codecs, sketches, radix/succinct structures, crypto profiles, calibration scores/ledgers — the front edge of the estimated 275–440 KLOC of new Rust (smaller than frankensqlite). The closed universe (constraint 1: only `core`/`alloc`/`std`, nightly, asupersync, `fnx-*`, design-level frankensqlite reuse; no serde/tokio/rocksdb/arrow/tantivy/hnswlib) is the moat: the entire dependency surface is auditable, deterministic under lab, and owned. All six bets rest on this layer; B5 most directly.

## Design — normative detail
Workspace rules that W1 makes concrete: (1) constraint 2 — every ordinary crate root and the workspace default use `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; raw-pointer code lives only in `fgdb-unsafe-*` islands with `deny(unsafe_code)` roots plus narrowly scoped, ledgered `allow` sites. (2) Constraint 1's packaging boundary — the Python package may consume `fnx-python`, but `fgdb-*` crates may never add a direct PyO3 dependency; engine, server, CLI, and durable formats stay free of that boundary. (3) Constraint 9 (prohibited shortcuts, constitutional): no serde-derived enum as a durable format, no parser-interprets-AST engine, no detached background thread — early code may implement a subset of a final abstraction, never a substitute. (4) Nightly pinned per repo; portable-SIMD isolated behind `fgdb-codec`/kernel traits with scalar fallbacks (§20 risk row). (5) Layering per §18.1 with Cargo-enforced boundaries; foundation crates are the only crates `fgdb-reference` may import (its allowlist: foundation value/type/claim crates plus G0-generated registries and golden vectors, nothing else; the parser crates `fgdb-gql`/`fgdb-cypher` are §15.4's one recorded sharing exception, exercised end-to-end by the TCK and the differential corpora).

## Invariants & claim types
Constraint 11 (claims have types) is implemented by `fgdb-claim`: every load-bearing statement is exactly one of `invariant`, `proof`, `bounded_model`, `statistical`, `slo`, `benchmark`; a weaker class may inform policy but may not enforce or justify a stronger one; `invariants.toml` holds only exact safety/liveness invariants, `evidence.toml`/`slo.toml` carry the rest. FG-INV-12's scalar-coherence clause (canonical scalar equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding are coherent) binds `fgdb-types`. FG-INV-09's digest-class clause (every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe) binds the generated parsers. The unsafe-boundary ledger is itself a CI-enforced constitutional artifact materialized at G0.

## Interactions
Children: w1-foundation-types, w1-authz-policy, w1-crypto, w1-codecs, w1-collections, w1-sketch-calibrate, w1-unsafe-ledger, w1-generated-parsers, w1-format-test-corpora (the test-artifact half split from w1-generated-parsers). Consumers: every W2a/W2b/W2c/W3/W4/W5+ anchor; verif-reference (allowlist limited to these crates); verif-sim (runs everything under the lab `Cx`); perf-cost-ci (constraint 12 cost registry discipline applies to anything W1 ships that adds barriers or identity structure).

## Success Criteria
Workspace compiles with workspace-level `forbid(unsafe_code)` and pinned nightly; CI enforces the unsafe ledger bijection, the registry/codegen bijections, and the `fgdb-reference` dependency allowlist (the allowlist rule and CI job are defined here, but the check activates once `verif-reference` lands — that crate is not a W1 deliverable and is outside this epic's closure; enforced no later than gate-genesis); every child bead's own gates pass; no `fgdb-*` crate has a dependency outside the constraint-1 allowlist (automated dependency-universe CI check). E2E: `w1_foundation_e2e` — a workspace-level integration script that builds every W1 crate on the pinned nightly, then drives one value through the full foundation chain under the lab runtime with a fixed seed: construct canonical scalars (`fgdb-types`) -> encode with a registry-generated encoder -> keyed-BLAKE3 digest (`fgdb-crypto`) -> verify against the checked-in golden vector -> compress/decompress through `fgdb-codec` -> index/probe through `fgdb-collections` -> evaluate one `PolicyIr` decision to an `AuthorizedMutationPermit`; the run executes twice and the canonical outputs must be byte-identical. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): every CI enforcement job emits a machine-readable manifest — unsafe-ledger bijection result (sites/rows/orphans), `fgdb-reference` allowlist verdict per import (emitted once `verif-reference` exists; an explicit `crate_absent` marker before then), dependency-universe scan listing each crate's resolved dependency set, registry epochs and generated-code digests — and the e2e run logs the seed, toolchain hash, and each stage's input/output digests so any cross-stage divergence is attributable from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
§20 rows: in-house cryptography failing despite vectors (mitigation: prefer audited foundation primitives, mandatory constant-time/misuse verification, external release audit); nightly MSRV churn (pinned toolchain, SIMD isolation). Rejected: linking `fsqlite-*` wholesale (graph objects are not SQLite pages; correctness does not transfer by analogy); reopening the dependency universe for convenience crates (destroys auditability/determinism moat); JVM/GC/mmap-as-durability/generic-KV fossils (constraint 7).

## Provenance
§1 constraints 1–3, 9; §2.1–2.4; §3.5; §18.1–18.2; §19 W1 row; §20.

title: Fabric (W10): embedded API, fgdbd, FGP protocol, adapters, and agent-native delivery
description:
## What & scope
W10 delivers every user-facing surface of FrankenGraphDB — the Fabric plane. Children: the embedded `fgdb::Database` API with its explicit ownership contract (`w10-embedded`); the `fgdb-python` binding that maps that contract onto Python idiom (`w10-python`); the FGP native wire protocol per Appendix D (`w10-fgp-core`), with wire-safe public projections and the taint checker (`w10-wire-projections`) and the flow-control/send-obligation write path (`w10-flow-send-obligations`); the four durable authority-bearing capabilities plus tombstones and lineage (`w10-capabilities`) and durable transaction-ownership leases with reattach/renew/expiry (`w10-txn-ownership`); the result, artifact-output, and protected-error delivery state machines (`w10-result-machines`); the `SnapshotQuery` ephemeral read class (`w10-snapshotquery`); HTTP/2+gRPC+WebSocket adapters (`w10-adapters`); the Bolt compatibility subset V1 plus the V2 write roadmap (`w10-bolt`); QoS/admission with `ResourceVector` and `ResourceLedgerState` (`w10-qos`); import formats, the in-house Arrow IPC export writer, and `fgdb-adbc` (`w10-formats`); `ArchiveReadOnlyOpen` single-file distribution (`w10-archive-open`); the deterministic UDF bytecode VM and native-procedure boundary (`w10-udf-vm`); CDC export (`w10-cdc`); and the `fgdbd` composition with drain choreography (`w10-server`). Crates (§18.1): `fgdb`, `fgdb-server`, `fgdb-cli`, `fgdb-protocol`, `fgdb-bolt`, `fgdb-formats`, `fgdb-udf-vm`, `fgdb-python`, `fgdb-adbc`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 (agent-native) is the load-bearing bet: agents disconnect, retry, and resume constantly, so BEGIN, transaction reattach/renewal, autocommit, subscription creation, export, replay, result resume/ACK/release, unsubscribe, and E-to-E2 capability migration are all durably idempotent, and exactly four durable authority-bearing capabilities survive connection loss with explicit lineage, rotation, and tombstones. B5 (determinism/evidence): every protected result, baseline, delta, proof, replay/export byte, cancellation explanation, and data-dependent error of the durable classes is buffered until its exact authorization and audit-visible release evidence exists, then consumes a fresh linear `PublicFrameSendGuard` immediately before each frame write. B1 shows on the wire as `WireGraphReferenceSpec` branch/system-time/valid-time selectors. Market: Bolt-family drivers leave lost-COMMIT ambiguity, finalizer-driven leaks, and hidden-fact leakage through error surfaces; Fabric makes ownership explicit (Rust `Drop` cannot release; iterator exhaustion IS `finish()`), splits results into two honest classes (durable `PublishedResultStream` versus session-owned ephemeral `SnapshotQuery`), and makes every error either public-mechanics or a bounded durable protected output.

## Design — normative detail
One connection machine (`TransportEstablished -> VersionNegotiated -> Authenticated{AuthContext} -> Ready{ReadyBinding} -> Draining -> Closed`) for all surfaces; `DatabasePosture` is exactly `Local|Sharded` and every role-sensitive public identity is a closed opaque posture union. Adapters cannot weaken Appendix D: HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, and Bolt preserve idempotency, posture, explicit release, output-guard, cancellation, result-resume, and cutover semantics. v1 restrictions: transaction-bound statements are serialized; unsupported savepoint, partial-rollback, or concurrent-statement profiles are rejected. Draining admits no new session-owned children and waits only for queued/writing transport obligations to become Sent/Failed, required audit publications, prepublication cancellations, admitted-decision recovery, terminal records, and durable detach/pause of senders; independently retained result/cursor/export/replay owners survive session/process close and never block drain. No `ObjectId`, reference tag, `WeakMarkerIdentity`, raw internal counter/frontier/generation, `ReplayManifest`, or storage-symbol type ever crosses the wire; a generated taint checker proves every wire path passes an exact projection constructor and fresh send guard.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15 (independent retention): every result-producing feature uses one generated, noninterchangeable owner arm and the state-shaped independent-retention machine; QUERY_CANCEL, Drop, disconnect, drain, and process death cannot release it. FG-INV-16: no ownership lease, result/workspace/cursor/output lease, or obligation is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated. FG-INV-01: each scoped begin/autocommit key maps to at most one immutable semantic terminal outcome; matching retries return the recorded lineage. FG-INV-20: authorization precedes every observation; capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, uniformly nonrevealing on failure. Latency budgets for the durable command classes are Appendix G `latency_anatomy.toml` rows and §17 `slo.toml` gates (benchmark-class claims, never invariant clauses); protocol conformance transcripts are FG-EVID-class artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-txn-lifecycle`/`w2-commit-protocol` transaction semantics, `w9-enforcement`/`w9-audit-release`/`w9-time-authority` security planes, `w6-subscriptions` cursor machine, `w5-binder`/`w5-determinism`/`w5-answer-contracts` statement and result contracts. Feeds `verif-differential`, `verif-torture`, `perf-bench-core`, `obs-observatory`.

## Success Criteria
All child beads closed. Appendix D closing suite green: state-model, golden, differential, fuzz, crash, and DPOR coverage of pre-auth database non-disclosure; missing/out-of-order AUTH_OK/READY; Local/Sharded dispatch parity; lost/duplicate/conflicting BEGIN, autocommit, subscription, result resume/ACK, unsubscribe, export, and replay requests; NotRequired versus RequiredVisible release; revocation/refresh/epoch change between every two chunks; protected-error silence; hidden zero-net provenance noninterference; E-to-E2 migration exclusivity; and adapter parity. No frame or state row ships without its exact generated wire tag, authorization/release rule, size bound, retry rule, and negative transition fixture. Epic-level e2e: one cross-surface agent-workload script (embedded, FGP, HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, Bolt V1) that begins transactions, kills and reconnects mid-delivery, presents each of the four durable capability kinds, exercises SnapshotQuery beside the durable read path, and drains `fgdbd`, asserting identical durable outcomes and release-evidence classes across surfaces; every protected write in the run logs frame class, send-guard arm, obligation state, and capability-lineage transition so the transcript can be replayed against the generated frame-class and time-requirement matrices for post-implementation verification.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: Appendix D's surface is the largest single contract in the plan; mitigated by generated registries (`wire_types.toml`, frame-class and time-requirement matrices) and session types. Rejected: reusing Bolt or gRPC-only as the primary protocol (cannot express durable capabilities, buffered-until-release, posture unions); finalizer-based resource management (silent leaks and unauthorized releases); a single mushy result class (hides the durable/ephemeral trade instead of contracting it).

## Provenance
§13 (990-1060), Appendix D (2763-3119), §18.1.

title: Epic W11 - Aegis: multi-member replication, HA, GC, backup/restore, format activation
description:
## What & scope
W11 turns the single-node FrankenGraphDB (quorum-one Raft from W2) into a replicated, highly available database. Scope: multi-member consensus over the exact same commit state machine (`w11-raft-multi`), stable prepared-owner payload availability with donor receipts (`w11-payload-availability`), membership and joint-quorum reconfiguration with `ConfigPayloadFloor` (`w11-membership-config`), linearizable and lease-based read contracts (`w11-read-contracts`), writer-anywhere follower preparation (`w11-writer-anywhere`), ATP anti-entropy/seeding (`w11-anti-entropy`), fenced consensus GC with quarantine and physical-operation evidence (`w11-fenced-gc`, `w11-gc-physical`), the full §16 backup machinery (`w11-backup`, `w11-backup-publication`, `w11-backup-release`), restore/clone with hidden activation and service promotion (`w11-restore`, `w11-restore-lease`, `w11-restore-promotion`), and rolling durable-format activation (`w11-format-activation`).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The Aegis doctrine (§14): **single-node correctness is the base product; replication adds crash-fault durability, availability, and read scale**. Canonical logical effects and digests agree across replicas, but repair ESIs, ciphertext encodings, cache state, and physical placement need not be byte-identical. Horizontal sharding is a post-1.0 protocol workstream (W12), not a configuration toggle — until the W12 gate passes, a database advertises `sharding=false` and rejects multi-shard topologies rather than weakening any 1.0 guarantee. This preserves B1 (One Version Universe): one `LogicalCommandSeq`/`CommitSeq`/HLC history, one commit state machine (§5.2) authoritative in one-member and multi-member configurations. B5 is served by evidence-first operation: every irreversible action (payload receipt, certificate, GC reclaim, backup publication, key destruction, format escape) is receipted, signed, and replayable; availability numbers are `slo.toml` rows, never invariants. B6 is served because agents get typed `Unknown` outcomes (capability-scoped, never a guess on leader loss) and a queryable ops surface. Market: the durability/HA story is what lets an embedded-first graph database compete with server-first incumbents without forking its semantics.

## Design — normative detail
The §19 W11 row fixes the deliverables: extend W2's quorum-one Raft to multi-member consensus; stable prepared-owner payload availability; joint/final/final-retirement-floor reconfiguration; current-root-recomputed, all-typed-root consensus GC with quarantine plus Requested/Started/Completed-or-cancelled physical-operation evidence, progress, and completion; anti-entropy/seeding; rolling durable-format activation and follower security/data fences; witnessed transparency. Dependencies: W2 commit/payload/Raft interfaces, W9 authority, W10 protocol/status contracts.

Structural laws that bind every child bead: (1) Raft persistence obeys the **no-extra-mutable-file doctrine** — all durable consensus state lives in Appendix A role-tagged objects (`RaftLogSegment`, `RaftHardState`, `RaftSnapshot`, `RaftStateRoot`, `ConfigurationState`, certificate/prepared-root/audit-visibility-pipeline formats) carrying the database/security-namespace/incarnation/role/group domain; no abbreviated ambient schema is normative. (2) A node syncs the new closure before vote/append/receipt/durability replies. (3) Truncation stops at visible audit-safe state and waits for the generated-complete floor including prepared transfers, cursors, replay, external continuities, remote trust/retention, backup, keys, and current/prospective configs. (4) Multi-member configurations must NOT fuse append-reply and post-apply publications (the Appendix G fusion law is one-member-only, because followers reply before commit). (5) SWIM+Lifeguard supplies suspicion/routing/donor evidence only; statistical suspicion never authorizes membership change, payload retirement, or GC. (6) Backup/restore follows §16, never a decode-proof shortcut. (7) Leader loss yields capability-scoped `Unknown`, never a guess.

## Invariants & claim types
This epic's children collectively enforce FG-INV-07 (acyclic durable reference graph, D1/D2 ownership, all-role Raft models), FG-INV-08 (contiguous sequences, exact-cut snapshots, gap-free audit pipeline), FG-INV-10 (two-slot root protocol, fencing, format activation), FG-INV-14 (GC follows every generated edge; obligations are roots), FG-INV-16 (no obligation lost/duplicated/exposed), and FG-INV-19 (replay grades across restore). Availability per operation class (apply-durability / visibility / delivery, §16.8) is `slo.toml` claim class; durability targets are `FG-CFG-01` (modeled MTTDL with sensitivity bounds); the writer-anywhere scaling claim is benchmark class per §14.4.

## Interactions
Consumes: `w2-order-raft` (quorum-one Raft core), `w2-commit-protocol` (§5.2 steps, D1/D2), `w2-gc-core` (single-node GC), `w2-continuity-profiles`/`w2-writer-takeover` (incarnation/fencing), `w9-key-lifecycle` (envelopes/DEKs), `w9-audit-release` (visibility certificates gating external dispatch), `w10-fgp-core` (protocol/status surfaces). Produces the substrate W12 (`epic-w12`) extends to Meta/Shard roles, the restore/backup surfaces `verif-torture` and the §19 deployment gates exercise, and the `ArchiveReadOnlyOpen` verification machinery `w10-archive-open` reuses.

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when: multi-member cluster passes the full §15.3 crash matrix and partition campaigns with zero invariant violations (the campaigns are executed by `verif-torture` over the matrices the w11 beads register — verif-torture is outside this epic's closure, so this criterion is validated at gate-g3, which joins the epic with verif-torture); Elle/SCC oracles pass on multi-member histories (the checkers are `verif-oracles` machinery hosted in those campaigns; likewise validated at gate-g3); reconfiguration ladder, GC pipeline, backup Released, restore-to-Operational, and format activation each survive every registered crash point idempotently; Local/Sharded restore drills and RPO/RTO gates (§16.6) pass; the three availability lines are measured and published per posture in `slo.toml`.
