A robust retaining-self version of B therefore needs an explicit registered
relationship discriminator such as `prior_instance`, validated independently
of field name.  That expands beyond one filter:

* add/parse/validate the discriminator on `identity::FieldRow`;
* include it in exact-key and transcript/robot output contracts;
* add corresponding Appendix catalog annotation evidence and projection
  comparison in appendix_a.rs;
* annotate only the approved lineage fields; and
* specify how generated GC/checkpoint/backup walkers cut such an edge.  Without
  the last item it is merely a construction exception, not a complete
  retention design.

That robust form moves durable-field/catalog contracts and likely their epoch
and assignment pins once rows are minted.  It therefore inherits the full
epoch-fixture and stale-rlib audit described above; it is no longer the
apparently tiny checker-only change.

Tests required for a retaining-self exception are stricter:

* ordinary and generic strong self cycles still fail;
* the exact approved prior-instance field succeeds;
* the same stable name on another schema fails;
* a different self field on the approved schema fails;
* conditional behavior is explicit;
* strong/weak mutual and future-result cases remain rejected; and
* a reachability/GC/backup closure test proves the approved predecessor is cut
  as specified.

One existing test is directly affected:
`idr_neg_self_edge_through_generic_family` uses the exact TimeSubject
`predecessor_ref`.  A standalone-B exception would make that fixture cease to
be negative.  It must be replaced with a different generic-signed strong
self-edge and paired with a positive approved-lineage fixture.  Weakening or
deleting it would let the generic-owner-normalization regression start passing
for the wrong reason.

Blast/reversibility/silent risks for B:

* The safe weak-only branch edit is tiny and reversible but not standalone.
* A hard-coded strong exception is tiny in files but system-wide in semantic
  blast because every generated retaining walker consumes durable_fields.
* A typed prior-instance/retention-cut design is safer than an allowlist but is
  a registry-schema change with an epoch/pin cascade and new generated-walker
  law; it is no longer cheaper than A.
* A checker exception is easy to revert before data exists, but poor to reverse
  after records rely on the admitted format.  A strong predecessor chain can
  silently defeat retention floors without producing a loader violation.
* The principal silent failures are removing weak_digest from the outer loop,
  keying the exception on a suggestive field name, preserving a green generic
  test by weakening its assertion, and validating construction order while
  never testing reachability retention.

COSTED VIEW, NOT A DECISION

The hard-coded standalone B has the smallest textual diff, but it is not the
cheapest complete engineering resolution: it leaves unbounded strong
reachability and therefore owes a second design.  The safe weak-self narrowing
is the cheapest checker change, but it only complements a source amendment.

For the two named outliers, I believe the source-only closed-union form of A is
cheaper in complete-system cost and safer: its pin blast is mechanical and
bounded, it follows the already-landed RestoreSourceLeaseRecord precedent, and
it makes non-retention true in the sole source consumed by GC/checkpoint/backup
walkers.  That is a recommendation about engineering risk, not authorization
to amend the normative Appendix.  Whether these two fields are spec errata,
whether the direct WeakDigest+A/B form is preferable, or whether the project
wants a first-class prior-instance relationship class is the repository
owner's decision.

title: Implement differential & conformance testing: TCK, ISO matrix, fuzzing, metamorphic
description:
## What & scope
Implement the 1.0 language/semantics/storage portion of §15.4 beyond the reference engine: openCypher TCK; ISO GQL feature matrix; curated external differentials; Prism-vs-fnx; model-based Strata testing; answer-equivalence metamorphics; generic parser/format/frame fuzz infrastructure; and canonical Local reference-machine generators. Live G3 adapter/authority/member state fuzzing and all W12 Meta/Shard/global machines are separate phase tasks.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B3 (Loom) claims standard GQL/Cypher semantics; the market checks that claim with the TCK and with behavior parity against incumbents — "behavior parity where standards align, documented divergence elsewhere." B6 agents need a published matrix, not a compatibility vibe. The Prism differential inherits fnx's NetworkX parity lock, a two-hop oracle chain to ground truth. Fuzzing extends fnx's 8-fuzzer precedent to every parser, frame, and reader; B2's seal/compaction equivalence claims are exactly the kind metamorphic testing falsifies cheaply.

## Design — normative detail
**Language conformance**: openCypher TCK; a GQL feature-conformance corpus keyed to ISO feature IDs, published as a matrix; differential vs Neo4j & Memgraph on a curated corpus — behavior parity where standards align, documented divergence elsewhere; Prism results differential vs standalone fnx (itself NetworkX-parity-locked). Model-generated histories run against both engines and compare snapshots, results, certificates, and permitted abort outcomes (shared harness with verif-reference).

**Storage oracles**: model-based testing of Strata against an in-memory reference graph — arbitrary op interleavings, equality after every op under every open snapshot; metamorphic suites in the house style: pattern-match results invariant under compaction, seal, branch-fork, and encode/decode round-trips.

**Fuzzing**: GQL/Cypher grammars, frozen FGP frame syntax/format codecs, every 1.0 `fgdb-formats` reader in this dependency closure, and SymbolRecord decoding. Live connection-state/adapter parity fuzzing waits for W10 and executes in `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4`; new W12 readers/role commands execute in `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0`.

**Protocol-state infrastructure**: simple canonical-map generators and comparison machinery for Local begin/attempt/statement/workspace/delivery/status/cut/GC primitives that exist in the 1.0 closure. W9-W11 concrete authority/network/restore machines are live only in the G3 oracle/torture tasks. Local-to-W12, Meta/Shard, distributed key/GC/backup/restore, and activation/retirement machines are registered as pending and live only in the W12 verification tasks.

**Ground-truth hierarchy** (inherited from verif-reference): the normative appendices and G0 golden vectors outrank both implementations AND external systems — Neo4j/Memgraph divergence is documented with a spec citation, never blindly adopted.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (restated): canonical scalar equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding are coherent; every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec/format rewrite, spill, factorize/flatten, workspace materialization, safe replan, and exact derived rebuild preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract — enforced by the scalar-law property/fuzz suite and the exact-rewrite metamorphic suites built here. FG-INV-18's bulk/derived clause (bulk ingestion commits only canonical logical batches through ordinary transactions; index/build controls remain invisible until a transactional SchemaOp activates a validated generation) gets its index shadow-build/activation races here; FG-INV-12's companion clause states the same law from the artifact side — no build progress or physical bulk/index artifact changes schema visibility before its ordinary transactional SchemaOp activation — and is exercised by the same race suites. Conformance results are exact pass/fail matrices; external comparisons are documentation and can never be CI gates when comparators move (per §17's law). TCK/ISO results feed gate-g4: 100% of G0's frozen 1.0 `LanguageContract` — ISO minimum closure, `GG01` or `GG02` plus one of `GG20`-`GG23` as applicable, all prerequisites, the required scalar profile, the validated synchronous Unicode/UTS #10/UAX #15/UAX #31 bundle and UCS_BASIC behavior, and named optional IDs — must pass its ISO-ID/TCK corpus, with every out-of-contract feature rejected/documented.

## Interactions
verif-reference is the semantics arbiter; W3/W5/W8 subjects supply storage, language, execution, branch, and Prism differentials; G0 freezes the 1.0 contract. The frozen FGP grammar may supply syntax corpus rows, but live W10 adapter/protocol semantics are delegated to G3. Protocol-state rows for W9/W11/W12 carry explicit phase owners and cannot count here. Gate G4 consumes the 1.0 ISO/semantic/storage evidence, never W12 evidence.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- TCK harness runs the full openCypher TCK against engine and reference; per-scenario pass/fail matrix committed; regressions block CI.
- ISO GQL matrix: every advertised feature ID has corpus coverage; every out-of-contract feature is rejected or documented; matrix is generated, published, and checked against the frozen LanguageContract.
- Neo4j/Memgraph corpus: pinned versions and datasets; a divergence registry where every divergence carries a spec citation.
- Strata model tests: randomized op interleavings with equality asserted after every op under every open snapshot; failures shrink via the sim substrate.
- Metamorphic suites: pattern-match invariance under compaction, seal, branch-fork; encode/decode round-trips; seeded corpora committed.
- Fuzzers: coverage-guided targets for GQL, Cypher, frozen FGP codec syntax, every active 1.0 reader, and SymbolRecord; sanitizer-clean with pinned corpora/dictionaries and bounded/nightly budgets. G3/W12 live-state targets are owner-tagged pending rows, not covered results.
- Local protocol-state trace generators compare every active Local field, refusal, release, and log field. Registry rows for G3/W12 must remain pending until evidence refs from their dedicated tasks exist; detailed/compacted Local status remains byte-identical.
- E2E script: a single conformance run boots engine + reference under the sim substrate, executes a pinned TCK/ISO/Neo4j-Memgraph corpus slice end-to-end (parse -> bind -> plan -> execute -> deliver results), regenerates the published matrices, and fails on any unexplained divergence; every mismatch emits the §15.1 structured artifact with an executable `replay_command`.
- Detailed logging: one JSONL record per scenario `{suite,scenario_id,phase_owner_bead,first_required_gate,row_state,feature_or_ISO_id,seed,engine_digest,reference_digest,relation_or_fuzz_target,corpus_dictionary_versions,coverage_counters,sanitizer_status,expected,actual,verdict,divergence_registry_ref,evidence_ref}`. Phase misattribution or a pending row counted as covered fails CI; every mismatch emits a reproducible §15.1 artifact.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: treating Neo4j as ground truth; TCK-only conformance; byte fuzzing without state ownership; treating a frozen frame-codec fuzz result as live adapter parity; using Local generators as W12 evidence; benchmark-style sampling for exact conformance. External corpora are pinned and non-gating; each claimed equivalence has a corresponding metamorphic relation.

## Provenance
§15.4 (1150-1155), §3.5, App F rows 12/18, §19 G4.


## Authoritative phase boundary
This bead supplies 1.0 language/semantic/storage conformance and generic fuzz/reference-machine infrastructure through G4. Live G3 protocol/HA work is `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4`; live W12 format/protocol work is `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0`. Any earlier W9-W12 wording is registry reservation only.

title: Prove the scoped formal anchors: Lean lanes, TLA+ models, clause-registry CI
description:
## What & scope
Execute the scoped formal-anchor program for the 1.0 Local/replicated product through G4: Lean visibility/SSI/witness/merge/Ripple/escrow/version-chain lanes; bounded TLA+/TLC root, commit, checkpoint/cut, delivery, audit visibility, prepared ownership/Raft, membership-floor, branch and allocator models; durable-reference checker; trace-conformance bridge; proof-lane manifests; and Appendix F clause-registry CI. The ten post-1.0 W12 models are explicitly excluded and owned by `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5's honesty discipline: formal results are `FormalModelClaim`s with named abstraction, bounds, and refinement status — "neither method is mislabeled as the other." The asupersync house style (Lean-checked invariants, TLA+ export discipline, proof-lane manifests, §2.1) is reused wholesale. Proofs target exactly the mechanisms whose failure is unrecoverable (B1's roots/commit/keys; escrow money-conservation; witness soundness for SSI) instead of promising a full-system refinement that would never land.

## Design — normative detail
**Lean lanes**: (1) the FULL visibility relation — publication, branch ancestry, create/retire, own writes, and reclamation — not merely three local MVCC facts; (2) SSI, separated into: dangerous-structure theorem; lifetime of dependency metadata; soundness of each witness constructor's concretization; refinement preservation of positive/negative/gap/path observations; optimizer transport of witness obligations; and statement-workspace transport plus cumulative-witness preservation; (3) merge proofs covering the registered algebra in its constraint context; (4) Ripple proofs covering only the explicitly registered operator/annotation subset; (5) the escrow conservation/bounds lane (FG-INV-02); (6) the version-chain model (FG-INV-03). Allocator first-escape (FG-INV-11's reservation-no-later-than-first-escape law) is deliberately NOT a Lean lane: App F row 11 enforces it with the per-profile `ExternalCas`/`DirectoryBound` continuity allocator and spent-range models plus first-escape/finalization crash and lost-response tests, which this bead builds in the model suite below.

**TLA+/TLC models**: dual-slot root and generated-complete checkpoint authority transfer; the exact writer-lease/takeover/fence-enable sequence; final-capsule commit; marker/global-branch links; fork-time envelope/write-key double rotation; delivery ACK/resume; audit candidate visibility fencing/external reconciliation; stable prepared ownership plus payload availability/Raft; membership reconfiguration floors; branch merge/token/range idempotency; and closed-sequence leases — §15.5's named list ends there. Beyond it, this bead also owns the App F enforcement-column models: checkpoint replacement/activation with provisional-cut inherited-absence/no-new-reclaim (rows 08/14) and the per-profile continuity-allocator/spent-range models with first-escape/finalization coverage (row 11).

**W12 phase delegation**: §15.5's ten bounded W12 models—global begin/attempt/statement/delivery; shard prepare/decision/audit/global delta; cut replacement; compaction/status; remote release; distributed key; GC; backup; restore; Local-to-W12 activation/retirement—are not built or claimed here. Their complete formal lanes, batch-reservation ownership model, Meta/shard reconfiguration, constraints, topology, fuzzing, crash matrices, and implementation trace evidence belong to `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0`. This 1.0 bead may reserve proof-lane schema IDs only; their status is `pending(owner_bead)`.

**Durable-reference checker**: generated; separately enforces per-field PriorObject construction annotations and rejects cycles in reachable object instances; recursive persistent-tree types remain legal because every concrete parent points only to already identified children.

**Honesty laws**: every model run states bounds; trace export demonstrates captured executions are allowed by a spec — trace conformance, NOT an implementation-refinement proof; runtime monitors detect selected violations but do not inherit model-check completeness; proof-lane manifests name abstraction, assumptions, bounds, refinement bridge, and exactly what remains unproved.

## Invariants & claim types
Direct 1.0 proof obligations: FG-INV-02 Local escrow conservation/bounds; FG-INV-03 finite acyclic generation-bound version chains; FG-INV-05 Local overlap/lifetime theorem; FG-INV-06 witness constructor/refinement/optimizer/partition/workspace/temporal transport; FG-INV-11 Local first-escape/spent-range models; and the named root/commit/checkpoint/audit/membership/branch/delivery models. All outputs are `FormalModelClaim`; bounded TLC never upgrades into a `SafetyInvariant`. W12 batch-scoped final-certification reservation and all Meta/Shard clauses are absent from this bead's evidence and require their dedicated task.

## Interactions
Proof subjects come from the 1.0 W2 root/commit/checkpoint/allocator, W4 witness/escrow/merge, W5 Ripple, and W9 Local audit visibility implementations. verif-oracles supplies runtime counterparts; G0 owns clause/proof-lane manifests. W12 proof-subject schemas may be reserved but no W12 clause can become live here. G4 checks only 1.0 clauses; Gate W12 consumes the separate W12 verification epic.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Every Lean lane compiles in CI with a proof-lane manifest naming abstraction, assumptions, bounds, refinement bridge, and the unproved remainder; manifest schema validated.
- Every active 1.0 TLA+ model has a pinned TLC configuration with explicit bounds; small bounds run in CI and larger bounds nightly. W12 configs are absent/pending here and execute only in `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0`.
- Trace-export bridge: captured lab executions checked against at least the dual-slot-root and commit models, labeled "trace conformance".
- Durable-reference checker: generated from the registries; cycle-injection fixture rejected; persistent-tree fixture accepted; a field missing its construction annotation fails.
- Appendix F CI: twenty-ID/table-hash, dependency-DAG, checker/negative-symbol, and compiled-plus-negotiated activation checks are phase-aware. A reachable 1.0 clause without a live checker forces its feature off; W12 clauses remain disabled/pending and cannot count toward G4.
- E2E formal pipeline: compile every 1.0 Lean lane, run every active 1.0 small-bound TLC config, validate proof manifests, run the durable-reference checker, execute trace conformance, and publish a machine-readable 1.0 anchor report. A boundary assertion rejects any W12 lane reported as covered.
- Detailed logging: every proof/model run emits JSONL `{lane_or_model_id,phase_owner_bead,first_required_gate,row_state,ClaimClass,abstraction,bounds,fairness,config_digest,state_count,result,trace_id,spec_id,first_divergent_step,unproved_remainder_ref,evidence_ref}`. Missing phase ownership, a pending row counted live, or an unlabeled refinement status fails CI.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: full-system refinement proof, narrowing Lean to three MVCC facts, mislabeling bounded TLC/runtime monitors/trace conformance, or importing W12 scope into the 1.0 proof bead. Drift is mitigated by trace export, generated checkers, phase-aware manifests, seeded counterexample tests, and the separate W12 owner.

## Provenance
§15.5 1.0 Local/replicated lanes, Appendix F phase-aware clause registry, §2.1 formal layer, §19 G4. W12 lanes are delegated to `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0`.


## Authoritative phase boundary
This bead stops at the 1.0/G4 proof surface. It does not prove W12 global certification, Meta/Shard protocol, distributed remote/key/GC/backup/restore, topology, or Local retirement. Any earlier W12 wording is superseded by this boundary and the dedicated post-1.0 task.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement consistency oracles: independent SCC, Elle-on-authorities, protocol checkers
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-oracles` (§15.2) as the reusable independent-checker engine and Local-through-G1 oracle suite: snapshot/branch visibility, independent Local SSI/strict-serializability dependencies, obligation/quiescence, root/capsule closure, Local authorization noninterference, canonical transition-trace infrastructure, and fixture-level Elle/CAS modeling. It registers schemas and ownership metadata for later G3 and W12 oracles but does not execute or claim those phases.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The anti-self-checking principle: "every invariant has at least one checker outside the optimized component it checks where practical." B1's serializability and visibility claims and B5's evidence discipline are only credible if the checker is independent — "production graph algorithms may be a secondary differential, never the sole checker of their own transaction graph." Elle-class history checking is the industry-standard external bar (Jepsen lineage); extending it to external-authority CAS chains is what makes the continuity story (identity, audit, restore) actually falsifiable.

## Design — normative detail
**SSI oracle**: a deliberately independent, small Tarjan/SCC implementation over trace-derived Local logical dependencies. It checks DSG-union-real-time acyclicity for the Local strict-serializability default and hosts the Local `SnapshotQuery` class-versus-durable-read, visible-endpoint, and admission-before-observation rows. The generic edge/trace APIs are reusable, but W12 global edge reconstruction and §14.6 batch-versus-serial equivalence are not delivered here; they are live only in `fgdb-w12-sim-global-oracles-p1cl`.

**External-authority modeling + Elle-on-authorities**: this base bead supplies the canonical linearizable-CAS register model, predecessor-digest law checker, trace schema, and fixture authority. It does not claim live coverage of W9/W11 authorities. Concrete identity/allocation, audit, archive/grant, reservation, catalog, restore-dispatch, time, and KMS authority models activate in `fgdb-g3-protocol-authority-oracles-w27f` after their implementations land.

**Fork-detection negatives**: fixture campaigns prove the generic checker detects double successors at one CAS version, predecessor-digest regression, and stale-head resurrection. The requirement that ticket admission, recovery, restore reconciliation, and completeness/status consumers all fail closed is a G3 integration obligation owned by `fgdb-g3-protocol-authority-oracles-w27f`, not evidence from this base fixture.

**Independent protocol oracles** cross-check the Local W2 begin/family/token/attempt/outcome, ticket ownership, statement/workspace/delivery, terminal-postcondition, cut-activation, and status primitives that are in this bead's dependency closure. G3 audit/DP/key/wire/restore/member machines and all W12 decision/global-delta/remote/distributed/role-transition machines have registry rows here only as `pending(owner_bead)`; their live canonical machines belong to the dedicated G3 and W12 verification tasks.

**Security negatives** here cover Local role/domain/incarnation/claim-owner/workspace substitutions and Local observation-before-release paths. Cross-transport/cross-capability, external-authority, restore-service, remote-grant, Meta/Shard, and topology negatives execute only in the phase-owning G3 or W12 tasks.

**Production stance**: production assertions and complete audits can enforce exact invariants; sampled e-processes are statistical sentinels in `evidence.toml`, not the enforcement column of `invariants.toml`. The base obligation-leak oracle is asupersync's leak/quiescence oracle. Later security suites reuse it but must publish their own phase-scoped live evidence.

## Invariants & claim types
Local/G1 enforcement here: FG-INV-05's Local strict-serializability dependency/lifetime clauses use the independent Local SCC/history oracle; FG-INV-04's Local visibility and SnapshotQuery-visible-endpoint clauses use the Local visibility differential; Local arms of FG-INV-01/16/20 use status, leak/quiescence, and admission-before-observation checkers. W9-W11 clause arms become live in the G3 oracle task. W12 global SCC/batch/protocol arms become live in the W12 oracle task. All fired exact oracle verdicts are `SafetyInvariant` evidence; sampled production sentinels remain `StatisticalClaim` rows and cannot enforce an invariant.

## Interactions
Runs inside verif-sim and consumes W2 transaction/commit transitions. It supplies Local SCC/visibility/status/leak checker primitives to w4 strict serializability and Gate G1. `fgdb-g3-protocol-authority-oracles-w27f` owns live W9-W11 authority/protocol integration; `fgdb-w12-sim-global-oracles-p1cl` owns W12 global SCC, batch equivalence, and Meta/Shard protocol integration. Schema registration is not live coverage, and neither later phase can satisfy a gate through this bead alone.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- SCC oracle: differential against a known anomaly corpus (Elle-style G-single/G2 histories); property tests that injected wr/ww/rw cycles are always detected; CI independence check — the oracle crate's dependency closure excludes production graph-algorithm crates.
- Authority-model unit/property tests: fixture CAS chains exercise legal direct successors and the three generic fork defects; generated traces are deterministic and every failure emits a §15.1 artifact. All-six-authority and all-consumer integration is explicitly deferred to the G3 oracle task.
- Protocol-oracle conformance, phase-scoped: Local/W2 live transition traces run here. G3 and W12 rows are emitted now only with `{owner_bead, first_required_gate, row_state:pending}`; activation requires evidence from their dedicated tasks, and CI rejects a pending row counted as covered.
- Local security negatives: at least one mutation test per Local substitution/observation class. G3 transport/authority and W12 cross-group/Meta/Shard matrices are delegated and cannot satisfy this bead.
- Leak/quiescence: every campaign closes with zero unreleased obligations or a typed, expected terminal state.
- W12 delegation test: the generic trace API can encode a same-basis batch row, but attempting to mark it live here fails; `fgdb-w12-sim-global-oracles-p1cl` alone executes and owns admitted-set/abort-set/committed-history equivalence.
- E2E script: one Local sim scenario drives begin -> statements -> commit/abort with all Local oracles attached, injects one fixture authority-chain fork and one Local dependency cycle, and asserts both are detected with reproducible §15.1 artifacts. Separate phase-boundary assertions prove G3/W12 rows remain pending here.
- Detailed logging: every oracle verdict logs `{oracle_id,clause_id,phase_owner_bead,first_required_gate,row_state,history_or_chain_id,seed,checked_edge_or_transition_counts,expected,actual,verdict,evidence_ref}`. A missing/misattributed phase owner or a pending row counted as covered fails CI.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: reusing production Tarjan/SCC (self-checking), treating registry presence as executed evidence, or letting a base fixture satisfy G3/W12. Risk of oracle blind spots is mitigated by per-clause registration, mutation tests proving each Local oracle fires, and dedicated phase owners for later machines.

## Provenance
§15.2 (1138-1144), App F rows 01/05/16/20.


## Authoritative phase boundary
Any earlier reference to W9-W12 in this description is a schema/interface reservation only. Live G3 evidence is `fgdb-g3-protocol-authority-oracles-w27f`; live W12 evidence is `fgdb-w12-sim-global-oracles-p1cl`. This paragraph and the rewritten scope above supersede any broader interpretation.

title: Build deterministic perf-regression apparatus with registry-derivable gates
description:
## What & scope
Build §15.6's performance-regression apparatus: the Criterion-style in-house microbench harness (`fgdb-bench`) plus macro-suite plumbing, committed-baseline and variance-aware gating discipline, complexity-witness regression locks, the waiver policy, deterministic replayable regressions, and the Appendix G registry-derivability checks. The bench binaries, fixtures, and specific gate values belong to the perf-obs region (perf-bench-core etc.); this bead builds the apparatus and laws they all run under.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: a performance number is a claim, so it is claim-typed (`EmpiricalGate`) and its harness must be deterministic enough that a regression replays. The discipline is inherited from the asupersync/fnx baseline-artifact practice and from §17's method: "profile -> remove one contention/allocation -> re-verify determinism and cancel-correctness -> commit with evidence — one lever per change, never a bundle." §1 constraint 12's law ("no unpriced protocol weight") makes the benchmarks and the operation-cost registry mutually derivable — the apparatus is what enforces that.

## Design — normative detail
Criterion-style in-house microbench harness plus macro suites (§17) with baselines committed, variance-aware gating, and complexity-witness regression locks: an algorithm or operator whose instrumented operation count exceeds its registered bound on an in-domain fixture fails CI. Harness determinism: seeded workloads, pinned schedules, so regressions replay. Every gate has a bench binary, a committed baseline, a variance budget, and a flamegraph artifact on regression.

**Manifest pinning (verbatim §17 list)**: a gate activates only when its benchmark manifest pins CPU/microcode, kernel/filesystem/mount options, NVMe model/firmware and measured fsync distribution, toolchain/build, database configuration, graph/schema, transaction size and concurrency, retention/FEC/encryption/index policy, cold/warm state, result consumption, and statistical comparison rule — plus its operation class (an Appendix G row) and counting unit (client-visible requests vs internal probes).

**Derivability law**: a latency gate below its class's ordered-barrier count times the manifest's pinned measured fsync p50, or a throughput gate above the apply ceiling its sequenced-command count implies, fails CI as a REGISTRY DIVERGENCE (§1 constraint 12), never as a missed benchmark. External "best" comparisons pin a publication, version, dataset, and configuration; moving or unavailable comparators cannot be CI gates.

**Six standing laws** (bind every published number): (1) no benchmark-only semantics — durability, isolation, and result consumption match the declared production mode; (2) distributions, not averages — p50/p95/p99/p99.9 and worst hot-key behavior always reported, extreme quantiles with fitted-tail confidence intervals; (3) never hide compaction — foreground latency during compaction, checkpoint, GC, and index build is part of the result; (4) memory is a first-class metric — bytes per live edge include versions, indexes, witnesses, allocator slack; (5) adaptive numbers disclose their policy epoch, with the fallback's number published beside; (6) no unpriced protocol weight — every gate names its Appendix G operation class and counting unit; any change adding sequenced commands, barriers, external-authority interactions, or per-object identity structure updates the cost registry in the same change.

**Waiver policy**: correctness, security, durable-format, recovery, authorization, invariant-checker, and required conformance gates are NONWAIVABLE. A public, expiring waiver may cover only a named empirical performance threshold, statistical-evidence threshold, or non-safety coverage budget; it records owner, evidence, reduced claim, expiry, and fallback, and cannot weaken an invariant or enable a feature whose safety checker failed.

## Invariants & claim types
Every §17 number is a provisional `EmpiricalGate` until its manifest pins the full list. Tail claims: p99.9 is empirical when sufficiently observed; POT/GPD extrapolation separately reports threshold, exceedance count, dependence/stability diagnostics, fit uncertainty, and sensitivity — a model failure blocks the extrapolated claim rather than "certifying" the tail (`StatisticalClaim`). FG-EVID-03 (restated): endurance-gate evidence requires duration and cadence, a compaction-debt ceiling stated in §6.6 write-amplification-model terms, a long-run memory-stability bound, and steady-state occupancy-model prediction versus observation — divergence is itself a finding. FG-CFG-04's capacity model feeds the sequencer-scale gates. The apparatus enforces that no statistical or empirical row lands in `invariants.toml`, and that a hardening change and its cost-registry update land in the same change.

## Interactions
g0-cost-registry supplies `latency_anatomy.toml`/`stream_capacity.toml` and the three CI laws the derivability checks implement; perf-bench-core, perf-bench-governance, and perf-bench-scale build their binaries on this harness; perf-cost-ci implements the same-change law in CI; verif-sextant types the statistical evidence and owns FG-CAL/FG-CFG rows; verif-sim provides the deterministic load/schedule substrate and the pinned simulated audit authority for governance-profile benches; gate-g4 requires all activated §17 manifests green and public.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Harness determinism: same manifest plus seed yields identical operation counts and an identical logical measurement stream; a two-run identity test lives in CI.
- Baseline discipline: baselines are committed artifacts; a regression beyond the variance budget fails and auto-attaches a flamegraph; baseline bumps require explicit commits.
- Complexity-witness locks: an instrumented fixture whose operation count is mutated above its registered bound fails CI.
- Derivability checks: a synthetic latency gate below the barrier-derived floor fails with the registry-divergence error class (not "missed benchmark"); a throughput gate above the implied apply ceiling likewise.
- Waiver machinery: waiver files validate schema (owner/evidence/reduced claim/expiry/fallback); an expired waiver fails CI; a waiver targeting a nonwaivable class is rejected; a waiver can never flip an invariant clause (negative test).
- Manifest validation: a gate missing operation class, counting unit, or a pinned fsync distribution reports but does not gate.
- E2E script: one demo gate wired end-to-end — bench binary + pinned manifest + committed baseline + Appendix G row — runs twice for the determinism identity check, then once with an injected slowdown to prove regression detection, flamegraph attachment, and the registry-divergence error class, all in a single CI job.
- Detailed logging: every bench run logs {gate_id, operation_class, counting_unit, manifest digest, seed, baseline ref, measured p50/p95/p99/p99.9, variance budget, verdict}; waiver evaluations log {waiver_id, owner, expiry, target gate, decision}; derivability checks log the computed barrier floor / apply ceiling beside the gate value — a divergence must be auditable from the log alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: external moving comparators as CI gates; average-based gating; benchmark-only semantics; silent or perpetual waivers; bundled optimization commits (one lever per change). Risk: variance-budget gaming — mitigated by committed baselines, pinned manifests, and mandatory flamegraph artifacts; risk: registry/bench drift — mitigated by the derivability CI and the same-change law.

## Provenance
§15.6 (1165-1167), §17 (1232-1273), Appendix G (3169+), §1 constraint 12.

title: Build fgdb-reference executable semantics oracle with dependency allowlist
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-reference` (§15.4): the executable semantics oracle — a deliberately simple, single-threaded, obviously-correct implementation of the FULL logical semantics over canonical maps, compiled for tests/fuzzing/model-checking only, never shipped, never optimized — plus its registered dependency allowlist, the recorded parser sharing exception, and the explicit ground-truth hierarchy. The point: "what should this return" is a program rather than a debate.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Every differential in §15.4 needs an independent second implementation of the semantics; without one, conformance devolves into opinion. B5 requires it; B3 (Loom unified execution) is validated against it; B1's visibility/branch/valid-time semantics are arbitrated by it. The allowlist exists so the differential cannot be quietly gutted by code sharing — the same discipline as the unsafe-boundary ledger. Precedent: fnx is NetworkX-parity-locked, giving Prism "a two-hop oracle chain to ground truth"; fgdb-reference plays the same role for the whole engine.

## Design — normative detail
Semantics coverage is exhaustive and normative: values, visibility, path modes, intents, temporal selectors, branches, multi-statement transaction-error policy, workspace generations/read-your-own-writes, statement publication/delivery, and terminal attempt semantics — all over canonical maps. Model-generated histories run against both engines (reference and real) and compare snapshots, results, certificates, and permitted abort outcomes.

**Dependency allowlist (a registered G0 decision)**: the foundation value/type/claim crates plus the G0-generated registries and golden vectors — nothing else. Importing any engine crate (`fgdb-txn`, `fgdb-algebra`, `fgdb-exec`, `fgdb-strata`, `fgdb-chronicle`, ...) is a CI-rejected boundary violation in the unsafe-boundary-ledger style, so the differential cannot be gutted by code sharing.

**Parser exception (recorded)**: `fgdb-gql`/`fgdb-cypher` (syntax only) is the ONE recorded sharing exception. Justification: the openCypher TCK and the Neo4j/Memgraph differentials exercise the front end end-to-end, and the grammars are fuzzed separately, so a shared-parser bug cannot hide unobserved in both stacks.

**Ground-truth hierarchy (explicit)**: the normative appendices and the G0-generated golden vectors outrank BOTH implementations. A differential mismatch is triaged against the spec and is never resolved by making the reference imitate the engine.

Intent semantics implement Appendix B's vocabulary (from w5-intent-log): the reference evaluates `CapturedIntentObservation`s and `NetEffectNormalForm` as the executable arbiter for effect/workspace differentials, including multi-statement error policy and terminal attempt semantics (one immutable outcome per attempt).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04's enforcement column opens with "Reference engine plus Lean visibility/slice model"; the row it enforces: visibility obeys system-time snapshot high sequence, selected branch ancestry for each graph-reference role, valid-time slice-set intersection and boundary normalization, create/retire and schema-coordinate rules, own-write/workspace overlays, the erasure-tombstone conjunct (§12.6), and the expiry predicate (§4.8); distinct branch heads or valid-time selectors never alias; a `SnapshotQuery` admission reads only the pipeline's visible candidate root and can never observe applied-hidden state. FG-INV-18 is enforced by "reference effect/workspace/valid-time differential": canonical committed effects equal logical before/after state over normalized valid-time slices; workspace finalization equals ordered published statements; synchronous constraints, resource budgets, and escrow bounds must hold before commit. Reference verdicts are `SafetyInvariant`-class evidence; the reference itself carries no statistical claims and no performance claims (non-goal by design).

## Interactions
verif-differential runs the TCK, ISO corpus, Neo4j/Memgraph corpus, and model-generated histories through it; verif-oracles uses it for visibility checking; verif-formal's Lean visibility model is developed against it; g0-identity-registries supplies the generated registries and golden vectors it may depend on; w5-intent-log supplies the intent vocabulary it implements; w5-parsers supplies the shared front end; gate-genesis requires "differentials against independent semantics/oracles" from day one.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- CI allowlist check: build fails if fgdb-reference's Cargo dependency closure contains any crate outside the registered allowlist; a negative test that adds `fgdb-txn` must be rejected.
- Golden-vector conformance: every G0 golden vector replays through the reference bit-exactly.
- Differential harness wired: sim-driven model-generated histories run against reference and engine; comparison covers snapshots, results, certificates, and permitted abort outcomes; any mismatch emits the §15.1 structured artifact; triage policy encoded in the runbook — the reference is never patched to match the engine without a spec citation.
- Property tests: single-threaded determinism (same history, same state); branch-head and valid-time-selector non-aliasing; boundary-time normalization; erased-subject and expired-element invisibility; workspace read-your-own-writes; one immutable terminal outcome per attempt.
- Coverage gating: a LanguageContract feature without reference coverage is absent from the advertised matrix, never "partial".
- E2E script: parse -> bind -> evaluate a pinned corpus (all G0 golden vectors plus one model-generated history) through fgdb-reference alone, then through the engine differential harness, asserting bit-exact golden replay and a mismatch-free differential; runs in CI on every change touching fgdb-reference or the registries.
- Detailed logging: the reference logs one structured record per evaluated statement {history_id, statement ordinal, snapshot basis, branch/valid-time selectors, canonical result digest}; the differential harness logs both engines' digests and the first divergent element on mismatch, feeding the §15.1 artifact so every divergence is replayable and triaged against the spec, never by imitation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: sharing engine components for efficiency (the gutting risk is the entire reason for the allowlist); resolving mismatches by imitation (ground-truth inversion); a prose spec without an executable. Risk: reference bugs masking engine bugs — mitigated because appendices + golden vectors outrank both and grammars are fuzzed separately. Risk: semantic breadth lag — coverage is gated per feature ID.

## Provenance
§15.4 semantics-oracles bullet (1152), §19 W1 row & Genesis slice, §18.1 Verification layer, App B.

title: Specify replay products: SessionReplayBundle and the chaos-facade decision rows
description:
## What & scope
Build the customer-facing replay/chaos products governed by §15.1's two registered G0 decision rows: (1) replay-artifact exposure — which internal artifacts (ReplayManifests, crashpacks, seeds/schedules) may become customer-facing, and the `SessionReplayBundle` agent-replay product; (2) chaos packaging — the fgdb-owned facade crate over `fgdb-sim`'s fault machinery. This bead turns internal verification artifacts into agent-facing products without overclaiming.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 agent-native: time-travel debugging of the database's recorded work for an agent session is a differentiated product — an agent (or its operator) can replay exactly what the database did, statement by statement, with an honest grade. B5's honesty discipline makes it safe to sell: grades are derived from evidence-slot matrices, never asserted. The exposure rows exist because "nothing here is implicitly public" — every externally visible artifact first receives a registered stability classification.

## Design — normative detail
**Replay-artifact exposure row (registered G0 decision)**: which replay artifacts may become customer-facing — `ReplayManifest`s, crashpacks, seeds/schedules — is a registered decision row; any artifact so exposed first receives a registered stability classification; nothing is implicitly public.

**SessionReplayBundle (the customer-facing agent-replay product)**: the ordered per-statement `ReplayManifest`s of a session plus its FGP frame transcript, graded with the existing `ReplayCompleteness` vocabulary — `Replayable | StructuralReplay{reproduced_classes[], omitted_classes[]} | VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied{missing_classes[]} | AuditOnly{missing_or_redacted_classes[]}` — time-travel debugging of the database's recorded work for that agent. Whole-agent byte-identity is NEVER claimed for customer code not threaded through the lab.

**ReplayManifest substrate (§8.6, consumed from w5-replay)**: pins database/security namespace/incarnation, logical-command and commit sequences, topology/policy/revocation epochs, the execution `AnswerRequirement`, realized `AnswerContract`, `LogicalOrbitId`/`PhysicalPlanId`, result-encoding version, and canonical result digest. Every evidence slot is `ReplayEvidenceRef<T> = Present{object: ReplayObjectRef<T>} | Unavailable{class, expected_logical_object_id?, expected_canonical_digest?, reason_code} | Redacted{class, commitment?, redaction_policy_oid}`. A versioned `ReplaySlotSchema` derives — not trusts — structural completeness from slot states and the recorded execution's actual semantic dependencies; at access time the verifier separately derives `effective_completeness` from live availability/lease/trust/resolver/authorization state, which can only stay equal or weaken. An encoded structural grade that disagrees with the generated slot matrix is invalid.

**Chaos packaging row (registered G0 decision)**: any customer-facing surface over `fgdb-sim`'s fault machinery ships behind an fgdb-owned facade crate with its own stability classification, never as a direct dependency on the foundation lab runtime; its reports are claim-typed falsification-only — structurally incapable of asserting "verified fault-free" — and chaos/fault-injection capabilities are absent from production `Cx` profiles BY CONSTRUCTION, a lab-only capability rather than a runtime flag.

Production incident bundles keep their fail-closed redaction contract; crypto entropy is never recorded; customer-safe bundles never overclaim byte identity.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-19 (restated): a registry-rooted replay manifest derives its structural maximum only from its versioned evidence-slot matrix, and its effective grade may only weaken as leases, resolution, trust, configuration, or authority change. `Replayable` requires every semantic slot — answer requirement, realized contract, authority, external inputs, executable artifacts, decisions, workspace-affecting statements, exact approximate generations — to resolve through exactly LocalStrong, live CertifiedRemote, or active Archived evidence and reproduce canonical logical output. Sharded replay is no stronger than its weakest required group. Erased subjects downgrade replay through the `Redacted` arm with the erasure tombstone as typed evidence; an `ErasureCutSpec` never silently breaks a byte-identity claim — the effective grade weakens attributably. FG-INV-20 applies to resolution: reading or resolving any replay item requires explicit `Replay` authority scoped to the complete evidence/artifact closure. Exposure/stability classifications are registry (`SafetyInvariant`-adjacent contract) rows; chaos reports are structurally falsification-only claims.

## Interactions
Consumes w5-replay (ReplayManifest, grades, FG-INV-19 machinery) and verif-sim (crashpacks/seeds, fault machinery, ReplayCompleteness vocabulary); g0-format-arms freezes both decision rows and the stability classifications; w10-fgp-core supplies the FGP frame transcript and the delivery surface; w9-redaction-erasure supplies `ErasureCutSpec` and the erasure-tombstone evidence the `Redacted` slot cites (the `Redacted` arm itself is defined by w5-replay’s `ReplayEvidenceRef` schema, §8.6); obs-observatory shares the fail-closed redaction contract for crashpacks.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Bundle builder assembles ordered per-statement ReplayManifests plus the FGP transcript; the bundle grade is computed by the generated slot matrix, never hand-encoded; an invalid-manifest test proves an encoded grade disagreeing with the matrix is rejected.
- Grade-weakening tests: expiring a lease, revoking trust, and erasing a subject each weaken the effective grade attributably; no code path re-strengthens a grade without new evidence.
- Redaction: fail-closed contract tests; an entropy-scan negative over emitted bundles; a customer-safe fixture proves no byte-identity claim appears for omitted classes and whole-agent byte identity is never claimed.
- Chaos facade: CI dependency check — no customer-visible crate depends directly on the lab runtime; the report type makes "verified fault-free" unrepresentable (type-level test); a production `Cx` profile compile check proves fault-injection capability is absent.
- E2E with logging: record an agent session, build the bundle, replay it; the Replayable case reproduces canonical logical output exactly; the AuditOnly case refuses byte-replay claims; every step emits §15.1 structured fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: implicit publicness of seeds/crashpacks; exposing the lab runtime directly (foundation coupling + capability leak into production); claiming whole-agent byte identity for un-labbed customer code. Risk: commercial pressure to overclaim grades — structurally prevented by derived-not-trusted grading and the falsification-only report type.

## Provenance
§15.1 final paragraph (1136), §8.6 (713-717), FG-INV-19/20, §19 G0 decision batch.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Build Sextant calibration plane: e-processes, conformal, SPRT/OPE, claim typing
description:
## What & scope
Build the Sextant calibration plane (§15.0): e-processes, conformal predictors, sequential tests (SPRT), robust estimators, regime/change detectors (one versioned BOCPD+SR signal), and propensity/OPE tooling — all as deterministic transformations of logged inputs over asupersync's e-process core — plus the claim-class constitution wiring, the FG-CAL/FG-EVID/FG-CFG registry rows, decision-card binding, the deterministic-fallback law, and the never-mislabel-statistics law. This is the runtime stratum of B5: the calibration discipline that governs the LIVE system, not a test suite.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5's third leg is calibrated adaptivity: the system tunes itself, but every adaptive choice is inspectable, evidence-typed, and reversible to a deterministic fallback — "this is how B5 makes adaptation inspectable without confusing 'well measured' with 'proved safe'." §15.7 paper 6 ("Calibrated adaptivity: anytime-valid statistical governance of a self-tuning DBMS") is the receipt. §3.5 fixes the verdicts: conformal prediction adopted as assumption-bearing evidence, never semantic enforcement; e-processes adopted for policy trials and health sentinels, kept in `evidence.toml`; SPRT adopted conditionally (may add evidence to migration cards, never replaces hard dwell/hysteresis guards); OPE adopted conditionally (logged probabilities, support exclusions, effective sample size, deterministic fallback, and explicit deployment evidence); CVaR/EVT as model-qualified control evidence (never call a fitted extreme quantile "certified"); empirical Bayes/Good-Turing/robust estimators to Evaluate per fixture.

## Design — normative detail
Sextant supplies its estimators as deterministic transformations of logged inputs; it governs performance and operational choices; it NEVER upgrades assumption-bearing evidence into exact correctness. Every evidence envelope carries a `ClaimClass`: `SafetyInvariant` | `FormalModelClaim` | `StatisticalClaim` | `ConfigurationModelClaim` | `EmpiricalGate` (with their §15.0-mandated disclosure fields). Registry split: `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness obligations; `evidence.toml` contains `FG-CAL-*` and `FG-EVID-*`; `slo.toml` contains `FG-CFG-*`, performance, durability-model, and controller targets.

Validity laws (all normative): e-processes may be anytime-valid only under their named filtration/null assumptions; conformal coverage is marginal under its named exchangeability or online-validity conditions; drift alarms do not retroactively preserve a broken assumption; OPE requires positivity/overlap and sufficient effective sample size. Dead-code law: a monitor that drives no named decision is dead code, but binding it to a decision does not make it an invariant. Fallback law: every adaptive policy retains a deterministic fallback valid without the statistical model. Binding laws: answer-affecting execution policies are bound to the `AnswerRequirement`, plan, result contract, and replay closure; canonical-state-affecting promotions are logical-command-sequenced and replay-pinned; only proved answer-preserving physical policies may remain local. Immutable evidence identity: calibration windows, selection policy, strata, propensity support, regime epochs, fallback, and failure behavior are immutable identities of the evidence. Decision-card binding: an SPRT may add evidence to §6.6 migration cards but never replaces the hard dwell/hysteresis guards; one versioned BOCPD+SR regime signal feeds controllers without being treated as ground truth.

## Invariants & claim types
The statistical/configuration gate rows this bead materializes and enforces (restated from App F): FG-CAL-01 adaptive-policy evidence vs pinned fallback — null/outcome filtration, alpha, support/overlap, effective sample size, loss and fallback; stream-sequenced promotion only. FG-CAL-02 cardinality/risk interval coverage — population, selection/window, exchangeability or nonexchangeability method, strata, marginal target, realized coverage and drift. FG-CAL-03 ANN recall/drift — authorized snapshot population, keyed sample, exact baseline, candidate policy, confidence interval and rebuild action. FG-EVID-01 decision-card/OPE completeness — state/actions/features, logged probabilities, zero-support exclusions, clipping/estimator, policy epoch and fallback. FG-EVID-02 scrub/corpus-health — population, keyed stratified sampling, dependence assumptions, exhaustive-sweep position, observed corruption. FG-EVID-03 endurance-gate evidence; FG-EVID-04 derived-state freshness (slo-class, never an invariant). FG-CFG-01 modeled durability (MTTDL); FG-CFG-02 controller stability; FG-CFG-03 staleness SLO feasibility; FG-CFG-04 maintenance-stream capacity model. None of these may ever appear in `invariants.toml` — the never-mislabel law is itself CI-checked.

## Interactions
Consumes w1-sketch-calibrate (`fgdb-sketch` + `fgdb-calibrate` over the asupersync e-process core) and g0-claim-registries (the three tomls). Serves: w3-write-amp decision cards (§6.6 SPRT/dwell), w5-planner optimizer intervals (§8.5, FG-CAL-02), w6-maintainers approximate-maintainer risk (§9.6), w7-vector recall evidence (FG-CAL-03), w2-fec-scrub (FG-EVID-02, FG-CFG-01), obs-slo production sentinels, perf-freshness-vector calibration rows, and verif-perf-apparatus evidence typing.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Determinism: identical logged inputs produce bit-identical scores/ledgers across runs and platforms under the pinned numeric profile.
- E-process validity harness: simulated null streams show Ville-bound violation rate within alpha; a filtration-violation fixture invalidates the claim rather than silently continuing.
- Conformal harness: synthetic exchangeable and nonexchangeable streams; realized marginal coverage reported per FG-CAL-02 fields; drift alarm fires and reverts to conservative costing.
- OPE: a positivity-violation fixture is excluded with a recorded zero-support exclusion; effective sample size below threshold blocks promotion; promotion is stream-sequenced.
- Registry CI: every FG-CAL/FG-EVID row lives in `evidence.toml`, every FG-CFG row in `slo.toml`, none in `invariants.toml`; a dead-monitor detector flags monitors bound to no named decision; every adaptive policy registers a deterministic fallback and a pulled-model test proves failover.
- Decision-card binding test: SPRT evidence present but dwell guard unsatisfied results in no migration.
- E2E script: replay one pinned decision-card episode end-to-end — logged inputs -> e-process/conformal/OPE scores -> FG-CAL-01 evidence row -> promotion decision -> forced assumption failure -> deterministic fallback engagement — asserting bit-identical scores across two runs and a fallback that operates without the statistical model.
- Detailed logging: every score/ledger update logs {estimator id, immutable evidence identity (window/selection policy/strata/propensity support/regime epoch/fallback/failure behavior), input digest, score, ClaimClass, decision binding}; promotion/rollback events log the named decision, policy epoch, and evidence refs; the dead-monitor detector logs every monitor-to-decision binding — calibration behavior must be fully reconstructible from logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected per §3.5: conformal coverage as semantic enforcement; e-processes in the invariant registry; SPRT replacing dwell/hysteresis; context-free CALM "no coordination" labels; calling fitted extreme quantiles certified; graph-workload slogans substituting for fixture-specific risk evidence. Risk: assumption drift silently invalidating evidence — mitigated by immutable evidence identities and drift alarms that block claims instead of patching them; risk: adaptive-policy sprawl — every policy needs a registered fallback and named decision, or it is dead code.

## Provenance
§15.0 (1106-1120), §3.5 (159-183), App F statistical gates (3151-3165), §2.1 statistical-governance row.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Build fgdb-sim: lab-runtime simulation harness with LDFI, shrinking, dual runs
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-sim` (§15.1): the simulation-first development harness that runs the ENTIRE database under asupersync's lab runtime — virtual time, virtual network, virtual disk, seeded deterministic scheduling, chaos injection, and deterministic pressure models — plus the five force multipliers (LDFI, model-qualified stopping, self-shrinking failures, lab-vs-live dual runs, graded production incident replay) and the mandatory structured failure artifact. Scope: harness integration, declared bounded scenario/state models, the LDFI campaign registry, and the artifact contract tests. Customer-facing exposure of sim artifacts is verif-replay-products' scope. Deliverable interface: the `fgdb-sim` crate exporting the scenario/state-model registration API, the campaign registry, the structured-artifact emitter, the shrinker, and the dual-run driver — plus a representative multi-component fixture state machine (virtual time/disk/network, chaos, seeded scheduling) that this bead's own acceptance runs against and that later campaign beads import as the harness smoke target.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: determinism as a bet means every failure is a replayable seed, never a flake. Per §2.1 the lab runtime is "the verification substrate for B5"; a query is an asupersync region, so MVCC interleaving bugs become seed-replayable test failures. §18.2 explicitly does not build the deterministic lab, LDFI, delta-debug, dual-run, or trace-export tooling — those are foundation assets; this bead wires the database into them. Simulation-first is the FoundationDB lesson; the lab-vs-live dual run closes the classic simulation-testing loophole ("we verified the simulator, not the system"). §3.5 adopts LDFI/delta-debugging/record-replay "with replay-completeness grades".

## Design — normative detail
The database runs entirely under the lab runtime. DPOR/Mazurkiewicz exploration is exhaustive only within the declared bounded scenario/state model and the soundness of its independence relation; broader campaigns remain falsification, never proof of bug absence. Every failure becomes a replayable seed/crashpack.

Five force multipliers, all normative. (1) **Targeted falsification (LDFI)**: derives minimal fault hypotheses from successful-run dependencies. Fixed target list: every file/directory action in D1/D2; every ordered, certificate, external-CAS, or physical side-effect boundary in dual-root publication; attempt generation/ticket claim/statement-workspace publication and delivery; checkpoint install/provisional-cut activation; prepared ownership and Raft; remote release; key stage/activate/zero/destroy/physical completion; GC preflight/authorization/quarantine/member completion; backup pin/copy/reopen/publish/release; restore reservation/transform/reconciliation/hidden activation/visibility/service preparation/continuity-plus-catalog receipt/finalize/open/reopen/completion; and Local-to-W12 seal/activation/authority-transfer/retirement. Residual random chaos guards lineage blind spots. (2) **Model-qualified stopping**: novelty estimates and coverage maximization prioritize finite CI time under a named sampling model; they may stop a campaign per policy but never certify that no unexplored bug remains; deterministic bounded-state completion is reported separately from statistical/heuristic stopping. (3) **Self-shrinking failures**: hierarchical delta debugging + replay minimization reduce every failing seed (schedule + workload trace) to a minimal reproducer before filing; divergence diagnostics explain exactly where a replay departed from its recording; crashpacks arrive pre-shrunk. (4) **Lab-vs-live dual runs**: the same scenario, same seed, runs under the lab and against the live build, and the traces are diffed — the runtime-behavior counterpart of the fgdb-reference semantics differential. (5) **Graded production incident replay**: production retains bounded mediated-nondeterminism records under a fail-closed redaction contract; each bundle carries `ReplayCompleteness = Replayable | StructuralReplay{reproduced_classes[], omitted_classes[]} | VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied{missing_classes[]} | AuditOnly{missing_or_redacted_classes[]}`. Crypto entropy is never recorded. Full internal forensic bundles may be exact when policy permits; customer-safe bundles never overclaim byte identity.

**Structured failure artifact (mandatory)**: every failing sim, live differential, integration, or E2E run emits ONE secret-redacted structured artifact containing `{seed, schedule, crashpoint, role, group, configuration, topology, incarnation, service_visibility_epoch, logical/commit/Raft/applied/visible/audit-visible positions, attempt/generation/statement/workspace/backup/restore/GC/key identifiers, object/spec/result/certificate/grant/floor identities, expected, actual, replay_command}`. Human prose is supplemental, never the record.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16 enforcement runs here: "no structured task, ownership lease, begin/allocation/finalization reservation, pin, scratch object, result/workspace/cursor/output lease, prepared closure, privacy charge/seed/result, audit freeze/plan/per-signer lock/share/pipeline entry, escrow/resource hold, backup pin, remote transition, GC quarantine, restore-source lease, or TerminalPending postcondition is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated ... under declared quorum/storage/network/time/continuity/resource fairness, every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state" — checked by the asupersync leak/quiescence oracle inside every campaign. Claim typing: a fired checker is `SafetyInvariant` evidence; campaign summaries are falsification-only; stopping heuristics are `StatisticalClaim` under a named sampling model; DPOR bounded completion is a bounded `FormalModelClaim` reported separately; no sim output may ever claim "verified fault-free".

## Interactions
Hosts verif-oracles' checkers and verif-torture's crash campaigns; verif-differential's model-generated histories run here; verif-replay-products packages crashpacks/seeds under the G0 decision rows (g0-format-arms); perf-bench-governance uses its pinned deterministic simulated audit authority; every w2/w4/w9/w10/w11/w12 bead registers matrices on this harness. Consumes w1-foundation-types (claim/evidence types) and g0-claim-registries (ClaimClass constitution).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Determinism gate, phased by build order (this bead's dep closure is only foundation types + claim registries — no server exists yet): the exported fixture state machine boots under the lab with virtual time/disk/network and a pinned seed, and two runs at the same seed produce byte-identical traces; the identical two-run gate re-executes over the whole server at gate-genesis, which consumes this bead.
- Artifact contract tests, phased: the artifact schema, per-class field-presence assertions, and `replay_command` execution (requiring the identical failure) are implemented and exercised NOW against harness-native synthetic failure classes injected into the fixture state machine. The §15.1 lifecycle coverage list — lost `BEGIN_ACCEPTED`; duplicate/conflicting begin keys; denial/abandonment before registration; workspace-zero recovery; successor Registered-outcome rooting; cancel with prior results/workspace/grants; terminal/autocommit ACK/release races; every TerminalPending missing-postcondition combination; status before/during/after compaction and detail reclamation — is delivered here as a registered machine-readable coverage matrix whose rows activate as their owning beads land (w2-txn-lifecycle, w2-prepare-terminal, w2-outcome-tokens, w2-compaction); a CI check fails when an owning bead is complete but its rows have no passing campaign; full-list enforcement binds at gate-genesis and verif-torture, not at this bead's position.
- LDFI campaign registry enumerates the full normative target list now (rows registered even for machinery not yet built); CI proves each target class has at least one campaign once its owning workstream's beads are complete — before that the row is explicitly `pending(owning_bead)`, never silently absent; injected-fault failures shrink to minimal reproducers automatically, with divergence diagnostics on replay mismatch (demonstrated now on fixture-state-machine faults).
- Lab-vs-live dual run: the dual-run driver and trace-diff machinery are delivered and demonstrated NOW by running the fixture state machine under the lab and under the live (real-clock/real-scheduler) runtime with the same seed and diffing traces; the first whole-database end-to-end dual-run scenario binds at gate-genesis and is re-asserted by later campaigns.
- ReplayCompleteness grading fixtures for all four grades; a redacted bundle downgrades rather than claiming byte identity; scan-based negative proves crypto entropy never appears in any bundle.
- Detailed logging: every sim run logs {scenario_id, seed, virtual-clock epoch, injected faults with injection points, artifact fields asserted, shrink iterations, final reproducer path}; the lab-vs-live dual run logs both trace digests side by side; determinism-gate failures log the first diverging trace offset — every campaign verdict must be reconstructable from these logs without rerunning.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: random-only chaos (LDFI targets causal fault hypotheses; random remains only as blind-spot guard); treating DPOR as proof of bug absence; unstructured text logs as failure records; building a lab runtime in-house. Risks: sim/live semantic drift — mitigated by dual runs; heuristic stopping hiding bugs — mitigated by the separate deterministic-completion report.

## Provenance
§15.1 (1122-1136), §2.1 lab rows, §3.5 LDFI row, §18.2.


## Authoritative phase boundary (supersedes any broader reading above)
This bead delivers the reusable simulation substrate, fixture-level proof that the substrate works, registration APIs, and machine-readable future campaign rows. Its implementation dependency closure is G0/W1, so references above to W9, W10, W11, or W12 boundaries mean **registry vocabulary and pending owner rows only**, not executed implementation coverage and not gate evidence. Live G3 protocol/authority/member campaigns are owned by `fgdb-g3-protocol-authority-oracles-w27f` and `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4`. Live Meta/Shard/global-certification campaigns are owned only by `fgdb-w12-sim-global-oracles-p1cl` and `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0` under `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike`. A pending row cannot satisfy an invariant or gate, and G4 cannot acquire W12 evidence through this substrate.

Phase-boundary tests: unit-test owner/gate metadata on every registry row; property-test that activation before the owning implementation/feature clause is rejected; E2E exercise one G3 and one W12 row through their dedicated campaign entrypoints and prove the base harness reports them as delegated rather than covered. Structured JSONL adds `{phase_owner_bead,first_required_gate,implementation_enabled,row_state:pending|live|disabled,coverage_evidence_ref}`; missing or mismatched ownership is a hard failure.

title: Build fault & recovery torture: crash matrices at every durability boundary
description:
## What & scope
Implement the phase-correct Local/W1-G1 portion of §15.3's fault-and-recovery torture program: exhaustive generated crash matrices for the W2 root, commit, prepared ownership, checkpoint, suffix recovery, FEC/scrub, and stale-writer boundaries in this bead's dependency closure; model-declaration lint; additional Local format/corruption campaigns; and real multiprocess takeover tests. Later G3 network/authority/member and post-1.0 W12 campaigns have dedicated owners and are not evidence from this bead.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's One Version Universe rests on a commit stream that survives arbitrary crashes at arbitrary points; the crash matrices are the empirical leg standing beside FG-INV-07/08/10's formal models. The model-declaration law prevents the classic vagueness of "we tested crashes" — every scenario states exactly which filesystem, failure, placement, quorum, external-authority, and fairness model it assumes, so a green matrix is a bounded, honest claim.

## Design — normative detail
**Local crash matrix** kills at every W2 D1/D2 file and directory barrier, both RootSlots, inode/incarnation takeover check, post-rebase capsule, marker/root publication, prepared ownership, payload receipt/one-member order/apply, checkpoint install/provisional-cut/activation, retained-suffix reconstruction, and Local statement/workspace/result/status transition already implemented in the W2 closure. Rows for later audit/network/restore/distributed machines may be registered as pending but cannot execute or count here.

**Delegated W12 campaigns**: the registry reserves owner-tagged rows for begin reservation, Meta/Shard prepare/decision/audit/global-delta, TerminalPending, remote release, distributed keys, GC, backup/restore, topology, and Local-to-W12 activation. Those rows remain `pending(fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0)` and only that task may execute or satisfy them.

**Delegated G3 campaigns**: W9 audit/DP/key, W10 wire/adapters/protected outputs, W11 multi-member/backup/restore/service/reopen, external-authority, leader-loss, joint-reconfiguration, and donor campaigns remain `pending(fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4)`. This base bead supplies reusable generator/hooks but no G3 green evidence.

**Activation scope**: this bead executes only W2 checkpoint/provisional-cut activation. Local-to-Sharded freeze/seal/certificate/projection/first-entry/authority-transfer/RetiredLocal/finalize/reclamation executes exclusively in the W12 formal/torture task.

**Model-declaration law**: every scenario declares filesystem, failure, placement, quorum, external-authority, time, continuity, resource, and fairness models. Inapplicable dimensions are explicitly `not_applicable(reason)`, never silently omitted.

**Additional Local campaigns**: partial marker tails; full-digest locator collisions; mixed `EncodingId` symbols; erasures within and beyond each W2 source-block budget; stale Local writers; and idempotent Local Unknown/status recovery. Uncertain multi-member membership, donor poisoning, distributed key loss, and remote-authority failures are G3/W12 tasks.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-10's Local two-slot/root/recovery and stale-writer claims, FG-INV-07's Local prepared/ownership no-timeout-release claims, and FG-INV-08's Local logical/transaction sequence and checkpoint-suffix claims are falsified here. Each matrix row is `SafetyInvariant` falsification evidence under its declared model. This bead does not claim the distributed/restore/key/GC/role-transition arms of those invariants; their owning phases must emit separate evidence.

## Interactions
Runs on verif-sim, asserts through the Local verif-oracles, and consumes only W2 root/commit/recovery/checkpoint subjects plus their generated command contracts. Gate G1 consumes this Local matrix. `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4` extends it over live W9-W11; `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0` extends it over live W12. A registered pending row never satisfies Gate G3 or Gate W12.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Local matrix-completeness CI: generated from activated W2 publication modes/barriers; every Local command in this bead's closure has a campaign row. G3/W12 rows must carry their different owner and pending state.
- Each live Local campaign: post-crash recovery converges to a Local oracle-legal state; root/capsule/sequence/visibility checks pass; every failure emits the §15.1 artifact and executable replay command.
- fsync-lie and path-replacement variants exist for every Local matrix row; rollback (block-level snapshot restore) variants per the declared threat-model scoping.
- Erasure campaigns: reconstruction succeeds within each source-block budget and fails cleanly beyond it with the correct typed error — never silent corruption.
- Multiprocess kill tests for takeover: a stale writer is fenced by the inode/incarnation check at every interleaving of lease->recover->fence-root->enable.
- Scenario lint: a scenario file missing any of the six model declarations is rejected.
- E2E campaign script: generate active Local rows, execute one row per W2 durable command class plus fsync-lie, over-budget erasure, and real multiprocess takeover, recover and oracle-check, then assert all G3/W12 rows remain delegated/pending. Publish one machine-readable Local campaign summary.
- Detailed logging: every row emits JSONL `{campaign_id,phase_owner_bead,first_required_gate,row_state,crash_point_id,command_class,seed,model_profile_digest,kill_phase,recovery_verdict,oracle_results,artifact_ref,verdict}`. Passing and failing rows share the schema; phase misattribution or counting a pending row is a hard failure. CI executes a sampled failure's replay command and requires the same divergence identity.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: sampled Local durability boundaries, trusting fsync, clean-shutdown-only recovery, undeclared models, or treating a pending future row as coverage. Later matrix growth is owned by explicit G3/W12 tasks; each uses registry enumeration, LDFI, self-shrinking failures, and separately reported deterministic/statistical stopping.

## Provenance
§15.3 Local/W1-G1 lanes, Appendix F Local clauses of FG-INV-07/08/10, §19 Gate G1. G3 and W12 rows are delegated to their dedicated tasks.


## Authoritative phase boundary
Any earlier broad §15.3 inventory is retained only as registry vocabulary. This bead's executable evidence ends at Local/G1. G3 lives in `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4`; W12 lives in `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0`. This boundary supersedes any broader interpretation.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.
