title: Freeze the universal verification, E2E, evidence, and diagnostic-event contract
description:
## What & scope
Freeze and enforce the repository-wide implementation verification, end-to-end scenario, evidence-artifact, and diagnostic-event contract. This is not a substitute for task-specific acceptance tests: it is the generated completeness schema that every implementation, protocol, format, operator, gate, benchmark, and operations bead must instantiate with concrete rows. It owns `verification_contracts.toml`, stable test/scenario/event IDs, the unit-to-E2E coverage matrix, failure-bundle rules, replay commands, fixture isolation rules, and CI lints that reject untested or unobservable normative clauses.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The plan makes verification a design pillar and the user requires comprehensive unit tests, E2E scripts, and detailed logging. A prose promise is insufficient at this scale. A generated, closed registry makes missing coverage visible before implementation, prevents a broad E2E test from disguising missing local semantics, and ensures every failure is diagnosable and replayable under B5 without leaking protected state under B6. It also turns future-self knowledge into executable metadata instead of relying on the source plan or institutional memory.

## Design — normative contract
`verification_contracts.toml` contains one stable `VerificationSubjectId` per durable schema, state-machine transition, algebra/operator law, invariant checker, protocol frame/state pair, recovery boundary, authorization noninterference surface, benchmark claim, and gate clause. Each subject declares: owning bead/workstream; normative clause IDs; applicable roles/postures/configuration epochs; unit/vector/property/model/fuzz/simulation/conformance/formal/benchmark test IDs; at least one E2E scenario ID unless the subject is proven compile-time-only with a registered justification; required fault and cancellation points; oracle independence class; required structured event IDs; secret/redaction classification; artifact retention class; replay command template; and the exact gate that consumes the evidence.

Every implementation bead must name task-specific tests for its owned clauses. Unit tests cover local totality, canonicalization, invalid tags/fields, arithmetic bounds, state preconditions, and error mapping. Property/model/fuzz tests cover generated inputs and mutation rejection. Simulation tests cover concurrency, cancellation, crash/restart, authority changes, virtual time, and deterministic seeds where applicable. E2E scripts exercise the public embedded/server/CLI robot surfaces through real subsystem composition, including success, refusal, degraded, retry, cancel, crash/recovery, and upgrade/restore paths appropriate to the subject. An E2E script cannot replace a missing unit/property oracle; a unit suite cannot satisfy the public composition row.

All E2E scripts are deterministic, noninteractive, bounded, and safe. They create isolated disposable fixture directories, use synthetic capabilities/keys and simulated donor/member loss, record exact inputs and toolchain/profile hashes, never target a pre-existing database, and never require deletion of user data. Cleanup is explicit best-effort fixture retirement; retained failure bundles are never silently removed. Robot output is versioned NDJSON and human decoration never contaminates it.

`DiagnosticEventId` rows define an exact versioned JSONL schema per transition/boundary: `event_version,event_id,subject_id,run_id,scenario_id,seed,virtual_time,role,posture,configuration_epoch,security_state_public_commitment,operation_id,state_before,state_after,decision_or_certificate_digest,oracle_id,verdict,failure_class,artifact_refs,replay_command`, with subject-specific typed extensions. Event ordering/cardinality and correlation are assertions, not merely debugging output. Secrets, capability bytes, plaintext protected values, DP seed material, hidden graph facts, raw tenant/principal identity, and nonpublic topology are forbidden; redaction/noninterference tests compare authorized and unauthorized runs including errors, sizes, timing class, and event presence. Logs use bounded cardinality and registered digest/public-commitment projections.

On any failure, the harness emits a content-addressed `VerificationFailureBundle` containing the minimal fixture manifest, exact binary/toolchain/profile hashes, seed and schedule, virtual-time trace, fault/cancellation plan, redacted ordered events, expected/observed oracle outputs, artifact refs, and one copy-paste replay command. Shrinking preserves the violated subject and authority posture. Successful gate evidence stores registry coverage summaries and digests rather than unbounded raw logs.

CI generation checks bijection and closure: every owned normative clause has a live subject; every subject has an owner, oracle, applicable unit/property layer, E2E row or approved compile-time-only justification, diagnostic schema, replay recipe, and consuming gate; every referenced test/scenario/event exists; every invariant/evidence/SLO/cost/command/frame row maps to verification subjects; stale tests and orphan logs fail. The same-change rule requires registry changes with any new normative schema, state arm, operation, frame, invariant, claim, or gate clause.

## Invariants & claims
Supports all FG-INV rows by making checker existence and coverage executable, especially FG-INV-01 structural concurrency, FG-INV-17 deterministic replay evaluation, FG-INV-19 byte replay, and FG-INV-20 authorization-before-observation. Test completion proves only the registered clause under the named configurations and oracle class; it never upgrades statistical evidence into proof or a partial model into a system-wide theorem.

## Interactions and ownership
Consumes G0 invariant/evidence/SLO/cost/command/durable-field/frame registries and the threat model. `fgdb-sim`, `fgdb-reference`, subsystem test crates, protocol conformance suites, formal lanes, performance apparatus, and Observatory instantiate its rows. Every workstream epic and gate consumes the generated coverage report transitively through G0. Observatory owns production event transport; this task owns semantic event schemas and verification assertions. The wire/log taint checkers share redaction classifications but neither bypasses the other.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Registry schema, generators, stable IDs, versioning rules, and same-change CI lint are specified with no wildcard subject classes.
- A generated clause-to-test-to-event-to-gate matrix covers every current invariant, durable schema/state transition, command, GLA operator, FGP frame/state pair, recovery boundary, benchmark claim, and gate clause; omissions, duplicates, orphan tests, and orphan events fail fixtures.
- Unit tests validate registry parsing, referential closure, role/posture/configuration expansion, compile-time-only justification rules, event cardinality/order, redaction classification, and deterministic failure-bundle encoding.
- Property/mutation tests delete or corrupt each required field/link and prove CI rejects the manifest; fuzzing covers unknown IDs, cyclic aliases, incompatible oracle claims, and hostile diagnostic payloads.
- Simulation tests exercise crash/cancel/retry/virtual-time/authority-change event sequences and prove identical seed/profile inputs yield byte-identical redacted evidence bundles.
- E2E harness scripts run representative embedded, server, FGP, and CLI robot scenarios through success, refusal, crash/recovery, and replay; they use isolated synthetic fixtures, never pre-existing data, and emit a single machine-readable summary plus content-addressed artifacts.
- Noninterference tests compare authorized/unauthorized and before/after-revocation runs across result, error, timing class, event presence, sizes, and artifact metadata; forbidden secrets never appear in logs or bundles.
- Detailed JSONL diagnostics conform to registered schemas; tests fail on missing, duplicate, out-of-order, uncorrelated, unbounded-cardinality, or secret-bearing events.
- Gate reports enumerate exact covered/missing/waived subject IDs, configuration coverage, oracle independence, artifact digests, and replay commands; no gate passes on an aggregate green bar with uncovered rows.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: one generic “tests pass” checkbox, E2E-only coverage, snapshot logs without schemas, free-form debug strings as evidence, and production logging that reveals hidden state. Risk: registry overhead. Mitigation: generate boilerplate and matrices from the same normative registries while keeping task-specific assertions hand-authored and independently reviewed.

## Provenance
Plan §15 verification doctrine, §16 observability/operations, Appendix F live-checker closure, Appendix G same-change law, and the explicit project requirement for comprehensive unit tests, E2E scripts, and detailed logging.

title: Implement fgdb-authz-types nonconstructible permits and fgdb-policy verifier IR
description:
## What & scope
Implement `fgdb-authz-types` — the nonconstructible authorization permit family, centrally `AuthorizedMutationPermit` — and `fgdb-policy` — the restricted, versioned policy IR (`PolicyIr`) plus its deterministic evaluator and the trusted policy verifier that is the sole permit constructor in the codebase. Includes the fail-closed revocation interface. Warden (W9) administers issuance later; the verifier, permit type, and revocation interface are W1/W2 dependencies, not optional server middleware.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 (agent-native): agents receive scoped, attenuable capabilities, so authorization must be a value the type system can carry, not a request-path filter. B1: permits bind branch/snapshot scope, so the One Version Universe's branches are security boundaries by construction. Market: every incumbent graph database treats security as server middleware that embedded mode silently loses; FrankenGraphDB makes enforcement a mandatory access type (§12.3) that even a forged internal call cannot bypass, because the coordinator independently re-verifies permits over FINAL effects. The restricted IR exists because the obvious alternative — evaluating policy as GQL — imports arbitrary recursion, procedure calls, and nondeterminism into the security boundary.

## Design — normative detail
No caller can submit bare mutation intents. `AuthorizedMutationPermit` is nonconstructible outside the trusted policy verifier (Rust type privacy: no public constructor, no Default, no deserialize-into-forgery; clients present credentials/token bytes, the verifier persists the record, and only a nonconstructible verified typed value crosses into database code). The permit binds, exactly: database security namespace/incarnation; tenant/principal/issuer; authority digest and a non-widenable operation ceiling; policy-semantics ObjectId; policy and revocation indices; root/snapshot and branch scope; exact read `GraphReferenceBinding[]` and write `CoordinateSchemaBinding[]`; topology epoch; expiry; channel/session binding where applicable; and a unique nonce. The coordinator (W4) verifies the permit's provenance and scope, recomputes authorization over the FINAL effects and any `CoordinateSchemaTransition[]`, and orders the authorization decision against revocation/policy changes.

`PolicyIr`: graph caveats compile to a versioned, deterministic, total, resource-bounded IR — never arbitrary GQL. Expressible: bounded label/type/property/system-field masks, scalar predicates, branch/time bounds, operation/resource limits, and finite allow-lists of procedure/UDF/module ObjectIds and invocation modes. Excluded: arbitrary recursion, procedure calls (policy evaluation never invokes those modules), nondeterministic functions, and unbounded path evaluation. A policy-version ObjectId identifies semantics permanently; old evaluators remain available for retained tokens or issuance is explicitly migrated/revoked — CI cannot enumerate hypothetical offline macaroons and pretend to prove semantic compatibility. The evaluator is packaged per `PolicySemantics {policy_id, version, policy_ir_ref, policy_ir_semantics_oid, evaluator_artifact_ref, scalar_profile_oid, unicode_and_collation_profile_oids, allowed_operation_classes, resource_ceiling_semantics, disclosure_contract_set, body_digest}`: deterministic, total, fuel/memory bounded, byte-matched to its semantics OID.

Revocation is fail-closed: an unavailable or stale revocation index denies; revocation is monotone (restored access requires a fresh subject/epoch — the full `RevocationSubject` machinery is W9, but the verifier-side check interface and its fail-closed contract land here). Downstream, `fgdb-secure-view` (W4) is the sole crate that can construct `AuthorizedSnapshot`/`AuthorizedCursor`/`AuthorizedGraphView`/`AuthorizedMutation`/`AuthorizedDerivedState`, with W1's verifier as the sole permit constructor behind that facade — planner pushdown is an optimization atop this boundary, never the authorization root.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 (binding clauses): "Authorization precedes every observation or effect across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, workspace, errors, constraints/witnesses/prepares, derived state, Prism/UDFs, streams, capabilities, replay/export/backup, audit, and observability." "Every authority-bearing durable schema binds one complete `SecurityStateBinding`; equal epoch scalars with different roots/service epochs never substitute." "Capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, and uniformly nonrevealing on failure." All invariant-class; no statistical claim may substantiate an authorization property.

## Interactions
Consumes: g0-threat-model (authority lattice, per-posture footprint), w1-foundation-types (binding/reference types), w1-crypto (MAC/signature verification for token bytes and body digests). Produces the verifier consumed by: w4-secure-view and w4-coordinator (permit verification + independent final-effect re-verification), w9-threat-tokens (macaroon caveats compile to `PolicyIr`; issuance/revocation administration), w2-commit-protocol (authorization decision ordering against revocation/policy changes), w10-fgp-core (credential presentation path).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Compile-fail tests proving `AuthorizedMutationPermit` is unconstructible and unforgeable outside the verifier module. Mutation tests: flip each bound permit field (namespace, incarnation, ceiling, scope binding, topology epoch, nonce, expiry) — verification must fail per field, with a distinct typed error that is uniformly nonrevealing at the client surface. IR determinism: same IR + same inputs ⇒ identical decision and identical fuel consumption, under the lab runtime across seeds. Fuel/memory-bound tests: adversarial IR programs (deep masks, wide allow-lists) hit typed resource rejection, never unbounded evaluation. Fail-closed revocation: unavailable index, stale index, and concurrent-advance interleavings all deny. Evaluator artifact byte-match: modified evaluator with unchanged OID is rejected. Differential: IR evaluator vs. an independent naive evaluator over generated policy/graph corpora — delivered NOW as a minimal dependency-free naive interpreter beside the tests (this bead's dep closure does not include `fgdb-reference`), then re-hosted verbatim inside `fgdb-reference` under its allowlist when verif-reference lands (verif-reference depends on this bead, so a dep here would cycle) with the fgdb-reference leg validated at gate-genesis; the corpora and the differential harness are this bead's deliverables either way. Fuzz the IR decoder under App A length-before-allocation rules. Logging: every denial in tests records decision inputs (policy OID, indices, epochs) — never secret material. E2E: `authz_policy_e2e` — a scripted lab-runtime scenario that registers a `PolicySemantics` version with its pinned evaluator artifact, issues credentials, presents token bytes to the verifier, obtains an `AuthorizedMutationPermit`, drives a mutation through a stub coordinator that independently re-verifies over FINAL effects, then revokes and asserts fail-closed denial on the next presentation; the script restarts the harness mid-sequence to prove the revocation-check interface consults durable state, and finishes with an unavailable-revocation-index injection that must deny. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): the implementation logs every verification attempt with {policy_semantics_oid, policy version, security_policy_epoch, revocation_index, decision, typed denial class, fuel consumed} — never token bytes or secret material (asserted by a log-redaction test); tests assert one log record exists per denial and that its typed class matches the returned error; the e2e asserts the revoked presentation's decision log records a fail-closed denial naming the stale/unavailable-index reason.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: GQL as the policy language (recursion/nondeterminism/procedures in the security boundary); post-filter authorization (constitutionally a G1 gate failure); trusting a serialized permit across a process boundary (permits are process-local typed values; only credentials/tokens cross the wire); ambient "admin mode" bypass. Risk: IR expressiveness gaps discovered late force policy-version proliferation — mitigated by the permanent policy-version ObjectId design, which makes coexisting evaluator versions a supported state rather than a migration crisis.

## Provenance
§5.2 step 2 (permit definition); §12.2 (PolicyIr, PolicySemantics); §12.3 (mandatory access types, secure-view facade); §18.1; §19 W1/W4 rows.

title: Build fgdb-codec: EF, varint, bitpack, snappy-class, roaring-like, identity-column codecs
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-codec`, the in-house compression/encoding library the closed universe requires: Elias–Fano monotone-sequence coding, delta-varint (canonical unsigned LEB128), bitpacking/FOR, a snappy-class block compressor, roaring-like compressed bitmaps, the registered identity-column codecs, and the `NeighborCodec` family — each with SIMD kernels (in `fgdb-unsafe-simd`) behind traits with scalar fallbacks.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B2 (Strata): the 2025 "Revisiting DGS" headline — 4–9× CSR space overhead across the dynamic-graph-store field — is the disease Strata's tiering cures: the hot minority pays delta overhead while the cold majority sits BELOW CSR via compression, and that compression is this crate. WCOJ machinery (§3.2 adopt row) is honest only if codec capabilities are honest: Elias–Fano neighbors support direct rank/select; other codecs get skip/decode paths — there is no pretending. Compression-ratio numbers are benchmark results tied to named corpora and encodings, never universal facts. Closed universe: no external codec crate exists in the allowlist, so every byte Strata stores flows through code owned here.

## Design — normative detail
`NeighborCodec` is the closed union `EliasFano | StreamVByte { skip_table } | DenseIntervals`. The intersection contract is normative: Elias–Fano neighbor lists support rank/select directly; StreamVByte lists use skip/fence metadata and bounded blockwise decode; dense intervals use interval arithmetic; Loom intersects without FULL-LIST decompression where the codec permits it — and there is explicitly no claim that Elias–Fano offsets provide rank/select over a separate varint stream. Sealed-run layout consumers rely on Elias–Fano offsets for O(1) list location. The identity-column codec (a G0-frozen decision, normative for `dst_VId`/`EId`/`stable_eids`/`OriginBirthOrder` columns): a registered order-preserving shared-prefix layout in which a block-header dictionary carries the `allocation_epoch`+`partition_id` components and the `monotone_slot` suffix is fixed-width or delta/FOR-coded; binary search and SIMD lower-bound operate on the fixed-width suffix under the header-extracted prefix, preserving canonical big-endian epoch‖partition‖slot order exactly; reverse-family blocks (destination-grouped, carrying source-partition EIds) may require multi-entry dictionaries and degrade gracefully toward raw width under adversarial prefix diversity. This encoding is what makes the ~4 KiB / ≤256-entry delta-block law hold (≤16 B per entry; raw 128-bit identities would cap a 4 KiB block near 95 entries). The layouts are registered as codecs in the run/block codec tables and, like every codec choice, are covered by the logical-digest validator over stable IDs — so encodings evolve without a format-identity change. Roaring-like bitmaps serve label bitmaps (§6.5) and hole/visibility metadata. The snappy-class compressor is deterministic under `CodecProfile` (canonical plaintext is deterministically compressed before AEAD — same input, same profile, same bytes). Encoding baseline for everything durable (App A): declared format major/minor, little-endian fixed integers, canonical unsigned LEB128 only where the field says varint, length-before-allocation, checked arithmetic, per-kind maximum sizes. Portable-SIMD is isolated behind `fgdb-codec`/kernel traits with scalar fallbacks; STRICT-mode kernels must be bit-identical across supported dispatch paths.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (binding clause): "Every claimed answer-equivalent ... codec/format rewrite ... preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract" — codec substitution is legal only under the logical-digest validator. Performance targets are `benchmark`/`slo` class, never invariants (constraints 11/12): §17 gate "Neighbor scans, sealed runs (decoded-cache path): ≥ 500M edges/s per core; ≥ 10B edges/s node aggregate (memory-bandwidth-bound: EF+varint decode ≥ 4 B/edge effective)". Decode-safety bounds (length-before-allocation, checked arithmetic) are invariant-class.

## Interactions
Consumes: g0-format-arms (identity-column codec definitions are a frozen G0 decision batch item), g0-identity-registries (codec-table registry rows), w1-foundation-types, w1-unsafe-ledger (SIMD islands). Produces codecs consumed by: w3-tier-r (per-list `NeighborCodec`, EF offsets), w3-tier-d + w3-identity-encoding (identity-column layout; w3 owns the 4KiB/256 block law built on it), w3-vertex-directory (roaring-like label bitmaps), w3-properties (columnar encodings), w7-fts/w7-btree (postings/keys), w1-generated-parsers (varint/framing primitives), w5-executor (decoded-cache path), perf-bench-core (gate rows).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Round-trip property + fuzz tests per codec (arbitrary monotone sequences for EF, adversarial gap distributions, malformed-input decode fuzz under allocation bounds); rank/select correctness differential vs. a naive oracle over randomized universes; identity-codec order-preservation property (decoded comparison order equals canonical big-endian epoch‖partition‖slot order — exhaustive small-domain enumeration plus randomized large-domain checks) and prefix-dictionary degradation tests under adversarial prefix diversity (must degrade toward raw width, never corrupt order); ≤16 B/entry accounting checks on representative corpora; snappy-class determinism (byte-identical output across runs/platforms for fixed profile); SIMD-vs-scalar bit-identity on every dispatch path (CI matrix across target features); compression-ratio benchmarks tied to named fnx-generator corpora with results recorded as benchmark-class rows; §17 neighbor-scan bench wiring with logged per-run manifests (corpus, codec table, machine profile). E2E: `codec_pipeline_e2e` — generate a named fnx-generator graph (the pinned Barabási–Albert fixture), build neighbor lists, encode every list under all three `NeighborCodec` arms plus the identity-column codec, run a seal -> scan -> intersect cycle (rank/select intersections checked against the naive oracle), decode, and assert logical-digest equality over stable IDs; the whole script repeats under SIMD and scalar dispatch with byte-identical encodings and identical scan results, under the lab runtime with a pinned seed. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): every encode/decode run emits structured rows {codec_id, corpus_id, entry_count, encoded_bytes, bytes_per_entry, dispatch_path, output_checksum}; the ≤16 B/entry accounting test asserts directly from the logged bytes_per_entry rows; fuzz harnesses log minimized failing inputs with seeds; bench runs log the full per-run manifest (corpus, codec table, machine profile) as stated above.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: LZ4/zstd/roaring-rs/other external crates (closed universe); raw 128-bit identity storage in blocks (space law fails); claiming rank/select capability for varint streams (the honest-contract rule exists precisely to forbid this); making codec choice part of format identity (the logical-digest validator decouples them so encodings can evolve). Risk: SIMD kernels drifting from scalar semantics — bit-identity CI is the guard; nightly portable-SIMD churn — isolation behind traits per §20.

## Provenance
§3.2 WCOJ row; §3.5 (Dostoevsky/S3-FIFO adapt context); §6.2 (identity-column law), §6.3 (run layout, NeighborCodec, intersection contract), §6.5; §17 scan gate; §18.2; App A.

title: Build fgdb-collections: ART/radix structures, succinct rank/select, vectorized hash tables
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-collections`: adaptive radix trees (ART) with path compression and lazy expansion, succinct bitvectors with rank/select support structures, and vectorized (SIMD-probed) hash tables. In-memory data structures only — nothing here is a durable format; durable bytes exist only through registry-generated encoders.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Closed universe (§18.2): ART/radix structures, succinct rank/select, and vectorized hash tables are on the explicit build-it-ourselves inventory. The SOTA context fixes their roles: Teseo (§3.1) is REJECTED as a primary store (PMA rebalance storms conflict with p99 goals) but its lesson — the vertex table must not be a straitjacket — makes the vertex directory an index, for which radix structures serve; GTX/Spruce/RapidStore/RadixGraph (§3.1 adapt row) contribute ART-indexed buffers and latch-free append lessons for Strata's write path. The FTS term dictionary is an ART over which Levenshtein automata walk for fuzzy(edit≤2) search (§10.3). Vectorized hash tables serve Loom's join/group-by kernels and the FreeJoin family (B3). Mechanical sympathy is inherited doctrine from frankensqlite (§2.3): cache-line-padded sharded tables, prefetch on descent.

## Design — normative detail
ART: byte-keyed adaptive nodes (the classical Node4/16/48/256 progression), path compression, lazy expansion; ordered iteration in key order (required for the term dictionary and any surface where iteration order can reach results); explicit interface for automaton-product traversal (Levenshtein automata over the term ART). Succinct rank/select: bitvector with o(n) directory supporting O(1) rank and select queries — the support structure under Elias–Fano high-bits queries (w1-codecs) and label/existence bitmaps. Vectorized hash tables: open-addressing layout with SIMD group probing (islanded in `fgdb-unsafe-simd` with scalar fallback), cache-line-conscious buckets, and an explicit determinism posture per B5/CGSE: any hash-table iteration order that can affect an answer or a canonical result encoding must either be canonically re-sorted by the caller or use a deterministic seed/iteration contract — hash seeds are never ambient entropy in strict execution; they come from the pinned execution context. All crates `forbid(unsafe_code)`; the only raw-pointer/SIMD code sits in ledgered islands behind safe traits with scalar fallbacks (constraint 2). Memory for query-scoped structures comes from asupersync region heaps with generational handles, so cancellation reclaims collection memory structurally (§2.1) — the collection types must be arena-compatible (allocator-parameterized) rather than hard-wired to the global allocator.

## Invariants & claim types
Constraint 2's ledger discipline binds every unsafe site used by these structures. FG-INV-12's coherence clause applies transitively: a collection whose iteration order leaks nondeterminism into a canonical result violates the determinism contract (constraint 4) — deterministic-iteration contracts are invariant-class where exposed. Throughput/probe-cost numbers are `benchmark` class on named fixtures only.

## Interactions
Consumes: w1-foundation-types (key/value types, canonical ordering), w1-codecs (rank/select shared with EF; bitmap interop), w1-unsafe-ledger (SIMD probe kernels). Produces structures consumed by: w7-fts (term-dictionary ART + Levenshtein automata), w3-buffer/w3-tier-d (buffer indexing per the RadixGraph/GTX lessons), w5-executor (vectorized hash join/aggregation, FreeJoin), w2-id-allocator (range bookkeeping), w8-kernels (masked-semiring workspaces).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property tests differential against `BTreeMap`/`HashMap` reference models (insert/delete/lookup/range/iteration over randomized operation sequences, including adversarial shared-prefix key sets for ART); ordered-iteration correctness (ART iteration equals sorted key order); rank/select exhaustive small-case verification plus randomized differential vs. naive scan; hash-table determinism test: fixed seed ⇒ identical iteration across runs and across SIMD/scalar dispatch; SIMD-vs-scalar bit-identical probe results; arena-compatibility test: structures allocate exclusively from a provided region heap and full reclamation occurs on region close (leak oracle from asupersync's suite); Miri/ASAN over island code paths; microbenchmarks (probe latency, ART point/range throughput) recorded as benchmark-class rows with machine profiles. E2E: `collections_e2e` — inside one lab-runtime region: build an ART term dictionary from a generated token corpus, run Levenshtein-automaton (edit≤2) product walks against a naive edit-distance oracle, execute a vectorized hash join of two generated relations against a BTreeMap-join oracle, answer rank/select queries over an EF high-bits bitvector, then cancel the region and assert full arena reclamation via the leak oracle; the script repeats across SIMD/scalar dispatch and two seeds with identical results. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): test-mode instrumentation logs {structure_kind, op_count, ART node-type histogram, probe-length distribution, iteration seed, dispatch_path, arena_id, bytes_allocated, bytes_reclaimed}; property tests log the failing operation sequence and seed on any counterexample; the e2e asserts the reclamation log shows bytes_reclaimed == bytes_allocated at region close and that iteration-order logs are identical across dispatch paths.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: PMA-based structures as primary (Teseo rebalance-storm lesson); external crates (im, hashbrown-as-dependency — note std's hasher is available but seed discipline is ours); pointer-chasing B-trees for in-memory dictionaries where radix wins on graph key distributions (the durable B-tree is w7-btree, a different artifact). Risk: ART worst-case memory on adversarial keys — bounded by resource accounting and documented degradation, never a correctness issue.

## Provenance
§2.1 (region heaps), §2.3 (mechanical sympathy row); §3.1 Teseo/GTX rows; §8.7 (executor kernels); §10.3 (FTS ART); §18.2.

description:
## What & scope
Implement `fgdb-crypto`: the crypto profiles and primitives not already supplied by an audited foundation — keyed BLAKE3 identity/digest functions, the object AEAD, KDFs (including the passphrase KDF of Argon2id lineage), signing profiles, `CryptoCx` entropy discipline, and zeroization. Where an audited foundation primitive exists (asupersync: rustls-backed TLS, RaptorQ per-symbol authentication machinery, macaroons), it is preferred; this crate fills only the gaps and wraps them under registered profile IDs. The external review pipeline (vectors, constant-time testing, misuse tests, expert review, release-blocking external audit) is part of this bead's deliverable, not an afterthought.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's One Version Universe is built on content-addressed, encrypted, RaptorQ-protected objects, so identity and encryption are load-bearing for everything: an `ObjectId` that does not recompute is a corrupted universe. The frankensqlite lesson (§2.3) is explicit: the Argon2id KEK hierarchy / per-object protection / encrypt-then-code design is a starting point whose nonce, AAD, per-encoding DEK, symbol-MAC, rewrap, and KMS/HSM details must be respecified — no correctness is inherited merely from the donor. The threat model is honest-but-curious storage: within one namespace it still observes equality and size/access patterns among opaque ObjectIds, but cannot perform an offline plaintext dictionary from the public slot alone; profiles that expose `K_oid` explicitly accept that leakage.

## Design — normative detail
Identity functions (consumed by W2 but implemented here): `ObjectId = BLAKE3_keyed(K_oid, "fgdb:logical:v1" ‖ DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId ‖ canonical_plaintext_header ‖ canonical_plaintext_payload)` — `K_oid` is an immutable random database identity key wrapped through the root/bootstrap/key-escrow chain; a 128-bit prefix is only a lookup accelerator and collision buckets always verify full digest, object kind, length, and canonical plaintext. Pipeline primitives: canonical plaintext deterministically compressed under `CodecProfile`; a random per-ciphertext DEK performs ONE object-level AEAD with AAD `("fgdb:object-aead:v1", ObjectId, CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest)` — the cipher descriptor excludes FEC and placement; `EncodingId = BLAKE3("fgdb:encoding:v1" ‖ canonical(EncodingDescriptorWithoutId))`; `PlacementId = BLAKE3("fgdb:placement:v1" ‖ canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId))` — neither ID nor a digest of the record is an input to itself. Symbol auth key: `K_symbol = KDF(DEK, "fgdb:symbol-auth:v1" ‖ EncodingId)`, authenticating the exact canonical `SymbolRecord` transcript — every serialized header field except the MAC bytes themselves, then the payload; no shorter competing transcript; symbols never reuse an object AEAD nonce and symbols from different `EncodingId`s never mix. DEK/ciphertext identity is separate from `wrap_key_epoch`: KEK/KMS recipient rewrap changes only immutable `KeyWrap` records, never `CiphertextId`/`EncodingId`. Appendix A fixes algorithms, profile IDs, tag lengths, AAD/MAC transcripts, bounds, and partial-tail rules; the crypto contract additionally pins algorithm agility, nonce/SIV mode, AAD digest, passphrase KDF parameters, KMS/HSM mode, rotation, zeroization, replica provisioning, backup escrow, signing-key rotation, and crypto-erasure limits. `CryptoCx` obtains production entropy independently of deterministic replay seeds, and secret entropy is never exported in incident bundles. BodyDigest recipes (`BLAKE3(domain_separator || canonical(schema_major, T excluding exactly the one BodyDigest field))`) are computed via this crate's digest API from generated recipes.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-09 (full text binds here): "`ObjectId` recomputes from the exact keyed, namespaced canonical logical transcript; `CiphertextId`, complete `EncodingId`, and non-self-referential `PlacementId` recompute from their registered descriptors and bytes/inventory. Root bootstrap reconstructs all identities without indexes; child-key AAD and symbol MACs cover their complete noncircular transcripts; collision buckets verify full identity and incompatible encodings never combine. Every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe." Constant-time behavior is a `bounded_model`/verification claim with named test methodology, never assumed; performance numbers for kernels are `benchmark` class. The §20 risk row is constitutional: "Prefer audited foundation primitives; constant-time/misuse verification, algorithm agility, independent review, and external release audit are mandatory."

## Interactions
Consumes: g0-identity-registries (AAD/transcript/digest recipes and profile ID rows), g0-threat-model, w1-foundation-types, w1-unsafe-ledger (any SIMD digest/cipher kernels live in `fgdb-unsafe-simd` with ledger rows and scalar fallbacks). Produces primitives consumed by: w2-object-identity (the identity pipeline), w2-root-bootstrap, w2-branch-fork/w9-key-lifecycle (envelope DAG wraps), w2-transparency (checkpoint signing), w1-authz-policy (token MAC verification), w1-generated-parsers (digest recipes in generated tests), w9-dp (noise seeding discipline via `CryptoCx`).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Published test vectors for every primitive and profile ID (checked into the golden corpus); constant-time verification: statistical timing-leak tests (dudect-style) plus a code audit lane asserting no secret-dependent branches or table indices in ledgered kernels; misuse tests: nonce reuse, wrong AAD, truncated/forged tag, wrong `K_oid`, wrong namespace, cross-`EncodingId` symbol mixing — all must fail closed with typed errors; zeroization tests (drop paths scrub key material; verified under Miri on the island crates); entropy-separation test: lab-runtime replay seeds never influence `CryptoCx` production entropy, and incident bundles contain no secret entropy (redaction assertion in crashpack tests); scalar-vs-SIMD bit-identity for every digest/cipher kernel dispatch path. The independent expert review and release-blocking external audit are tracked gate artifacts — the bead is not closable as "done for 1.0" without the audit engagement plan registered. E2E: `crypto_pipeline_e2e` — exercise the complete §5.1 pipeline on generated objects: canonical plaintext -> `CodecProfile` compression -> per-ciphertext DEK AEAD with the exact AAD -> `EncodingId`/`PlacementId` derivation -> `K_symbol` MAC over canonical `SymbolRecord` transcripts -> decode/verify round-trip; run twice under the lab runtime with different replay seeds asserting identical content-addressed identities but fresh DEKs/nonces (entropy separation made observable), then perform a KEK rewrap cycle asserting `CiphertextId`/`EncodingId` stability; repeat once per registered profile ID. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): every verify path logs {profile_id, object_kind, plaintext_len, ciphertext_len, encoding_id prefix, outcome, typed failure class} — never keys, nonces, or plaintext (asserted by a log-redaction test); each misuse-test rejection must emit a log record whose failure class matches the typed error; the timing-leak harness logs per-kernel sample counts and test statistics so the constant-time evidence is auditable from artifacts.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: importing RustCrypto/ring (closed universe); reimplementing RaptorQ or macaroons (asupersync owns them); accepting donor crypto composition by analogy; "functional vectors pass therefore secure" (§12.5 explicitly forbids this inference). Risk: in-house primitive subtly broken despite vectors — mitigated by preferring audited foundation primitives wherever they exist, algorithm agility for replacement, and the external audit gate.

## Provenance
§5.1 (identity pipeline, symbol auth); §12.5; §2.3 encryption row; §20 crypto risk row; App A; App F FG-INV-09.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Generate golden vectors, mutation corpora, cross-version fixtures, and fuzz targets
description:
## What & scope
The test-artifact half of the registry generation pipeline (split from w1-generated-parsers): for every registered durable kind, generate and check in golden vectors, mutation corpora, cross-version fixtures, and a fuzz target — all derived from the same registry rows and digest recipes as the encoders themselves, so tests and code can never disagree about a transcript.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: the ground-truth hierarchy is explicit — the normative appendices and the G0-generated golden vectors outrank BOTH the engine and `fgdb-reference`, so a differential mismatch is triaged against the spec and never resolved by making the reference imitate the engine. That only works if the vectors exist for every kind and are regenerated deterministically. B1: content addressing is falsifiable only via corpora that prove transcript boundaries byte-by-byte.

## Design — normative detail
Per kind: (1) golden vectors — canonical encodings of representative values (including extreme-value/null/boundary cases in the `CanonicalResultChunkDescriptor` golden-vector style), stable across regeneration for unchanged rows; removed experimental bytes remain reserved in the golden corpus forever. (2) Mutation corpora — systematic flips of every INCLUDED field of each digest transcript (must change the digest or be rejected) and every EXCLUDED field (must NOT change the digest — proving the include/exclude boundary), plus truncations, wrong tags, wrong-class codes, and test-range (`0xc000..=0xfffe`) discriminants that production readers must reject. (3) Cross-version fixtures — additive-minor unknown-field skip behavior and required-flag fail-closed behavior, exercised in both directions. (4) Fuzz targets — one per kind, respecting the kind's registered allocation/resource bounds, asserting length-before-allocation and checked arithmetic on malformed input. Encoder, decoder, field-table, golden-vector, mutation, and cross-version tests all use the same generated recipe (§5.1 digest law); the corpora are inputs to FG-INV-09's required "mutation, golden, cross-version, collision, wrong-key/namespace, mixed-symbol, and FEC-wire fuzz campaigns".

## Invariants & claim types
Serves FG-INV-09's enforcement column (generated digest/field checker plus mutation/golden/cross-version campaigns) and FG-INV-07's generated checker discipline. Corpus completeness (every kind has all four artifact families) is a CI invariant; corpus contents are evidence artifacts, not claims.

## Interactions
Consumes w1-generated-parsers (generator, recipes) and g0-identity-registries (rows/bounds). Consumed by: every durable-schema owner's test suite (w2a/w2b/w2c, w3, w9, w10, w11), verif-reference (golden vectors under its allowlist), verif-differential (mutation corpora feed campaigns), w10-fgp-core (wire-type fixtures).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
CI completeness check: every registry row of every class has golden/mutation/cross-version/fuzz artifacts or the build fails. Determinism: regeneration from identical registries is byte-identical (diff check). Boundary proof: excluded-field mutations leave digests unchanged; included-field mutations change them — both asserted per row. Fuzz targets run in CI smoke mode (bounded iterations) and in extended campaigns; findings are minimized and archived with seeds. Logging: corpus manifest records per-kind artifact digests and registry epoch. E2E: `corpora_regen_e2e` — from a pristine checkout, regenerate all four artifact families for every registry row and diff against checked-in bytes (byte-identical or fail); then, for one representative kind per identity class, run the full consumer loop: decode golden vectors with the generated decoder, replay the mutation corpus asserting included-field digest changes and excluded-field digest stability, run cross-version fixtures in both directions, and execute the fuzz target in smoke mode. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): beyond the corpus manifest above, generation logs per kind {kind_id, registry_epoch, artifact_family, artifact_count, output_digest, duration}; campaign runs log seed, iteration count, and minimized-input digests for findings; the completeness check logs the exact registry rows missing artifacts on failure so gaps are enumerable from CI output alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: hand-curated vectors (drift; the generator is the sole author); vectors stored only as test code (they are checked-in bytes so external implementations and the future verifier SDK can consume them). Risk: corpus bloat — bounded by representative-case selection rules in the generator, never by dropping a kind.

## Provenance
§5.1 (digest/registry law); §8.8 (golden-vector style); §15.4 (ground-truth hierarchy); App F FG-INV-07/09.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement fgdb-types/bigint/delta-types/claim/evidence/resource foundation crates
description:
## What & scope
Implement the value/type spine of the workspace: `fgdb-types` (core scalar values, identity newtypes, typed references), `fgdb-bigint` (canonical exact integers), `fgdb-delta-types` (the G0/W2 delta schema only), `fgdb-claim` (the claim-type constitution as a Rust type system), `fgdb-evidence` (evidence envelopes), and `fgdb-resource` (typed resource vectors/ceilings). These are pure-type crates: no I/O, no durable state, `forbid(unsafe_code)`, and they sit inside `fgdb-reference`'s dependency allowlist.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5 (determinism/evidence) begins with value semantics: if equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding are not provably coherent, byte-identical canonical results (constraint 4) are impossible. B1 (One Version Universe) needs typed references (`StrongRef<T>`, conditional refs, weak digests) as first-class values so the durable content graph can be checked as a DAG. B4 (Ripple) needs an exact integer domain: Z-set weights must live in the true integer additive group, not a bounded imitation. B6 needs resource types so agent workloads are admission-controlled by construction. The claim-type constitution (constraint 11) is the anti-benchmarketing weapon this market lacks: measured numbers can never quietly become correctness claims.

## Design — normative detail
`fgdb-types`: identity newtypes (`ObjectId` full 256-bit, `VId`/`EId`, `DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId`, epoch/sequence scalars), the typed reference family (`StrongRef<T>`, `Conditional*Ref<T>`, weak-digest target types — all of which must resolve to `logical_object_kinds.toml` rows), `BoundedBytes<N>`, and the canonical scalar value union governed by `CanonicalScalarProfile`: equality, hashing, total ordering, collation, coercion, and durable/result encoding for every value, with property tests enforcing `equal ⇒ same_hash`, comparator totality/transitivity, and encode/decode/order coherence. The `STRICT_PORTABLE` profile canonicalizes NaNs and signed zero; fixes decimal scale/rounding/overflow; stores timestamp instant plus zone/offset semantics and a content-addressed tzdb version; pins Unicode data/normalization/segmentation and each non-binary collation by ObjectId; fixes map-key order over canonical bytes; and rejects unavailable profile artifacts rather than consulting host locale/tzdb. (Executor-side numeric/reduction-tree rules are w5-determinism; the value types, orderings, and encodings live here.)

`fgdb-bigint`: in-house canonical signed-limb exact integers with a unique (canonical) representation so compare/hash/encode are coherent; checked arithmetic throughout; designed as the promotion target for Ripple's `ZWeight`, which uses checked `i128` as the fast representation and promotes before overflow; limb allocation/spill is resource-accounted so exhaustion aborts or lags a derived computation without publishing partial state.

`fgdb-delta-types` (G0/W2 delta schema ONLY — the differential machinery itself is w2-delta-batches): exact typed delta rows — create/delete/property/valid-time/counter/escrow/sketch/schema/constraint deltas; the sequence-neutral `LogicalDeltaTemplate` keyed by graph/branch/relation/schema/`IntentSemanticsOid`; and the rule that only a committed `MarkerRef` turns a template into an ordered `LogicalDeltaBatch`.

`fgdb-claim`: two closed vocabularies. Registry claim classes per constraint 11: `invariant | proof | bounded_model | statistical | slo | benchmark`, with the lattice law that a weaker claim class may inform policy but may not enforce or justify a stronger one, and the routing law (`invariants.toml` only exact safety/liveness; `evidence.toml` and `slo.toml` for the rest). Evidence-envelope `ClaimClass` per §15.0: `SafetyInvariant` (must hold on every execution; failure is a correctness defect), `FormalModelClaim` (theorem/model-check with abstraction, bounds, refinement status), `StatisticalClaim` (population, sampling/selection rule, alpha, power/effective sample size, assumptions), `ConfigurationModelClaim` (model version, fitted inputs, sensitivity, validity domain), `EmpiricalGate` (fixture, machine/profile, sample count, variance budget, comparison rule).

`fgdb-evidence`: envelope types binding a `ClaimClass` to an immutable evidence identity — calibration windows, selection policy, strata, propensity support, regime epochs, fallback, and failure behavior are immutable evidence identities. `fgdb-resource`: typed resource vectors/ceilings consumed later by permits, `FrameLimits`, and W10 admission.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (binding clause): "Canonical scalar equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding are coherent." The claim-type constitution itself: a weaker claim class never enforces a stronger one — this crate makes that a type error, not a review comment. Everything here is `invariant`-class scaffolding; no slo/benchmark rows originate in this bead.

## Interactions
Consumes g0-claim-registries (claim vocabulary), g0-identity-registries (reference/field classes), g0-command-contracts (delta-row field registry). Produces types consumed by literally every other bead; specifically: w1-generated-parsers (encoders over these types), w1-authz-policy (binding types), w2-delta-batches (delta machinery over `fgdb-delta-types`), w6-zset-circuits (`ZWeight` promotion into `fgdb-bigint`), w5-determinism (`CanonicalScalarProfile` execution rules), verif-reference (allowlisted import), verif-sextant (evidence envelopes).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property suites: `equal ⇒ same_hash`, comparator totality/transitivity, encode/decode/order coherence for every scalar type under `STRICT_PORTABLE`; bigint ring laws (associativity/commutativity/distributivity), canonical-representation uniqueness (no two byte encodings of one value), checked-overflow behavior at `i128` promotion boundaries, and encode/compare coherence under randomized + adversarial limb patterns; delta-row golden vectors and exhaustive per-arm encode/decode round trips; claim-lattice negative tests (constructing an invariant from statistical evidence is a compile error or typed rejection); tzdb/collation-artifact-unavailable tests reject rather than fall back to host locale. Fuzz: scalar decode with malformed bytes under length-before-allocation bounds. Logging: property-test failures must emit the exact seed and canonical byte encodings of counterexamples. E2E: `foundation_types_e2e` — one lab-runtime script that constructs representative values of every canonical scalar type under `STRICT_PORTABLE`, round-trips encode/hash/order coherence, promotes a `ZWeight` across the `i128` boundary into `fgdb-bigint` and back, builds every delta-row arm into a `LogicalDeltaTemplate` and (with a synthetic committed `MarkerRef`) an ordered `LogicalDeltaBatch`, and constructs one evidence envelope per `ClaimClass`; outputs must be byte-identical across two seeds, and a scripted claim-lattice violation must produce the typed rejection. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): in addition to counterexample seed/byte logging above, coherence suites log {scalar_type, profile_oid, value_digest, comparator outcome} per checked pair class, bigint tests log {limb_count, promotion boundary hit}, and tzdb/collation rejection paths log the missing artifact ObjectId, so every failure is reproducible from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: serde-derived enums as durable formats (constraint 9 — encoders come from the registries, w1-generated-parsers); floating-point or saturating Z-weights (breaks the integer-group semantics B4 requires); host locale/tzdb consultation (destroys cross-machine determinism); a single flat "claim" type without the lattice (would let benchmark numbers justify invariants). Risk: canonical scalar profile churn after G1 would invalidate golden vectors — mitigated by freezing the profile artifacts by ObjectId at G0.

## Provenance
§1 constraints 4, 9, 11; §8.6 (scalar profile); §9.1 (ZWeight); §18.1–18.2; App B (delta rows); §15.0.

## Fresh-eyes contract addition — narrowed Cx obligation vocabulary
The purpose-typed context surface is exact and load-bearing, not merely a naming convention. Subsystems receive only `QueryCx`, `TxnCx`, `CommitCx`, `MaintCx`, or `ReplCx` wrappers over asupersync `Cx`; the registered obligation vocabulary includes `pin_snapshot`, `reserve_prepared_bytes`, `reserve_raft_payload_space`, and `publish_segment`, plus the complete owner-specific set generated from command/resource registries. Compile-fail unit tests prove each wrapper cannot invoke another role's effects. Simulation/E2E tests cancel each obligation at acquisition, transfer, publication, and cleanup boundaries and assert zero leaks with ordered redacted lifecycle events. The merge evaluator's narrowed Cx has no clock, entropy, network, or filesystem capability, and a compile-fail surface proves that negative capability set.

title: Generate durable encoders/decoders, field tables, digest recipes, and walkers
description:
## What & scope
Build the code-generation pipeline that turns G0's frozen registries — the five identity-class registries `logical_object_kinds.toml`, `physical_record_kinds.toml`, `bootstrap_frames.toml`, `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml`, and `wire_types.toml`, plus the cross-index and contract registries `durable_fields.toml`, `command_contracts.toml`, `command_type_classification.toml`, and `durable_state_slots.toml` with its backing plane registries (`state_payload_fields.toml`, `protocol_state_fields.toml`, `prepared_state_fields.toml`, `consensus_state_fields.toml`), and the registered BodyDigest/transcript recipes — into canonical Rust encoders/decoders, field tables, and digest-recipe implementations. Every durable schema in the system gets its serialization from this pipeline; no hand-written durable encoder exists outside it. (The generated golden vectors, mutation corpora, cross-version fixtures, and fuzz targets are split into w1-format-test-corpora.)

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Constraint 9 bans serde-derived enums as durable formats; constraint 6 makes published bytes constitutional. The only way to keep hundreds of durable schemas honest across a decade is to make the registry the single source of truth and generate everything — encoder, decoder, checker, test — from the same rows, so a schema cannot drift from its registration and FG-INV-07/FG-INV-09 checkers are generated rather than hand-maintained. This is B5's evidence discipline applied to bytes; B1 depends on it (content addressing is only sound if canonical encoding is unique and reproducible); B6 rides it (robot-readable schemas/docs are generated from the same registries per G4).

## Design — normative detail
Registry law (restated): each registry has its own 16-bit code space with `0x0000` and `0xffff` permanently invalid, `0x0001..=0x7fff` permanent core assignments, `0x8000..=0xbfff` negotiated extension assignments, and `0xc000..=0xfffe` test/experimental assignments that production readers reject. A released code changes status to `Retired` but is never reassigned; removed experimental bytes remain reserved in the golden corpus. `registry_epoch` changes only when rows are added or retired, not when prose moves. Every class requires the appropriate canonical encoder/decoder, construction-order annotation, version/feature/posture compatibility rule, size/resource limits, and fuzz/golden corpus; a missing, duplicated, cross-class, untyped-field, or orphan row is a build failure. G0 enforces four separate bijections (logical schema↔logical-object row, physical record↔physical identity row, bootstrap frame↔bootstrap row, embedded durable type/tag↔wire-type row) plus disjointness across all five identity classes and code-range/nonreuse rules — the generator consumes those validated registries and re-verifies them. The fifth identity class, `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` (restore artifacts that necessarily predate target `K_oid`), has its own identity law — `PreBootstrapArtifactId = BLAKE3("fgdb:restore-prebootstrap:v1" ‖ target_claim_or_reservation_domain ‖ artifact_kind ‖ schema_version ‖ canonical_wrapper_bytes)` — whose IDs are never `ObjectId` and never accepted by `StrongRef`; its wrapper encoders/decoders and canonical-import record generation belong to this pipeline like every other class. `durable_state_slots.toml` is the total cross-plane registry whose rows each point to exactly one backing field registry (`state_payload_fields.toml` for canonical semantic payloads; `protocol_state_fields.toml` for the protocol plane; `prepared_state_fields.toml`/`consensus_state_fields.toml` for prepared ownership and Raft hard/snapshot/configuration state), and every required checkpoint/snapshot/floor/backup/restore/GC/transition walker is generated from it; a feature with no slot, a slot with no writer, or an unclassified protocol mutation is a G0 failure.

Encoding baseline (App A, normative for all generated code): declared format major/minor; little-endian fixed integers; canonical unsigned LEB128 only where the field says varint; length-before-allocation; checked arithmetic; per-kind maximum sizes. Unknown additive-minor fields are length-delimited and skipped; unknown required flags fail closed. Readers authenticate/validate headers and resource bounds before allocating or decompressing.

Digest generation: stored digest fields are never defined by naming convention — every `durable_fields.toml` digest row declares exactly one semantic class: `TargetDigest` (of separately identified bytes), `TranscriptDigest` (with a registered transcript recipe), `WeakIdentityDigest`, or `BodyDigest`. A `BodyDigest<T>` row fixes `{domain_separator, schema_major, included_field_tags, excluded_field_tags}` with default recipe `BLAKE3(domain_separator || canonical(schema_major, T excluding exactly the one BodyDigest field))`; signatures/MACs are excluded only when the row explicitly lists their stable tags. Unknown exclusions, two body-digest fields, an implicit zero placeholder, or computing over bytes that include the digest itself are G0 errors. Encoder, decoder, field-table, golden-vector, mutation, and cross-version tests all use the same generated recipe.

DAG law enforced by generated encoders: the canonical content graph is a DAG — every strong, conditional, and weak-digest value in newly encoded bytes must already be known; a future applied result may be described only by a sequence-neutral spec, body recipe, or assigned scalar order, never by its not-yet-computable ObjectId/digest; self IDs, mutually strong cycles, and an input command that names its own applied result are invalid and unencodable.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07 (binding clauses): "every field, typed reference, transcript digest, and weak identity is registry-resolved and names already identified bytes, and every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root. `command_contracts.toml` is bijective with every role command arm/handler and `state_payload_fields.toml` roots every written state class." FG-INV-09 (binding clause): "Every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe" — with its enforcement column requiring the generated digest/field checker plus mutation, golden, cross-version, collision, and fuzz campaigns. All invariant-class; generation determinism itself is an invariant of the build.

## Interactions
Consumes: g0-identity-registries (the five identity-class registries + durable_fields + the durable_state_slots/plane field registries + BodyDigest recipes), g0-command-contracts (command/state field registries + bijection CI), g0-format-arms (frozen decision-batch rows: identity-column codec registrations, `PackedObjectGroup`, `externally_verifiable` markings, activation-batch specs — all of which must have rows before generation), w1-foundation-types (target types), w1-codecs (varint/framing primitives), w1-crypto (BLAKE3/keyed digest implementations behind the recipes). Produces generated encoders consumed by every durable-schema owner (all w2a/w2b/w2c beads, w3-tier-d/w3-tier-r, w9-audit-*, w10-fgp-core wire types, w11-*), by w1-format-test-corpora (test artifacts), and by verif-reference (generated registries under its allowlist).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Generation determinism: identical registry inputs produce byte-identical generated code (CI diff check). Round-trip: generated encode∘decode is identity on arbitrary valid values (property tests per kind). DAG enforcement: encoding a self-referential or forward-referencing value is a compile-time or typed construction error with a negative fixture. Digest recipes: generated BodyDigest implementations match hand-computed BLAKE3 transcripts on reference examples for every recipe class. Registry-law negatives: retired codes rejected; test/experimental-range (`0xc000..=0xfffe`) codes rejected by production-configured readers; unknown required flags fail closed; additive-minor unknown fields skipped (length-delimited). Bounds: no generated decoder allocates before validating declared sizes (length-before-allocation assertions). Bijection re-verification: generator fails on missing/duplicated/cross-class/orphan rows with diagnostics naming the row. Logging: generator emits a per-build manifest (registry epochs, row counts, output digests) for provenance. E2E: `codegen_pipeline_e2e` — run the generator on the frozen G0 registries from a clean tree, compile the generated crates, re-run and diff (byte-identical); then drive one encode -> digest -> decode -> field-table-walk cycle for a representative kind of each of the five identity classes, plus the negative path (retired code, test-range discriminant, unknown required flag) against a production-configured reader — wired as a single CI job. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): beyond the per-build manifest above, codegen logs per kind {kind_id, identity class, encoder/decoder symbols, recipe_id}; decoders log rejections as {kind_id, offending field/tag, rejection class} and the negative tests assert those records; a generation-nondeterminism failure must log the first differing output file and byte offset.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: serde/derive-based durable encoding (constraint 9 — no transcript control); hand-written per-schema encoders (guaranteed drift at this schema count); digests defined by field-naming convention (a G0 error class); generated code depending on engine crates (generation stays in the foundation layer so `fgdb-reference` can consume it). Risk: generator bugs become correlated bugs across all formats — mitigated by the independent `fgdb-reference` decode path and the ground-truth hierarchy placing appendices + golden vectors above both implementations.

## Provenance
§5.1 (registry classes, code spaces, DAG law, digest classes); §19 G0/W1 rows; App A preamble; App F FG-INV-07/09.

title: Implement the canonical durable resource-ledger and accounting transition contract
description:
## What & scope
Implement the canonical durable resource-accounting contract: split ephemeral versus durable requests, fixed charge vectors, authority roles, quota paths/policies/owner keys, ledger state/basis/transition/spec/applied record, and exact Reserve/Charge/Release/Expire/Transfer/Adjust laws. Runtime QoS is a consumer, not the ledger definition.

## Why
Admission estimates and durable ownership are different. If a process-local budget is mistaken for a durable charge, restart can refund work; if a prepared/result/backup owner is expired or partially transferred, obligations leak or bytes are reclaimed early. One exact ledger makes accounting atomic with object ownership.

## Design — exact normative contract
**Resource accounting.** `ResourceRequest` is `{ephemeral:EphemeralResourceBudget,durable:DurableChargeVector}`. Ephemeral budget is `{cpu_ns,resident_bytes,temp_bytes,read_iops:WindowedRateBudget,write_iops:WindowedRateBudget,egress_bytes,output_bytes,output_rows,max_snapshot_age,maximum_subscription_backlog}` and is enforced by cancel-correct runtime obligations, never canonical state. Durable vector is the fixed versioned checked nonnegative `{canonical_durable_bytes,retained_history_bytes,branch_count,index_count,view_count,subscription_count}`. Replica/FEC/cache/placement bytes are operational capacity, not semantic tenant charges. Only `ResourceAccountingRole::Local|Meta` authors canonical durable quota; shards enforce ephemeral local capacity.

`QuotaPath` is a canonical nonempty root-to-leaf path of `Database|Tenant|Graph|Branch|Feature`. `ResourceLimitPolicy` fixes the path tree, per-bucket hard vectors, protected maintenance reserve, class rules, and `ResourceLimitPolicyEpoch`. Every transition updates the exact leaf and each unique ancestor once. `ResourceOwnerKey` is `Attempt{posture,registration_identity}|Statement{posture,registration_identity,statement_seq}|ResultDelivery{posture,result_delivery_id}|Subscription{cursor_id}|DurableObject{object_class,stable_logical_owner_key}|Replay{replay_manifest_key}|BackupPin{backup_id,scope}|PreparedClosure{prepared_ownership_id}|Maintenance{job_id,registered_class}` and never a future ObjectId.

`ResourceLedgerState` is `{format_version,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,role,ledger_generation,limit_policy_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLimitPolicy>,limit_policy_epoch,bucket_state_root,reservation_entry_root,charge_entry_root,applied_transition_index_root,body_digest}`. Each bucket is `{hard_limit,protected_maintenance_reserve,ordinary_reserved,maintenance_reserved,committed}`. All arithmetic is checked; ordinary use satisfies `committed+ordinary_reserved <= hard_limit-protected_reserve`, and registered maintenance consumes only its named reserve. The transition index maps a transition ID to immutable body digest and applied outcome, making exact retry idempotent and body drift invalid.

`ResourceLedgerBasis` is the nonretaining `{role,state_identity:WeakStateIdentity,ledger_generation,ledger_root_digest,limit_policy_oid,limit_policy_epoch}`. `ResourceLedgerTransition<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the sequence-neutral pre-order object `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,transition_id,idempotency_key_digest,basis:ResourceLedgerBasis,owner:ResourceOwnerKey,resource_class,quota_path,operation,exact_sorted_before_buckets,exact_sorted_after_buckets,checked_arithmetic_commitment,authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>>,release_or_measurement_evidence_ref?,body_digest}`. `operation` is exactly `Reserve{reservation_id,reservation_generation:0,vector,expiry:None|ProfiledDeadline}|Charge{reservation_id,expected_reservation_generation,charge_id,vector,release_unused_reservation:true,stable_subject_key}|Release{subject:Reservation|Charge,expected_generation,exact_vector,release_authority_ref}|Expire{reservation_id,expected_generation,exact_vector,owner_quiescence_proof_ref,time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>}|Transfer{subject:Reservation|Charge,expected_generation,source_owner,source_path,target_owner,target_path,exact_conserved_vector,transfer_authority_ref}|Adjust{charge_id,expected_generation,before_vector,after_vector,stable_subject_key,measurement_or_logical_change_proof_ref}`. The header, basis role, owner, decision, and containing command must byte-match. Expire evidence must be `Expired` for the exact subject/action.

Reserve creates one active reservation. Charge consumes it completely, creates one charge, and releases the deterministic unused remainder. Release/Expire/Transfer operate on a whole entry; partial changes use Adjust. Transfer conserves the vector globally and checks destination ancestors after netting shared ancestors. No timeout, disconnect, process death, logical delete, or stale cache releases an entry, and expiry fails while prepared ownership, final certification, result delivery, backup, or remote grants retain the subject. `ResourceLedgerTransitionSpec {expected_basis,sorted_transition_refs,complete_transition_id_set_commitment,semantic_subject_basis,terminal_audit_gate}` is the standalone-control wrapper; transactions and exact lifecycle specs embed transition refs directly. A generated enclosing-command matrix fixes legal operation tags.

Apply verifies one common basis, IDs, exact before buckets, canonical net deltas, policy/authorization/evidence and constructs the new state, then `ResourceLedgerAppliedRecord {command_ref,assigned_role_logical_position,transition_refs,before_root_ref,after_root_ref}`, then payload/command record. Pre-order transitions never name the applied record or after payload. `ResourceChargeEffect` is exactly `{transition_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>,stable_subject_key,before_vector,after_vector}` and the effect set requires a generated bijection with transaction-owned transition refs. Graph/object and ledger state apply atomically. Tests exhaust arithmetic boundaries, ancestor races, idempotency drift, remainder release, shared-ancestor transfer, destination insufficiency, every hold/release/expiry race, every crash/root/audit publication cut, Local/Meta differential replay, and checkpoint/backup/restore/activation/GC coverage.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-16 and resource portions of FG-INV-17/18/20. Consumes authority bindings, command/state slots, foundation exact arithmetic and time evidence. W4 coordinator/constraints/escrow, W9 DP/audit, W10 QoS/result/output, backup/restore/GC and W12 Meta custody consume it. Shards may hold only certified ephemeral allocations; durable authority is Local or Meta.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact schemas/rows/codecs exist for every request/vector/role/path/policy/owner/state/basis/transition/spec/applied type and operation arm.
- Unit/golden tests cover checked arithmetic, ancestor quota aggregation, idempotency/body drift, charge class, whole-entry transfer/release, state basis and atomic object+charge publication.
- Property/model tests prove nonnegative conservation, every live durable object has exactly one owner/charge, release once, transfer without split/loss, prepared-owner nonexpiry, and current-authority enforcement.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects overflow/underflow, wrong role/tenant/path/owner, stale basis, duplicate key with drift, partial transfer, expiry of protected owner, Shard durable charge and object-without-charge publication.
- Crash/DPOR E2E races reserve/charge/transfer/release/expiry with result activation/ACK, prepare/commit/abort, backup/restore, GC and service restart; ledger and rooted owner remain bijective.
- JSONL emits {event_version,role_and_group,operation,request_key,owner_key,quota_path,charge_class,amount_vector,basis_generation,transition_id,from_state,to_state,ancestor_balances_digest,object_publication_digest?,time_evidence_digest?,verdict,recovery_action,replay_command}; principal-safe IDs only, no hidden query/data.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: process counters as durable truth, floating charges, partial owner transfer, timeout expiry of prepared/result obligations, and Shard-local durable authority. Conservative quota refusal is correct on stale/missing evidence.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 1980-1990; sections 7.6 and 13.3.

comments.text:
Increment landed as cdf0ef2 (crate lane only: crates/fgdb-resource/src/ledger.rs). Added the exact ResourceRequest split with validated WindowedRateBudget, EphemeralResourceBudget, and versioned six-axis DurableChargeVector. Added ResourceLimitPolicyEpoch, immutable per-path ResourceBucketPolicy, exhaustive ResourceClassRule operation tags, canonical ancestor-closed single-root policy trees, and registered maintenance-class identities.
