Apply verifies the direct external successor, constructs the compact operation summary/terminal common/role-specific tombstone recipe, and removes the canonical lease edge exactly when the candidate becomes audit-visible. `RestoreSourceLeaseReleaseNoEffectFinalizeSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the distinct refusal/conflict path: it consumes the action-typed zero-effect terminal artifact/evidence/import, proves the archive head remains the exact Active predecessor, returns to `AwaitingSourceRelease + Current`, and inserts a permanent release-operation tombstone; it never releases a pin or pretends the source lease ended. A fresh release requires a new operation ID and current eligibility.

Successful Local finalize releases the exact matching `RestoreTerminalPinBasis<Local>` pin and enters ReleasedTerminal; an Operational terminal consumes its promotion-seal basis, while an Abandoned terminal consumes its abandonment-publication/inventory basis. Successful Meta finalize instead enters `SourceReleasedAwaitingPinReleaseAuthorizationPublication`: it retains its exact terminal pin basis, freezes the exact required Shard set, and commits only `RestoreTerminalPinReleaseAuthorizationBody {restore_id,restore_epoch,terminal_disposition:Operational|Abandoned,target_identity_incarnation_and_service,release_finalize_applied_identity,release_operation_request_receipt_terminal_evidence_and_no_successor_commitment,required_shard_set_and_each_expected_terminalizing_projection_commitment,meta_terminal_pin_basis_commitment,authorization_generation}`. After that Meta root and audit visibility are durable, a certificate attempt creates `RestoreTerminalPinReleaseAuthorization {SameGroupCertificateHeader,body:RestoreTerminalPinReleaseAuthorizationBody,post_release_meta_state_root_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStateRoot>,root_slot_durability_digest,visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}`. `GlobalRestorePinReleaseAuthorizationInstallSpec` consumes that already-created certificate, byte-matches the frozen body recipe, and alone enters `SourceReleasedAwaitingParticipantPinRelease`; no future certificate identity is embedded in the release-finalize predecessor.

`ShardRestoreTerminalPinReleaseSpec` is the exact `{authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<RestoreTerminalPinReleaseAuthorization>,expected_registry_state:OperationalParticipantComplete|AbandonedParticipantComplete,expected_terminalizing_projection,own_terminal_pin_basis_ref:StrongRef<RestoreTerminalPinBasis<Shard>>,source_lease_projection_ref:StrongRef<ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection>,current_root_no_other_pin_owner_proof_ref,post_release_tombstone_body_recipe}`. The authorization disposition, registry arm, terminal projection, and pin-basis arm must all match. Apply verifies its Shard is exactly one authorization member, drops only its own seal-or-abandonment-basis/pin/projection edges, creates `ShardRestoreTerminalTombstone`, and enters `ParticipantTerminalPendingAck`; it cannot name the future acknowledgement. Only after that root is RootSlot-durable may a certificate attempt create `ShardRestoreTerminalPinReleaseAck {SameGroupCertificateHeader,authorization_identity,restore_id,restore_epoch,terminal_disposition,shard_id,terminal_tombstone_ref:StrongRef<ShardRestoreTerminalTombstone>,pin_release_applied_identity,post_release_shard_state_root_ref:StrongRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,root_slot_durability_digest,current_root_no_pin_proof_ref,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}`.

`GlobalRestoreParticipantPinReleaseFinalizeSpec` consumes the installed authorization and every-and-only required certified `ShardRestoreTerminalPinReleaseAck`, verifies their disposition/tombstone/root/no-pin subjects and the frozen bijection, releases the matching Meta terminal pin basis, builds `MetaRestoreTerminalTombstone`, and alone selects Meta ReleasedTerminal. Only after that finalize root and its audit visibility are durable may a certificate attempt create `GlobalRestoreParticipantPinReleaseCompletionCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,restore_id,restore_epoch,terminal_disposition,pin_release_authorization_identity,participant_pin_release_finalize_applied_identity,exact_sorted_ack_identities,meta_terminal_tombstone_ref:StrongRef<MetaRestoreTerminalTombstone>,post_finalize_global_state_root_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStateRoot>,meta_pin_no_owner_proof_ref,root_slot_durability_digest,visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}`. Each Shard orders exact `ShardRestoreParticipantTerminalConfirmSpec {completion_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalRestoreParticipantPinReleaseCompletionCertificate>,expected_registry_state:ParticipantTerminalPendingAck,own_terminal_tombstone_ref:StrongRef<ShardRestoreTerminalTombstone>,own_pin_release_applied_identity,expected_authorization_identity,expected_terminal_disposition}` and changes only to compact ParticipantTerminal carrying the certificate's portable commitment; it adds no acknowledgement back-edge and cannot substitute another restore, authorization, disposition, shard set, or Meta terminal. Heavy prior inputs remain rooted until their respective visibility/pin-ack/final-projection floors close, then compact terminal state cuts them. Conflicting operation, inventory, holder, authority, generation, transcript, disposition, or shard set fails closed.

## Invariants & interactions
Consumes the prebootstrap journal/acquisition protocol, RestoreSourceLease implementation, key lifecycle, universal dispatch terminal evidence, archive grant lineage, time validation/expiry, and canonical import. Feeds transform/reconciliation, abandonment, bridge readiness, promotion, backup/restore inventory, GC and key-destruction floors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact schemas/rows exist for lease operation terminals, source-key inventory/cleanup progress, physical inventory, terminal pin families, cleanup/refusal/tombstone evidence, and all strong/weak reference/floor rules.
- Unit/golden tests freeze portable versus canonical histories, every key-access class/disposition, terminal pin operation, physical locator identity, body digest, and no-plaintext-key encoding.
- Property/model tests prove inventory/disposition bijections, monotone cleanup, one terminal provider outcome, no key use after revoke/destroy, no unowned target byte, and pins retained until exact successor ownership.
- Fuzz/mutation rejects missing/duplicate inventory members, wrong restore/lease/grant generation, cross-plane receipt, stale operation, mismatched source/target key identity, plaintext key material, and premature pin release.
- Crash/DPOR E2E interrupts every recover/rewrap/decrypt/re-encrypt/revoke/destroy/delete/pin/lease status/import boundary; restart resumes by terminal records and finishes with zero ambient source access.
- JSONL emits {event_version,restore_id,lease_identity,lease_generation,operation_family,operation_id,terminal_disposition,key_access_class?,key_identity_commitment?,cleanup_state?,physical_inventory_ordinal?,pin_family?,pin_state?,provider_counter_or_cas_version?,recovery_action,replay_command}. Secret/plaintext key bytes and protected archive locators are never logged.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: cleanup on Drop, best-effort key revocation, one aggregate done bit, deleting target bytes without a registered disposition, and releasing source lease before terminal pins/cleanup are authoritative. Missing evidence blocks readiness.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 2343-2413.

title: Implement restore transform and reconciliation through the hidden pre-readiness handoff
description:
## What & scope
Implement §16.6 restore through the hidden reconciliation boundary: `RecoverSameIdentity` incarnation fencing, the leaves-first `RecoveryIncarnationTransformPlan`, `PendingRestoreCreationGuard` publication of the first `RecoveryReconciling` root, and exhaustive obligation reconciliation through the reconciled hidden pre-readiness handoff. `fgdb-w11-restore-bridge-readiness-9f8l` owns bridge/readiness attestation; hidden activation/visibility/service state machines, service promotion, reopen/completion, and `CloneNewIdentity` live in the dedicated promotion successors.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Restore is where identity, security, and continuity systems are easiest to break: a restored node that serves before reconciling obligations can double-spend allocations, leak hidden audit candidates, resurrect revoked capabilities, or split-brain against a still-live incarnation. The design forces: external incarnation CAS before any write authority, a total transform of identity-bearing bytes, exhaustive per-class obligation reconciliation, and hidden-until-promoted service state. B5: every phase is a typed root with certificates consumed by later commands; B1: the restored history is the backup's history — never a fork.

## Design — normative detail
**Identity fencing.** Restore acquires a new archive-owned `RestoreSourceLease` (`w11-restore-lease`). `RecoverSameIdentity` first advances the external `ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord` through `Operational(I) -> RestoreFencePending -> RestoreReserved(J)` where all old-incarnation leases are revoked/expired and `J > max(external retired floor, current live incarnation, backup incarnation)`; only one CAS contender can reserve `J`. A member-bound `ClusterIncarnationLease(scope=RecoveryOnly|OrdinaryWrite)` is checked together with the inode lease/fence immediately before **every** irreversible seal, prepared publication, receipt, Raft proposal/ack, certificate, and RootSlot publication. Recovery-only authority cannot serve or perform ordinary work; unavailable/stale continuity authority makes same-identity recovery read-only or forces `CloneNewIdentity`.

**Transform.** Archived content crosses only through `BackupArchiveRef<T> -> PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T> -> RestoreArchiveRef<T>` under the live lease; the publication envelope separately through `BackupPublicationArtifactRef<T> -> RestorePublicationArtifactRef<T>`; a raw manifest artifact ref is not restore authority. `RecoveryIncarnationTransformPlan` is pre-order; **leaves-first** execution produces `RecoveryIncarnationProjectionResult` before any bridge. For every changed canonical body: verify/decrypt the source, rewrite only already-produced target references, recompute `ObjectId`, perform new AEAD (AAD includes that ObjectId), build new `CiphertextId`/`EncodingId`/`Placement`/openers/wraps, prove target availability. Registry-proved incarnation-neutral values alone may reuse a realization. Externally signed historical evidence remains byte-identical as `CarryPriorIncarnationEvidence` — never rewritten or fraudulently re-signed. Current configurations/certificates/keys/trust are recreated; old sessions/capabilities are invalidated with tombstones — new capabilities require fresh authentication/authorization.

**First root.** `PendingRestoreCreationGuard` is the **only** filesystem path that can publish the first non-Genesis `RecoveryReconciling` root; it is limited to the exact projection result, recreated current authority, role-tagged `RestoreState`, bridge, bootstrap closure, manifest, and RootSlot — it cannot encode user work, ordinary receipts/Raft, `Operational`, or service advertisement. It follows the same exclusive staging-inode, sync, no-replace rename, directory-sync, inode-reread, and loser-isolation discipline as creation, then yields only `RecoveryWriterLeaseGuard`. The bridge (`RecoveryBridgeSpec<Role>`: role authority, transform/projection refs, lease basis, generated role payload, `InitialRestoreStateRef`/`InitialRestoreRegistryRef` tag-refined refs, allocation-epoch authority, dependency coverage bitmap) carries already-authenticated recipes and earlier objects only, never future Protocol/Prepared/Consensus/manifest/slot identities; restore never validates an old root as current and never creates a headless non-Genesis state.

**Reconciliation.** Before activation, recovery CAS-reserves an allocation epoch above the external identity floor; **burns every possibly issued post-backup range**; reconciles latest privacy/audit continuity and pending DP/audit transitions; resolves or explicitly retains prepared/decision, remote retention/trust, key, backup/replay, cursor/delivery, resource, and derived obligations; and rotates current channel/signing/wrap/verifier authority. Branch lifecycle is reconciled the same way: §5.6's permanent `BranchRetireTombstone` survives backup/restore and fences same-identity revival, so a restore of an older root that still contains a retired branch head must reconcile against the tombstone before service promotion — exactly as identity/audit continuity are reconciled — under its own generated reconciliation slot; the branch-merge ledger's non-forgetting token/coverage idempotency maps are likewise preserved across restore, never reset. `RestoreReconciliationRoot` has one generated slot per obligation class, each `Pending|Resolved|ExplicitlyRetained|DisabledFailClosed`; **readiness forbids `Pending`**. Unavailable privacy authority disables DP; unavailable audit evidence disables completeness-gated work; a permanent gap requires the exact external CAS plus local mirror. Incarnation change hides no obligation.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-11 (excerpt): allocation epochs, leases, and canonical spent commitments are monotonic under the registered `AllocationContinuityProfile` and prevent VId/EId/generated-key alias, overlap, or reuse across restore; disappearance creates permanent spent tombstones. FG-INV-10 (excerpt): before the ordinary token, only the typed takeover, fresh-creation, or **guarded restore publication** may occur; every irreversible seal, receipt, Raft action, certificate, and slot write rechecks both authorities. FG-INV-09 (AAD includes the recomputed ObjectId, forcing re-AEAD of changed bodies). FG-INV-19 (replay grades weaken attributably across incarnations). RPO/RTO and restore drills are deployment-gate evidence class.

## Interactions
Consumes `w11-restore-lease` (all archive access), `w11-backup`/`w11-backup-publication` (manifests, projections, `PortableRoleRecoveryCut` dispositions, reopen machinery), `w2-continuity-profiles` (`ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord`), `w2-writer-takeover` (guard discipline), `w2-id-allocator` (epoch reservation/burning), `w9-key-lifecycle` (rewrap/rotation), `w2-recovery`, and `w2-branch-retire` (the permanent `BranchRetireTombstone` semantics and merge-ledger compaction state whose revival fencing restore must reconcile, §5.6). `fgdb-w11-restore-bridge-readiness-9f8l` consumes the reconciled hidden root and proves readiness; the promotion successors exclusively own activation, service exposure, reopen, and completion. `w10-archive-open` reuses the verifying-reader path read-only.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Split-brain: live incarnation I racing a `RestoreReserved(J)` contender — old leases fail every irreversible action; two contenders — exactly one reserves J. Transform differential: every changed body recomputes ObjectId and re-AEADs (wrong-AAD decryption fixtures); incarnation-neutral reuse only via registry proof; `CarryPriorIncarnationEvidence` byte-identity asserted; leaves-first ordering verified (no bridge before `RecoveryIncarnationProjectionResult`). Guard: crash at every staging/rename/sync/reread step with loser isolation; guard encoding user work/ordinary receipts/`Operational` is a generated negative. Reconciliation: each obligation class forced to `Pending` blocks readiness; unavailable privacy/audit authority flips exactly the DP / completeness-gated `DisabledFailClosed` slots; permanent-gap path requires external CAS + mirror. Branch-retire fencing: restoring an older root that still contains a retired branch head must reconcile against the permanent `BranchRetireTombstone` before readiness/service promotion — serving, forking, subscribing to, or otherwise reviving the retired head from the restored root is a negative — and the branch-merge ledger's token-outcome/imported-coverage idempotency state is asserted intact post-restore (a merge retry returns its original outcome; overlapping re-import is still detected). Allocation: post-backup issued ranges burned; FG-INV-11 alias/reuse campaign. E2E with logs: back up an isolated disposable lab fixture, simulate complete source-storage loss only inside that fixture, and run `RecoverSameIdentity` through the reconciled hidden pre-readiness handoff; logs record epoch J, per-class reconciliation slot map, projection counts, and the explicit handoff identity.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: manifest-file-as-authority restore (lease + receipt + grant subject set required); in-place reuse of source ciphertexts for changed bodies (AAD binds ObjectId — re-encryption mandatory); re-signing historical evidence (carry it byte-identical); recovery-only authority performing ordinary work. Risk: reconciliation stalls on dead external authorities — typed `DisabledFailClosed`, read-only, or `CloneNewIdentity` paths, never silent gaps.

## Provenance
§16.6 (lines 1200-1206), §5.6 (459, 469), App A lines 2071-2073, 2545-2557; App F FG-INV-09/10/11/19.

### Fidelity addendum — hard scope boundary
This bead must not create a bridge-readiness certificate, activation/visibility/service certificate, continuity/catalog promotion receipt, Operational or OperationalPendingIndependentReopen state, shard open/reopen acknowledgement, public endpoint, capability, session, or ordinary writer authority. Its terminal artifact is the exact reconciled hidden root plus a complete per-class reconciliation/disabled-retained disposition inventory suitable for the next bead to evaluate. Tests assert every promotion command/tag is uninhabited from this bead's output alone; logs end with `handoff_state=ReconciledHiddenPreReadiness` and the next required contract ID.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

### Phase boundary correction — restore reconciles continuity without activating DP
Local restore must import/reconcile the exact privacy accounting continuity and opaque permanent request/debit/seed/output-or-no-output commitments before service, including split-brain and stale-CAS negatives. It does not execute a DP query, draw noise, charge a budget, or advertise DP. Tests use the signed synthetic continuity-authority fixture from `fgdb-w9-dp-continuity-import-bhtn`; the restored capability manifest keeps DP disabled until W9/G3 separately proves and activates the live mechanism.

title: Implement follower writer-anywhere preparation with leader-only ordered publication
description:
## What & scope
Implement §14.4 writer-anywhere: followers may prepare `TxnProposal`s and candidate physical work (validation, capsule candidates, payload staging), but only the leader / global Raft order validates final effects, builds or approves the final capsule, and publishes.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Preparation is the expensive part of a write (parsing, binding, witness construction, payload encoding, D1 staging); ordering is the serialized part. Letting any replica do preparation scales write throughput without forking the commit discipline (B1: one ordered history; B3: the same Loom execution runs anywhere). B5 demands honesty about the ceiling: **no near-linear committed-write claim ships without a benchmark separating preparation from ordered publication** — ordered commitment remains bounded by validation, payload distribution, and Raft.

## Design — normative detail
A follower may: accept a session's statements, run binding/planning/execution against its authorized snapshot (under `w11-read-contracts` rules), construct the `TxnProposal` and candidate physical work, stage prepared payload as a donor (producing `PreparedCommitRecord` + `PayloadReceipt` per `w11-payload-availability`), and forward the proposal. The leader (or the global Raft order) alone: validates final effects at the certification basis, performs or approves final capsule construction, assigns `LogicalCommandSeq`/`CommitSeq`/HLC, and publishes. Follower-prepared work is candidate-only — it holds no semantic authority, and any drift between the follower's preparation basis and the leader's certification basis triggers the FG-INV-17 regeneration path (rebase under capability-stripped deterministic contexts pinned to `IntentSemanticsOid`; every semantic drift regenerates effects, workspace/read/write state, constraints, escrow/resource requirements, witnesses, logical deltas, allocation plan, RETURNING bytes, and capsule before final-certification reservation and terminal signing).

Prepared ownership stays stable across the handoff: the follower's staged payload is owned under a stable `PreparedOwnershipId` (never re-keyed by leader adoption), so the leader's `PayloadAvailabilityCertificate` can bind the follower's receipts directly. Leader change mid-preparation neither loses nor duplicates the prepared closure (FG-INV-16); the new leader either adopts via the recorded ownership or the proposal is re-prepared under drift rules.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-17 (excerpt): once an Active final-certification reservation freezes the basis, rebase is forbidden; conflicting drift must use the proved pre-signature cancel/restart path. FG-INV-07 (excerpt): W12-analog ordering — validation, payload distribution, then Raft; timeout releases no prepared owner. FG-INV-01 (excerpt): each registered attempt maps to at most one immutable semantic terminal outcome; matching retries return the recorded lineage. The scaling claim is **benchmark class**: a §17-registered benchmark must publish preparation throughput and ordered-publication throughput as separate curves.

## Interactions
Consumes `w4-coordinator` (WriteCoordinator choreography, final-certification reservation, holds), `w11-payload-availability` (donor staging/receipts), `w11-raft-multi` (proposal/ordering), `w2-commit-protocol`. Precursor of `w12-prepare` (shard prepare fragments keyed by admission generation are the sharded generalization). `w11-read-contracts` supplies the follower's authorized snapshot.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property/sim: follower prepares, leader certifies — assert identical final effects to leader-local preparation (deterministic-context differential); forced-drift tests (head moved between preparation and certification) must regenerate, never sign stale capsules. Leader-change campaign: crash leader after follower staged payload, before/after proposal, before/after certification reservation — assert exactly-one-outcome per attempt (FG-INV-01 oracle) and no prepared-closure leak (FG-INV-16 quiescence oracle). Bench gate: publish separated preparation-vs-ordered-publication throughput; the near-linear-preparation claim may only cite the preparation curve. E2e with logging: N-follower cluster, mixed write load routed to all members, logs record per-txn prepare-member, certify-term, drift-regenerations count.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: multi-leader/leaderless commit (would fork the One Version Universe); follower-certified commit with leader ratification (certification must see the one ordered basis); shipping "scales linearly" marketing without the separated benchmark (explicitly forbidden by §14.4). Risk: high drift rates under contention erase the preparation win — the drift-regeneration counter is a first-class benchmark output so this is measured, not assumed.

## Provenance
§14.4 (line 1077), §7.4/§8.6 via FG-INV-17, App F FG-INV-01/07/16/17.

title: Implement sharded backup at barrier P, receipt-first restore, and capability migration
description:
## What & scope
Sharded backup/restore plus Local-to-Sharded capability migration: the exact-barrier backup pipeline (intent/pin/closure/seal/publication/grant/verify/release with two-phase abort), the hidden receipt-first restore ladder, and `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationSpec` with its consumed-tombstone index.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: a backup is a portable, quorum-signed, bijection-proved artifact at one exact global prefix `P` — never "latest at least P". B6: agent-held capabilities survive posture migration with exactly-one-successor semantics; nothing ever reinterprets an old ObjectId. Rejected: decode-proof shortcuts for backup, timeout-based abort of publication-ambiguous backups.

## Design — normative detail
**Backup.** `GlobalBackupIntentSpec` fixes `backup_id`, barrier `P`, expected global state root, the generated complete Meta pinned-closure union, topology, exact sorted required shard domains, history interval, archive/key-recovery/format profiles; apply pins the Meta closure (`GlobalBackupIntentRecord` -> quorum `GlobalBackupIntentCertificate`). Each shard orders `ShardBackupPinSpec` with `barrier_state:ExactCurrentPrefix{global_applied_prefix=P}|ExactHistoricalCut{...}` — **there is no `LatestAtLeastP` tag** — pinning the generated-complete closure at `P`; `ShardBackupCopyVerification` proves inventory bijection, per-object decode, recoverability/failure domains, content reopen, and a canonical shard semantic digest; `ShardBackupClosureCertificate` (no retaining source-pin edge) is installed only via `ShardBackupClosurePublishSpec` (sole `Pinned -> Certified`). `GlobalBackupSealSpec` accepts one certificate from every and only required shard, all at exact `P`. Publication is state-shaped: `GlobalBackupPublicationAuthorizeSpec` -> receipt import -> transparency -> `GlobalBackupGrantIssueImportSpec` (installs Published, never releases a source pin) -> `GlobalBackupArtifactVerifySpec` (ArtifactVerified) -> `GlobalBackupReleaseAuthorizeSpec` (Releasing, portable `GlobalBackupReleaseAuthorizationCertificate`) -> per-shard `ShardBackupReleaseSpec::Authorize|Finalize` (Finalize alone removes the pin; signed `ShardBackupReleaseAck`) -> `GlobalBackupReleaseFinalizeSpec` (every and only configured shard ack under the still-current Activated hold) -> archive-hold completion -> Released. Abort is two-phase (`GlobalBackupAbortBeginSpec`/`ShardBackupAbortSpec`/`GlobalBackupAbortFinalizeSpec`) and legal only with `BackupNoPublicationProof<Meta>` — any publication receipt or ambiguous external state permanently forces roll-forward.

**Restore.** Receipt-first, hidden until independently reopened. Meta issues `RestoreShardBootstrapProjection` + certificate (continuity recovery-only projection, `RestoreAllocationEpochShardSlicePayload`, prior-lease barrier, source-lease projection, archive inventory/key recipients, transform recipes); each shard builds consumer-local `ShardAllocationEpochAuthorityProjection` (duplicate/overlapping/gapped/wrong-parent slices fail before bridge construction). Both roles stay `RecoveryReconciling` through their hidden phases — Meta: `ActivationOrdered -> VisibilityCommitted -> ServicePreparedHidden`; each shard: `ActivationAppliedHidden -> VisibilityApplied -> ServicePreparedHidden` (per-stage `RestoreShardActivationAck`/`RestoreShardVisibilityAck`/`RestoreShardServiceReadyAck`, all `service_gate:Hidden`). The Meta ladder is `GlobalRestoreActivationSpec/Certificate -> RestoreVisibilityCommitSpec/Certificate -> GlobalRestoreServicePrepareSpec/Certificate -> GlobalRestoreServiceFinalizeSpec/FinalCertificate -> GlobalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec` (finalize clears Meta only into `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed`; completion — consuming the Meta seal, `MetaRestoreIndependentReopenProof`, and one `RestoreShardOperationalAck` from every and only required shard — alone selects Operational); shards use `ShardRestoreServiceOpenSpec` into `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed`, then seal + `ShardRestoreReopenConfirmSpec` with a fresh independent reopen proof into `OperationalAwaitingSourceAccessClosure`, and only after `ShardRestoreSourceAccessCloseSpec` installs the exact closure may the ParticipantComplete root produce `RestoreShardOperationalAck`. Abandonment: `GlobalRestoreAbandonFinalizeSpec`/`ShardRestoreAbandonApplySpec` select `RecoveryAbandoned` with `RestoreRetentionAnchor::AbandonmentPinPending`, then the pin-install specs alone install `TerminalPinBasis`; only afterwards are source-access cleanup, participant pin release, and tombstone compaction legal. Gate: "Restore proves continuity reservation, exhaustive leaves-first readdress/re-encryption, hidden activation/visibility/service preparation, receipt-first continuity/catalog publication, Meta finalize, shard open, independent reopen, operational acknowledgements, completion, and source-lease release."

**Capability migration.** Local-to-Sharded capability migration is exclusive and service-epoch fenced. `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationSpec` is the Meta union `TerminalTxnOutcome|TerminalMergeOutcome|ReadYourWrites|BufferedResult|SubscriptionCursor|DurableArtifactOutput`; each arm embeds one fresh E2 `AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>` and a byte-matched current same-principal/no-wider authorization decision — a raw `AuthorityBindingRef`, scalar epoch set, or legacy Local authority cannot inhabit the command. `CapabilityMigrationIndex` maps `(transition_identity,legacy_capability_commitment) -> LiveSuccessor|Consumed{migration_tombstone_ref}` plus a secondary idempotency map, so a legacy capability yields exactly one successor even under retries with different request keys; `CapabilityMigrationConsumedTombstone` prevents reuse without retaining live authority. Outstanding Local results/cursors either follow their certified transition policy or require a new baseline, never reinterpret an old ObjectId; subscriptions always start a new baseline and emit no cross-role delta. Owners without capabilities are transferred separately, never smuggled through capability migration: PendingVisibility and ReleasedAwaitingActivation promises have no legacy capability, so `RoleTransitionProtectedPromiseInventory` enumerates every Local result, initial/pending cursor output, artifact output, and protected error in those states — each with its semantic detachment/escrow/byte closure, release state, and certified import recipe — and `PostActivationProtectedPromiseTransferSpec` consumes each inventory member exactly once through `ProtectedPromiseTransferIndex (transition_identity,legacy_owner_key) -> Transferred{new_meta_owner_key,import_commitment}|TerminalTombstone`, creating a Meta pending or released owner with no lease/capability and preserving release evidence without treating E authority as valid E2 authority. Current E2 reauthorization is deferred to activation; subscription members create a new Global initial baseline; the role-transition seal/floor retains both indexes and every untransferred member; promise transfer must complete before capability migration can complete. `CAPABILITY_MIGRATE/CAPABILITY_MIGRATED` is the sole capability frame family — legacy `RESUME_MIGRATE` is only a wire alias for its SubscriptionCursor arm.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-19: sharded replay is no stronger than its weakest required group; activation/legacy evidence uses certified transition wrappers, never raw old-group refs; missing/expired trust yields the declared weaker grade only. FG-INV-10: durable-format writes only under activated `FormatCompatibilityState`; old decoders retire only after exhaustive reachable/backup/restore/replay floors. FG-INV-16: backup pins/restore-source leases are obligations that cannot be lost or silently released. FG-CFG-01 covers modeled archive durability; restore-drill timings are benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes single/multi-member backup-restore machinery from `w11-backup`/`w11-restore`, six-stage release + floors from `w12-recovery-gc`, key recipients from `w9-key-lifecycle`, capability schemas from `w10-capabilities`. Barrier interacts with `w12-topology` (movement retains grants across moves).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate: "Exact backup at barrier P proves per-shard copy/reopen/closure, portable Global manifest publication, archive grants, ordered shard release acks, and Meta finalize"; capability migration "exclusive and service-epoch fenced." Tests: pin/closure/seal crash matrix; wrong-shard/duplicate/missing closure certificates rejected; abort attempted after publication receipt permanently illegal; restore hidden phases never serve traffic (direct-endpoint negatives); allocation-epoch slice gap/overlap rejection; migration idempotency under retried requests with new keys (one successor, byte-identical replay); stale legacy capability post-migration returns typed failure, not reinterpretation. Promise-transfer completeness: every enumerated PendingVisibility/ReleasedAwaitingActivation promise is consumed exactly once (Transferred or TerminalTombstone), untransferred members block the role-transition seal, and capability migration cannot complete before promise transfer. E2E: full backup at P during write load in an isolated disposable lab fixture, simulated total source loss followed by restore to a new incarnation, replay-grade audit of a sampled synthetic workload, then capability-migration drill on fixture cursors/results; log every state transition of the Meta/shard backup registries.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: exact-`P` pins pause reclamation on lagging shards (bounded by pin floors). Rejected: `LatestAtLeastP` barriers; content-proof pin release; migrating active transactions/merges (freeze gate proves none exist).

## Provenance
§14.6/§16 backup-restore doctrine; App A 2121-2139, 2409-2447, 2535-2595, 1636-1640 (promise inventory/transfer); App D 3112; §19:1352-1354.

### Fidelity addendum — exact sharded backup schema group
`GlobalBackupIntentSpec` is exact: `{backup_id,barrier_global_prefix:P,expected_global_state_root_ref,expected_meta_pinned_closure_refs[BackupPinnedClosureRef<Meta>],expected_meta_pinned_closure_coverage_bitmap,expected_topology_ref,exact_sorted_required_shard_domains,exact_partition_and_authority_commitment,expected_global_history_interval,meta_live_closure_inventory_ref,archive_profile_ref,recipient_and_key_recovery_profile_ref,format_matrix_ref,terminal_audit_gate}`. Its record pins the exact Meta closure and its certificate uses the universal signer lock.

Each required shard consumes exact `ShardBackupPinSpec` with `barrier_state=ExactCurrentPrefix{P}|ExactHistoricalCut{current_prefix,historical_state_ref,checkpoint_and_history_proof_ref}`, configuration/topology, complete generated closure bitmap, and remote-retention grant. `ShardBackupCopyVerification` proves source/archive bijection, per-object decode, failure-domain recoverability, content reopen, and canonical semantic digest. `ShardBackupClosureCertificate` binds shard/domain/partition, source and archive identities, copy proof, active Meta projection, key/derived/remote obligations, inventory/recoverability/semantic/reopen digests, signing attempt and signatures; it contains no retaining pin edge. `ShardBackupClosurePublishSpec` is the sole Pinned-to-Certified edge. `GlobalBackupSealSpec` accepts every-and-only shard certificate at exact P plus the Meta copy proof and manifest.

Release/abort remain exact: `ShardBackupReleaseSpec::Authorize` retains the pin; `Finalize` alone removes it and enables `ShardBackupReleaseAck`. `GlobalBackupReleaseFinalizeSpec` requires every-and-only configured ack under the current Activated hold. Abort is `GlobalBackupAbortBeginSpec -> GlobalBackupAbortAuthorizationCertificate -> ShardBackupAbortSpec/ShardBackupAbortAck -> GlobalBackupAbortFinalizeSpec` and is legal only with exact no-publication proof; ambiguity forces roll-forward. Meta states and Shard states are the closed inventories in Appendix A, and every nonterminal state is covered by checkpoint/configuration/backup/restore/GC floors.

E2E uses an isolated disposable sharded lab fixture, simulates complete source loss only inside that fixture, and uses simulated archive/KMS/escrow/catalog/continuity authorities. It drives write load at P, backup, hidden new-incarnation restore/reopen, replay audit, and capability migration. Logs record intent/certificate, topology/partition/shard set, each pin/copy/closure/seal/publication/hold/release/abort state, exact-P proof, manifest/grant/receipt commitments, restore hidden-state ladder, and capability successor/tombstone; no raw locator, credential, key, or protected graph data is logged.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement global certification: GlobalConflictIndex, DSC, and the virtual-serial batch law
description:
## What & scope
The Meta certifier: `GlobalConflictIndex`, `DistributedSerializationCertificate`, and the complete registered **virtual-serial batch certification law** of §14.6. The reservation schemas it selects into live in `w12-final-reservation`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1+B5: distributed serializability, not "local SSI plus hope" — Meta-Raft canonically owns the conflict graph and a deterministic certifier decides every outcome with replayable evidence. The batch law exists to lift sequencer throughput without a second execution discipline; this is explicitly NOT the §3.4-rejected Calvin-style deterministic transaction lane.

## Design — normative detail
**Conflict state.** `GlobalConflictIndex {basis_global_logical_command_seq,entries[(global_txn_id,registration_generation) -> {snapshot/start/terminal prefixes,state:Active|PrepareAdmitted|Committed|Aborted|ReadClosed,admission_generation?,participants,read_witness_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef],write_summary_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef],incoming/outgoing_edges,overlap_close_floor}],safe_snapshot_frontier}` — for every registered active or recently completed overlapping serializable transaction, INCLUDING read-only work, it retains all `wr`,`ww`,`rw` edges with proof references until no live transaction can add one; a new registration generation never overwrites an older overlapping generation. **Certificate.** `DistributedSerializationCertificate` is meta-owned, sequence-neutral, counter-free: `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,attempt_key,lifecycle_basis:ReadOnly{read_routing_certificate_ref}|ReadWrite{prepare_admission_record_ref,admission_generation,routing_certificate_ref},held_final_certification_basis_commitment,conflict_index_basis:WeakStateIdentity,conflict_index_basis_digest,overlapping_attempt_key_set_commitment,candidate_read_witness_refs,candidate_write_summary_refs,candidate_edges[{kind:wr|ww|rw,from,to,witness_or_version_proof_ref}],retained_graph_projection_digest,scc_verifier_version,acyclic_result,conservative_fallbacks[],quorum_signatures}`. Every meta follower reconstructs `may_affect` in BOTH directions against every overlapping prepared/committed/closed transaction, verifies every routed shard/constraint contribution, reruns the registered SCC algorithm, and rejects FCW/uniqueness conflicts or any cycle; assigned counters occur only in `MetaOrderAttemptInput`.

**The virtual-serial batch certification law (complete).** V1 forbids speculative semantic certification and replaces the fully serial certify-then-apply reading with this registered law: (1) A certification batch — commit and read-close certificates alike — names exactly one applied **basis** prefix and the exact ordered certification **frontier** of decided-but-unapplied predecessor batches. (2) "Fully applied" is pinned against Raft durability: an entry is basis-eligible when its command is quorum-durable AND its deterministic apply has executed on the certifier's state machine; decided predecessors enter through the frontier, so certification never waits on a later fsync of its own batch to begin the next. (3) Candidates are certified in canonical meta registration order: candidate i's complete predicate set — SCC acyclicity, FCW/uniqueness, constraint-aggregate folds, expected-branch-head/key-epoch checks, and drift — is evaluated against the named basis folded with the frontier's and members 1..i-1's decided effects, with meta registration order as the deterministic intra-batch loser/abort priority, so no two candidates ever certify against an identical fold state. (4) An intra-batch member naming a branch head already consumed by an earlier member aborts deterministically under the existing drift rule; head identities are apply-assigned and never pre-chained into a virtual head. (5) The acyclicity check consumes the complete cross-candidate edge set in both directions, intra-batch and batch-to-frontier. (6) Apply order and Raft proposal order equal canonical certification order, and a batch never orders ahead of a frontier predecessor; a frontier predecessor that fails to order voids every dependent certificate through admitted abort/release and a new registration generation — digest substitution never recertifies stale work (failed-frontier recovery). (7) Epoch, projection, topology, configuration, and format-changing controls, and every quiescence-proof-bearing escrow or constraint transition, are **batch singletons**. (8) Speculation remains forbidden: any basis or fold state not derivable from already-decided outcomes, and any omitted cross-candidate edge, rejects the batch. (9) Escrow custody, sequence/HLC assignment, and audit-event bases are batch-safe by construction — exclusive Held custody precedes certification, counters are assigned only at apply through `MetaOrderAttemptInput`, and order supplements are never signed into audit bodies. (10) The batch's `GlobalFinalCertificationReservation` **batch arm** — a registered generalization of Appendix A's single-candidate schema whose member set carries per-candidate sub-holds, each with its own selection and each consumed only by its member's terminal command; the single-candidate form is exactly the degenerate one-member batch — is the single legal owner of the shared final-certification basis under FG-INV-02's exclusive-ownership clause as scoped by its Appendix F row. (11) Not-Calvin: this is a batching law inside the existing certifier — explicitly not the §3.4-rejected Calvin-style deterministic transaction lane; no second execution discipline exists. (12) Dual ceilings: certification of batch n+1 may overlap application of batch n; the residual ceiling is the per-command Meta apply chain, and the §19 W12 gate publishes the serial and batched ceilings side by side. Missing/stale support, partition, or resource exhaustion waits or aborts conservatively; monotone coarsening may add false positives only. Read-only results return only after ordered `ReadClose`.

**Reservation.** The `GlobalFinalCertificationReserveSpec/Reservation` schemas, hold roots, and pre-signature cancellation path are built in `w12-final-reservation`; this bead consumes an Active reservation (single or batch arm) as the held certification basis.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02 (batch clause): under §14.6's law the batch-scoped `GlobalFinalCertificationReservation` is the single legal live owner of a shared certification basis and carries per-candidate sub-holds; exclusivity is per generation, not per candidate, and no candidate-level owner may coexist with a live batch owner. FG-INV-05: W12 Meta histories remain plain serializable unless Meta registers the same real-time certification rule that makes Local strict serializable; Meta state contains every local, cross-shard, read-only, statement-workspace, positive/negative/gap/path edge; compaction removes detail only after overlap closure. FG-INV-17: once an Active reservation freezes the basis, rebase is forbidden; conflicting drift uses the proved pre-signature cancel/restart path. Ceilings are benchmark-class (both published); the SCC/history and batch-vs-serial oracles are verification-class.

## Interactions
Consumes prepares/reservations from `w12-prepare`, witnesses from `w4-ssi-witnesses`, ordering from `w12-meta-clock`. Produces certified terminals for `w12-decision-visibility`; batch-singleton rule constrains `w12-constraints-authority` and `w12-escrow-dp-alloc`. The independent oracle lives with `verif-oracles`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
An independent SCC/history oracle checks every history — including same-I/O-batch and same-basis-batch two-writer, rw-cycle, aggregate-overflow, and same-head cases — plus batch-vs-serial equivalence: a batched history must produce the identical admitted set, identical abort set, and identical committed history/state digests as virtual-serial replay of the same submission order. Tests: fold-order determinism (permuted arrival, fixed registration order, identical outcomes); frontier-order failure voiding dependents; batch-singleton and omitted-edge rejection. Bench gate: publish serial and batched sequencer ceilings plus the residual per-command Meta apply ceiling. E2E: scripted 3-shard cluster under a sustained mixed commit/read-close storm with contention hotspots and forced same-basis batches; run the independent oracle over the complete logged history AND a virtual-serial replay of the same submission order, asserting identical admitted sets, identical abort sets, and identical committed history/state digests; mid-run, inject a frontier-predecessor ordering failure and assert every dependent certificate is voided through admitted abort/release with new registration generations (no digest substitution). DETAILED LOGGING (required): every certification batch logs `{batch_id, basis_prefix, ordered frontier batch ids, canonical member order, per-candidate predicate results (SCC/FCW/uniqueness/fold/head/key-epoch/drift), consumed cross-candidate edge set, per-candidate decision, singleton_class?}`; every voided or retired certificate logs its failed-frontier cause and successor generation; the oracle consumes only these logs plus ledgered certificates, so post-implementation verification requires no debugger.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: conservative coarsening inflates aborts under contention (false positives only; measured). Rejected: Calvin lane (§3.4); speculative certification; pre-chained virtual heads; candidate-level owners coexisting with a batch owner.

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet "Distributed serializability" (1087); App A 1736-1754, 1854; §19:1354; §20:1379; App F FG-INV-02/05 (3131/3134).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement exact W12 compaction, reconfiguration, and distributed-GC formats
description:
## What & scope
Implement exact W12 terminal/never-registered compaction, expiry, evidence publication, Meta reconfiguration, remote-grant retirement, and distributed-GC authorize/cancel/completion-required/progress/completion formats. This splits schema precision from the oversized recovery/topology implementations.

## Why
Heavy detailed state may be released only after all public status, result, workspace, remote grant, audit, delta, backup, replay and conflict obligations transfer. Distributed GC additionally changes irreversibly from cancellable to completion-required when any participant starts. These are durable protocols, not background job flags.

## Design — exact normative contract
The autocommit-write arm byte-matches the preparation retained by `GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord` and is legal only for committed WriteReturning. Its `AtomicProtocolDetach` publication creates `ResultDeliveryOwner::AutocommitWriteTerminal`, charge transfer/Protocol escrow, a PendingVisibility, ReleasedAwaitingActivation, or legal inline ActiveDeliverable record/index leaf, and only `{delivery_id,detachment_commitment}` in the semantic frontier. Independent Protocol retention—not activation or client ACK—is the result postcondition. Matching retry returns the same applied record and owner commitments; a different bitmap, participant set, frontier, public bundle, result arm, or predecessor fails. ReadYourWritesCapability and ordinary terminal success remain unavailable until TerminalReady and its exact audit release; output bytes remain unavailable until the result owner is ActiveDeliverable. No prose “mirror” is sufficient evidence.

Attempt-history compaction is cumulative and has three separately ordered phases; deterministic apply never manufactures a quorum signature. `AttemptLookupKey` is the closed tag `ByAttempt{database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,global_txn_id,registration_generation}|ByOutcomeCapability{capability_domain_commitment,scoped_token_digest}`. `PublicNeverRegisteredOutcome` is the frozen `{posture,public_reason:PublicReasonProjection,original_response_commitment}` copied from `NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle`. `TerminalAttemptSummaryLeaf` is `NeverRegistered{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,outcome_capability_key:AttemptLookupKey::ByOutcomeCapability,internal_reason_class,public_outcome:PublicNeverRegisteredOutcome,audit_terminal_commitment,internal_staging_generation,internal_terminal_global_prefix}|Terminal{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,attempt_key:AttemptLookupKey::ByAttempt,outcome_capability_key:AttemptLookupKey::ByOutcomeCapability,operation_class,internal_terminal_global_prefix,public_outcome:TerminalPublicOutcome,audit_terminal_commitment}`. The summary retains protected frozen response bytes and therefore must retain the full binding; the later expiry rewrite alone may replace it in lookup indexes with a payload-free `TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Meta>` tombstone. A NeverRegistered leaf has no optional or synthetic attempt identity: absence of registration is part of the tag's meaning. Both public outcomes are copied byte-for-byte from their detailed bundles and include the original response commitment; neither leaf has a retaining edge to audit detail. Internal reason/generation/prefix fields are never serialized by the public status projector. `TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot` is a canonical authenticated persistent map from keyed lookup hashes to leaves plus `{summary_generation,covered_closed_prefix,leaf_count,root_digest}`. Its membership proof is consumed server-side after exact capability validation; the client receives only the frozen public projection plus a blinded proof projection, never the full leaf/path containing attempt keys, prefixes, or authority bindings. A successor root must equal the prior root plus the command's sorted insertions, proven by `PersistentMapExtensionProof`; it may structurally share map nodes but contains no `StrongRef` to a predecessor summary root, audit detail, or heavy attempt evidence, and an existing key can only be an identical idempotent leaf.

`NeverRegisteredEvidence` is `{begin_reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBeginReservationRecord>,terminal_record_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredTerminalRecord>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,outcome_capability_key:AttemptLookupKey::ByOutcomeCapability,staging_generation,authenticated_detailed_value_proofs:{global_begin_idempotency_index:NeverRegisteredDetailed,global_outcome_directory:NeverRegisteredDetailed},no_reservation_binding_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoReservationBindingProof>,audit_terminal_commitment,absence_of_exported_registration_or_shard_import_commitment}`. `NoReservationBindingProof` is generated from the current begin-index terminal leaf, the reservation-key uniqueness proof, the Meta prepared/certificate/export roots, and the registered inverse-reference index for reservation identities; it proves that this reservation was never consumed by registration or exported, without inventing an attempt/family key. `NeverRegisteredFloorSpec` is `{basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_global_prefix,basis_begin_index_digest,basis_outcome_directory_digest,basis_prepared_root_digest,basis_certificate_ledger_digest,basis_reservation_inverse_index_digest,sorted_evidence_refs[StrongRef<NeverRegisteredEvidence>],expected_prior_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,candidate_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,extension_proof_ref:StrongRef<PersistentMapExtensionProof>,exact_detailed_to_compacted_begin_and_directory_rewrite_commitment,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply revalidates every detailed value and nonbinding proof against current roots, inserts the exact never-registered summary leaves, atomically changes begin-index and outcome-directory entries from Detailed to Compacted while preserving their same replay ref, and creates compact `NeverRegisteredFloorRecord {assigned_global_logical_command_seq,source_command_digest:WeakDigest,rewritten_lookup_key_commitment,summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,applied_global_prefix}` with no retaining edge to its command/spec/evidence. It creates, burns, or rewrites no attempt/family/conflict entry and can never change the previously returned reason or response bytes.

`GlobalOutcomeExpirySpec` is a separate ordered control `{capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,expected_begin_index_entry:BoundCompacted|NeverRegisteredCompacted,expected_outcome_directory_entry:CompactedTerminal|NeverRegisteredCompacted,time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,expected_verifier_key_and_profile_floors,expected_begin_retry_and_lookup_floors,expected_retention_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedHistoryCut>,permanent_begin_tombstone_body,permanent_outcome_tombstone_body,terminal_audit_freeze:AuditFreezeField::Required<MetaControl>,terminal_audit_gate}`. The evidence must classify the replay object's exact window `Expired` for this action, the two compact leaves and replay identity must agree, and every promised retry/lookup floor must be closed. Apply atomically changes both leaves to `ExpiredTombstone` values containing the same scoped-key/token/capability commitments and expiry-evidence digest, drops the replay edge only in that transition, and permanently prevents key/token reuse. A valid old capability thereafter returns `TokenExpired`; an invalid or unauthorized input remains `NotVisibleOrUnknown`. Expiry does not remove the internal terminal summary leaf or fabricate an attempt identity.

`AttemptDeltaCompletionEvidence` is `Committed{global_delta_batch_ref:StrongRef<GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch>,global_delta_publish_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,published_frontier_at_or_beyond_commit_proof_ref:StrongRef<GlobalDeltaFrontierProof>}|NoDeltaApplicable{terminal_kind:Aborted|ReadClosed,proof_digest}`. `AttemptCompactionEvidenceRef` is the exact closed union `MetaDecision{record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>}|MetaConstraintRelease{record_ref:StrongRef<ConstraintReleaseRecord>}|MetaAuditTerminal{visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,audit_outcome_identity_and_commitment:WeakDigest}|MetaResultDisposition{disposition:ResultDispositionRef}|MetaWorkspaceRelease{evidence:WorkspaceReleaseEvidenceRef}|MetaBackupRelease{record_ref:StrongRef<BackupReleaseRecord>}|MetaReplayRetention{record_ref:StrongRef<ReplayRetentionRecord>}|MetaRemoteRelease{record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone>}|ShardPostVisibility{ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardAppliedAck>}|ShardConstraintRelease{ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardConstraintReleaseAck>}|ShardWorkspaceRelease{ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardWorkspaceReleaseAck>}`. `IndependentAttemptObligationRef` is `Result{retention_ref:StrongRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord>}|Backup{retention_ref:StrongRef<BackupIndependentRetentionRecord>}|Replay{retention_ref:StrongRef<ReplayRetentionRecord>}|RemoteGrant{grant_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>}|CapabilityFloor{floor_ref:StrongRef<CapabilityLookupFloor>}`. `ClosedAttemptEvidenceBundle` is the heavy pre-order closure `{sorted_terminal_ready_outcome_refs[StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord>],begin_idempotency_and_public_status_proof_refs[StrongRef<BeginPublicStatusProof>],sorted_evidence_refs[AttemptCompactionEvidenceRef],sorted_delta_completion_evidence[AttemptDeltaCompletionEvidence],statement_terminal_summary_proof_refs[StrongRef<StatementTerminalSummaryProof>],result_delivery_disposition_proof_refs[StrongRef<ResultDeliveryDispositionProof>],workspace_generation_and_local_overlay_release_proof_refs[StrongRef<WorkspaceReleaseProof>],workspace_remote_grant_release_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardWorkspaceReleaseAck>],overlap_close_proof_refs[StrongRef<ConflictOverlapCloseProof>],complete_selected_attempt_and_public_outcome_commitment}`. `ClosedAttemptCompactionSpec` is `{compaction_id,basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_global_prefix,basis_attempt_index_digest,basis_begin_index_digest,basis_outcome_directory_digest,basis_conflict_index_digest,basis_authoritative_floor_digest,basis_pending_root_digest,selected_terminal_attempt_keys[],evidence_bundle_ref:StrongRef<ClosedAttemptEvidenceBundle>,expected_prior_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,candidate_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,extension_proof_ref:StrongRef<PersistentMapExtensionProof>,retained_active_attempt_commitment,still_live_independent_obligation_refs[IndependentAttemptObligationRef],terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply verifies every selected attempt is `TerminalReady` and audit-visible and that its candidate leaf exactly reproduces the detailed `TerminalPublicOutcome`; decision/certificate publication, every admitted shard post-visibility acknowledgement, committed Global-delta publication/frontier, and applicable abort/read-close no-delta proof must be complete. Every statement is `Published|Failed|Abandoned`; every statement output is NoResult/NotApplicableTerminal or, together with every terminal/autocommit result, Acknowledged, ReleasedUnacked, or independently retained; every workspace overlay and remote grant has exact release evidence or a listed independent owner; overlap is closed; and no untransferred backup/replay/retention/capability obligation remains. Apply creates unsigned compact `ClosedAttemptCompactionFloorRecord {compaction_id,assigned_global_logical_command_seq,source_command_digest:WeakDigest,through_global_prefix,terminal_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,selected_attempt_commitment,selected_public_outcome_commitment,retained_active_attempt_commitment,still_live_independent_obligation_commitment,meta_checkpoint_identity:WeakDigest}` with no retaining edge to the command/spec/evidence and inserts it into `PendingAttemptCompactionRoot {generation,entries[compaction_id->StrongRef<ClosedAttemptCompactionFloorRecord>],nonretaining_predecessor_digest}`. Build does **not** advance the authoritative floor, rewrite detailed indexes, or release heavy evidence. Generated plane-negative fixtures reject both former `StrongRef<AuditOutcomeRecord>` back-edges.

Only after the compact record and its audit visibility advance are durable does the Meta quorum create `AttemptCompactionAttestation {SameGroupCertificateHeader,compaction_id,floor_record_identity:WeakDigest,build_control_identity:WeakGlobalCommandIdentity,build_resulting_root_identity:WeakDigest,visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,selected_attempt_commitment,selected_public_outcome_commitment,through_global_prefix,retained_active_attempt_commitment,still_live_independent_obligation_commitment,one_digest_signer_lock_ref:StrongRef<CertificateSignerLock>,quorum_signatures}`. It has no strong edge to the compact record, build command/root, prior floor, spec, or heavy evidence; the certificate is the exact portable release proof, not a semantic command identity. The certificate ledger temporarily retains the build closure until publication. `GlobalClosedAttemptFloorPublishSpec` is `{floor_record_ref:StrongRef<ClosedAttemptCompactionFloorRecord>,attestation_ref:StrongRef<AttemptCompactionAttestation>,expected_pending_entry_digest,expected_prior_authoritative_floor:WeakDigest,expected_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,exact_selected_attempt_index_rewrite_commitment,exact_selected_outcome_directory_rewrite_commitment,exact_overlap_closed_conflict_rewrite_commitment,exact_begin_status_result_workspace_remote_grant_and_statement_closure_commitment,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply revalidates monotonic extension, removes exactly that pending entry, replaces selected detailed family/attempt/outcome entries with `CompactedTerminal{capability_replay_ref,summary_root_ref,leaf_key_digest,public_outcome,lookup_floor}`, removes only proved overlap-closed conflict detail, and leaves every independently retained result/workspace grant/backup/replay/capability object rooted by its own typed lease or floor. The installed public outcome must byte-match the authenticated leaf and the pre-compaction detailed response. It installs `GlobalAttemptCompactionFloor {summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,closed_through_global_prefix,retained_active_attempt_commitment,still_live_independent_obligation_commitment,last_update:Genesis|NeverRegistered{applied_prefix,record_identity:WeakDigest}|Closed{attestation_ref:StrongRef<AttemptCompactionAttestation>}}`. This floor has no strong/CRSR path to the previous floor, the build record, spec, or heavy evidence. Fresh Meta Genesis and Local activation both create the canonical empty `TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot`, empty `PendingAttemptCompactionRoot`, and `GlobalAttemptCompactionFloor{closed_through=0,last_update=Genesis}`; therefore the first extension has a real prior root. `GlobalClosedAttemptFloorInstallSpec` is the closed tag `InstallNeverRegistered{spec_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredFloorSpec>}|BuildClosed{spec_ref:StrongRef<ClosedAttemptCompactionSpec>}|PublishClosed{spec_ref:StrongRef<GlobalClosedAttemptFloorPublishSpec>}`. Heavy evidence becomes reclaimable only after `PublishClosed`, its audit visibility advance, and an activated checkpoint cut covering the publish/build command and certificate-ledger transfer, subject to every independent live floor. Neither phase decides, aborts, or times out prepared work. Status tests race build, audit visibility advance, attestation, publish, expiry, and post-cut detail reclamation and require identical validated-capability response bytes, service epoch, and privacy shape before expiry and the exact privacy-collapsed expiry response afterward.

`MetaConfigurationTransitionSpec` is `{phase:ProposeJoint|CommitJoint|CommitNew|CommitRetirementFloor,basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,prospective_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,candidate_closure_proof_ref:StrongRef,expected_global_prefix,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,resulting_topology_body_digest,paired_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>?,paired_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConfigPayloadFloor>,required_certificate_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaCertificateFloor>,required_remote_obligation_floor_ref:StrongRef<RemoteObligationFloor>,prepared_ownership_transfer_refs[StrongRef<MetaPreparedOwnershipTransferRecord>],terminal_audit_gate}`. Deterministic apply constructs a `TopologyState` successor with identical epoch, form, shard assignments, and routing but the phase-appropriate current/joint/new `meta_configuration_ref` plus this applied control; no topology object may retain the retired Meta configuration as current. Every phase is separate, and `CommitRetirementFloor` proves the new set owns all Meta prepared, certificate, and certified-remote obligations. The sole transfer format is the role-specialized `PreparedOwnershipTransferRecord<Meta>` defined above; no later generic or cross-role encoding exists. A current Meta prepared root may carry a prior-configuration entry only in that exact transfer state, and old ownership releases only after new ownership plus Raft/snapshot/apply/GC acknowledgement.

Shard membership is Meta-authorized and later Meta-adopted. `ShardReconfigurationAuthorizationSpec` is `{shard_id,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,old_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_meta_remote_trust_generation,expected_meta_selected_old_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,joint_and_final_canonical_configuration_bytes_and_digests,transition_nonce,payload_predicates,required_checkpoint_floor_remote_prepared_certificate_obligations,successor_evidence_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}`; its applied `ShardReconfigurationAuthorizationRecord` fixes the one permitted transition and current trust selector. Each `ShardConfigurationTransitionSpec` consumes the certified record and transfers every old-configuration owner. After `CommitRetirementFloor`, old and new quorums create `ShardConfigurationAdoptionEvidence {SameGroupCertificateHeader,authorization_identity,old/joint/new configuration identities,final_floor,through_shard_index/global_prefix,remote_obligation_commitment,predecessor_remote_configuration_evidence_identity,old_and_new_quorum_signatures,one_digest_signer_lock_ref}`. The successor `RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence::Successor` is authenticated from the currently trusted predecessor and both quorums; new members alone cannot bootstrap it.

`RemoteGrantRetirementPlan` is the Meta-local pre-order object `{plan_id,basis_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,basis_remote_trust_generation,retired_authority_domain,retired_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,successor_configuration_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,sorted_entries[{old_grant_id,old_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,target_identity,consumer_domain,target_closure_commitment,disposition:ReplaceWithSuccessorGrant{successor_grant_body_recipe,required_consumer_adoption_predicate}|Release{release_request_body_recipe},required_six_stage_transition:RequestConsumerRelease->PublishConsumerReleaseEvidence->ApplyAuthorityRelease->PublishAuthorityReleaseAck->ConsumeReleaseAck->Acknowledged,completion_predicate}],complete_old_grant_set_and_target_coverage_digest,expected_consumer_root_digest,completion_floor_body_recipe}`. It names no future request, tombstone, ack, applied record, or result; adoption verifies the exhaustive old-grant set before selecting it. `ShardConfigurationAdoptionSpec` is Meta input `{authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,adoption_evidence_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardConfigurationAdoptionEvidence>,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_old_shard_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_remote_trust_generation,expected_selected_old_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,successor_configuration_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,expected_successor_evidence_digest,old_grant_retirement_plan_ref:StrongRef<RemoteGrantRetirementPlan>,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply verifies the direct trust transition and atomically CASes both the topology shard entry and `RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot` selector/generation; neither may advance alone. Only then may the six-stage handshake release old-configuration grants and membership. Stale trust generation, anchor, topology, old/new signature domain, or successor bytes reject with no partial adoption.

Distributed GC separates preflight, semantic authorization/quarantine, physical completion, and aggregate completion. A stage-4 certificate is not release completion. `PortableRemoteAuthorityConfigurationProjection` is the reference-free `{authority_domain,configuration_oid,configuration_digest,canonical_configuration_bytes,payload_predicate_digest,trust_transition_proof_bytes,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `PortableRemoteReleaseAckEvidence` is `{authority_domain,consumer_domain,grant_id,target_identity,release_nonce,ack_leaf_bytes_and_identity,authority_configuration_evidence:PortableRemoteAuthorityConfigurationProjection,summary_entry_key,summary_inclusion_proof,permanent_release_proof_floor,authority_signatures}` and contains no CRSR, new retention grant, or cross-group strong edge. `GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef` is the closed role-checked union `AuthorityPublished{publish_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionAckPublishRecord>,summary_entry_ref:StrongRef<RemoteReleaseSummaryEntry>,ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>}|ConsumerAcknowledged{consume_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionConsumeAckRecord>,ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,current_no_old_grant_ref_proof_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionNoOldGrantProof>}|ImportedPermanent{evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableRemoteReleaseAckEvidence>}`. The candidate's ownership/consumer role selects the one legal arm; every arm proves stage 5 or stage 6 plus the permanent summary floor. A request, stage-4 certificate, tombstone, plan, unsigned identity, or a newly granted CRSR cannot inhabit it. A shard first orders `ShardGcPreflightSpec {basis_shard_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_shard_raft_index,basis_global_prefix,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,topology_epoch,complete_typed_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<GcRootInventory>,candidate_derivation_profile,excluded_obligation_commitment}`. Apply creates `ShardGcPreflightRecord {source_spec_ref:StrongRef<ShardGcPreflightSpec>,basis identities,generated current/cut/prepared/certificate/lease/key/derived/backup/replay/restore/remote inventories,exact_candidate_local_reclaim_set,excluded_obligations,candidate_set_digest}`; only afterward does the quorum create `ShardGcPreflightEvidence {SameGroupCertificateHeader,preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardGcPreflightRecord>,candidate_set_digest,root_inventory_digest,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. Meta likewise builds `MetaGcPreflightRecord` for its local physical universe before ordering `GlobalGcAuthorizationSpec {basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_global_prefix,meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,meta_preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<MetaGcPreflightRecord>,exact_meta_candidate_set,sorted_shard_preflight_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardGcPreflightEvidence>],exact_per_shard_candidate_commitments,excluded_global_obligation_commitment,completed_remote_release_proof_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply creates `GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord` authorizing only those bounded sets; a planned remote release is not completion, and an active/ReleaseRequested grant target is never a reclaim candidate.

Each participant next orders a role-specific **Semantic quarantine** command. `GcMemberOperationPlan` is the exact `{generation,operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,storage_member_id,storage_profile_oid,target_inventory_digest,canonical_action_body_recipe_and_digest}`. `GcOperationFamily` is `{family_id,base_target_set_commitment,base_generation_zero_plan_set_commitment,successor_operation_id_recipe,max_generations,body_digest}`. `ShardGcApplySpec` is `{authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord>,authorization_visibility_projection_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardGcPreflightRecord>,expected_current_shard_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_topology_epoch,expected_root_inventory_digest,exact_authorized_local_reclaim_set,completed_remote_release_ack_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],current_reachability_recomputation_ref:StrongRef<GcReachabilityProof>,newly_reachable_disjoint_proof_ref:StrongRef<GcDisjointnessProof>,operation_family:GcOperationFamily,sorted_generation_zero_plans[GcMemberOperationPlan],complete_member_target_plan_and_family_bijection_digest}`. `MetaGcApplyQuarantineSpec` is the exact Meta-local `{authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord>,authorization_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,meta_preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<MetaGcPreflightRecord>,expected_current_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_root_inventory_digest,exact_authorized_meta_reclaim_set,completed_remote_release_ack_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],current_reachability_recomputation_ref:StrongRef<GcReachabilityProof>,newly_reachable_disjoint_proof_ref:StrongRef<GcDisjointnessProof>,operation_family:GcOperationFamily,sorted_generation_zero_plans[GcMemberOperationPlan],complete_member_target_plan_and_family_bijection_digest,terminal_audit_gate}`. Followers recompute from the **current** Semantic state, both RootSlots, Protocol/Prepared/Consensus state, and the candidate result. They require `reclaim_set ⊆ authorized_set ∩ preflight_set`, disjointness from the current reachable set, and exact family/base-plan coverage; “unchanged or stronger” is not a relation. Apply creates the role-specific reclaim-authorization record and `GcSemanticState::Quarantined` only. Every object encoder, dedupe lookup, prepared receipt, command validator, and root publisher rejects a new retaining edge or realization selection to a quarantined identity. All floors retain the family, every generation, and all cancellation/abandonment/status receipts through aggregate terminality.

After each quarantine is visibly certified, that group's Protocol plane uses the common physical machine defined for Local GC. Neither Shard nor Meta quarantine apply creates a Protocol Requested record, and no maintenance transition mutates Semantic quarantine. `PortableGcPhysicalTerminalEvidence` binds role/group, authorization/quarantine/family/all-generation commitments, complete receipt bijection, pre/post physical-root set, configuration/fence/slot ancestry, and terminal kind. A role-specific `GcPhysicalDispositionImportSpec` then imports that evidence into Semantic state. Only after the resulting Semantic disposition is applied, role-validly published, and audit-visible may a signer-locked certificate attempt create one of four noninterchangeable acks: `MetaGcCompletedAck`, `ShardGcCompletedAck`, `MetaGcCancelledAck`, or `ShardGcCancelledAck`. Completed acks bind reclaimed inventory/post-physical roots; cancelled acks bind global cancellation authority, exact participant no-start evidence, unchanged/no-reclaim physical-root proof, and cancelled-disposition visibility. No apply handler emits an ack or certificate directly.

Distributed cancellation is a fenced protocol, never an independent per-group choice. Global coordination is monotone `Executing -> CancellationPreparing -> CancellationAuthorized|CompletionRequired -> CancelledBeforeAnyParticipantStart|Completed`. `GlobalGcCancellationPrepareSpec {authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord>,expected_global_gc_state:Executing,cancellation_nonce,exact_required_participant_commitment,expected_latest_progress_generation,terminal_audit_gate}` creates `GlobalGcCancellationPrepareRecord`; only after that record is applied and audit-visible may the quorum create `GlobalGcCancellationPrepareCertificate`.

Each participant then orders Protocol `GcParticipantCancellationFenceInstallSpec<Role> {authorization_identity,cancellation_prepare_certificate:RoleValidMetaEvidence,expected_quarantine_generation,expected_operation_family,expected_protocol_generation}`. It does one thing atomically: installs `CancellationFenceInstalled`, increments a fence generation, and blocks every new Armed->SentUnknown, send, and successor creation. Status/cancel I/O occurs only afterward under the published fence through the universal dispatch protocol. `GcParticipantCancellationStatusImportSpec` imports authenticated provider status, and `GcParticipantCancelBeforeStartSpec` may request the provider's permanent cancellation tombstone for a NotRegistered or Requested operation. Ambiguous/unavailable status, provider Requested without a terminal cancellation receipt, or unresolved SentUnknown remains blocking. `GcParticipantCancellationEvidenceFinalizeSpec<Role>` then creates exactly one local record: `NoStartFenced{complete base/current-generation target bijection over Armed-AbandonedBeforeSend or provider-CancelledBeforeStart,dispatch-never-sent_and_cancellation_receipt_refs,fence_generation,unchanged_physical_root_commitment}` or `StartedObserved{exact first Started|Completed receipt/status observation,operation,target,member_counter,remaining_family_commitment}`.
