Genesis alone uses no cut body and produces `CheckpointInstalled`; an operational replacement requires the body and paired floor, atomically installs the matching provisional cut, and preserves `Operational`. The single exact `ShardOperationalBootstrapBarrier` schema is the origin-tagged, strongly retaining definition in the activation/genesis contract above; no digest-only alternate encoding exists. `MetaInitialFloorInstallSpec` is `{checkpoint_installed_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>,checkpoint_state_vector_digest,initial_meta_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConfigPayloadFloor>,initial_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,sorted_active_shard_barrier_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardOperationalBootstrapBarrier>],expected_global_logical_command_seq,terminal_audit_gate}` and is the sole fresh `CheckpointInstalled -> Operational` transition. The barrier set equals every and only `Active` topology entry, all at one global prefix; `Joining` shards are unroutable. `GlobalHistoryCutActivationSpec` is `{provisional_cut_ref:StrongRef<ProvisionalRetentionCutSet>,checkpoint_install_record_ref:StrongGlobalCommandRef,expected_retention_map_basis:WeakStateIdentity,verified_contiguous_suffix_start,terminal_audit_gate}` and only strengthens that exact provisional set to `ActivatedRetentionCutSet`.

Meta-owned directories change only through typed CAS controls. `PublishShardCheckpointCertificateSpec` is `{checkpoint_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardCheckpointCertificate>,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_shard_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_prior_directory_value:WeakDigest?,required_remote_grant_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,terminal_audit_gate}`; apply byte-matches shard/config/topology/prefix/history interval and installs the exact CRSR. `PublishShardAppliedAckSpec` similarly binds `{ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardAppliedAck>,prepare_key,decision_record_identity,decision_publish_record_identity,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_shard_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_prior_directory_value:WeakDigest?,required_remote_grant_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,terminal_audit_gate}` and is required for commit and abort acknowledgements.

`GlobalTerminalCompletionSpec` is the sole W12 postcondition transition `{pending_outcome_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord>,semantic_outcome:SemanticTerminalDescriptor::Sharded,terminal_public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<TerminalPublicProjectionBundle<Meta>>,prebuilt_read_your_writes_issuance_ref:None|Some{StrongRef<ReadYourWritesIssuanceBundle<Meta>>},expected_required_postcondition_bitmap,observed_satisfied_postcondition_bitmap,decision_publication_evidence:Committed{decision_publish_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>}|NoDecisionApplicable{terminal_kind:ReadClosed},exact_sorted_post_visibility_shard_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardAppliedAck>],shard_ack_coverage_commitment,delta_completion:Committed{global_delta_batch_ref:StrongRef<GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch>,global_delta_publish_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,published_frontier_proof_ref:StrongRef<GlobalDeltaFrontierProof>}|NoDeltaApplicable{terminal_kind:Aborted|ReadClosed,proof_ref:StrongRef<NoDeltaProof>},configured_durability_evidence_ref:StrongRef<GlobalDurabilityEvidence>,result_disposition:NoTerminalResult|ReadTerminalResult{delivery_disposition_proof_ref:StrongRef<ResultDeliveryDispositionProof>}|AutocommitWriteReturning{preparation_ref:StrongRef<TerminalWriteResultPreparation>,required_posture:Sharded,initial_retention_recipe:ResultInitialRetentionRecipe<Meta>},resource_release_refs[StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition<Meta>>],terminal_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,expected_conflict_overlap_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConflictOverlapCloseProof>,terminal_audit_freeze:AuditFreezeField::Required<MetaControl>,terminal_audit_gate}`. The portable visibility certificate, not a Protocol-plane `AuditOutcomeRecord` edge, proves that the terminal candidate and audit release are public. Every evidence arm and required bit is generated from terminal kind, participants, result class, and durability policy; arrays are canonical bijections. Apply CASes the exact pending predecessor, monotonically adds only verified bits, validates rather than manufactures the frozen public/capability artifacts, constructs the succeeding outcome, and selects `TerminalReady` only when required equals satisfied.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-02 through FG-INV-06, FG-INV-12, FG-INV-15 through FG-INV-20. Consumes Meta/Shard core formats, result-owner registry, audit terminal contracts, authority bindings, answer/replay contracts, resource/escrow, constraints and certified workspace projections. W12 registration/statement/prepare/decision/terminal tasks depend on it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact rows/codecs exist for every begin key/reservation/never-registered, attempt/claim, statement/index/workspace, read admission/release, result owner, outcome/directory/summary, status/capability, terminal completion and visibility type.
- Unit/golden tests freeze initial/retry/conflict/terminal/compacted public bytes, role-exclusive encodings, workspace generations, owner arms, response commitments and construction order.
- Property/model tests prove response only after reservation, no observation before registration/statement claim, one active family generation, statement sequence/idempotency, workspace RYW, no stream before audit release/lease, exact result disposition, and detailed/compacted equivalence.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects Local object substitution, wrong authority/claim/ticket/key/body, stale workspace/frontier, missing participant/effect/witness, future result ref, internal descriptor on wire, incomplete postconditions and status leakage.
- Crash/DPOR E2E covers lost BEGIN/EXECUTE/ACK/release responses, multi-statement RYW across shards, statement failure policy, cancel/read close/write commit, result resume, compaction and status lookup with restart at each publication.
- JSONL emits {event_version,global_txn_id?,registration_generation?,begin_key_digest,attempt_state,statement_seq?,statement_state?,workspace_generation?,delivery_frontier?,owner_arm?,result_state?,outcome_state,completion_bitmap?,public_status_class?,audit_ticket_state?,role_prefix,recovery_action,replay_command}; no internal keyed IDs or hidden reasons on public channels.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: response-before-reservation, Local/Global shared durable unions, parser-interpreted statements, implicit RYW, result streaming at semantic commit, cancel as durable release, and status reconstructed from unrooted process state.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 1696-1784; W12 gate.

title: Implement branch fork: boundary reservation, epoch records, key-envelope DAG, fork bundle
description:
## What & scope
Implement branch creation and forking as one canonical command: `BranchManifest`, `BranchEpochBoundaryReserveSpec`/`BranchEpochBoundaryReservation`, `BranchKeyEpochRecord`, the `KeyEnvelopeNode`/`KeyEnvelopeRoot` DAG with its four AAD domains, `BranchForkBundle`/`BranchForkSpec` build-and-apply, the fork-time double rotation, and the cancel/abandon paths. Grant issuance/revocation surfaces are split to w2-branch-grants; merge to w2-branch-merge; retirement to w2-branch-retire.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1+B6: branches are "git for graphs" — what-if analysis, agent isolation, schema experiments, reproducible feature snapshots. §3.1's Aspen verdict: adopt the spirit of immutable structural sharing (free snapshots) at run granularity. §3.3's 2026 market synthesis flags governance/access control as the field's gap: FrankenGraphDB's fork isolation is cryptographic (key epochs + envelope DAG), not ACL-only, so a fork is a security boundary a hostile reader cannot cross even with stolen storage bytes. frankensqlite's ECS lesson adapted: fork is a canonical ordered command, never an out-of-band KMS effect.

## Design — normative detail
`BranchManifest {graph, branch_id, origin:Genesis{creation_checkpoint_or_genesis_basis:GenesisBranchBasis}|Fork{parent_branch, parent_head:StrongMarkerRef, fork_boundary_logical_command_seq, boundary_reservation_identity}, base_checkpoint_ref?, key_envelope_root_ref:StrongRef<KeyEnvelopeRoot>, current_envelope_epoch, current_write_key_epoch, policy}`. Genesis forbids parent/head/boundary fields; Fork requires all four and verifies parent ancestry/head/epochs at the exact already-assigned boundary. The boundary sequence is `BranchEpochBoundaryReservation.boundary_logical_command_seq`, NEVER the later bundle-install sequence; install provenance lives only in the applied control record/registry projection. Branch creation adds only metadata and key wraps — data-copy complexity O(1); metadata is proportional to the bounded envelope-root fanout, not falsely O(1) for arbitrary recipient lists; durable creation still pays ordered root-publication latency and is never promised below an fsync-independent microsecond constant. Reads select the branch head and follow explicit branch-parent links atop structurally shared objects.

Ordered first: `BranchEpochBoundaryReserveSpec {reservation_id, operation:Fork|SnapshotGrant|StartOrContinueAdvancingGrant|RevokeAdvancingGrant|Rotate, graph, branch, parent_or_target_scope, expected_head:WeakMarkerIdentity, expected_envelope_epoch, expected_write_epoch, transition_nonce, complete_affected_coordinate_set, expected_boundary_index_absence, terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply validates current state and creates immutable `BranchEpochBoundaryReservation {source_spec_ref, reservation_id, operation, graph_branch_scope, frozen_head_and_epoch_commitment, boundary_logical_command_seq, transition_nonce, exclusive_branch_head_and_epoch_hold_root_ref, state:Active}`; every branch mutation/key transition consults the hold root — conflicting work waits or rejects, disjoint commands proceed. `ObjectCreationBoundary` is the exact tag `CommittedExisting{creation_marker_identity, creation_commit_seq}|TransactionReserved{final_certification_reservation_identity, permanent_object_ordinal}|BranchEpochReserved{boundary_reservation_ref, permanent_object_ordinal}`, supplying stable AAD identity before ordering.

`BranchKeyEpochRecord {database_security_namespace_id, cluster_incarnation, graph, branch, kind:Envelope|Write, epoch, key_id, predecessor:Genesis|SameEpochLifecycle{ref:StrongRef<BranchKeyEpochRecord>}|PriorEpoch{identity:WeakEpochIdentity}, transition_nonce, boundary_reservation_ref, state:Active{opened_at_boundary}|Closed{opened_at_boundary, closed_through_boundary, close_reason}}`; both boundary fields carry the reservation identity/sequence. Closing uses the strong same-epoch predecessor; opening a successor uses only the weak prior-epoch identity/rotation-chain digest — the current epoch never retains every old key forever; old envelope roots/nodes/grants/backups are the strong owners that keep an old key decryptable, and when they disappear two-stage destruction can prove zero references.

`KeyEnvelopeNode` carries `children[{range, child_ref, child_ciphertext_ref, wrapped_child_dek, wrap_profile, aad_bytes, aad_digest}]`, `inherited_roots[{source graph/branch/epoch, source_root_ref + ciphertext_ref, maximum_logical_command_seq, maximum_marker?, wrapped_source_envelope_key, wrapped_source_root_dek, wrap_profile, aad}]` (every inherited edge carries a maximum logical-command/marker cut), and `write_epochs[{write_epoch_record_ref, allowed_creation_range, wrapped_write_epoch_key, wrap_profile, aad}]`. `KeyEnvelopeRoot {namespace, incarnation, graph, branch, envelope_epoch, envelope_epoch_record_ref, current_write_epoch_record_ref, root_node_ref, root_node_ciphertext_ref, coverage_cut, profile_oid}`. This is a constructively verified immutable DAG, not an opaque closure. Four exact AAD domains: `"fgdb:key-envelope-child:v1"` (namespace, incarnation, graph, branch, envelope_epoch, parent_node_kind, child_range, child_oid, canonical child_ciphertext_ref, wrap_profile, envelope_key_id); `"fgdb:key-envelope-inherit:v1"` (namespace, incarnation, target_graph, target_branch, target_envelope_epoch, source_graph, source_branch, source_envelope_epoch, source_root_oid, canonical source_root_ciphertext_ref, maximum_logical_command_seq, maximum_marker, wrap_profile, target_envelope_key_id); `"fgdb:key-envelope-write:v1"` (namespace, incarnation, graph, branch, envelope_epoch, write_epoch_record_oid, allowed_creation_range, wrap_profile, envelope_key_id); `"fgdb:branch-object-dek-wrap:v1"` (namespace, incarnation, logical_oid, ciphertext_id, dek_id, graph, branch, write_epoch, canonical object_creation_boundary, wrap_profile, write_key_id). Stored AAD bytes must equal the canonical transcript; a digest alone is not usable AAD.

`BranchForkBundle<Role>` is built bottom-up under a stable prepared owner: epoch records -> ciphertexts/encodings/placements/openers -> typed `StrongCiphertextRef<T>` availability certificates -> envelope nodes/roots -> portable grant bytes -> local grant records/registry successor -> manifests -> bundle; fields include the reservation ref, closed parent envelope+write epoch records (through boundary L-1), frozen path-copied parent root + ciphertext, disjoint parent-successor and child epoch records/roots/manifests at boundary L, grant records/bytes, resulting `KeyGrantRegistry`, bijection proof, complete object-wrap ciphertext-realization inventory, and closure_digest; one payload-availability certificate covers that exact closed inventory, excluding only the future install control/order supplement. `BranchForkSpec<Role> {boundary_reservation_ref, required_reservation_state:Active, bundle_ref, bundle_payload_availability_certificate_ref, expected_parent_head, expected_parent_envelope_epoch, expected_parent_write_epoch, transition_nonce, terminal_audit_gate}`: deterministic apply creates NO key/ciphertext/node/record/grant/manifest — it byte-validates bundle, certificate, reservation, held head/epochs, nonce, closure disjointness, and isolation laws, atomically installs the already-known manifests/registries, consumes the reservation, and releases holds. The double rotation is the isolation boundary: the child receives the now-closed parent envelope key, never a key under which post-fork parent grants or ciphertexts may be created; parent writes admitted after the boundary use only the successor; the child opens frozen history but no successor/sibling epoch; a prepared old-epoch parent write must be revalidated and rewrapped/re-encoded or abort before order. Epoch material is never reused after crash, restore, or merge. `BranchEpochBoundaryCancelSpec` is legal before any bundle/prepared owner/certificate/wrap exists (requires `NoBoundaryClosureProof`); `BranchEpochBoundaryAbandonSpec` after construction requires complete signer/prepared closure, no install order/candidate/external grant publication, and typed cleanup/zeroization evidence. Once a grant or revocation is externally published, recovery must complete the matching install; timeout cannot release the hold.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-13 (invariant, restated): commits are immutable and branch heads move only by atomic expected-head updates; fork closes the parent envelope/write epochs before opening independent parent/child successors; every envelope, object-DEK, grant, and wrap is bound to one authenticated root/cut/epoch. FG-INV-07 (invariant): every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root. FG-INV-16 (invariant): no boundary hold is lost, duplicated, or released while obligated. Fork latency/metadata cost is an Appendix G latency-anatomy + benchmark-class claim, never an invariant.

## Interactions
Boundary reservation and bundle install ride w2-commit-protocol's D1/order path with prepared ownership; manifests/registries publish via w2-txn-lifecycle state roots; identities from w2-object-identity; key lifecycle states and destruction pipeline from w9-key-lifecycle; crypto profiles/entropy from w1-crypto; command rows from g0-command-contracts. w2-branch-grants, w2-branch-merge, w2-branch-retire, and w11-payload-availability all build on the reservation/bundle idiom defined here.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Mandatory suites from the plan: Genesis/no-fake-parent, cross-branch/head substitution, boundary substitution, unrelated-command interleaving, and reproposal tests; fork/handoff/rotation coverage over sibling, post-fork-parent, post-snapshot, post-revocation, expired-grant, stale-prepared-wrap, merge overbreadth, cancel/abandon, restore, every reserve/build/order/apply crash boundary, and collected-key decryption (child cannot decrypt post-fork parent ciphertext and vice versa). AAD mutation tests independently perturb every transcript field per domain. Microbench: O(1) data-copy verified; durable-creation latency reported against the Appendix G anatomy row with fsync attribution logged. E2e script: genesis-create a branch, write, reserve+fork, write divergent data on parent and child, verify cross-branch decryption denial both ways, then exercise the cancel-before-closure and abandon-after-construction paths end-to-end. DETAILED LOGGING (required of implementation and tests): every reserve/build/order/apply/cancel/abandon step logs reservation_id, operation, boundary_logical_command_seq, transition_nonce, hold-root acquisition/release, closed/opened epoch-record identities (kind, epoch, key_id), bundle closure_digest, availability-certificate identity, per-check apply validation verdicts, and cleanup/zeroization evidence identities; the crash-boundary suites assert post-recovery state from these logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: out-of-band KMS fork effects (unauditable, unrecoverable); deriving boundary identity from the install order (future-OID cycle); opaque key closures (unverifiable). Risk: envelope fanout blowup for wide grants — costed as metadata proportional to fanout, never hidden behind an O(1) claim.

## Provenance
§5.6 (451-453, 461), App A branch/envelope rows (~1994-2025), §3.1, §3.3.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement branch key grants: portable bytes, local records, grant bundles, registry
description:
## What & scope
Implement branch sharing/handoff: `KeyEnvelopeGrantBytes` (portable), `KeyEnvelopeGrantRecord<Role>` (local authority/retention owner), `KeyGrantRegistry<Role>`, `BranchGrantBundle<Role>`/`BranchGrantTransitionRef<Role>`/`BranchGrantSpec<Role>`, and the snapshot/advancing/revocation semantics. Split from w2-branch-fork to keep each bead within budget; the reservation/bundle/apply idiom is inherited from there.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: cross-organization branch sharing (agent memory handoff, regulated data rooms) needs a portable cryptographic artifact whose authority is still locally owned, revocable, and time-bounded. The market's governance gap (§3.3) is answered by grants that are keys plus policy, not ACL rows: a snapshot recipient physically cannot open post-grant writes.

## Design — normative detail
`KeyEnvelopeGrantBytes` is the portable signed `{format_version, grant_id, generation, predecessor_grant_digest:WeakDigest?, authority_binding_public_commitment, security_state_binding_public_commitment, tenant_principal_ceiling_purpose_commitment, graph, branch, envelope_root_identity_and_digest, root_ciphertext_identity_and_digest, envelope_epoch, write_epoch?, coverage_cut, mode:SnapshotAtHead|AdvancingBranch, recipient_id, recipient_public_key_id, wrapped_root_object_dek, wrapped_envelope_key, wrap_profile, time_authority_profile_oid, not_before:AuthorityInstant, expires_at:AuthorityInstant, issuer_id, grant_aad_bytes, grant_aad_digest, signer_set_epoch, signature}` with no local `StrongRef`. Its AAD is exactly `canonical("fgdb:key-envelope-recipient:v1", every unsigned field except wrapped_root_object_dek, wrapped_envelope_key, grant_aad_bytes, grant_aad_digest, and signature)` — excluding the ciphertexts avoids a circular encryption input; the outer signature covers the entire portable body including both wrapped ciphertexts and the exact AAD bytes/digest, excluding only the signature. `KeyEnvelopeGrantRecord<Role>` binds those exact bytes to current roots/ciphertexts/policy/time evidence: `{authority_bound_header, grant_id, generation, predecessor_record_ref?, portable_grant_bytes_ref, portable_grant_digest, graph, branch, envelope_root_ref, root_ciphertext_ref, envelope_epoch, write_epoch?, coverage_cut, mode, recipient_id, recipient_public_key_id, time_basis_ref:StrongRef<KeyEnvelopeGrantWindow<Role>>, issuance_time_validation_evidence_ref, state:Current|Revoked{revocation_evidence_ref}|Expired{time_validation_evidence_ref}, body_digest}`. Generation one has no predecessor; renewal is the exact prior+1 direct successor preserving authority/subject/recipient/mode/coverage and wrapped-key identities, advancing only the profiled window and issuance fields, with checked arithmetic. `KeyGrantRegistry<Role>` is the sole CAS-linear owner `{generation, entries[grant_id -> current_record_ref | Terminal{terminal_authority_commitment, grant_identity, terminal_portable_digest, status:Revoked|Expired}], recipient_and_subject_indexes, nonreuse_floor, body_digest}`; exact retry joins one generation; competing renew/revoke/expire transitions race one current leaf.

A snapshot/revocation `BranchGrantBundle` prebuilds the same close/freeze/double-rotation as fork, grants only the frozen root through boundary `L-1`, carries both portable bytes and local record, and provides the successor manifest before ordering; `BranchGrantTransitionRef` is `IssueOrRenew{record_ref, portable_bytes_ref}|Revoke{current_record_ref, revocation_evidence_ref, terminal_registry_body_recipe}`; `BranchGrantSpec` apply only validates/installs the bundle and registry successor. Semantics: a snapshot grant names only a frozen closed root, so a snapshot/revoked recipient never retains a key under which later wraps are legal; an advancing grant intentionally binds the exact current root/epoch and covers new wraps under that named active epoch until rotation — every later epoch needs another ordered grant. Revocation claims only prevention of future access, never erasure of plaintext/keys already received; expiry without ordered revocation/rotation does not claim cryptographic cutoff — the ordered `Expired` successor ends new use and releases retention only after every independent promise floor closes. Handoff wraps metadata/keys, not graph data, and reports metadata and recipient cost. GC/backup/restore/key destruction follow every live LOCAL record/registry edge; portable grant bytes never become a local reachability edge by themselves; a live local record pins its exact named root/ciphertext even if compaction creates another realization; an equal-scalar portable grant under another authority binding is noninterchangeable and cannot be imported without its matching local record.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-13 (invariant): every envelope, object-DEK, grant, and wrap is bound to one authenticated root/cut/epoch. FG-INV-16 window class: `KeyEnvelopeGrantWindow<Role> {authority_bound_header, grant_id, generation, recipient_id, graph, branch, envelope_epoch, coverage_cut, grant_record_digest}` rides the common profiled prefix `{subject_kind, time_authority_profile_oid, not_before, expires_at, subject_body_digest, intended_use_set, owner_plane_and_slot, body_digest}` with `not_before < expires_at`; ambient wall time never substitutes. FG-INV-20 (invariant): authorization precedes every observation; grant lookup failure is uniformly nonrevealing.

## Interactions
Builds on w2-branch-fork's reservation/hold/bundle machinery and envelope DAG; time windows and `TimeValidationEvidence` from w9-time-authority; key states and destruction interlock from w9-key-lifecycle; signatures/wraps from w1-crypto; command/registry rows from g0-command-contracts. w2-branch-retire consumes grant drain; w2-compaction must respect record-pinned ciphertext realizations.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Signature/AAD mutation tests independently perturb every included and excluded field. Renewal-race property: competing renew/revoke/expire race one current leaf; exact retry joins one generation; checked-arithmetic overflow rejected. Security tests: revoked/snapshot recipient cannot open post-boundary wraps (collected-key decryption); portable bytes without a matching local record cannot be imported; equal-scalar grant under a different authority binding rejected. Expiry tests: window lapse alone releases nothing until the ordered `Expired` successor and independent floors close. E2e handoff script issuing, renewing, revoking a grant with logged metadata/recipient cost accounting. DETAILED LOGGING (required of implementation and tests): every issue/renew/revoke/expire transition logs grant_id, generation, mode, registry generation before/after, envelope_root/root-ciphertext identities, recipient_id and recipient_public_key_id, the profiled window {not_before, expires_at} with time_authority_profile_oid, issuance/revocation/expiry evidence identities, and registry-race outcomes (winning and losing leaf digests); import attempts log the authority-binding match verdict uniformly so the nonrevealing-failure property is checkable from the logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: bare KEK or ambiguous branch DEK handoff (invalid per §12.5); grants as ACL rows without keys; portable bytes as retention roots (would let a recipient pin server storage). Risk: clock abuse around expiry — mitigated by profiled `AuthorityInstant` windows plus time-validation evidence, never local wall clocks.

## Provenance
§5.6 (463), App A grant rows (~2019-2025), §12.5 (900-902), App A window rows (~2163-2165).

title: Implement squash branch merge: MergeRecord, token capabilities, ImportedRangeKey ledger
description:
## What & scope
Implement branch merge Chronicle machinery: the squash-merge visibility model, `MergeRecord`, pre-order `MergePrepareSpec` + `MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord`, `BranchMergeLedgerRoot` (token outcomes + imported coverage), `ImportedRangeKey` derivation and overlap semantics, `MergeRejectSpec`, and merge-time key/DEK-wrap behavior. The merge evaluation ladder itself (rungs, CALM classes) is w4-merge-ladder; this bead owns the durable records, idempotency, and visibility contract.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1+B6: agent sessions fork, work, and merge back; merge must be exactly-once under retries, crashes, and head movement, or agents corrupt shared memory. frankensqlite's intent-log/rebase-ladder lesson (§2.3) is adapted, not copied: same-granule conflicts are sometimes semantically reconcilable, but eligibility depends on reads, constraints, authority, and operation algebra — hit rate is measured, never assumed. The squash model was chosen so reads never guess ancestry; the shared difference engine makes merge, `DIFF` (Appendix C), and §9.5 subscription deltas one canonical semantics rather than three approximations (B4 synergy).

## Design — normative detail
Squash-merge visibility: against declared merge bases, the evaluator computes the canonical logical difference contributed by each source and emits ordinary target-branch retractions/insertions at ONE new target `MarkerRef`; source heads are provenance/idempotency inputs, not additional visibility parents; the target head follows exactly one target predecessor, and reads never need to guess whether imported source marker ranges became ancestors. A source-created element keeps its globally unique VId/EId and immutable `OriginBirthOrder`; the target version's `created_by` is the merge marker. Pre-order merge effects store only `BranchAdmissionOrdinal {merge_ordinal, element_id}`; apply combines it with the assigned marker's CommitSeq to derive `BranchAdmissionOrder {commit_seq, merge_ordinal, element_id}`; `InsertionOrder` never silently rewrites an element's origin, and no pre-order/audit/D1 transcript names a future merge sequence.

`MergeRecord {merge_token, merge_request_commitment, target, target_basis:StrongMarkerRef, source_heads[StrongMarkerRef], merge_bases[StrongMarkerRef], imported_range_tokens[{branch, first:WeakMarkerIdentity, last:WeakMarkerIdentity, base:WeakMarkerIdentity, chain_digest}], imported_range_keys[], resolution_policy_oid, resolution_digest, final_effect_digest}` is hash-linked from both capsule and marker; range tokens are weak provenance, never target ancestry or implicit retention. Idempotency has two independent keys. (1) Token: before ordering, the authorized coordinator uses production entropy to mint the unguessable token and construct a complete `MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord` (its body is the sole exact `MergeOutcomeCapability` body; the common header supplies the complete namespace/incarnation/service/tenant/principal/authority/policy/revocation/key/profile/window domain). The graph-effect-free `MergePrepareSpec {client_request_nonce, request_commitment, candidate_merge_token, capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>, expected_merge_index_absence_or_matching_retry, terminal_audit_gate}` durably maps the `{tenant, principal, target, client_request_nonce}` scope to that stable token and exact capability bytes; deterministic apply invents neither. Retrying preparation with the same scoped nonce and request returns the record's original bytes even if the retry proposed a different candidate; conflicting commitment reuse is rejected. Evaluation/charging cannot begin until the capability is acknowledged and resubmitted. `BranchMergeLedgerRoot` maps `outcomes[merge_token -> {original_request, capability_replay_ref, basis:WeakMarkerIdentity, state:InFlight|Committed{target_marker:WeakMarkerIdentity, final_effect_digest}|Rejected{stable_reason_digest}|Compacted{summary_ref}|ExpiredTombstone{token_digest, capability_commitment, expiry_evidence_digest}}]`; detailed and compacted nonexpired states retain the replay record — only evidence-bound expiry drops it. Transaction apply validates token/request/range keys and atomically installs `Committed` plus coverage with the merge marker; a deterministic pre-effect rejection uses the typed `MergeRejectSpec` control command to install `Rejected`. A retry with the capability returns the original outcome even if the target head has advanced; an old-incarnation or old-service-epoch capability never resolves the new state. (2) Coverage: every requested source interval derives `ImportedRangeKey = H("fgdb:imported-range:v1", database_namespace, target_graph_branch, source_branch, source_range_and_chain_digest, merge_semantics_oid, resolution_policy_oid)`, deliberately excluding `target_basis` (which remains an FCW/head-CAS validation input, not an idempotency key). The ledger's `coverage_domains[H(namespace, target, source_branch, source_chain_domain, merge_semantics, resolution_policy) -> normalized_nonoverlapping_ranges[{first, last, chain_digest, imported_range_key}]]` maintains canonical imported coverage per source chain: exact or partial overlap returns `AlreadyImported` or, only under a declared subtract-previously-imported policy, evaluates the canonical uncovered remainder — it never reapplies the overlap. Both maps are non-forgetting idempotency state preserved across checkpoint/history cuts, backup/restore, reconfiguration, and GC; weak terminal identities prevent duplicate application without retaining old marker/capsule bytes forever.

Order independence: only intent families with proved associative, commutative, idempotent joins may claim it; all other eligible operations use the resolution policy's pinned total order; unresolved conflicts produce a capability-redacted conflict graph. "A vague cocycle check is not a substitute for algebraic laws or explicit ordering." Keys: shared encrypted objects keep their existing ciphertext and object DEKs; a squash merge that reuses source ciphertext adds only per-object DEK wraps under the target's CURRENT write epoch — it never grants the target the source branch's envelope/write epoch wholesale unless an independently authorized handoff says so. Escrow: squash merge never imports source rights — it replays unique operation-key deltas against target rights; AuthorityGlobal domains are consumed once at the source transaction and merge recognizes the permanent summary rather than charging it again.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-13 (invariant, restated): merge tokens/nonces/capability generations are pre-minted, each has one terminal outcome, imported-range coverage prevents partial or repeated application across drift/cuts/restore/reconfiguration, and effects obey proved ACI algebra or their recorded total order. FG-INV-17 (invariant): merge executes under capability-stripped deterministic contexts pinned to `IntentSemanticsOid`; drift regenerates everything before final-certification signing. Merge hit rate and difference-engine cost are benchmark-class claims.

## Interactions
Difference engine is shared infrastructure consumed by w5-diff-operator and §9.5 subscriptions (w6-subscriptions); evaluation rungs from w4-merge-ladder; escrow replay semantics with w4-escrow; boundary/epoch context from w2-branch-fork; capsule/marker linkage via w2-commit-protocol; outcome/idempotency plumbing shares w2-txn-lifecycle patterns; token entropy from w1-crypto; command rows from g0-command-contracts. w2-branch-retire compacts this ledger and fences merges naming a retired source.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property: token retry returns byte-identical outcome under head advance, crash, and restore; apply consumes zero entropy (deterministic-apply harness). Fuzzed interval-coverage suite: exact and partial overlap detection, subtract-policy remainder canonicalization, never-reapply oracle. Non-forgetting oracle: ledger survives checkpoint cuts, backup/restore, reconfiguration, and GC storms. Differential: merge result equals the DIFF-engine difference applied at the target basis. Conflict-graph redaction respects capability scope (noninterference test). Crash matrix at prepare/order/apply boundaries including lost-response replay and conflicting-nonce rejection. E2e: two agents fork, diverge, merge with logged token lineage, coverage ranges, and final-effect digests.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: DAG visibility parents (reads would need ancestry guessing; retention couples branches); implicit wholesale key grant on merge; cocycle-style commutativity checks; `target_basis` in the idempotency key (retries after head movement would spuriously re-import). Risk: ledger growth — bounded by `Compacted{summary_ref}`/expiry tombstones while preserving overlap detection.

## Provenance
§5.6 (455-459, 461), App A MergeRecord/ledger row (~2027), §4.7 escrow row (256), §2.3.
design:
## Authoritative post-decomposition contract delta (d96bf0f)

The merge execution/status authorization record below is mandatory in addition to the merge ledger and token machinery already described.

   `MergeOutcomeCapabilityBody` is exactly `{merge_handle:PublicMergeHandle,target:WireGraphReferenceSpec,canonical_request_commitment,capability_lineage_token:PublicStateToken<MergeCapabilityLineage>}`. `MergeOutcomeSubjectBasis<Role>` is `{merge_token,target_internal_binding,target_basis:StrongMarkerRef,source_heads[StrongMarkerRef],merge_bases[StrongMarkerRef],resolution_policy_oid,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,lookup_and_retention_floor,public_body_digest}`. `MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord` owns that basis plus canonical body/bytes/commitment/request/verifier/window/floor fields and repeats the same complete header only where the generated schema row requires a byte-equality cross-check. `MergePrepareSpec` strongly names it; detailed/compacted/tombstone states follow the same retention rules. `MergeCapabilityOperationAuthorizationRecord<Role>` is the same-group immutable `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,authority:Execute{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,expected_ledger_leaf_digest}|StatusLookup{classification:DurableCapabilityStatusClassification,ledger_selection:Usable{expected_ledger_leaf_digest}|NegativeTime},merge_token,target_binding,canonical_request_digest,request_nonce,body_digest}`. Execute selects exactly `MergeExecute` and byte-matches the validation subject/current membership/capability/request/header/target. StatusLookup selects `MergeStatusLookup`; `ledger_selection=Usable` is required exactly with `classification=Usable` and may inspect the exact leaf, while `NegativeTime` is required with any negative-time classifier and forbids any ledger read. `MergeExecuteSpec` strongly carries the Execute record before evaluation or charging; `MergeStatusProjectionAuthorization<Role>` strongly carries the StatusLookup record through the terminal or pending status frame send. Neither a ledger token nor a status handle can replace it. A public marker selector resolves only through its authenticated retained mapping and exact authority; it is never decoded as an internal marker identity.

title: Implement two-phase branch retirement: tombstone, proved drain, key destruction
description:
## What & scope
Implement branch retirement as a first-class two-phase control protocol: `BranchRetireSpec` + permanent `BranchRetireTombstone` (phase one), proved drain and `BranchRetireFinalizeSpec` with retention-cut activation and staged key destruction (phase two), the total disposition set, subscription-cursor termination, escrow burn, resource release, merge-ledger compaction, restore fencing, and the terminal-pin idiom. Never an operator procedure.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: an agent session that ends IS a branch retire — retirement is part of the use case, never an operator afterthought. B1: retirement removes a head, never history reachable elsewhere. The 10k-branch objective is meaningful only with sustained create+retire churn in the loop: it is an empirical gate parameterized by retained deltas, key wraps, subscriptions, lease cost, and per-branch `StatsSegment`/Ripple-maintainer cost (§8.5), not an assumption embedded in correctness. Without proved retirement, "cheap branches" is a leak generator.

## Design — normative detail
**Phase one** is an ordered `BranchRetireSpec` — an ordinary semantic control command with its own terminal audit gate and `command_contracts.toml` row — which validates an authorized retire request against the current branch head, envelope/write-key epochs, and registry generation, and atomically installs a permanent `BranchRetireTombstone` in the branch registry. An unknown branch, stale head, epoch mismatch, or already-installed tombstone fails closed; exact retry of the same authorized request is idempotent against the installed tombstone. From that command's visibility the branch admits no new writes, forks, merges-as-target, grants, subscriptions, statements, or snapshot acquisitions at the retired head, while historical reads through other branches' ancestry are untouched — FG-INV-04's selected-branch-ancestry predicates are unaffected. Outstanding subscription cursors take the registered no-successor terminal arm of §9.5's reset contract: typed `GAP` supersession whose `CursorResetRecord` declares no successor baseline; the acknowledged `GAP` notice (`GAP` emitted only from `ResetNoticeDeliverable`, `GAP_ACK` durably completing it) closes the cursor into terminal `Closed`, framed `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED` — never a silent drop. The same capsule carries the `ResourceLedgerState` branch-count release as its ordered `ResourceChargeEffect` (the §13.6 branch delete/expiry charge event) and the registered `EscrowRightsTransitionSpec::RetireBranchOverlay` arm, which burns the branch's CoordinateLocal `EscrowBranchSeed` overlay rights with an exact before/after conservation proof and is orderable only from this capsule — FG-INV-02 admits no silently dropped rights, so overlay capacity is burned by a registered transition or not at all.

**Phase two** is gated on drain, and drain is proved, never waited out. Only after every covering retention floor, snapshot/delivery lease, backup pin/legal hold, remote-retention consumer grant, current/prospective configuration floor, and in-flight merge naming the branch has passed the retired head or been terminally disposed — established by the same generated checkpoint/floor/backup/restore/GC walkers that gate GC — may `BranchRetireFinalizeSpec` activate the branch's retention cut and enter the branch's envelope root and write-key epochs into §12.5's staged `KeyDestroyProposal`/`KeyDestroyFinalizeSpec` destruction pipeline (RetainedDecryptOnly -> DestroyPending no-new-reference quarantine with one durable idempotent operation per KMS/HSM/storage target -> DestroyedPendingCertificate -> certificate publication -> Destroyed). Destruction is safe by construction: the fork-time double rotation makes post-fork parent/child epochs disjoint, and shared pre-fork ciphertext keeps its object DEKs wrapped under the surviving branches' envelopes, so destroying the retired branch's envelope orphans nothing reachable elsewhere. A merge naming the retired branch as source remains legal only while the frozen history it imports is retained; past the finalize cut it takes the proved cut's `HistoryUnavailable` contract rather than a partial result. Physical reclamation follows §5.3's ordinary exclusive-lease retirement discipline (generation removed from every root, cut activated, both slots converged, exclusive whole-inode lock held through the destructive operation).

**Dispositions are total.** `TemporalConstraintStateRoot` and `ConstraintStateRoot` branch overlays are retired with the cut. The branch-merge ledger is compacted, never forgotten: token outcomes collapse to `Compacted{summary_ref}`/expiry-tombstone summaries and `ImportedRangeKey` coverage keeps its compact authenticated digest map, so overlap detection and idempotent merge retries survive retirement. Per-branch `StatsSegment`s and Ripple maintainer instances are dropped as derived state. The tombstone is permanent: it survives checkpoint/history cuts, backup/restore, reconfiguration, and GC, and fences same-identity revival — a restore of an older root that still contains the retired head reconciles against the tombstone before service promotion, exactly as identity/audit continuity are reconciled. Retirement follows the restore lineage's terminal-pin idiom: every phase is a proved transition with an explicit terminal pin, and no timeout, client death, or operator impatience substitutes for a proof. The retire/finalize command contracts, tombstone and registry rows, and the escrow-transition arm land at G0.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02 (invariant, restated): escrow custody is a disjoint exhaustive partition; finite-side conservation equations hold at every transition; only registered creation/reconfiguration/quota-epoch/branch-overlay-retirement transitions with exact before/after proof may mint or burn rights. FG-INV-04 (invariant): selected-branch-ancestry visibility unaffected by head removal. FG-INV-13 (invariant): branch/key lifecycle binding. FG-INV-14 (invariant): independent obligations remain roots until their exact terminal transfer/release. The 10k-branch create+retire churn objective is a benchmark-class gate (perf-bench-scale), never a correctness assumption.

## Interactions
Requires w2-branch-fork (epochs/envelope roots being destroyed), w2-branch-merge (ledger compaction, source-merge fencing), w2-retention-checkpoints (branch retention cut activation), w2-gc-core (walkers, quarantine, physical reclaim), w9-key-lifecycle (`KeyDestroyProposal`/`KeyDestroyFinalizeSpec`), w4-escrow (`RetireBranchOverlay` arm and conservation proofs). Cursor termination consumes w2-delta-batches' GAP contract and w6-subscriptions' reset machine; restore fencing coordinates with w11-restore; command rows from g0-command-contracts.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Crash matrices: before and after each phase, between cut activation and key destruction, and during physical reclaim; both specs registered with checkpoint/floor/backup/restore/GC/role-transition coverage. Idempotency: exact retry vs installed tombstone; unknown-branch/stale-head/epoch-mismatch fail closed. Visibility: retired head admits none of the seven barred operation classes while other-branch historical reads pass. Cursor: GAP -> GAP_ACK -> SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED lineage logged; silent-drop is a test failure. Drain oracle: finalize rejected while any floor/lease/pin/grant/in-flight merge is outstanding. Restore fencing: an older root containing the retired head must reconcile the tombstone before service promotion. Escrow: exact before/after burn conservation asserted by in-bead ledger tests; the Lean conservation lane (`verif-formal`) re-verifies it formally — lane-green is a gate-g4 requirement, not a close-time check here. E2e: create -> fork -> subscribe -> retire -> finalize -> reclaim with full logged lineage (tombstone, cut, key-destruction operations, receipts).

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: operator-procedure retirement (unauditable, races GC); timeout-based drain (releases obligations without proof); deleting merge-ledger idempotency state (would allow re-import after retire); tombstone garbage collection (revival hazard). Risk: long drains blocking finalize — acceptable by design; the tombstone already stops new load, and drain progress is observable via the walker reports.

## Provenance
§5.6 (465-471), §12.5 (902), §5.3 (417), §9.5 (794), §4.7 escrow rows (250, 256), App D GAP/GAP_ACK rows (~3011-3016, 3106).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement the six-step commit protocol: capsules, D1/D2, prepared ownership
description:
## What & scope
Implement the complete §5.2 commit protocol — the crown jewel of Chronicle. One state machine for single-node and replicated commits (single node = quorum-one specialization): `Draft -> Validated -> FinalPrepared -> PreparedRootDurable -> PayloadAvailable -> Proposed(term,index) -> CommandCommitted -> Applied(logical_command_ref,marker_ref) -> Acknowledged`. The durable unit is never the user's unresolved intent log; it is a post-rebase, post-constraint, post-SSI canonical effect capsule. Delivery boundary (build order — these are dependents, not dependencies): this bead delivers the nine-state machine, admission, capsule construction, D1/D2 publication, prepared ownership, and deterministic apply. Step 2–3's FCW/SSI validation, merge ladder, constraint checking, and durable-quota ledger are consumed through a registered validation-interface trait — this bead ships the trait plus a deterministic pass-through fixture validator; the real validators land in w4-coordinator/w4-ssi-witnesses/w4-merge-ladder/w4-constraints. Apply's delta step is implemented against the `fgdb-delta-types` schemas behind a registered apply-transition hook; full `LogicalDeltaBatch` materialization, `LocalDeltaBatchIndex`, and frontier maintenance are w2-delta-batches' scope, completing behind that hook. Apply's audit-pipeline append is implemented here for the NotRequired/StructurallyInapplicable same-publication visibility arms against a minimal pipeline representation; the bounded pipeline with gap proofs, security barriers, and the Required hide/release path is w9-audit-pipeline's scope behind the same append point. None of these boundaries changes any frozen command/state schema.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: the capsule/marker stream is the One Version Universe's source of truth — retention tiers, branches, time travel, and CDC all derive from it. B5: every commit carries evidence (witnesses, authorization decision, certificates) and deterministic apply; nothing is blessed by timing. B6: durable idempotent outcomes let agents retry blindly. The WriteCoordinator ordering shape is adopted from frankensqlite (§2.3) but the complete D1/D2/Raft path is respecified, benchmarked, and failure-tested — no correctness inherited by analogy.

## Design — normative detail
Admission: no caller submits bare mutation intents. `fgdb-authz-types`'s nonconstructible `AuthorizedMutationPermit` (produced only by the trusted policy verifier) binds namespace/incarnation, tenant/principal/issuer, authority digest and non-widenable operation ceiling, policy-semantics ObjectId, policy/revocation indices, root/snapshot and branch scope, exact read `GraphReferenceBinding[]` and write `CoordinateSchemaBinding[]`, topology epoch, expiry, channel/session binding, unique nonce. Re-evaluable intents bind `IntentSemanticsOid` (content digest of intent-schema version, `language_contract_oid`, semantic/scalar profiles, binder/normalizer version, every influencing procedure/UDF/module artifact); rebase evaluates canonical typed intents under this object, never reparses source; unavailable artifact => fail closed.

**Step 1 Propose.** Writer submits `TxnProposal {snapshot, expected_write_coordinates[], intent_semantics_oid, intents, predicate_witnesses, authorized_mutation_permit, ephemeral_reservation, requested_durable_charge_effects, txn_token}`. Precomputed physical candidates are never publishable truth. **Step 2 Order and validate.** WriteCoordinator deterministically orders a group; verifies permit provenance/scope, live writer lease/fence, schema/topology/policy/revocation epochs, branch write/envelope-key epochs, resource reservation, expected branch heads; then FCW/SSI validation and the merge ladder. Each accepted txn is evaluated against the committed basis plus earlier accepted effects in that group; a rebase produces new reads/writes/constraints/effects/key-epoch bindings — it never blesses an old capsule. **Step 3 Canonicalize final effects.** Verify and preserve every previously ordered escaping allocation; resolve only still-confined temporary IDs/generated keys; evaluate CAS/upsert/no-op; expand cascades; compute explicit logical retractions/insertions with `BirthOrdinal`s only for genuinely new identities; preserve source origin and assign sequence-neutral `BranchAdmissionOrdinal {merge_ordinal,element_id}` for imports; recompute final authorization including hidden-state cascades; validate constraints and the authoritative durable-quota ledger; materialize canonical `ResourceChargeEffect`/release effects; rerun SSI over the final footprint. Rebase may preserve an escaping binding or reject the attempt; it may never remap an identity already returned, referenced by a later statement, or durably exposed. Result: sequence-neutral `CommittedEffectSet` + `LogicalDeltaTemplate` (§9.1), independent of block/run layout; the later canonical `MarkerRef` supplies `CommitSeq`, so apply derives `OriginBirthOrder`, `BranchAdmissionOrder {commit_seq,merge_ordinal,element_id}`, effect order, and ordered delta time without changing the approved capsule digest. **Step 4 Finalize capsules.** Persist one canonical `LogicalDeltaTemplate`, then construct `CommittedEffectCapsule {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>, read_snapshot_basis, validated_apply_basis, intent_semantics_oid, read_graph_reference_bindings, validated_write_coordinate_bindings, validated_write_key_epoch_bindings, coordinate_schema_transitions, topology_epoch, policy_epoch, revocation_index, committed_effects:StrongRef<CommittedEffectSet<Local>>, final_read_witnesses, final_write_summary, constraint_evidence, authorization_decision_ref, authorization_decision_digest, resource_transition_refs[], resource_charge_effects, txn_outcome_preparation_ref, logical_delta_template_ref, logical_delta_template_digest, optional_physical_accelerators, txn_token, final_effect_digest}`. Header, effect set, decision, resource transitions, outcome preparation, reservation, and command must byte-match one complete Local binding; repeated digests are integrity cross-checks, never replacements for typed strong edges; template digest must match referenced bytes and template must match final effect set; write-key bindings fix the branch envelope/write epoch wrapping every new ciphertext DEK; unresolved/conditional commands forbidden; physical patches carry an apply-basis digest and may be ignored; capsule builders return bytes+digest which the coordinator verifies against its approved final effects.

**Step 5 — D1 payload durability + stable prepared ownership.** Seal and make directory-durable the capsule and its entire mandatory strong closure: coordinate effect payloads, `LogicalDeltaTemplate`, schema/constraint/resource transitions, authorization decision, merge record, outcome-preparation record, active final-certification reservation when terminal, referenced accelerator bytes, and every new semantics/module/profile object. HLC observation and expected order are excluded — they live only in the repeatable order-attempt supplement. `PreparedOwnershipId = H("fgdb:prepared-owner:v1", storage_member, replica_namespace_or_incarnation, prepare_id, configuration_state_oid, payload_predicate_digest, base_closure_inventory_digest)` (a scalar config epoch is insufficient). Each replica/donor issuing a receipt creates an immutable `PreparedCommitRecord {prepared_ownership_id, prepare_id, record_generation, predecessor_ref, database/incarnation/configuration-ref/predicate/fence tuple, txn_token, capsule_ref, command_ref?, base_closure_inventory_digest, current_closure_inventory_digest, strong_logical_refs[], exact_realizations[{object_or_subobject_id,encoding_id,placement_id,key_opener_ref}], status, receipt_nonce}`; successors repeat the stable ownership ID and identical base closure, with current closure identical or a strict authenticated superset. Pre-existing objects are revalidated and promoted into the prepared closure; a digest or locator without reachable authenticated bytes is insufficient. `PreparedPayloadRoot` maps ownership ID to latest record; no in-place mutation. Order: insert record -> authenticated nonretaining locators -> persist `RootManifest` -> durably publish `RootSlot` **before** D1 completes or any payload receipt is emitted. `PayloadAvailabilityCertificate` covers this exact pre-command semantic base closure under the exact configuration ObjectId/predicate (including the quorum-one local predicate); each receipt binds config OID, predicate digest, ownership ID, base-closure digest; an observed record OID/root generation is diagnostic freshness, never the sole ownership identity. Bytes not admitted to a prepared root are staging data, unreachable after crash.

**Step 6 — authorize, command, order, publish D2.** Per proposal/reproposal the coordinator builds a fresh D1-certified `LocalOrderAttemptInput` over the stable semantic owner, Active final-certification reservation, expected next order, and `LocalHlcProposalEvidence` (machinery in w2-hlc-order-attempt). Voters verify supplement/certificate, reservation, prepared ownership/configuration, writer fence, selected terminal, HLC observation age/source policy — and do NOT revalidate mutable heads/key/policy/revocation/conflict/resource bases outside the reservation (validated and held before signing; later changes cannot reinterpret). The immutable `CommitCommand` is `{command_version, authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>, database_security_namespace_id, cluster_incarnation, txn_token, final_certification_reservation_ref, required_reservation_state:Active, order_attempt_input_ref, order_attempt_availability_certificate_ref, capsule_ref, logical_delta_template_ref, authorization_decision_ref, resource_transition_refs[], txn_outcome_preparation_ref, payload_availability_certificate_ref, expected_branch_heads, expected_branch_key_epochs, topology_epoch, policy_epoch, revocation_index, final_effect_digest}`; the expected-basis fields are redundant integrity projections that must byte-match the reservation, never fresh CAS gates. The semantic availability certificate covers the stable base; the order-attempt certificate separately covers only the repeatable order/HLC supplement. The coordinator publishes a prepared-record successor adding/strongly owning the completed command and marks the supplement Ordered in the same accepted transition. After log acceptance, the Raft closure and certificate donors retain the command/base/supplement closures through apply and compaction. Abandonment: only an unreceipted provably-unordered attempt under a current fence, or a receipted attempt after consensus proves it cannot be ordered and every certificate/configuration retention floor expired; once any terminal audit lock exists, neither semantic prepared ownership nor final certification may be abandoned — only a provably unordered stale supplement may be retired/replaced; timeout/process death is never proof.

Apply (deterministic): verify command/closure/evidence, assign next `LogicalCommandSeq`, advance HLC (rules in w2-hlc-order-attempt), assign `CommitSeq`, build marker/results/payload/record/root, transfer ownership before prepared terminalization. In the same state transition, materialize the self-contained `LogicalDeltaBatch<LocalCommitted>`, verify against capsule/template/marker, insert `(next_commit_seq -> batch_ref)` into `LocalDeltaBatchIndex`, advance `local_delta_frontier` — no separate delta-publish command, no unrooted interval; rematerialization must reproduce identical bytes; missing/duplicate/gapped/wrong-marker/wrong-frontier insertion fails apply. Every semantic apply appends its candidate to `LocalAuditVisibilityPipeline` (RootManifest owns applied root, protocol root, pipeline); NotRequired/StructurallyInapplicable candidates become visible in the same composite publication only if no earlier gap exists; Required candidates stay hidden until external batch receipt plus quorum-durable maintenance advance. Client receives semantic completion only after configured durability, durable outcome, protected-audit release, and final `RootSlot` publication; later revocation fences subsequent work without rewriting a committed result. Other semantic families use typed `ControlCommand` (advances LogicalCommandSeq/HLC, not CommitSeq); its `typed_payload_ref` always names a registered sequence-neutral pre-order spec, never an applied result; `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` and activation/ACK/release/expiry/resume are maintenance-only.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-01: each scoped key/token/attempt maps to at most one immutable semantic terminal outcome and final-effect digest; commit has exactly one marker; Abort/NeverRegistered/ReadClosed can never later Commit. FG-INV-07: acyclic durable graph; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; before receipt/order, D1 owns one exact closure under stable prepared ownership; timeout releases no owner. FG-INV-08: contiguous command order and marker subsequence; only `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` moves the visible endpoint. FG-INV-17: drift regenerates everything before final-certification reservation; once Active reservation freezes the basis, rebase is forbidden. Claim types: the two-barrier anatomy is an Appendix G registry row (exact structural counts); commit latency budgets are `slo.toml` rows keyed {operation_class,posture,audit_class}.

## Interactions
Consumes w2-order-raft (ordering), w2-hlc-order-attempt (supplements/HLC), w2-root-bootstrap (RootSlot/Manifest publication), w2-writer-takeover (lease/fence), w2-object-identity (identity pipeline), w1-authz-policy (permit verifier), w2-id-allocator (escaping allocations, via w2a). Produces the capsule/marker/delta stream for w2c (w2-delta-batches, w2-retention-checkpoints), w4-coordinator/w4-ssi-witnesses (validation plugs into steps 2–3), w6-delta-consumption, w9-audit-pipeline, w10-capabilities. w2-group-commit owns barrier amortization; w2-recovery owns crash reconciliation; w2-fused-autocommit registers the fused arm over this machinery.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit/property: capsule byte-match laws (header/effects/decision/preparation/reservation/command one binding); template-digest pairing law (neither field without the other); PreparedOwnershipId recomputation; successor base-closure equality and superset checks. Crash matrix: kill at every step boundary and inside D1 closure publication; assert staging bytes unreachable, receipted-unordered handling per abandonment arms, no receipt before RootSlot. DPOR: reproposal vs apply races; supplement Ordered-marking atomicity. Oracle: in-bead assertions cover delta-batch rematerialization byte-equality and audit-pipeline gap-freeness — these run through the registered apply hook and Required-audit arms once w2-delta-batches and w9-audit-pipeline land, and at this bead the hook contract, the fixture-validator pass-through, and the NotRequired visibility path are asserted directly; the FG-INV-01 CAS models (lost response, concurrent retry/cancel) and Elle-style history checks over committed markers are the independent `verif-oracles` checkers — verif-oracles depends on this bead, so those verdicts execute there and are validated at gate-g1. E2E: scripted commit under the audit-NotRequired profile with full structured logging of every barrier (plane, files synced, amortization class) compared against the Appendix G row; client completion withheld until all four conditions logged (protected-audit release structurally satisfied under NotRequired at this bead; the Required-profile variant re-runs once w9-audit-pipeline lands). Bench: quorum-one commit p50/p99 gated per §17 with pinned fsync p50 derivability check. DETAILED LOGGING: implementation and tests log every state-machine transition (Draft -> Validated -> FinalPrepared -> PreparedRootDurable -> PayloadAvailable -> Proposed -> CommandCommitted -> Applied -> Acknowledged) with {scoped txn_token digest, prepare_id, PreparedOwnershipId, capsule/final-effect digest, reservation state, command OID, assigned LogicalCommandSeq/CommitSeq}; every rejection or abandonment decision logs its typed reason and evidence identities; the e2e script asserts these fields against the log.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: coordinator hot path minting ~15–20 durable objects per write — priced in Appendix G, amortized by w2-group-commit; any weight increase requires a same-change registry update. Rejected: durable unresolved intent logs as the commit unit (reparse under new corrigendum breaks determinism); rejected: scalar configuration epoch as prepared identity (same-epoch candidates/joint states differ); rejected: revalidating mutable heads at vote time (reintroduces TOCTOU the reservation already closed); rejected: separate delta-publish command (unrooted interval between commit and delta).

## Provenance
Plan §5.2 l.380–408, §14.W1 item 1 l.1068, App A l.1518–1534, App F FG-INV-01/07/08/17, App G.

title: Build the Chronicle compactor: verify-equivalence pipeline and root-slot convergence
description:
## What & scope
Implement §5.5's compaction actor for Chronicle segments: the `BUILD -> VERIFY_EQUIVALENCE -> D1_NEW_OBJECTS -> ROOT_PUBLISH -> SLOT_CONVERGE -> WAIT_SAFE_POINT -> RETIRE` pipeline, the complete mark-root inventory, the serialized `CompactionRootPublish` permit, the `RootSlotConvergenceGuard`/`SlotConvergence` permit protocol with `RootSlotConvergenceEvidence`, marker-batch and `PackedObjectGroup` rewrite ownership, and staging-namespace durability. Retention-cut semantics live in w2-retention-checkpoints; GC decision/quarantine in w2-gc-core.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's immutable content-addressed store only works economically if dead bytes are rewritten out without ever mutating published objects in place. frankensqlite's ECS native mode (§2.3) supplies the mark-and-compact-with-leases starting point, but Chronicle re-specifies root protocol, digest identity, and equivalence proof — graph durability does not inherit correctness by analogy. B5: compaction emits reconstructible evidence (equivalence digests, convergence evidence), not trust-me rewrites.

## Design — normative detail
The pipeline marks from BOTH valid root slots and explicitly traverses: logical-command/generated-complete installed-checkpoint cuts, stable prepared-payload and consensus-log ownership, every branch/base, branch key-epoch/envelope/grant roots and the branch-merge ledger, transaction/DP outcomes, all external continuity links, resume-cursor/delivery/replay registries and archives, delivered-output payloads, audit ticket/event/resolution/CAS-receipt/gap/audit roots, snapshot and delivery leases, backup/legal holds, key/key-wrap, and current/prospective configuration/floors. It resolves marked logical/subobject identities through nonretaining physical locators, builds new immutable encodings, **proves old/new canonical logical digests equal**, and publishes the new `RootManifest` through a serialized `CompactionRootPublish` permit.

Slot convergence: after rereading and fully validating the highest slot/closure, a linear `RootSlotConvergenceGuard` requests a `SlotConvergence` permit whose acquisition rechecks that the CURRENT winner is still the exact target manifest, writer/continuity/service tuple, and bootstrap. Only while holding the permit may it publish the other slot at checked `winner_generation+1` with byte-identical target fields. Any intervening ordinary, audit, checkpoint, restore, role-transition, retirement, or other convergence publication changes the winner and makes acquisition or the immediate pre-write recheck fail stale; convergence restarts from the new winner and can never overwrite it with an older manifest at a higher generation. Success syncs and rereads both slots and produces reconstructible `RootSlotConvergenceEvidence {manifest_identity, first_slot_generation, second_slot_generation, identical_bootstrap_digest, two_slot_reread_digest, durability_profile, first_and_second_root_publication_evidence}`. Convergence is physical-only: it advances no logical/Raft/commit/HLC sequence and cannot select a different manifest. Recovery at every crash chooses the highest credible slot; retry converges the remaining slot.

Old encodings retire only after (a) both valid slots converge away from the old closure, (b) convergence evidence is reproducible, and (c) no independent lease can expose them. Active marker batches are never rewritten in place. Compaction owns the rewrite of partially dead `PackedObjectGroup`s: reclamation coarsens to the pack (a pack is reclaimable only when every member is), member ObjectIds are stable across rewrite, and the object-location index locators are republished — the same trade marker batches already accept. Staging namespace creation, sealing, rename, convergence, and retirement include the required directory durability operations; staging files are unreachable state cleaned only by a recovery procedure that proves it.

Safe point: computed under a consensus-fenced membership epoch (§14); loss of quorum, uncertain membership, an unacknowledged root, or a missing key wrap stops reclamation. Replica positions and CRDT gossip are observations, never GC authority. The actor is supervised and rate-limited against foreground latency; space amplification, checkpoint cadence, and controller settings are empirical/configuration gates with named workloads and model assumptions, not safety invariants.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (invariant): every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec/format rewrite preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. FG-INV-10 (invariant): the two-slot `manifest.root` protocol always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure; every irreversible slot write rechecks both authorities. FG-INV-14 (invariant excerpt): GC/compaction follows every generated strong and currently uncut conditional edge; only registered weak/locator/observation fields are nonretaining. FG-CFG-02 (configuration-model class): controller stability with predicted margin and soak results. §6.6 write-amplification component breakdown and §17 byte-economy metrics (benchmark class) price the pack-rewrite trade.

## Interactions
Traverses cuts and floors from w2-retention-checkpoints; publishes via w2-root-bootstrap's publication sequencer; rewrites packs per w2-object-packing's homogeneity/locator laws; respects snapshot generation leases from w2-snapshots-leases (a held shared lease pins the old closure); never touches prepared/consensus ownership from w2-commit-protocol. w2-gc-core consumes the safe-point discipline; w2-branch-retire relies on compaction for merge-ledger summary rewrite. Format rows from g0-format-arms.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Crash/DPOR tests cut before/after each convergence write, sync, reread, cancellation, and generation allocation while racing ordinary, prepared/Raft-only, audit-candidate-visibility, checkpoint, restore, role-transition, retirement, and another convergence publication; equal-generation ambiguity and checked generation exhaustion are covered. Equivalence oracle: old/new canonical logical digest equality proof is mandatory before publish; a mutated rewrite must be rejected. Property: convergence never regresses the winner; recovery always picks the highest credible slot. Pack tests: partially dead pack rewritten with stable member OIDs and republished locators; mixed-domain pack build fails closed. E2e: sustained-load compaction with logs of permit acquisitions, winner generations, evidence digests, and reclaimed-byte accounting; foreground p99 regression gate per §17.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: in-place rewrite of published objects (immutability is the foundation of content addressing); convergence without a permit/recheck (older-manifest-at-higher-generation hazard); gossip-derived safe points (unfenced membership loses data). Risk: convergence livelock under high publication churn — bounded by restart-from-winner semantics; risk: compaction debt under churn — FG-EVID-03 endurance gate with compaction-debt ceiling stated in §6.6 terms.

## Provenance
§5.5 (441-448), §5.3 (417), §5.1 PackedObjectGroup row (342), §2.3.

title: Implement incarnation+allocation continuity: DirectoryBound/ExternalCas/TPM-NV arms
description:
## What & scope
Implement the paired continuity profiles: `IncarnationContinuityProfile` (`DirectoryBound | ExternalCas`, carried in every `RootSlot` as `incarnation_continuity_profile_id` + `cluster_incarnation_continuity_digest` + `continuity_cas_version`) and the 1:1-bound `AllocationContinuityProfile` (closed union `ExternalCas | DirectoryBound`, plus the registered TPM-NV-class variant of the `DirectoryBound` arm), including `IdentityContinuityRecord`, the fenced local allocation-continuity journal, the exact threat-model scoping, and the FG-INV-11 residual-risk registry row.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 makes history authoritative, so the deadliest attack is rollback: restoring an old copy and re-issuing identities or epochs already spent. The embedded posture (B6 agents on laptops) cannot require a network authority for every epoch advance, while W12/Meta/Sharded postures must have externally anchored anti-rollback. The profile pair makes this trade explicit, registered, and priced (§16 per-posture external-authority footprint table) — and the residual risk of the local arm is a first-class registry row, not fine print (B5 honesty discipline).

## Design — normative detail
**IncarnationContinuityProfile**: `DirectoryBound` — ordinary embedded/local writes rely on the exact whole-inode lease; same-identity restore to another directory is forbidden (clone only); payload headers use no external record ref and a fixed local continuity digest. `ExternalCas` — the Appendix A `ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord` and a live member-bound `ClusterIncarnationLease` are mandatory; takeover fetches the exact current continuity head, byte-matches namespace/incarnation/CAS/visibility, and acquires `OrdinaryWrite` or `RecoveryOnly` scope; a stale/later/unavailable head makes the database read-only. W12 requires ExternalCas. RootManifest and RootSlot repeat and cross-check the same continuity/profile/digest/version/visibility tuple; the generated payload common header carries `{incarnation_continuity_profile_id, cluster_incarnation_continuity_record_ref?, cluster_incarnation_continuity_digest, continuity_cas_version, service_visibility_epoch}` — `DirectoryBound` = None-ref + fixed digest; `ExternalCas` = Some + exact byte equality with the live authority.

**AllocationContinuityProfile** is a closed union `ExternalCas | DirectoryBound` bound 1:1 to the slot's IncarnationContinuityProfile. Under `ExternalCas`, before an epoch may issue an ID, a threshold-signed/witnessed `IdentityContinuityRecord { database_security_namespace_id, allocation_epoch, predecessor_digest, external_registry_id, cas_version, status, issued_at, signer_set_epoch, threshold_signatures }` is durably CAS-published outside the rollbackable database closure (operator HSM/KMS registry or configured witnesses) and copied into Chronicle; the external copy is the anti-rollback authority, the Chronicle copy is checked against it. Under `DirectoryBound` there is no external record: the epoch fence is a local allocation-continuity journal record ordered under the same whole-inode fence and fixed-local-continuity-digest pattern the cluster-incarnation record registers for that profile; every epoch advance is an ordered, fenced local publication — an embedded DirectoryBound database mints its first and every subsequent epoch with no external service. W12, Meta, and Sharded postures require ExternalCas.

**Threat-model scoping (exact and registered)**: the DirectoryBound arm fences *copy-based restore* — a copied directory fails inode-identity takeover — and is never an anti-rollback authority; block-level or volume-snapshot rollback preserves device and inode identity and is **outside** DirectoryBound's declared threat model for the entire database closure, allocation included. The carve-out is cheap by construction: the external fence detects only cross-epoch rollback and enforces restore floors — the record binds epoch and predecessor digest, never high-water marks — so DirectoryBound forfeits protection only on a same-identity-restore path that posture already forbids outright. **TPM-NV variant**: a registered DirectoryBound variant may bind epoch advances to a local hardware monotonic counter (TPM-NV-class) as the allocation-epoch fence, restoring cross-epoch rollback detection for embedded deployments without a network authority. **Restore law**: a same-identity restore must acquire an epoch strictly above the external continuity floor before writes; if that authority/floor cannot be proved, the database opens read-only or requires `CloneNewIdentity`. `AllocationEpochReservation` under DirectoryBound (mode `CloneNewIdentity` only) takes `external_retired_floor`/`external_allocator_floor_digest` from the source's fenced local allocation-continuity journal, authenticated from the source manifest closure, with the same strictly-beyond checked arithmetic; under ExternalCas they remain the external authority's floors.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-11 (verbatim): allocation epochs, leases, and canonical spent commitments are monotonic under the registered `AllocationContinuityProfile` bound 1:1 to the incarnation-continuity posture — externally monotonic under `ExternalCas` (mandatory for W12/Meta), locally monotonic under `DirectoryBound`'s allocation-continuity journal beneath the same whole-inode fence — and prevent VId/EId/generated-key alias, overlap, or reuse across crash, label change, branch, merge, clone, restore, topology movement, and role activation; the registered residual-risk row applies to the whole closure: under `DirectoryBound`, block-level volume rollback is outside the declared threat model, allocation included. The residual-risk row lives in Appendix F with the same conditional-clause structure FG-INV-10 uses for filesystem profiles. Footprint-table entries are cost/SLO-class artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `g0-format-arms` (frozen AllocationContinuityProfile decision incl. TPM variant), `g0-threat-model` (copy-restore vs block-rollback scoping), `g0-claim-registries` (residual-risk clause registration), `w2-root-bootstrap` (slot fields). Produces continuity validation for `w2-writer-takeover` (step 4), the epoch fence for `w2-id-allocator`, restore floors for `w11-restore` and the restore bridges, and the ExternalCas discipline reused by `w9-audit-continuity`/`w9-time-authority`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
ExternalCas model: CAS races, stale head, skipped version, fork detection, threshold-signature validation, Chronicle-copy/external-head byte-equality. DirectoryBound: copied-directory takeover fails inode-identity validation; journal ordering under the whole-inode fence; epoch advance with zero external calls (no network dependency). TPM-NV: simulated NV-counter regression detected. Restore drills: same-identity restore without a provable floor opens read-only or demands CloneNewIdentity; floor-arithmetic overflow fail-closes; DirectoryBound clone takes floors from source journal digests.
