This is the plan's answer to the classic audit dilemma (block everything vs audit nothing): partial-prefix progress with honest backpressure. The security barrier extends it: an applied-but-hidden policy change must neither grant authority early nor leak its existence through a distinguishable denial.

## Design — normative detail
Visibility uses a bounded ordered pipeline, never a role-global stop-the-world fence. `AuditVisibilityPipelineEntry<Role>` is `{pipeline_order,role_order,raft_index,predecessor_candidate_identity:WeakStateIdentity,candidate_state_root_ref:StrongRef<RoleStateRoot>,proposal_configuration_ref,post_apply_configuration_ref,origin_local_writer_fence_epoch,release:RequiredPending{ticket_ref,event_ref,terminal_resolution_ref,gate_commitment}|NotRequiredReady{nonrequired_evidence}|AuditSystemReady{system_authority_evidence},candidate_publication_commitment,retained_closure_bytes,body_digest}`. `AuditVisibilityPipeline<Role>` is `{role_and_group,generation,visible_pipeline_order,visible_role_order,visible_raft_index,visible_state_root_ref,applied_tail_pipeline_order,applied_tail_role_order,applied_tail_raft_index,applied_tail_state_root_ref,ordered_entries[every pipeline order in (visible,applied_tail]],total_retained_bytes,entry_limit,byte_limit,external_continuity_head_ref:StrongRef<AuditContinuityRecord>,body_digest}`. `LocalAuditVisibilityPipeline` fixes Role=Local/`LogicalStateRoot`; Meta fixes `GlobalStateRoot`; Shard is uninhabited (it uses `ShardStatePublicationCertificate`, w9-audit-release). The pipeline is separately addressed and owned by RootManifest/Raft state — not by either state root — so construction is acyclic. Every Local/Meta *semantic* logical command — Required, NotRequired, or audit-system scaffolding — applies to the pipeline's current applied semantic tail, constructs its complete command result/payload/record/candidate root *first*, then constructs one pipeline successor. A NotRequired/AuditSystem-ready candidate may be released in that same composite publication only when no earlier gap exists; otherwise the successor appends exactly one entry while its effects remain unpublished. Entry `i` byte-matches candidate `i-1` as its semantic predecessor. `pipeline_order` and role logical-command order are strictly contiguous; entry Raft indexes are strictly increasing but not contiguous (registered maintenance may intervene); each entry carries `raft_gap_proof_ref:StrongRef<RaftGapClassificationProof>` covering every index since the previous semantic entry as exact role-valid zero-semantic/pipeline-effect maintenance; missing, duplicate, unclassified, or semantic skipped entries fail apply/recovery — recovery keeps one linear semantic candidate chain without lying about the consensus log. NotRequired/AuditSystem-ready entries cannot leapfrog an earlier Required entry. The visible root stays at the last released entry; ordinary mutation/recovery may continue from applied semantic state only under the security-prerequisite rule, while reads use visible state. At pipeline limits (entry/byte), user semantic work receives deterministic backpressure while audit/recovery/ownership-preserving maintenance uses reserved capacity. Prepared ownership, snapshots/checkpoints, reconfiguration, GC, backup, restore, and takeover retain and transfer both the queue and every gap proof. No candidate result/error/changefeed/system-graph/metric/ack is observable before release.

Security barrier (deliberate v1 conservatism): `command_type_classification.toml` marks every policy, revocation, verifier/evaluator, grant, service-epoch, descriptor-visibility, time-authority, and other authorization-semantic mutation `security_barrier=true`. The pipeline records `earliest_unreleased_security_barrier_order?` with exact predecessor/successor binding commitments. Once such a candidate is applied but not visible, no later user/protected admission, graph observation, authorization decision, capability issuance/refresh, query execution, or data-dependent response may be ordered from the applied tail; only audit advancement, recovery, already-admitted terminalization under its pinned non-widenable authority, and ownership-preserving maintenance proceed, and every output still reauthorizes against visible current state. The public response to a newly attempted operation is the same bounded, data-independent audit-backpressure class used at pipeline saturation — never a policy-specific denial or existence signal. Hence a hidden widening never grants authority and a hidden narrowing never produces a distinguishable early denial. A selective meet/intersection optimization requires a separately proved noninterference feature and is off in v1.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04 (restated): Local/Meta applied state may advance ahead of public state only through the rooted gap-free audit visibility pipeline, and every read/result/side channel begins at its visible endpoint; `SnapshotQuery` admission reads only the visible candidate root. FG-INV-08 (restated): pipeline orders, role orders, and Raft indexes are contiguous/strictly-increasing as specified; only `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` moves the visible endpoint. FG-INV-14/16: pipeline entries are retained obligations. Pipeline entry/byte limits are registered configuration; saturation behavior is priced in FG-CFG-04 and the governance bench profile.

## Interactions
w9-audit-protected-orders supplies candidate construction; w9-audit-continuity supplies the external head the pipeline imports; w9-audit-release owns the advance/release; w2-order-raft supplies `RaftGapClassificationProof` and maintenance-entry classification; w2-root-bootstrap owns the pipeline via RootManifest; w10-snapshotquery and all read paths bind the visible endpoint; w9-threat-tokens' policy/revocation transitions trigger the barrier.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Model checking: pipeline-prefix contiguity, no-leapfrog, and entry-i/candidate-(i-1) byte matching under concurrent appends/releases/crashes. Negative: unclassified intervening Raft index fails recovery; NotRequired release past an unresolved Required entry fails; observable side effect (metric/changefeed/ack) from an unreleased candidate is a test failure. Barrier suite: apply a hidden policy widening — later admissions must get uniform backpressure (byte-compared against saturation responses); hidden narrowing must not change any response distribution (differential fixture). Backpressure: saturate limits, assert reserved-capacity classes still progress and user work gets the deterministic typed class. E2E with logs: run a stalled-authority scenario to limits, resume, and verify a byte-identical visible chain. Detailed logging: every append/release/backpressure/barrier event logs {pipeline_order, role_order, raft_index, entry release class (RequiredPending/NotRequiredReady/AuditSystemReady), gap-proof coverage range, visible vs applied-tail positions, entry/byte totals against limits, typed backpressure class, earliest_unreleased_security_barrier_order set/clear}; the barrier suite logs and byte-compares the uniform response class against saturation responses, and the stalled-authority e2e reconstructs the byte-identical visible chain from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: stop-the-world visibility fence; per-tenant visibility partitions (registered rejection — see w9-authority-surface); selective security-barrier meet in v1. Risk: head-of-line blocking behind one slow Required entry — inherent and disclosed; bounded by limits + reserved capacity.

## Provenance
§12.8 (954–958), FG-INV-04/08.

### Fidelity addendum — security-barrier fields are durable
`AuditVisibilityPipeline<Role>` additionally stores `earliest_unreleased_security_barrier_order?` and the exact predecessor/successor security-binding commitments for that entry. `command_type_classification.toml` marks policy, revocation, verifier/evaluator, grant, service-epoch, descriptor-visibility, time-authority, and every other authorization-semantic mutation with `security_barrier=true`. Once the earliest such candidate is applied-hidden, later user/protected admission, graph observation, authorization, capability issuance/refresh, query execution, and data-dependent response are structurally blocked; only audit advance, recovery, pinned-authority terminalization, and ownership-preserving maintenance remain legal.

Model tests insert each registered security-barrier command behind every earlier-gap shape and prove no later ready entry leapfrogs or leaks policy-specific status. Mutation tests remove/change the barrier order or either binding commitment and require recovery failure. E2E holds external audit resolution unavailable during a narrowing and a widening and verifies the identical bounded audit-backpressure response shape. Logs emit barrier order, predecessor/successor binding commitments, blocked operation class, allowed maintenance class, pipeline byte/entry occupancy, and stable backpressure reason; policy identity and protected data are not disclosed.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Specify the four protected construction orders and sequence-neutral audit signing
description:
## What & scope
Implement §12.8's protected-construction contract: the four explicit noninterchangeable orders, sequence-neutral event/resolution bodies and their commitments, the signing-plan/lock/share machinery, `TerminalAuditGate` placement, and the ticket claim/ownership types.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: audit events are signed *before* ordering assigns sequence/HLC — bodies are sequence-neutral, and apply proves the ordered artifact is their unique deterministic extension. Four distinct orders exist because Local transactions, controls, W12 writes, and reads have genuinely different preparation shapes; conflation is how leaks happen.

## Design — normative detail
Four orders (noninterchangeable): **Local admitted transaction:** ticket admission/claim -> authorization/final rebase/outcome preparation -> ordered final-certification reservation plus coordinate/obligation holds -> sequence-neutral audit event/resolution bodies and immutable semantic plan -> replaceable event attempt/locks/shares/event -> replaceable resolution attempt/locks/shares/resolution -> triple-bearing `TerminalAuditGate` -> stable capsule/template/semantic prepared closure -> repeatable `LocalOrderAttemptInput` plus availability certificate -> command/order/candidate. **Local control or pre-effect terminal:** ticket/claim -> authorization -> `AuditTerminalFreezeSpec::Arm` plus generated control-basis hold -> same body/plan/attempt triple -> stable typed control base -> repeatable Local order supplement -> command/order/candidate. **W12 admitted write:** ticket/registration claim -> union authorization/resources/gate-free outcome preparation -> published admission -> shard fragments/prepares/constraints/serialization -> ordered Global final-certification reservation/holds -> plan and replaceable attempts -> gate -> stable Meta command base -> repeatable `MetaOrderAttemptInput` -> Global command/candidate. **Read (either posture):** ticket/claim -> read admission -> authorized traversal/buffered result -> release decision -> freeze/hold where required -> bodies/attempts/gate -> stable publication/read-close base -> role order supplement -> candidate -> external batch receipt -> gap-free `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` (ReleasedAwaitingActivation) -> independent fresh `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec` -> output. Consequences: Local outcome preparation carries its eventual gate, W12 preparation never does, a read-release decision cannot authorize the traversal that produced it, time-authority failure cannot block the audit prefix, and neither HLC nor assigned order appears in signed audit bodies.

The event binds the exact ticket request, namespace/domain/profile/principal, authorization decision, and one tagged outcome commitment: `TransactionMutation{final_effect_digest,transaction_effect_basis_commitment}`, `ControlMutation{control_kind,spec_body_digest,expected_state_conditions_digest,semantic_transition_basis_commitment}`, canonical read result, denial, or stable failure/no-effect proof. `transaction_effect_basis_commitment` hashes only the sequence-neutral final effect, role-free coordinate/head expectations, schema/constraint/resource/authorization inputs, intent semantics, and transaction token — explicitly excluding capsule/command/certificate identities, `TerminalAuditGate`, assigned sequence/HLC/marker identity, and chain hash. Attestation times are pre-order signer observations. `spec_body_digest` hashes only canonical `SequenceNeutralSpec.spec_body`, excluding its terminal gate; `semantic_transition_basis_commitment` hashes the deterministic pre-order before/after relation expressed by that body and expected conditions, never an applied record/root identity; expected sequence/state conditions make a stale prebuilt terminal fail closed. `AuditTicketResolution` terminals `Completed|Denied|Failed` each strongly name their exact event; `Abandoned` carries a signed typed no-effect reason; no optional unbound `event_digest` exists. `AuditEventRecord`/`AuditTicketResolution` carry body ref, terminal plan ref, concrete attempt plan ref, sorted signer lock/share refs in exact `(signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_set_epoch,key_epoch)` bijection, subset bitmap, threshold, and canonical aggregate; the signing transcript binds plan ID, attempt ID, body digest, and signer identity/epochs. `TerminalAuditGate` is `StructurallyInapplicable{exemption}|NotRequired{evidence}|Required{ticket_ref,event_ref,terminal_resolution_ref}` — encodable only in the ticket-owning consensus domain with all three objects agreeing with the earlier authorization gate; every transaction command carries its one gate in its transaction input, every semantic control obtains its gate only through its referenced spec wrapper; `AuditTicketAdmissionSpec`, `AuditRecoverySpec`, and `AuditCompletenessTransitionSpec` are `StructurallyInapplicable{AuditSystemAuthority}`; `AuditTerminalSpec {ticket_ref,expected_pending_ticket_digest,event_ref,terminal_resolution_ref}` consumes exactly one already-pending ticket for non-mutating/pre-effect paths. Local ownership types (`LocalAuditTicketOwner: Operation|Statement|Control`, `LocalAuditTicketClaimRecord`, `LocalOperationAuditAdmission`/`LocalStatementAuditAdmission`) are Local-only; no Local field can encode a global txn ID or GlobalControlRecord.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 (restated): a protected candidate becomes observable only after its signer-locked terminal event, external resolution batch, and gap-free visibility advance. FG-INV-17: any terminal audit plan/lock/share requires completion of the selected certification basis. FG-INV-07: no final event/resolution body points back into a plan that embeds it — the durable strong graph stays acyclic.

## Interactions
Consumes tickets from w9-audit-continuity; produces the candidate-forming inputs w9-audit-pipeline appends; w4-coordinator wires the Local order; w12-certification wires the W12 order; w9-audit-release batches resolutions.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Mutation fixtures: flip each included commitment field and each forbidden exclusion independently. Negative: stale prebuilt terminal fails on expected conditions; gate in wrong consensus domain unencodable; unbound event digest unrepresentable; read-release decision reused as traversal authorization fails. Crash-inject each order at every arrow. Property: lock/share bijection exactness. E2E: one Local Required commit fully logged from claim to candidate. Detailed logging: each construction-order step logs {order_kind, step_name, ticket digest, body digest(s), terminal/attempt plan IDs, sorted (signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_set_epoch,key_epoch) lock/share bijection verdict, gate arm and consensus-domain check, expected-condition mismatch reason on failure}; crash-injection tests must be able to identify the correct recovery continuation from the last logged step alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: signing after ordering (circular); one generic order; command-level duplicate gates. Risk: schema breadth — controlled by registry generation and golden fixtures.

## Provenance
§12.8 (950–952, 982), App A 1466, 2631–2633.

title: Implement the audit release plane: batches, visibility advance, portable certificates
description:
## What & scope
Implement the Protocol-plane release half of the two-plane architecture: `AuditExternalResolutionBatch` and its CAS receipt, `AuditVisibilityProtocolState`, release recipes, the sole visibility input `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec`, the released-ticket/pending-output bijection, `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate`, the Shard publication analogue, `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec` semantics, RootManifest publication, and recovery.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: release-time facts (external receipts, visibility, leases) must never be retconned into older candidate roots — so release lives outside canonical semantic state, joined to it by commitments and certificates. This separation is what lets an audit suffix stall without corrupting semantics, lets delivery terminate independently, and keeps activation (which needs time evidence) from ever blocking the audit prefix.

## Design — normative detail
`AuditExternalResolutionBatch` is the pre-CAS portable `{audit_domain_id,role_and_group,expected_prior_continuity_digest,expected_prior_cas_version,first_pipeline_order,last_pipeline_order,ordered_required_entries[{pipeline_order,ticket_digest,event_digest,resolution_digest,candidate_root_digest}],interleaved_ready_entry_commitment,resulting_ticket_and_unresolved_commitments,resulting_audit_chain_head_digest,batch_digest}`. The external authority verifies every required entry and atomically installs the direct `TicketsResolvedBatch` successor, returning reference-free `AuditExternalBatchCasReceipt {authority_id,expected_head_digest,expected_cas_version,resulting_head_bytes_and_digest,resulting_cas_version,batch_digest,cas_before,cas_after,monotonic_counter,signatures}`. Partial acceptance is impossible; conflict returns no successor and recovery rereads the head. Batching may stop before any not-yet-resolved Required entry but cannot omit/reorder one inside its range. Both objects are registered `PreOrderArtifact`/`ExternalCertificateInput`, never logical commands; `AuditTicketResolutionBatchSpec` does not exist. The release plane is `AuditVisibilityProtocolState<Role>`, manifest/Raft-maintenance-owned: `{role_and_group,maintenance_generation,maintenance_applied_index,pipeline_ref,visible_audit_outcome_index_ref,result_independent_retention_index_ref,subscription_cursor_delivery_index_ref,pending_cursor_output_index_ref,artifact_output_delivery_index_ref,protected_error_delivery_index_ref,protocol_resource_escrow_index_ref,external_continuity_head_ref,security_barrier_state:None|AppliedHidden{pipeline_order,predecessor_binding_commitment,successor_binding_commitment},nonretaining_predecessor_digest,body_digest}`. `VisibleAuditOutcomeIndex` maps each released ticket/candidate to its exact `AuditOutcomeRecord`, batch receipt/member ordinal, advance identity, and public release commitment — it contains no unreleased outcome. Delivery indexes own PendingVisibility/ReleasedAwaitingActivation/ActiveDeliverable/terminal records, capability lineage, typed resource escrow, and byte-retention closure; canonical payloads own only semantic effect, admission/freeze/gate commitments, and an opaque detachment commitment — never claiming a later release-time fact was part of an earlier candidate root.

`AuditVisibilityProtectedOutputReleaseRecipe<Role>` is the closed union `Result|SubscriptionInitialBaseline|SubscriptionDelta|SubscriptionReset|ArtifactOutput|ProtectedError`, each `{pending_ref,release_subject_commitment}` — no clock, time evidence, absolute window, lease, capability nonce, or activation recipe. `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec<Role>` is `{expected_protocol_state_ref,expected_pipeline_ref,expected_maintenance_generation,expected_visible_pipeline_order,advance_through_pipeline_order,external_batch_receipt_refs[],ordered_entry_release_evidence,sorted_audit_outcome_recipes[],sorted_protected_output_release_recipes[],complete_released_ticket_and_pending_output_bijection_proof_ref:StrongRef<ReleasedVisibilityBijectionProof<Role>>,expected_returned_continuity_ref,resulting_pipeline_body_recipe,resulting_protocol_state_body_recipe,system_authority_evidence:StructuralAuditExemption::AuditSystemAuthority}` — the sole ordered Local/Meta visibility input, but command-contract class `Maintenance` on the Protocol plane: it consumes one same-group Raft maintenance-log position and advances no LogicalCommandSeq/GlobalLogicalCommandSeq, CommitSeq, logical HLC, semantic command head, or semantic state root, and appends no pipeline candidate; a semantic `AuditVisibilityAdvance` command does not exist. Maintenance apply verifies a gap-free prefix, direct external-head succession, every Required resolution, every NotRequired/system proof, exact candidate/configuration/fence identities, and one release recipe for every and only PendingVisibility output entering the prefix; it then atomically (a) moves the visible endpoint to the last released candidate root even when a later unresolved suffix remains, (b) installs exact release-time audit outcomes, (c) replaces each PendingVisibility owner with `ReleasedAwaitingActivation` (immutable release evidence, still no clock/lease/capability), (d) advances the imported external continuity head, and (e) clears a security barrier exactly when its entry is released. Time-authority unavailability, an expired prospective lease recipe, or missing capability bytes cannot block it — none is an input. Bijection mismatch or RootManifest/maintenance CAS change applies nothing; matching retry returns the same result and generation; stale/overlapping/gapped/wrong-role/substituted/partial/leapfrog inputs fail.

Later Semantic commands prove earlier visibility via `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Role:Local|Meta>` `{authority_domain_projection,semantic_applied_identity,candidate_state_commitment,pipeline_order,release_kind:InlineAuditSystem|MaintenanceVisibilityAdvance,audit_release_commitment,resulting_visible_endpoint_commitment,resulting_protocol_state_commitment,root_manifest_and_slot_durability_commitment,authority_binding_public_commitment,certificate_attempt_and_signatures}` — constructed only after the releasing RootManifest/RootSlot is durable, no local ObjectId refs to Protocol state; `freeze_mirror_record_ref` and direct Semantic->Protocol edges are invalid schema fields. Shard has no pipeline: `ShardStatePublicationCertificate` is its publication proof, and `CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>` is the generated closed union `Local{visibility_certificate_ref}|Meta{visibility_certificate_ref}|Shard{publication_certificate_ref}` used by any subsystem (GC, key dispatch) needing durably-published authorizing state. `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec<Role>` (Result/SubscriptionInitialBaseline/SubscriptionDelta/SubscriptionResetNotice/SubscriptionResetBaseline/ArtifactOutput/ProtectedError arms — each carrying its released ref (SubscriptionResetBaseline instead consumes the reset-ack ref), its lease time-basis ref, and its time-evidence ref; every arm except ProtectedError also carries its prebuilt initial or successor resume-replay ref — ProtectedError has none, consistent with errors having no durable resume capability) reauthorizes the released subject against current security binding and service authority, proves the full minimum delivery window, and CASes only that record to Active; missing/stale evidence delays only that output; same-publication inline activation is legal only for an already-visible NotRequired subject — Required release and activation are always distinct v1 transitions (batched in w9-activation-batching). `RootManifest` publishes protocol root and visible endpoint in one D2 slot update after the maintenance entry commits; public semantic reads use the visible candidate root; audit/status/output guards additionally require the matching protocol entry. Recovery reconstructs the semantic queue and protocol indexes from RootManifest, the maintenance log, prepared ownership, and exact external heads/receipts, then idempotently finishes committed maintenance before serving. Required-audit throughput/latency is benchmarked as a separate governance profile (pipeline limits, batch size, external RTT, resolution throughput, visible-prefix lag, head-of-line saturation); baseline no-audit numbers never imply the same visibility latency.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-08 (restated): only `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` moves the visible endpoint; batches are direct continuity successors over exactly one gap-free prefix. FG-INV-15/16 (restated): released outputs follow the state-shaped independent-retention machine; audit candidates remain hidden until their exact batch and gap-free advance; matching retry is idempotent. Governance throughput numbers: benchmark class; visibility availability line: `slo.toml`.

## Interactions
Consumes w9-audit-pipeline entries and w9-audit-continuity heads; produces `ReleasedAwaitingActivation` owners consumed by w9-activation-batching and w10-result-machines; produces `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate`/`CanonicalPublicationEvidence` consumed by w9-key-lifecycle, w9-time-rotation, w2-gc-core, w11-backup, w12-decision-visibility; w2-root-bootstrap performs the D2 publication.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property: bijection proof rejects one-missing/one-extra/duplicated/substituted recipe; advance with time evidence as input is unrepresentable (compile-level). Crash matrix: batch send vs CAS vs receipt import vs maintenance apply vs D2 publication — recovery idempotently completes committed maintenance. Negative: partial batch acceptance, merely-signed head without CAS succession, wrong-role certificate, Semantic strong ref into Protocol state (schema-rejected). E2E with logs: stall the simulated authority mid-suffix, verify partial-prefix advance releases exactly the resolved prefix, outputs stay ReleasedAwaitingActivation with no lease, then activate after time evidence returns. Bench: governance profile published with the six required metrics. Detailed logging: every batch/advance/activation-handoff logs {role_and_group, first/last_pipeline_order, expected/resulting continuity head digests and cas_versions, receipt monotonic_counter, bijection-proof verdict naming the offending recipe on failure, per-recipe owner transition (PendingVisibility -> ReleasedAwaitingActivation), maintenance generation, D2 slot publication identity, idempotent-completion events during recovery}; the stalled-authority e2e verifies from logs that exactly the resolved prefix was released and that no output gained a clock/lease/capability before activation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: release-time mirrors inside semantic candidates; `AuditTicketResolutionBatchSpec` as a logical command; pretending Shard has a pipeline. Risk: two-plane recovery complexity — bounded by the recovery equation and idempotent maintenance completion.

## Provenance
§12.8 (960–972, 978, 980), App A 2615 gates.

### Fidelity addendum — exact released outcome object
`AuditOutcomeRecord` is created only by `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec<Local|Meta>` maintenance apply and is exact: `{domain:{database_security_namespace_id,audit_domain_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Local|Meta},terminal_attempt_visible_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalAttemptRecord::VisibilityReleased>,ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,event_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>,resolution_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketResolution>,external_resolution_batch_ref:StrongRef<AuditExternalResolutionBatch>,external_batch_cas_receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuditExternalBatchCasReceipt>,batch_member_ordinal,pipeline_order,advance_input_ref:AuditVisibilityAdvanceInputRef,assigned_maintenance_index,candidate_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity,outcome_commitment}`. The terminal attempt must first be `ExternalBatchCasCommitted` for this same batch/receipt/member, then its VisibilityReleased successor and outcome name the same already-built advance input/maintenance command and assigned index; neither may name a future applied record.

Construction order is fixed: maintenance input/command -> per-entry VisibilityReleased successors -> outcomes and protected-output release successors -> visible outcome/delivery indexes -> successor Protocol/pipeline state -> maintenance applied record -> RootManifest. Activation is absent and occurs only later. Golden DAG and crash tests reject future/back edges, wrong batch ordinal, wrong role/domain/candidate, missing CAS-committed predecessor, duplicate released ticket, or activation folded into visibility. Logs emit role/domain commitment, pipeline order, batch/member, attempt from/to tag, maintenance index, candidate/outcome commitments, released owner counts, and RootSlot publication identity; protected event bytes are redacted.

title: Publish the external-authority surface: footprint, availability lines, succession
description:
## What & scope
Implement §16 item 8: the per-posture authority footprint table, the three-line availability doctrine, the external-authority HA/succession contract, and the database-as-isolation-unit doctrine with its registered per-tenant rejection.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: FrankenGraphDB deliberately moves trust anchors (time, audit, allocation, DP, incarnation) outside the process — which is only honest if every posture states exactly where those authorities sit on synchronous paths, what fails when they fail, and how a dead authority is succeeded. This bead is the anti-marketing artifact: availability is never one product number, and the embedded posture's zero-external-authority story is provable, not implied.

## Design — normative detail
Every registered posture publishes its authority footprint table: for each external authority — identity/allocation continuity (`IdentityContinuityRecord`/`AllocationEpochReservation`), cluster incarnation (`ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord`), the time authority (`PortableTimeAuthorityObservation`), audit continuity (`AuditContinuityRecord`), the DP registry (`PrivacyContinuityRecord`), archive/grant (`ArchiveRetentionGrant`), reservation (`ReservationAuthorityHead`), catalog (`CatalogAuthorityHead`), the restore dispatch journal's `ExternalCasContinuity` head, transparency witnesses (`WitnessPolicy`), and KMS/HSM — the table states whether the authority sits on a synchronous operation path and exactly where. The v1 footprint: audit continuity touches a Required operation exactly three times (the strictly serial one-at-a-time `TicketIssued` issuance CAS, the admission visibility advance, and its share of one batched `TicketsResolvedBatch` resolution); the time authority is consumed per protected-output activation tick — batch-subject amortized under §12.8 — and per `IdRangeLease` use window; incarnation continuity only at `ExternalCas` lease acquisition/renewal; KMS/HSM only at a key-unwrap miss; identity/allocation continuity only at allocation-epoch mint; the DP registry only at DP charges; archive, reservation, catalog, and the restore journal only in backup/restore flows; witnesses only at transparency-proof freshness. The embedded `DirectoryBound` posture's footprint table is empty: it consumes zero external authorities.

Availability is stated per operation class as three lines, never one product. **Apply-durability availability** is local storage plus Raft only — applies continue behind a stalled Required entry up to §12.8's pipeline limits, then degrade to deterministic backpressure, so a stalled audit authority cannot lose or block durable ordering. **Visibility availability** multiplies in the audit authority's availability under Required profiles, because only the Protocol-plane `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` can release a Required entry. **Delivery availability** multiplies in the time authority's per-tick availability, deliberately kept off the audit prefix. Per-posture numbers for all three lines are `slo.toml` rows, never invariants; the §20 authority-availability risk row tracks them.

The external authorities are inside the declared trust boundary and carry their own registered HA/durability contract: threshold signer sets with registered rotation, durable CAS heads with an explicit anti-rollback story, and a specified successor-authority migration. A threshold-authorized authority-succession transition — recorded as a permanent continuity event in the affected chain, format reserved at G0 — is the *only* path off a permanently dead authority; the completeness-transition escape hatch is not one, because its `CompletenessChanged` successor is CAS-installed by the same authority it would have to replace. §15.2's authority-chain checking runs the same no-fork lineage verification over succession events as over ordinary direct CAS successors.

The audit-stall isolation unit is the **database**. Each same-identity lineage has its own `AuditDomainId`, its own `AuditVisibilityPipeline`, and its own `RootManifest`, and `fgdbd` is multi-database by capability (§13), so tenants requiring independent audit-availability domains are separate databases under one server. Intra-database per-tenant audit-visibility domains are a *registered rejection* with the reason recorded: pipeline entries are cumulative role state roots in one linear chain — entry `i` byte-matches candidate `i-1` — so releasing one tenant's entry past another tenant's unresolved Required entry would expose a state root containing the unaudited effects, and §12.8's security-barrier noninterference argument requires one total admission order; independent per-tenant visibility would demand partitioned candidate roots — a W12-scale redesign, not an additive registry change. Within one database the mitigations are per-tenant ticket-resolution SLOs at the external authority (an `slo.toml` surface, not a pipeline change) plus §12.8's reserved capacity and pipeline limits.

## Invariants & claim types
This bead is predominantly claim-class governance: all three availability lines and per-tenant ticket-resolution targets are `slo.toml` rows; the footprint table is a registered posture artifact validated by CI (a posture consuming an authority absent from its table fails registry generation); succession-event format is a G0-reserved decision; the §20 authority-availability risk row is the living tracker. FG-INV-08's no-fork lineage clause extends over succession events.

## Interactions
Aggregates the surfaces of w9-audit-continuity (issuance/advance/resolution touches), w9-audit-release (visibility line), w9-time-authority (delivery line, per-tick consumption), w9-dp (charge touch), w9-key-lifecycle (KMS/HSM miss), w2-continuity-profiles (incarnation/allocation, `DirectoryBound` emptiness); obs-slo wires the `slo.toml` rows; verif-oracles implements the no-fork succession checking; risk-register restates the §20 row; w10-server exposes the multi-database capability doctrine.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
CI: footprint-table completeness check — every synchronous external-authority consumption in code is annotated and must map to a table cell; the `DirectoryBound` posture build asserts zero external-authority call sites (link-time/feature-gate proof). Chaos/e2e with logs: kill each authority independently and verify exactly the predicted line degrades (apply continues to limits under dead audit authority; visibility resumes on recovery; delivery stalls only under dead time authority while audit advances). Succession drill: threshold-sign a succession event on a simulated dead authority, verify chain verification accepts it and rejects a forked successor; verify a completeness transition cannot substitute. Doc artifact: generated per-posture footprint/availability page kept in sync (g0-doc-sync style check). Detailed logging: chaos drills log {authority identity, kill/restore markers, per-line degradation onset (apply backpressure at pipeline limits, visibility stall, delivery stall), typed backpressure class observed, recovery/resume markers}; succession drills log {dead-authority id, succession event digest, chain-verification verdict, rejected-fork evidence, refused completeness-substitution reason} - so the three-line availability behavior is verifiable from logs against the published footprint table.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: single-number availability claims; intra-database per-tenant visibility (recorded rejection with W12-scale reasoning); using the completeness transition as succession. Risk: operators under-provision external authorities — mitigated by the published three-line math and SLO alerts.

## Provenance
§16 item 8 (1222–1228), §12.8, §15.2, §20 authority-availability row.

title: Implement DP: mechanism contracts, Renyi accounting, irreversible debit, seed lineage
description:
## What & scope
Implement §12.7's core: DP as an explicit Warden authority class — mechanism/accounting contracts, the nonce/request-key identity plane, protected seed material and envelopes, the external irreversible-before-access charge protocol, execution leases and access guards, Meta-only noise in W12, and DP output through the ordinary result machine. Continuity import, the request state machine, and restore/clone semantics are split to w9-dp-continuity-import.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5's purest expression: a privacy budget that a compromised or rolled-back local node cannot refund. §3 adopts DP (Dwork; Renyi accounting, Mironov; smooth sensitivity, Nissim) as a Warden capability class with a per-tenant ledger; a locally subtracted epsilon is worthless under restore or compromise. The debit is external and charged before any sensitive access, and the seed is derived — never sampled ad hoc — so one charge can never yield two answers.

## Design — normative detail
`DpMechanismContract` binds the neighboring relation, allowed fixed-shape query family, contribution/clipping bounds, sensitivity proof artifact, canonical output shape, seeded-noise algorithm, Renyi-debit derivation, observable timing/error/size contract, distributed-combination rule, implementation version, and proof/test manifest. `RenyiAccountingProfile` fixes an ordered finite grid of canonical rational orders > 1, checked fixed-point amounts, exact addition/comparison/overflow rejection, epsilon/delta conversion, and per-principal/domain ceilings; floating composition, negative debit, saturation, or grid reinterpretation is invalid. Smooth-sensitivity mechanisms charge their declared parameters *before* access and compute data-dependent scale only inside charged execution — no sensitive prepass may choose the debit, mechanism, plan, or error. Each population has a stable `PrivacyAccountingDomainId` spanning aliases/tokens, incarnations, same-identity restores, branches, and backups; incarnation is provenance, not a budget reset. `DpClientNonceKey` is `{privacy_accounting_domain_id,privacy_principal_or_alias_domain_commitment,database_security_namespace_id,client_nonce}`; `DpRequestKey<Role>` binds authority header, domain, principal, alias root digest, logical snapshot identity, exact wire-safe graph binding set, normalized bound query and parameters, neighboring relation, contribution/clipping bounds, mechanism and accounting profile refs, and canonical output encoding — the nonce is deliberately outside this content key. `DpRequestNonceIndex<Role>` permanently maps nonce key to `Bound{request_key_digest,canonical_request_digest,prepare_applied_identity}|Spent{request_key_digest,charge_operation_id,debit_and_output_or_no_output_commitments}`; `DpTransitionSpec::Prepare` atomically inserts or byte-matches that leaf before seed creation — same nonce + identical request joins; any drift returns a stable conflict *before* a charge request exists.

`DpSeedMaterial` is the secret plaintext `{format_version=1,privacy_accounting_domain_id,request_key_digest,mechanism_contract_identity_and_digest,renyi_accounting_profile_identity_and_digest,noise_derivation_profile_oid,seed_bytes:[u8;32],body_digest}` with `seed_commitment = BLAKE3('fgdb.dp-seed-commitment.v1'||canonical(fields sans body_digest))`; every draw is `BLAKE3_keyed(seed_bytes,'fgdb.dp-draw.v1'||request_key_digest||mechanism_contract_digest||draw_domain_tag||checked_draw_ordinal)` and never consumes the runtime/lab replay seed. Max encoded size 512 bytes; one secret-classified `logical_object_kinds.toml` row; production seed bytes exist only in the nonspillable secret arena or authenticated ciphertext, redacted from debug/metrics/audit/errors/crashpacks/decision cards, synchronously overwritten on every ownership path; secret-memory profile failure fails before preparation. `CryptoCx` creates exactly one `DpSeedEnvelope<Role>` (header byte-matching the request and every opener/wrap scope; public certificates carry only the seed commitment and authority public commitments). External accounting is the *sole* irreversible debit authority: `DpDebitDerivationCertificate<Role>` derives `derived_debit:RenyiDebitVector` from byte-matched bases; `PrivacyChargeAuthorization` is the portable signed authorization (domain, principal/alias-domain commitment, request-key and canonical-request digests, contract/profile identities, maximum authorized debit, ceiling basis digest, authority/security-state public commitments, tenant/principal/ceiling/purpose and snapshot/graph/disclosure/answer commitments, time window, signer epoch, signature) containing no local StrongRef, policy root, revocation root, audit ticket, or `SecurityStateBinding`; `PrivacyRequestTombstoneLeaf` is minimal `{nonce_key_digest,request_key_digest,canonical_request_digest,charge_operation_id,debit_digest,seed_commitment}` — forensic detail is a separately encrypted, expiring record. `PortablePrivacyChargeRequest` is reference-free and pre-effect; `charge_operation_id` depends on the stable nonce/key/contract/profile/debit/seed commitment, never a CAS attempt. `DpTransitionSpec::ArmCharge` selects ChargeRequested and owns the exact local `PrivacyChargeOperationRecord<Role>` before a linear `ExternalPrivacyChargeSendGuard` may contact the registry; only unarmed Prepared may abandon; timeout/crash after arming leaves ChargeRequested and recovery retries the same operation ID and bytes. The registry atomically checks/inserts the nonce binding, adds exactly one debit and tombstone, constructs the direct-successor reference-free `PrivacyContinuityRecord {privacy_accounting_domain_id,privacy_epoch,accounting_profile_identity_and_digest,cumulative_renyi_state_commitment,client_nonce_binding_root,request_tombstone_root,predecessor_digest,external_registry_id,cas_version,status:Active|Frozen|Retired,last_transition:Genesis|Charge{...}|Administrative{...},issued_at,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}` and an `ExternalPrivacyChargeReceipt`; retry returns identical bytes without another debit; no refund transition exists. `PrivacyExecutionLease<Role>` (signed; snapshot/graph bindings, mechanism/debit/seed commitments, compute generation, fences, time window) plus `DpComputeOwnerLease` gate compute; the nonserializable `DpSensitiveAccessGuard` exists only from the current Computing record plus matching admission/charge/seed/authority/lease. In W12 Meta alone owns seed/noise: `GlobalDpExecutionGrant` and `DpShardAggregateFragment` bind request/charge/generation/profile/mechanism, clipped shape, shard/configuration, security projection, idempotency digest — and carry no seed or public-output authority; Meta verifies the complete participant set and applies one seed. Output uses the ordinary cross-plane result machine: `DpOutputCandidate` -> CommitResult atomically constructs `DpCommittedOutput`/ResultCommitted detachment plus the Protocol PendingVisibility owner and resource escrow in one manifest publication; required audit creates no lease/capability; independent fresh activation creates the first lease/capability without blocking the audit prefix; later delivery maintenance never redraws or recharges. `DpSpentTombstone` permanently retains only nonce/request/op/debit/receipt/seed/output-or-no-output/result-disposition commitments.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16 (restated): DP has one external charge request/tombstone/receipt lineage and noise is generated only by Meta after the charge is mirrored; privacy charges/seeds/results are never lost, duplicated, refunded, or exposed while obligated. FG-INV-14: DP seeds/charges are GC roots until exact terminal release. FG-INV-20: one union-wide authorization decision covers the complete effect set. Per-domain ceilings and grids are registered configuration (FG-CFG class); mechanism proofs are evidence artifacts in the proof/test manifest.

## Interactions
w9-threat-tokens supplies authority headers and `SecurityStateBinding`; w9-audit-release supplies visibility/activation; w9-time-authority validates `PrivacyExecutionLease`; w1-crypto supplies keyed derivation and the secret-memory profile; w9-dp-continuity-import completes import/restore; w10-result-machines hosts the `DpResult` owner arm; w12-escrow-dp-alloc owns W12 grant/fragment execution.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Permanent tests (per plan): fixed-point accounting exactness, alias composition, arm-before-send ordering, lost external replies, every seed/CAS crash point, no-access-before-guard compile failures, compute fencing, W12 fragment completeness/no-shard-noise, audit-visibility and ordinary-result races, seed secrecy (crashpack/log scrub assertions). Property: same bound key => one debit, one seed, one canonical output; any drift => stable pre-charge conflict. Fuzz: seed decoder, synthetic-only corpus. E2E: two racing identical-nonce requests produce one debit and byte-identical outputs, logged per protocol step. Detailed logging: each protocol step logs {nonce_key_digest, request_key_digest, charge_operation_id, debit_digest, seed_commitment, external head cas_version before/after, receipt digest, request-state transition, guard arm/consume events}; seed bytes and plaintext query/parameters must never appear in any log (the scrub assertions run over the captured logs), and retry paths log the identical-bytes verdict.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: local-ledger-only accounting; floating-point composition; data-dependent prepass choosing debit/mechanism/plan; per-shard noise. Risk: external registry RTT on the charge path — inherent to irreversibility, disclosed in the authority footprint (w9-authority-surface).

## Provenance
§12.7 (916–942), App A 2627–2629 (construction DAG), §3 SOTA DP row (176).

### Fidelity addendum — complete seed-wrap and ceiling-basis schemas
The previously named supporting types are mandatory independently addressable registry rows, not opaque placeholders. `DpSeedEnvelope<Role>` is exact: `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,request_key_ref:StrongRef<DpRequestKey<Role>>,seed_profile_oid,entropy_source_profile_oid,seed_commitment,seed_ciphertext_ref:StrongCiphertextRef<DpSeedMaterial>,sorted_key_wrap_refs[StrongRef<DpSeedKeyWrap>],noise_derivation_profile_oid,mechanism_contract_ref:StrongRef<DpMechanismContract>,body_digest}`. `DpSeedKeyWrap` is `{authority_bound_header,privacy_accounting_domain_id,request_key_digest,seed_commitment,seed_ciphertext_id,wrapped_seed_dek,opener_scope:CurrentCompute|RecoveryRetainedSeed|ThresholdEscrow,wrap_algorithm,wrap_key_id,wrap_key_epoch,aad_transcript_digest,retention_floor,body_digest}`. Its AAD binds domain, role, request, seed commitment/ciphertext, opener scope, key identity/epoch, and profile; every envelope/header/opener value byte-matches. Wraps never contain seed plaintext, and Shard is uninhabited.

`PrivacyCeilingBasis` is `{authority_bound_header,privacy_accounting_domain_id,privacy_principal_or_alias_domain_commitment,identity_alias_root_digest,renyi_accounting_profile_ref:StrongRef<RenyiAccountingProfile>,canonical_ceiling_vector,current_cumulative_renyi_state_commitment,remaining_ceiling_vector,purpose_class,allowed_snapshot_graph_disclosure_and_answer_commitment,policy_epoch,revocation_index,basis_continuity_head_digest,basis_checker_version,body_digest}`. Checked component-wise subtraction must prove `cumulative + remaining = ceiling` without negative, overflow, saturation, grid drift, or alias-domain substitution. `DpDebitDerivationCertificate` strongly owns this basis and its authorization carries only the basis digest.

Golden/mutation/property tests cover wrap AAD, sorted uniqueness, wrong role/request/ciphertext/key epoch/opener scope, decrypt-only recovery, ceiling arithmetic at every grid order, alias composition, policy/revocation drift, and charge at exact ceiling. E2E rotates the wrap key during an armed charge and restores one charged request under retained-seed and unavailable-seed dispositions. Logs emit request/seed commitments, wrap count/scope/key epoch and AAD verdict, ceiling-basis digest/profile/grid, arithmetic verdict, and retention disposition; seed bytes, wrapped DEK bytes, principal IDs, and protected query material never appear.

### Phase dependency correction — activate the already-proved owner machine
This W9 task consumes `fgdb-w2-local-protected-output-owners-by8v`: it replaces the verification-only inactive candidate source with the real Local authority-owning-role external charge/receipt, seed wrap, noise execution, audit, time, and continuity evidence, then activates the same frozen `DpResult` owner arm. It may not fork a Warden-specific result stream or weaken the G2 retention/release state machine. G3 E2E proves the first real candidate is unconstructible before every required irreversible-debit and authority prerequisite is satisfied.

The live DP activation dependency is directional: this task depends on the independently verified continuity/import substrate. It cannot substitute a new ledger or bypass restore reconciliation, and its capability activation test requires both `continuity_state_valid=true` and all real charge/seed/noise/audit/time prerequisites.

title: Implement DP continuity import, request state machine, and restore/clone semantics
description:
## What & scope
Implement the Chronicle-side import of external DP accounting state, the exact DP request state machine, administrative transitions, and restore/clone semantics (§12.7 back half).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: the external registry is only irreversible if local state can *prove* it mirrored every debit — including debits issued after the backup a restore came from. Import is the sole bridge, and it is typed, chained, and recomputed, so rollback cannot orphan or duplicate a charge.

## Design — normative detail
The sole Chronicle import is bounded `PrivacyContinuityImportSpec<Role>` (Local or Meta) with exact expected current portable head, local ledger/request-index, current profile refs, and a nonempty direct-successor chain. `PrivacyContinuityImportStep<Role>` is the closed union `Charge{prior_ref,returned_ref,receipt_ref,operation_record_ref,disposition:BindChargeRequested{expected_request_record_ref,expected_seed_envelope_ref}|RestoreBindRetainedSeed{expected_predecessor_record_ref,seed_envelope_ref,reconciliation_evidence_ref}|ImportSameNamespaceMaterialPending{request_absence_or_backup_cut_proof_ref,reconciliation_evidence_ref}|AccountingOnlyForeignNamespace{foreign_namespace_id}}|AdministrativeFreeze{prior_ref,returned_ref,transition_ref,freeze_authorization_ref}|AdministrativeRetire{prior_ref,returned_ref,transition_ref,complete_local_nonterminal_disposition_proof_ref}|AccountingProfileChange{prior_ref,returned_ref,transition_ref,successor_profile_ref,exact_grid/ceiling_carry_proof_ref}`. Steps form one direct-successor chain; apply recomputes every nonce/Renyi/tombstone/admin transition, validates every portable identity against its local typed owner, creates `DpChargeBinding {role,request_key_ref,nonce_key_digest,charge_operation_record_ref,receipt_ref,prior_and_returned_continuity_refs,accounting_profile_ref,debit_digest,seed_commitment,tombstone_inclusion_proof_ref,source_import_spec_ref,assigned_role_order,body_digest}`, advances the exact `PrivacyLedgerState`, and selects role-valid request/admin states; the preexisting spec and assigned scalar order replace any forbidden reference to the future applied record. There is no RecordCharge command. Portable `PrivacyContinuityAdministrativeTransition` is exactly `Freeze{reason,authorization,effective_epoch}|Retire{replacement_or_terminal_basis,complete_live_charge_and_lease_disposition,authorization}|AccountingProfileChange{predecessor/successor profile identities,grid_conversion:Forbidden|ExactRegisteredEmbedding,ceiling_carry_proof,authorization}` — no StrongRef or local locator; a frozen/retired head forbids new Prepare/ArmCharge and profile drift cannot reinterpret an old vector. The request machine is exactly `Prepared -> AbandonedBeforeCharge|ChargeRequested`; `ChargeRequested -> ChargeRefused|ChargedIdle|ChargedMaterialPending`; `ChargedMaterialPending -> ChargedIdle|UnavailableAfterCharge`; `ChargedIdle -> Computing(generation)`; `Computing -> ChargedIdle|Computing(generation+1)|ResultCommitted`; transitions are Prepare/Abandon/Arm/Refusal/Attach/Unavailable/Start/Yield/Reclaim/Commit/Compact; exact restore/import dispositions are the only way to select ChargedMaterialPending; no state is Delivered/Acknowledged/Released; `ResultCommitted` stores charge binding, seed envelope, committed output ref, delivery id, and a result-detachment commitment — never a strong protocol-retention back-ref. `DpRequestIndex<Role>` maps to Detailed or permanent `DpSpentTombstone`; compaction cannot select a charged nonterminal state or release an independently retained result/forensic object. Same-identity restore remains hidden while it imports every post-backup external debit: matching retained seed becomes ChargedIdle, exhaustively missing material becomes UnavailableAfterCharge, and ResultCommitted must reconstruct its ordinary result index or fail as corrupt. Clone shares the source accounting domain unless threshold-authorized `PrivacyDomainSplitAuthorization` proves disjoint populations.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16: one external charge lineage per request; import steps are obligations reaching one legal terminal. FG-INV-07: portable objects contain no local refs; no pre-order object names its applied successor. FG-INV-14: retained seeds/results remain GC roots through import resolution.

## Interactions
Completes w9-dp; w2-recovery hosts the restore reconciliation phase this feeds; w11-restore/w12-backup-restore invoke the import before service; w2-gc-core respects Spent-commitment permanence.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Crash matrix at every import-step boundary; backup-behind restore drills with retained seed, missing material, and committed-result cases (the three dispositions), asserting hidden-until-imported. Negative: out-of-order chain, foreign-namespace charge binding as local, profile-grid reinterpretation, Prepare on a frozen head — all fail closed. Property: recomputed cumulative Renyi state matches the returned head commitment for randomized charge sequences. E2E with logs: restore from a pre-charge backup, import two post-backup debits, verify ledger equality with the external head. Detailed logging: each import step logs {step kind, prior/returned continuity digests and cas_versions, selected disposition, recomputed cumulative Renyi state commitment vs returned head commitment, created DpChargeBinding identity, request-state transition, hidden-until-imported status flips}; restore drills must show from logs alone that no service was offered before the last post-backup debit imported.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a local RecordCharge command (would let a local writer fabricate debits); refunds; treating restore as a budget reset. Risk: import chains grow — bounded by direct-successor compaction of terminal detail into Spent commitments.

## Provenance
§12.7 (934–942).

### Fidelity addendum — exact state-shaped DP request owner
`DpRequestRecord<Role>` is predecessor-weak and a closed state union over one common `{authority_bound_header,request_key_ref:StrongRef<DpRequestKey<Role>>,client_nonce_key_digest,canonical_request_digest,weak_predecessor_identity,body_digest}`. Its exact states are:

- `Prepared{seed_envelope_ref,prepare_identity,nonce_index_binding}`;
- `AbandonedBeforeCharge{seed_disposition,stable_no_charge_reason,terminal_no_output_commitment}`;
- `ChargeRequested{seed_envelope_ref,charge_operation_record_ref,charge_operation_id}`;
- `ChargeRefused{portable_refusal_evidence_ref,zero_debit_proof,seed_disposition,terminal_no_output_commitment}`;
- `ChargedMaterialPending{charge_binding_ref,receipt_ref,material_reconciliation_ref}`;
- `ChargedIdle{charge_binding_ref,seed_envelope_ref,compute_generation}`;
- `UnavailableAfterCharge{charge_binding_ref,exhaustive_missing_material_proof_ref,terminal_no_output_commitment}`;
- `Computing{charge_binding_ref,seed_envelope_ref,execution_lease_ref,compute_owner_lease_ref,compute_generation}`;
- `ResultCommitted{charge_binding_ref,seed_envelope_ref,committed_output_ref:StrongRef<DpCommittedOutput<Role>>,delivery_id,result_detachment_commitment}`.

The only legal transition graph is `Prepared -> AbandonedBeforeCharge|ChargeRequested`; `ChargeRequested -> ChargeRefused|ChargedIdle|ChargedMaterialPending`; `ChargedMaterialPending -> ChargedIdle|UnavailableAfterCharge`; `ChargedIdle -> Computing(generation)`; `Computing -> ChargedIdle|Computing(generation+1)|ResultCommitted`. The command tags remain exactly `Prepare|Abandon|Arm|Refusal|Attach|Unavailable|Start|Yield|Reclaim|Commit|Compact`. No Delivered, Acknowledged, Released, standalone encrypted-result, or semantic-to-Protocol retention arm exists. Restore/import is the only source of ChargedMaterialPending.

`DpRequestIndex<Role>` maps each request key to Detailed or permanent `DpSpentTombstone`; compaction cannot select a charged nonterminal or release an independently retained result/forensic owner. Exhaustive model tests generate every legal edge and reject all other pairs; crash tests cut each edge and import step; same-identity restore covers retained seed, missing seed, committed result reconstruction, and foreign-namespace accounting-only import. Logs emit role, request key commitment, from/to state, compute generation, charge/receipt/seed commitments, restore disposition, output/no-output/result-owner commitments, and compaction verdict; secret/query/principal bytes remain redacted.

### Phase boundary correction — continuity substrate is independently implementable
This task implements the exact privacy-accounting-domain lineage, opaque request/tombstone/receipt commitments, continuity CAS/import/reconciliation state machine, same-identity restore rules, clone-new-identity split, and fail-closed unknown/degraded states without enabling DP query execution. It consumes frozen G0 schemas and W2 recovery and can be exercised with signed synthetic external-authority fixtures; `dp_capability=false` remains mandatory. W9's live DP task depends on this substrate and is the only task that activates external charge authorization/debit, seed/noise execution, and DpResult production. Unit/E2E reports distinguish `continuity_state_valid` from `mechanism_activated` and never promote the former into a DP correctness claim.

title: Build mandatory access-type enforcement: facade, disclosure contracts, derived state
description:
## What & scope
Implement §12.3–§12.4: enforcement as a mandatory access *type* (not a call convention), the `ConstraintDisclosureContract` union, enforced descriptor masking, and the `DerivedIdentity`/`AuthorityReuseLaw` regime for every derived object, cache, and error.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6/B3: Loom's unified executor and Prism's analytics run arbitrary plans over shared storage; if authorization were a convention, one forgotten check in an optimizer rewrite would leak hidden subgraphs. Making `AuthorizedSnapshot` and friends nonconstructible outside `fgdb-secure-view` turns the Rust type system into the enforcement boundary — a forged internal call cannot bypass policy by reaching a lower crate. B5: caches and statistics are evidence-bearing; reusing them across authority domains without a proved projection is a covert channel, so reuse is a law, not a heuristic.

## Design — normative detail
Only `fgdb-secure-view` can construct `AuthorizedSnapshot`, `AuthorizedCursor`, `AuthorizedGraphView`, `AuthorizedMutation`, `AuthorizedMutationPermit`, and `AuthorizedDerivedState`; W1's verifier is the sole permit constructor behind that facade. Fabric, Loom, Ripple, Beacon, Prism, UDFs, backup/export, observability, and constraint reporting cannot obtain raw Strata cursors or unscoped commit submission. Planner pushdown is an optimization atop this boundary, never the authorization root. The coordinator independently verifies the permit and final-effect authorization as §5.2 requires. Authorization occurs before retrieval/statistics/ANN traversal/expansion and both before and after mutation. Hidden-state constraints require an explicit `ConstraintDisclosureContract`: `CompleteDomainAuthority` (mutator may observe the entire constrained domain), `AuthorityPartitioned` (integrity defined independently inside a tenant/authority partition), or `ExplicitConflictDeclassification` (a narrowly scoped capability deliberately releases one padded conflict bit, with audit ticket, rate limit, and no conflicting identity/value). A blind writer without one of these is rejected *before probing* — error redaction cannot make global uniqueness and zero disclosure coexist, so the plan refuses to pretend. The disclosure-contract regime also covers hidden-edge cascades, property/provenance/embedding masks, invoker-versus-definer view rights, subscription reauthorization, capability-safe conflicts and certificates, branch merge, system graph, backup/restore, and descriptor masking; every API and operator declares permitted declassifications and has a noninterference row plus cross-capability differential tests.

Descriptor masking is an enforced object: only `fgdb-secure-view` constructs `DescriptorVisibilityProjection {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,graph_reference_binding,snapshot_identity,canonical_visible_descriptor_keys,per_descriptor_predicate_digests,degree_mode:ExactAuthorityPartition{visible_count_index_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizedVisibleCountIndex>}|FilteredScanRequired,projection_digest}`. The permit, access admission, AuthorizedSnapshot, witness/routing basis, plan certificate, cache key, and release decision all bind that digest and exact authority record. An `ExactAuthorityPartition` count is usable only when authority partition/predicates match; otherwise degree uses authorized filtered scan. Hidden descriptors/rows affect no visible enumeration, cardinality, routing, plan/error/timing/statistics/cache fact.

§12.4: one canonical type keys every persisted or reusable derived object: `DerivedIdentity {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,kind,definition_oid,source_coverage:sorted Vec<DerivedSourceCoverage{input_role_id,source_relation_id,base_binding:CoordinateSchemaBinding,tracking_mode:Fixed|Advancing,lineage_digest}>,global_batch_frontier?,topology_epoch,language_contract_oid?,semantic_profile_oid,scalar_profile_oid,collation_profile_oid?,redaction_profile_oid,build_profile_oid}`. Equal epoch/digest scalars under another policy/revocation root cannot share an identity or cache/build generation. Fields irrelevant to a kind are explicit canonical `None`, never ambient defaults. View, index, statistics, subscription, plan/result cache, `DerivedGenerationRegistry`, certificate, and replay schemas embed this exact identity or its digest plus a strong ref; a lookup must match all fields before applying a registered tail/rebuild rule. Derived objects carry an `AuthorityReuseLaw`: row-complete raw caches may derive a narrower domain only through an authorization-preserving projection that also masks metadata; aggregates, cardinalities, sketches, BM25 statistics, DP results, and constraint outcomes require exact-domain state or a proved sufficient decomposition; HNSW/graph-routing topology requires exact authorized topology or a separately proved filter-aware construction. Definer views pin definer authority plus result-exposure policy; invoker state is authority-partitioned. Revocation or incarnation advance removes reachability even if bytes remain cached. Hardened errors use bounded capability-safe classes; plans, abort reports, witnesses, timing padding, and telemetry are redacted before crossing the boundary.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 (restated core): authorization precedes every observation or effect across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, workspace, errors, constraints/witnesses/prepares, derived state, Prism/UDFs, streams, capabilities, replay/export/backup, audit, and observability; hidden constraints follow one explicit disclosure contract and only named ticketed declassification is legal. Timing/cardinality leakage mitigation results are deployment-specific `StatisticalClaim`s (never universal noninterference proofs) naming secret distribution, attacker observations, concurrency assumptions, padding schedule, sampling design, confidence bound, and identity-level cumulative budget.

## Interactions
w4-secure-view owns the facade crate this bead specifies the contract for; w9-threat-tokens supplies verified authority and `SecurityStateBinding`; w5-planner must preserve authorization through rewrites; w7-* index beads and w8-projection consume `AuthorizedDerivedState`/`DescriptorVisibilityProjection`; w6-views consume the definer/invoker rules; w9-dp consumes the exact-domain law; w9-redaction-erasure extends the visibility conjunct.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Compile-fail tests: constructing any `Authorized*` type outside `fgdb-secure-view` fails. Differential noninterference: hidden-vs-physically-removed database pairs must produce byte-identical visible enumeration, cardinality, plans, errors, timing classes, statistics, and cache facts across every operator with a noninterference row — this bead ships the pair-construction harness and runs it over the non-operator surfaces in its dependency closure (enumeration, cardinality, errors, statistics, and cache facts via `fgdb-secure-view` reads); the per-operator instantiations accrue as `w5-gla-algebra` operator registrations land, and full-matrix closure is an epic-w9/gate-g2 prerequisite, not this bead's merge blocker. Negative: blind uniqueness probe without a disclosure contract is rejected pre-probe; `ExactAuthorityPartition` count under mismatched predicates falls back to filtered scan. Property: `DerivedIdentity` lookup requires all-field match; equal-scalar/different-root cache reuse is rejected. E2E: revoke a token, prove cached derived bytes become unreachable, with logs showing the reachability cut. Detailed logging: authorization decisions, pre-probe disclosure-contract rejections, degree-mode fallbacks (ExactAuthorityPartition -> FilteredScanRequired with the mismatch reason), DerivedIdentity cache-reuse rejections naming the mismatched field, and revocation/incarnation reachability cuts each emit a typed structured event carrying authority-binding and projection digests - commitments only, never hidden identities or values; the differential noninterference suites additionally assert the boundary-crossing log/telemetry surface is byte-identical between hidden and physically-removed runs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: enforcement-by-convention/pushdown-as-root; global uniqueness with zero disclosure (impossible — padded declassification bit instead); generic subset-slogan cache reuse (replaced by `AuthorityReuseLaw`). Risk: filtered-scan degree on mismatched partitions costs latency — priced honestly as an `slo.toml`/benchmark-class cost under §17's disclosure laws rather than weakened (filtered-scan degree is execution latency, not an Appendix G operation class: Appendix G registers structural protocol counts, and µs budgets are `slo.toml` rows keyed {operation_class,posture,audit_class}).

## Provenance
§12.3–12.4 (884–898), §5.2 coordinator verification, App A 2615–2623 (decision records).

### Fidelity addendum — exact policy semantics and root
`PolicySemantics` is the immutable exact `{policy_id,version,policy_ir_ref:StrongRef<PolicyIr>,policy_ir_semantics_oid,evaluator_artifact_ref:StrongRef<PolicyEvaluatorArtifact>,scalar_profile_oid,unicode_and_collation_profile_oids,allowed_operation_classes,resource_ceiling_semantics,disclosure_contract_set,body_digest}`. `PolicyEvaluatorArtifact` is deterministic, total, fuel/memory bounded, byte-matched to `policy_ir_semantics_oid`, and carries an executable/proof-test manifest under the closed dependency universe; evaluator selection by ambient binary version is forbidden.

`SecurityPolicyRoot` is exactly `{format_version,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,role:Local|Meta,generation,security_policy_epoch,scope_assignment_root,accepted_semantics_root,active_issuance_map_root,retention_floor_ref:StrongRef<SecurityPolicyRetentionFloor>,applied_transition_index_root,body_digest}`. Entry status is the closed `Candidate|ActiveForIssuance|RetainedForVerification|RetiredTombstone`; every scope has exactly one Active issuer or explicit DenyAll. Shards receive certified, clipped projections only and never instantiate this authority root.

Golden/mutation tests cover every field/transcript, evaluator/semantics mismatch, unsupported scalar/Unicode/collation profile, duplicate active issuer, missing DenyAll, wrong role/incarnation, ceiling widening, and retired artifact still used for issuance. Differential/property tests run the reference IR and compiled evaluator under fixed fuel and require identical decision/disclosure/resource outputs. E2E rotates Candidate to Active while old semantics remain RetainedForVerification, then retires only after the exact floor. Logs emit policy/semantics/evaluator commitments, root generation/epoch/role, scope commitment, selected entry status, fuel consumed, decision/disclosure/resource commitment, and stable rejection; policy contents and protected attributes are not logged.
